scope: All experiment README reports currently present under repository-root results and test2026/metal/results.
limitations: Inventory presence does not establish success or independent replication.
Reports retain their original historical status; live-state changes belong in the research journal.

reports.title: GPU-verified contiguous prompt-slot lookup: repeated latency gains
reports.report_text:
# GPU-verified contiguous prompt-slot lookup: repeated latency gains

The existing chunk-attention kernel repeatedly scans preceding tokens for
each visible cache slot to find its latest writer. This experiment checks
the current query's active prefix once per threadgroup. If every earlier
token is active and has consecutive integer slots, the writer follows
directly from `slot - first_slot`. Otherwise it retains the original scan.
Cached slots preceding the chunk still read the old cache. Inactive queries
still produce zero output. Score, softmax, value accumulation and gating
remain FP32, with unchanged learned values and arithmetic order.

`GARNET_METAL_ATTENTION_PREFIX` defaults OFF. The GPU verifies actual control
values at every query; it does not assume that callers always use consecutive
slots. The experiment introduces no request-to-request prefix reuse, encoder
reuse or speculative decoding. The selected primary library is preserved.

Two terminal component runs pass 36 shape profiles / 1,008 changed-input
comparisons. They cover batches 1/2, chunks 16/32/80, three GQA layouts,
gated/ungated output, changed data and seven control patterns: consecutive
slots from zero, a cached prefix, paused tail, duplicate overwrites, gaps,
paused/resumed tokens and leading pauses. Output is bit-identical to the
extracted control kernel, including forced padded strides. Independent FP64
references pass with a maximum tolerance ratio of 0.005630 against the
unchanged `5e-6 + 5e-5*abs(reference)` bound.

| VL-shaped component | Initial control / shortcut GPU ms | Initial ratio | Confirmation control / shortcut GPU ms | Confirmation ratio |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| B1, chunk 80, 8 query / 2 KV heads, dimension 256 | 2.1644 / 0.6212 | 3.4844× | 2.6735 / 0.7363 | 3.6307× |
| B2, chunk 32, same head layout | 0.3276 / 0.1804 | 1.8159× | 0.3283 / 0.1796 | 1.8281× |

The 288 ABBA timing records contain 12 completed submissions each. Synthetic
inputs and warm command-buffer spans are used; these are component gains,
not model throughput or end-to-end TTFT improvements. Absolute timings vary.
The production MSL conditional resolves to exactly the tested shortcut body;
default-OFF resolution preserves the control body.

The initial component attempt exited before shader generation because the
guard observed an unverified WorldSense PID. That PID was already missing
when audited, and the saved service source fingerprints were unchanged.
The guard now rechecks PID liveness after a failed service audit; a still-live
unknown worker remains rejected. Three process-exit regression cases verify
the disappeared-PID, live-unknown and verified-service decisions. No other
job was stopped or reclassified without verification. Later GPU runs completed
with guarded 0.5-second monitoring.

During the first full-model run, the Mac volume filled and the final worker's
monitor write failed with `ENOSPC`. The queued confirmation correctly refused
to start. That incomplete timing run is retained but excluded from conclusions.
An initial retry then stopped on an updated WorldSense supervisor fingerprint.
Read-only inspection confirmed the same pinned HTTP launch payload/file and
no inference/GPU libraries in either live process. The inspected supervisor
fingerprint was added to the existing environment-name exclusion, retaining
all loaded-library and unknown-worker checks. No WorldSense process was stopped.

Storage recovery removed 705 verified, reproducible `.bin` matrix assets from
old isolated component jobs, totaling 15.17 GiB. Before deletion, original
checkpoint, manifest, size and asset hashes were revalidated. Only individual
derived files inside the investigation logs were removed; canonical models,
libraries, source, manifests and textual evidence were retained. All three
retained checkpoint hashes are recorded in `source-history/cleanup-removed.json`.
The volume subsequently reported 19 GiB free. Clean timing reruns monitor free
space and reject runs below 2 GiB. Complete discarded runs, cleanup provenance
and supervisor audits remain available for review.

The candidate is isolated in `build-attention-prefix`. Other experimental
vision-fusion, joined-prefill and native-BF16-body flags are OFF. Standard
handoff checks, exact 22/26-token references and extended Qwen3.5 references
are recorded separately from native ABBA timing. The current matched text,
coder and VL workloads retain their prompts, image bytes, capacities,
precision, caps and prefill plans. Native outputs record the actual backend
feature marker after the measured work.

All 16 configure/build/validation stages pass: standard native handoff,
48 exact-tail comparisons and 36 extended Qwen3.5 comparisons. Two complete
healthy native ABBA runs cover all six model/batch profiles and 144 complete
outputs. Every prompt, generated token sequence, stopping state and VL patch
hash matches the frozen control. Four non-first requests per build/profile
form each warm mean. The incomplete and guard-rejected runs are excluded.

| Model | Batch | Initial TTFT reduction | Confirmation control → candidate ms | Confirmation TTFT reduction | Confirmation decode ratio |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Qwen3-0.6B text | 1 | 2.12% | 54.41 → 51.57 | 5.21% | 0.9866× |
| Qwen3-0.6B text | 2 | 4.96% | 89.53 → 86.87 | 2.97% | 1.0000× |
| Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B | 1 | 8.15% | 38.13 → 35.33 | 7.34% | 1.0012× |
| Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B | 2 | 9.20% | 60.89 → 56.97 | 6.44% | 0.9965× |
| Qwen3.5-0.8B VL | 1 | 5.36% | 214.24 → 205.64 | 4.01% | 1.0033× |
| Qwen3.5-0.8B VL | 2 | −0.68% | 386.08 → 381.85 | 1.10% | 1.0011× |

Warm TTFT gains repeat for text/coder at both batches and VL at B1. VL B2
does not establish a repeatable gain. Decode computation is unchanged and
the small mixed decode ratios do not establish improved token generation
speed. The selected primary/control library remains unchanged; the optional
candidate is available for the five profiles with repeated latency gains.
The next matched comparator study should retain the control for VL B2.
The CMake flag remains OFF by default while this selection is investigated.

Confirmation first-use TTFT (excluding initialization) is 154.23 → 149.69 ms
for text B1, 191.46 → 189.35 for text B2, 123.75 → 121.03 for coder B1,
145.53 → 137.06 for coder B2, 338.98 → 326.65 for VL B1 and 565.69 → 557.79
for VL B2. Some initial first-use gains do not repeat in direction; these are
worker first-use observations, not flushed hardware/driver cache measurements.
Confirmation initialization ratios are 0.9814–0.9999; individual RSS changes
range −18.71 to +11.30 MiB. No memory-allocation saving or broadly faster
startup is established by this lookup-only change.

The candidate library SHA-256 is
`f2c5c448ec4f3c8431be37b48a2634d8fa4cc31de4aa163ec367a319c9263088`.
The preserved primary/control remains
`73c10e5dc62eb97607e9ded9a1df8bb6702d87375620bd5dc160d8b871f78ce2`.
The archive SHA-256 is
`42fab335acc54a5e794c9a47e3d4948b4250d7e07dac9cc8e5ed97a0a5b1458a`.
The verifier checks 1,091 archived hashes, actual compiler definitions,
control/shortcut MSL equivalence to tested source, all terminal results,
1,008 component comparisons, 3,456 timed component submissions, all 144
healthy model outputs/warm means and recorded disk-space guards.

Initialization, first-use and warm requests are separate; OS/driver caches
are not flushed. Individual worker RSS is not unique GPU memory or aggregate
process-tree memory. No new vLLM-Metal result is established by the native
control/candidate study. The overall 2x decode / half-TTFT goal remains unmet.

reports.title: CPU foundation for a parallel recurrent prefill experiment
reports.report_text:
# CPU foundation for a parallel recurrent prefill experiment

This is mathematical/numerical evidence, not a GPU implementation or speedup.
The current serving recurrence remains unchanged by this prototype.

With state layout key-by-value, normalized keys/queries and update vectors U:

- S_i = d_i S_initial + sum(j<=i) D_ij k_j U_j.
- U_i = beta_i (v_i - d_i k_i^T S_initial)
  - sum(j<i) beta_i D_ij (k_i^T k_j) U_j.
- y_i = d_i q_i^T S_initial + sum(j<=i) D_ij (q_i^T k_j) U_j.

D_ij is the product of original FP32 exp(log_decay) factors from j+1 through i.
d_i is the product from the start through i. Inactive rows use decay 1/beta 0
and return zero output. No clipping, log(0), inverse decay or learned-value
change is introduced. A unit-lower triangular solve produces U; matrix
contractions produce token outputs and final state. Blocks may also be
processed consecutively using their actual carried state.

The latest explicit-contraction CPU version passes 144 synthetic cases:
batches 1/2, lengths 2/16/32/40/64/80, ordinary/no decay, exact zero decay
from exp(-1000), inactive/all-inactive tokens, beta 0/1 and carried random
state. Both whole and 32-token segmented forms are checked.

It also passes 108 real-weight full-layer comparisons for Qwen3.5-0.8B:
first/last linear layers 0/22, batches 1/2, chunks 16/32/40/64 and chunk 80
at batch 1, three state-carry steps, inactive rows, and whole/32-slot
segmented forms. Outputs, convolution state and recurrent state are compared
against the existing independent sequential reference, including normalization,
output projection and MLP. The unchanged bound is 5e-6 + 5e-5*abs(reference).

Worst real-layer bound ratio is 0.127150753 (<= 1 passes).


The first two real-weight attempts failed. Diagnostics show prepared
sequential recurrence matches the original reference (state differences
<= 1.2e-7), while the batched NumPy matmul formulation returns inconsistent
results across repeated identical inputs. Changing a zero-stride view alone
did not resolve this. The same formula with explicit FP32 einsum contractions
is stable and passes; the specific backend cause remains unproven. Failed
source/results and both diagnostics are preserved rather than discarded.

The installed MLX-VLM Qwen3.5 source was inspected for its chunk formulation,
but its comments about CUDA performance are not M4 evidence. Its decay
clipping is not adopted. The algebra here uses actual decay products and
forward-substitutes the right-hand side, without constructing a full inverse.
An MPS/Metal implementation still requires primitive/full-layer validation,
complete generated-output checks, repeated real performance measurements
and a matched comparator study before any serving promotion.

A separate bit-preserving norm-cache experiment follows the observation
that current Garnet repeats query/key norms for every value tile and uses
two threadgroup barriers per token. It does not implement this matrix solve.

No 2x/half-TTFT target is achieved by CPU proof. The full goal remains active.

Evidence archive SHA256: 320c7cdf813d4ca12afa26053aa72f847df88c04b998165fe26c5e2e5511cbe8.

reports.title: Compact joined half-weight storage: lower memory, no repeated latency gain
reports.report_text:
# Compact joined half-weight storage: lower memory, no repeated latency gain

The existing joined-prefill experiment reduced warm TTFT by about 2–3%
in its admitted text B2 and coder B1 workloads, but retained duplicate half
weights and increased worker peak RSS by about 335/167 MiB. This candidate
lets individual projections share offset MPSMatrix views of the joined
half-weight allocation. The original learned BF16 decode buffers remain.
Per-row scale buffers are also shared, with explicit offsets. Repacking
reads both matrix and scale offsets, including a reversed weight pair.

`GARNET_METAL_COMPACT_JOINED_PREFILL` defaults OFF and requires the existing
default-OFF joined-prefill option. Admission shapes, floating-point
arithmetic, prompts, caps, batching and cache behavior are unchanged.
The selected primary and attention libraries are not replaced. This is an
allocation experiment, with no claimed decode algorithm improvement.

## Actual validation

The isolated Mac build and CTest completed with exit 0. The native joined
tests compare complete dyadic outputs bit for bit for both admission
shapes. Added tests exercise individual projections after joining,
reversed-pair repacking and individual projections after reversing. The
existing independent vision, convolution, delta, direct-write and matrix
tests also pass. All 18 guarded validation stages completed with exit 0,
including 48 trained text/coder exact-tail/state comparisons with unchanged
numerical bounds and dispatch assertions, 24 private-cache profiles,
trained VL/dense layer and output-head checks, and pretrained vision.
Pending snapshots remain historical observations; `evidence` contains the
completed job results.

Candidate library SHA-256:
`b58260e7e3a8488bf888d6f3d27a957ea209b1e28f5ee1afd12cbd4dfda1762b`.

The durable validation job PID **75480** completed with exit 0 after
847.82 seconds. Its authoritative directory is
`/Users/zsdx/garnet-metal-investigation/logs/compact-joined-checks-20261013`.
Initial benchmark PID **92146** and confirmation PID **94979** also
completed with exit 0, after 144.44 and 40.60 seconds. No inference job
from this experiment remains running.

## Actual matched native measurements

The original joined library and compact candidate ran sequentially in
ABBA order across all six frozen profiles, followed by a repeat of the
two admitted profiles. All 96 complete generated IDs, prompt IDs, finish
flags, input cases and actual joined dispatch counts match. Every VL
request freshly encodes the image. The comparison control is
the original joined library, SHA-256
`cc41fde1f3905fcfb02fed6a50ab0f9d68933e94358352b92db4e44cb5f43dfe`;
the validation build metadata separately fingerprints the unchanged
primary library. No fresh vLLM baseline has been run for this candidate.

| Admitted profile | Peak RSS reduction, initial / repeat | Warm TTFT, initial control → compact | Repeat control → compact | Repeat decode ratio |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Text B2 | 338.84 / 337.86 MiB | 84.99 → 83.14 ms | 85.63 → 86.07 ms | 1.00006 |
| Coder B1 | 166.86 / 165.41 MiB | 36.88 → 36.72 ms | 36.56 → 37.31 ms | 0.99452 |

The memory reduction repeats, but the small initial warm-TTFT benefit
does not. First use after initialization is slower in both runs: repeat
text B2 257.97 → 259.82 ms and coder B1 193.07 → 200.24 ms. Initialization
is separately measured and approximately unchanged: repeat text B2
1.73404/1.73462 seconds; coder B1 1.38242/1.38369 seconds. No combined
startup sum is presented as an observed clock. OS/driver caches were not
flushed; these are fresh-worker first-use measurements, not proven
hardware-cold samples. Unsupported profiles do not share joined storage;
their changes are not attributed to this method.

RSS is macOS `/usr/bin/time -l` worker/process-family peak resident set,
including initialization and first use. It is not unique GPU allocation,
an aggregate of parallel workers or per-request current memory. Two fresh
workers per policy supply four non-first warm requests per workload.
The comparison preserves arithmetic and learned values; its original
compact BF16/exact-half weight traffic differs from the investigation's
losslessly expanded FP32 vLLM comparator. This experiment establishes no
stock-BF16 vLLM advantage.

Commands, from the isolated source's `test2026/metal` directory:

```text
python3 run_compact_joined_job.py ROOT ROOT/logs/compact-joined-checks-20261013
python3 run_compact_joined_job.py ROOT ROOT/logs/compact-joined-native-20261013 --profiles
python3 run_compact_joined_job.py ROOT ROOT/logs/compact-joined-native-confirm-20261013 --profiles --confirm
python3 archive_compact_joined.py ROOT ROOT/compact-joined-evidence.tar.gz
python3 verify_compact_joined.py EXTRACTED_EVIDENCE VERIFICATION_JSON
```

All listed commands executed successfully. Do not rerun them against the
existing output/build directories. The installer hash-checks prior source bytes and preserves a
backup before installing only the isolated investigation's source files.
The original GPT-OSS and Pi checkouts remain clean.

Packing still occurs on first use; this change alone does not remove that
latency. Cross-pair reuse can retain multiple joined allocations. As with
the existing context encoding API, simultaneous calls on shared mutable
weight/context objects are outside this experiment's tested usage.
Native tests establish offset-view compatibility on the actual macOS/M4;
the API is documented in Apple's [MPSMatrix buffer/offset initializer](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/metalperformanceshaders/mpsmatrix/init(buffer:offset:descriptor:)).

The evidence archive SHA-256 is
`372490609bb8656a8d041360a0d138918cb5f4ccfba6578adeb7c122fa61b307`.
The local verifier checked all 486 archived file hashes, validation stages,
dispatch counts, full outputs, chunk plans, fresh image encoding, actual
worker peak RSS and recomputed warm means/ratios. See `verification.json`
and `first-use-summary.json`. The full 2x decode and half-TTFT objective
remains unmet. The memory improvement does not establish a latency or
decode improvement, so the experiment remains default OFF.

python3 run_compact_joined_job.py ROOT ROOT/logs/compact-joined-native-20261013 --profiles
python3 run_compact_joined_job.py ROOT ROOT/logs/compact-joined-native-confirm-20261013 --profiles --confirm
python3 archive_compact_joined.py ROOT ROOT/compact-joined-evidence.tar.gz

reports.title: Actual comparator precision audit
reports.report_text:
# Actual comparator precision audit

The installed vLLM-Metal normal text and VL loaders retain checkpoint weight
dtype. Requesting `dtype=float32` alone changes its KV dtype, not all loaded
weights or activations. Six actual loaded-model inspections establish this
on the M4 GPU, without changing comparator math, loaders or security settings.

The final probe inspects both public model parameters and the original
projection modules held privately by paged-attention wrappers. It evaluates
one embedding, first input norm and first attention projection on GPU and
records their actual output dtypes. Each engine closes before the next starts.
These are dtype diagnostics, not inference speed measurements.

| Model | Requested dtype | Actual parameter tensors | KV dtype | Probed activations |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Qwen3-0.6B | BF16 | 310 BF16 | BF16 | BF16 |
| Qwen3-0.6B | FP32 | 310 BF16 | FP32 | BF16 |
| Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct | BF16 | 290 BF16 | BF16 | BF16 |
| Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct | FP32 | 290 BF16 | FP32 | BF16 |
| Qwen3.5-0.8B | BF16 | 437 BF16 + 36 FP32 | BF16 | BF16 |
| Qwen3.5-0.8B | FP32 | 437 BF16 + 36 FP32 | FP32 | BF16 |

The loaded parameter counts are 596,049,920 for text, 494,032,768 for coder,
and 852,985,920 for VL. The hybrid model already contains some FP32 state/
gating parameters; this does not make its entire model FP32.

The first probe failed because callable RPC serialization is disabled by
default. Its engine shut down cleanly. Using the supported in-process engine
permits direct inspection without enabling insecure serialization. Initial
successful inspections counted only public parameters and missed private
attention owners; the final six inspections correct that coverage. All
historical commands, exits and source versions are retained and hash-checked.

`comparator-actual-dtypes-complete-20261013/jobs/summary.json` is authoritative.
Each result includes installed versions, actual model/KV/activation dtypes,
GPU device, wrapper owners and representative parameter shapes. The archived
installed loader and wrapper sources explain the observed behavior.

This confirms that existing Garnet FP32 versus stock comparator BF16 results
have a precision difference. A separate exact-value FP32 representation study
is prepared next; it will stay separate from the default BF16 benchmark.
The 2× throughput / half-TTFT goal remains unmet.

# Refreshed operation attribution for the selected implementation

Six sequential real native workloads cover text, coder and Qwen3.5 VL at
batches 1/2. All complete token IDs, prompt IDs and finished flags match the
latest retained equivalent-FP32 comparison's native outputs. The library is
the selected extended-prefill build, SHA256
cc5539990dcb4effbece7c611787a656df56b51271f1f40e1c3e8b5dbf90c8f8.

at batch 2. Prompt lengths, image bytes, stop rules and output caps are unchanged.

The diagnostic enables GARNET_METAL_PROFILE_OPS=1, which serializes operations.
Its 60,816 operation records identify costs, but their times must not be
presented as serving performance, added to warm TTFT, or compared to vLLM
tokens/sec. There is one actual request per profile, including first-use;
this is not a cold/warm throughput study. Before/after process guards reject
competing inference. External services and existing checkouts are untouched.

| Model / batch | Decode-width up projections, aggregate GPU ms | Vocabulary head, aggregate GPU ms | Down projections, aggregate GPU ms |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Text / 1 | 29.07 | 23.38 | 14.51 |
| Text / 2 | 28.83 | 23.56 | 15.68 |
| Coder / 1 | 73.29 | 45.29 | 35.86 |
| Coder / 2 | 73.87 | 45.59 | 36.71 |
| VL / 1 | 106.35 | 137.14 | 55.25 |
| VL / 2 | 106.50 | 138.06 | 57.19 |

The table groups recorded operations by shape; it includes the final prefill
head and all decode heads. Aggregates across models have different token and
layer counts. VL has other substantial QKV projections omitted from this
compact table. Exact shapes/counts and the full ranking are in summary.json.

The largest batched prefill up-projection groups cost 12.23/11.31 ms for text,
10.68/16.11 ms for coder, and 16.84/23.28 ms for VL (batches 1/2). The next
experiments should address these projections and the substantial head cost;
the rejected parallel-delta algorithms are not supported by this evidence.
These ranks alone do not prove memory bandwidth or any hardware bottleneck.

For perspective, the latest uninstrumented VL comparator records already
saved in qwen35-extended-prefill/comparator have four warm native requests
per batch. Their worker prefill wall means are 107.76/206.14 ms, vision/reset

The much older 431/580 ms prefill attribution is no longer representative.

Commands, six terminal statuses, raw operation logs, current guard evidence,
case files, complete outputs, rankings and runner/worker source snapshots are
in completed/ and source/. Fresh image tensor/RGB files are omitted from the
archive; their identity is recorded in the retained request records.
Archive SHA256:
5955939be8329d35a8bedc3f6a5f9194c6237a223f535bbaed578b1a208de4ab.

objective for all three matched Qwen workloads remains active and unmet.

reports.title: Independent decode accumulators: component candidate, not a serving gain
reports.report_text:
# Independent decode accumulators: component candidate, not a serving gain

This experiment breaks a projection's FP32 accumulation dependency into two
or four independent per-lane sums, then combines them before the SIMD
reduction. BF16 learned values and FP32 inputs, accumulation and outputs
remain; summation order changes. The production source and selected native
libraries are unchanged. No quantization, prefix reuse or speculation is used.

An actual isolated M4 run tests four variants (two/four sums, 64/128 threads)
on real first-layer matrices and complete vocabulary heads for all three
checkpoints, batches 1/2 and irregular synthetic tails. All 272 candidate
checks pass an independent host FP64 dot-product reference. The fixed
forward-error bound is `gamma(n) * sum(abs(products)) + 1e-7`, where
`n = ceil(inner / 32) + 32` and `gamma(n) = n*float_epsilon / (1-n*float_epsilon)`.
The original control must pass that bound too. Output padding is preserved.
Worst error/bound ratio is 0.00997264. Archive audits verify finite learned
values and finite dot-product bounds for every asset. Candidate output bits
can differ from control; no existing full-layer tolerance has been changed.

Most body projections are slower or flat. The two-sum/64-thread variant has
a small text batch-1 vocabulary-head signal. A separate sequential repeat
therefore tests only that variant and the three complete heads at both
batches. All six repeat checks pass; worst error/bound ratio is 0.00343388.

| Actual vocabulary head | Batch | Initial GPU speedup | Repeat GPU speedup |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Qwen3-0.6B | 1 | 1.073 | 1.086 |
| Qwen3-0.6B | 2 | 0.972 | 0.994 |
| Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct | 1 | 1.004 | 1.026 |
| Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct | 2 | 0.994 | 0.995 |
| Qwen3.5-0.8B | 1 | 1.052 | 1.019 |
| Qwen3.5-0.8B | 2 | 1.000 | 0.999 |

Each timing uses two ABBA rounds, three warm-ups and twelve samples per
position. These are warm isolated matrix timings with deterministic finite
sinusoidal inputs, not actual model hidden states or model throughput.
Text batch 1's head improves in both runs; the VL effect shrinks in the
repeat, coder remains marginal and batch 2 is flat. Small-output body
controls here use the general four-output kernel, whereas selected serving
uses its separate small-output kernel. These body results cannot justify
replacing that serving path.

Only a bounded text batch-1 head candidate merits a full-model investigation.
It has not been integrated or validated against real normalized hidden
states and complete generated outputs. Even an 8.6% head improvement would
be a smaller whole-model gain. No decode-TPS, TTFT or vLLM speedup is claimed.
The full three-model 2x decode / half-TTFT goal remains active and unmet.

## Actual commands and evidence

```text
python3 run_decode_accumulators_probe.py INVESTIGATION_ROOT OUTPUT_DIR
python3 run_decode_accumulators_head_probe.py INVESTIGATION_ROOT OUTPUT_DIR
```

Both durable jobs have authoritative exit code 0. The second waits for the
first's successful terminal status. Exact shader-generation, compiler and
GPU commands, source/checkpoint/matrix hashes, raw timing windows, device
limits, numerical checks and process snapshots are under `evidence/`.
The runner monitors every 0.5 seconds and terminates only its owned process
group on contention or deadline; unrelated jobs are not stopped. Sampling
cannot prove absence of arbitrarily short jobs between polls. No concurrent
inference was admitted. Existing WorldSense services remained untouched.

Raw matrix copies and compiled binaries are omitted from Git with individual
hashes and sizes retained in `evidence-proof.json`. All executed source
versions and generated shaders are retained. Archive SHA256:
`ee356339e9455bd2f3f26477f34b5b21b41547aa7acc65f3d72a61bb70797f86`.

python3 run_decode_accumulators_head_probe.py INVESTIGATION_ROOT OUTPUT_DIR

reports.title: Decode work distribution: component evidence, not a model speed claim
reports.report_text:
# Decode work distribution: component evidence, not a model speed claim

Two actual isolated runs on the M4 Mac mini test four alternatives to the
selected BF16 kernel's four outputs per SIMD group / 128 threads per group:
two outputs / 64 or 128 threads, and four outputs / 64 or 256 threads.
The variants retain the original per-output FP32 accumulation and SIMD
reduction order, original BF16 bits and row-sharing for batch 2.

Each run validates and times 272 cases: actual first-layer projections and
complete runtime vocabulary heads for all three models, plus irregular
synthetic tails, at batches 1 and 2. All 544 checks are bit-identical to the
selected kernel, including output padding. Timings use repeated ABBA order,
three warm-ups and twelve samples per policy position. Only one GPU probe or
inference runtime runs at once. These are warm matrix-component measurements;
they do not represent model decode throughput or vLLM performance.

The two-output / 64-thread variant has a repeatable small-matrix signal:

| Actual matrix | Batch | Initial GPU speedup | Repeat GPU speedup |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Coder key projection, 128×896 | 1 | 1.636× | 1.609× |
| Coder key projection, 128×896 | 2 | 1.583× | 1.589× |
| Coder value projection, 128×896 | 1 | 1.652× | 1.563× |
| Coder value projection, 128×896 | 2 | 1.618× | 1.599× |
| Qwen3.5 `in_proj_a`, 16×1024 | 1 | 1.697× | 1.512× |
| Qwen3.5 `in_proj_a`, 16×1024 | 2 | 1.524× | 1.405× |
| Qwen3.5 `in_proj_b`, 16×1024 | 1 | 1.409× | 1.370× |
| Qwen3.5 `in_proj_b`, 16×1024 | 2 | 1.519× | 1.522× |

These save approximately 2–5 microseconds per small projection in the repeat.
Large matrices show mixed results and the complete heads do not demonstrate
a consistent gain. Therefore the variants have not been integrated into
serving, and cannot support a 2× whole-model claim. A bounded small-output
dispatch remains a possible later experiment with full-model validation.

`probe-source/` retains the actual driver, generator, asset collector and
runner. Both job directories preserve commands, terminal exits, generated
Metal source, matrix hashes, process guards and raw samples. Raw matrix
copies are excluded from the archive. The initial metadata accidentally
records the older input-tile runner's digest; that script and the initial
runner are both retained explicitly. The repeat corrects self-hashing and
retains its actual native source. Both runs use the same decode arithmetic.

reports.report_text:
# One-output SIMD decode: rejected

Three isolated Metal variants compute one output column per SIMD group,
with threadgroups of 32, 64 and 128 threads. The control computes four output
columns per SIMD group with 128 threads. Learned BF16 bits, FP32 input,
per-column accumulation sequence, reduction order and batch-2 weight sharing
are unchanged. There is no quantization or weight-layout expansion.

The actual M4/16 GiB run passes 204 bit-exact comparisons on first-layer
matrices and full vocabulary heads from all three checkpoints, plus irregular
synthetic tails. Both batches 1/2 and output-padding preservation are checked.
Every profile runs two ABBA rounds, three warmups per position, and twelve
samples per position. One GPU/inference job runs at a time.

Full-head control/candidate median GPU time ratios:

| Model / batch | 32 threads | 64 threads | 128 threads |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Text / 1 | 0.959 | 0.980 | 0.984 |
| Text / 2 | 0.923 | 0.922 | 0.985 |
| Coder / 1 | 1.011 | 0.966 | 0.999 |
| Coder / 2 | 0.929 | 0.950 | 0.977 |
| Qwen3.5 VL / 1 | 1.070 | 0.937 | 0.861 |
| Qwen3.5 VL / 2 | 0.820 | 0.810 | 0.954 |

Greater than one means faster. There is no consistent head improvement:
the single positive VL batch-1 result is paired with a substantial batch-2
regression. No serving integration, favorable-sample repeat, full-model A/B
or new vLLM comparison follows this rejected candidate. The selected library
is unchanged. Component ratios are not model tokens/sec claims.

Commands, source hashes, guards, terminal statuses, numerical checks and raw
timing windows are in completed/. Exact probe sources are in source/ and
test2026/metal/. Raw matrices and binaries remain on the Mac; their sizes

reports.title: Sixteen-lane decode groups: full-model integration rejected
reports.report_text:
# Sixteen-lane decode groups: full-model integration rejected

The broad 64-thread integration is rejected and its five serving/worker files
are restored to their verified originals on Windows and the isolated Mac.
All 19 validation stages and 72 complete native outputs pass, but decode is
slower in every full-model profile. The repeated component gains below did
not carry into serving. No favorable-number repeat or fresh vLLM comparison
is justified for this rejected integration; the full goal remains unmet.

## Actual native request results

Native ABBA uses two fresh workers per build/profile, three requests each,
with four warm samples after excluding each worker's first request. Same
checkpoint values, precision, prompts, capacities, caps, stopping rules,
image bytes and chunk plans; fresh image encoding and sequential execution.

| Model | Batch | Control TPS/row | Candidate TPS/row | Decode ratio | Control TTFT ms | Candidate TTFT ms |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Qwen3-0.6B | 1 | 58.05 | 57.81 | 0.9960 | 51.89 | 52.89 |
| Qwen3-0.6B | 2 | 57.57 | 56.83 | 0.9871 | 86.09 | 87.31 |
| Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct | 1 | 71.77 | 68.45 | 0.9538 | 36.21 | 35.79 |
| Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct | 2 | 70.84 | 67.33 | 0.9504 | 56.62 | 57.84 |
| Qwen3.5-0.8B | 1 | 47.78 | 47.21 | 0.9882 | 218.43 | 216.67 |
| Qwen3.5-0.8B | 2 | 44.57 | 43.86 | 0.9843 | 383.28 | 384.77 |

Coder loses about 4.6–5.0% decode, while text/VL lose about 0.4–1.6%.
Small coder/VL B1 TTFT improvements do not justify the throughput regression.
No cause for the component/serving difference is established. Aggregate TPS
at B2 is twice the displayed per-row rate for these equal rows. First-use
TTFT after setup is mixed; all separate means are in
[native/summary.json](native/summary.json). Initialization is also separately
recorded, and peak RSS changes are small/mixed (-3.1 to +1.1 MiB). No memory
saving is established. OS/driver caches were not flushed; separate intervals
are not summed and labeled an observed hardware-cold TTFT.

All numerical/serving/head/vision checks retain their previous bounds,
including 48 exact-tail comparisons, 24 private-cache profiles and 36 extended
VL comparisons. Complete prompt/output IDs, stopping flags and chunk plans
match across all 72 requests. Native evidence, source/build/checkpoint hashes,
actual feature flags, guards and exits are in [native/evidence](native/evidence/).

Two actual component runs pass 272 comparisons on real first-layer matrices,
complete vocabulary heads and irregular shapes from all three checkpoints,
at batches 1/2. Both candidates preserve BF16 learned values and FP32
input/accumulation/output. Reduction order changes: results are not generally
bit-identical. No numerical bound is widened.

The candidate gives each 32-lane SIMD group two independent 16-lane output
groups. Each lane holds the original two 32-way partial sums, combines them,
then reduces within its 16 lanes using XOR shuffles. No weight repacking,
additional weight allocation, prefix reuse or speculative decoding is used.
The measured variants have 64/128 threads; the native candidate uses 64.

## Component results

Ratios below pool control GPU ms / candidate GPU ms across collected matrices
with more than 256 outputs, once per matrix/batch. They are unweighted by
model layer counts and cannot be treated as decode TPS improvements.

| Model | 64 threads initial / repeat | 128 threads initial / repeat |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Qwen3-0.6B | 1.0254 / 1.0195 | 1.0179 / 1.0102 |
| Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct | 1.0276 / 1.0137 | 0.9976 / 1.0171 |
| Qwen3.5-0.8B | 1.0526 / 1.0303 | 1.0354 / 1.0372 |

The initial 64-thread batch-1 head ratios are 1.0556/1.0814/1.0957
for text/coder/VL; the repeat is 1.0288/1.0235/1.0291. This contraction is a
reason to require full-model measurements, not infer the larger initial gains.
The repeat's batch-2 head ratios are 1.0223/1.0202/1.0414. Full individual
shapes and timings remain in raw summaries and [component-pooled.json](component-pooled.json).

Each shape/variant uses two ABBA rounds, three warmups per position and
twelve measured operations per position. GPU times are component command
durations; CPU wall timings are also retained. Checks cover input/output
strides, output padding and odd/aligned inner/output tails. Every candidate
passes `5e-6 + 5e-5*abs(control)` and an independent FP64 envelope:
`gamma(ceil(K/32)+32)*sum(abs(products)) + 1e-7`, with float epsilon.
The control independently passes that envelope too. Worst candidate FP64
ratio is 0.00997263774 in both runs. This checks sampled matrix inputs;
it does not prove complete model generation or all future states.

## Tested integration, now reverted

The tested `GARNET_METAL_SUBSIMD_DECODE` defaulted OFF and conflicted with the separate
experimental native-bfloat body option. Only BF16 one/two-row projections
with more than 256 outputs select the candidate. Prefill, FP32-weight paths
and the selected small-output kernel retain their existing routes. The new
pipeline requires 32 hardware lanes and at least 64 threads. The primary
library remained unchanged; a fresh `build-decode-subsimd` was used. The
build option, appended shader, selector and feature marker are now removed
from current serving sources. Reproduction of the rejected candidate must
use the archived candidate source/worker files; its binary is retained.

The integrated 64-thread shader matches the tested source exactly, SHA256:
`b762de547c14fbf567b68470e12522fb88a287334d61ff6cc893ed5ef37c1342`.
Eight source files were installed into the isolated Mac root after verifying
original/new identities and preserving originals. The
[native source manifest](native-source-manifest.json) records them.
Source bundle SHA256:
`576f3ae0265f45997a471cf82db37c3a685dec5cbc1033810db38af2e0a72bc9`.

The candidate configured, built, passed the native MPS reference CTest and
all remaining trained-model, cache, head, vision, exact-tail and extended-VL
checks. The six-profile native ABBA then completed with the regressions above.

Owned root: `/Users/zsdx/garnet-metal-investigation`. Checks wrapper PID 33098,
`logs/decode-subsimd-checks-20261013`; queued inference wrapper PID 35033,
`logs/decode-subsimd-inference-20261013`. Both are terminal exit 0, with no
live handle remaining. Their launchers retain exact absolute commands.
Native control is the unchanged attention-prefix library SHA256
`f2c5c448ec4f3c8431be37b48a2634d8fa4cc31de4aa163ec367a319c9263088`.
CPU-direct reset remains OFF on both sides to isolate the decode layout.
There is no second native timing run of this uniformly slower candidate.

## Reproduction and evidence

Component command: `run_decode_subsimd_probe.py ROOT NEW_OUTPUT_DIR`.
Both component jobs exited 0 (PIDs 31269 and 32059). Exact source snapshots,
generated shader/harness, commands, hardware, checkpoint/matrix hashes,
all quality/timing records and process monitors are in [evidence](evidence/).
Raw `.bin` matrices are omitted and retained privately, with 68 verified
size/hash records in `omitted-matrix-proof.json`; their source can regenerate
them from the pinned checkpoints. No matrix array was deleted by this work.

```text
python test2026/metal/verify_decode_subsimd.py results/20261013/decode-subsimd
```

The verifier checks 81 file hashes, both terminal runs, source identities,
272 numerical/padding checks, checkpoint-derived matrix proofs and timing
calculations. Component archive SHA256:
`dcf1f709c54350db4144f6cb78424de9d97672c0c26c22db14ecab2c4e5ed1b6`.
The [Metal language resources](https://developer.apple.com/metal/resources/)
provide the specification for the shuffle operations; actual support is
established here by compilation and execution on the M4.

The additional native archive has 417 verified files, 19 terminal stages and
72 complete matching outputs. Its SHA256 is
`60ea68ffd5353bf38426e03474e587affc8f90d086220f3a1502dda47934cae3`.
Rejected candidate library SHA256:
`9d051795c22c4f5d0df30329370204e0328fe5ce8338b5f20e3fc601dd8fba6e`.

```text
python test2026/metal/verify_decode_subsimd_native.py results/20261013/decode-subsimd/native
```

The native verifier checks raw hashes, original/installed/reference identities,
explicit validation counts, build identities, complete outputs, actual layout
flags with CPU-direct reset OFF on both sides, fresh frames, timing arithmetic
and all 24 monitored worker exits. The old template's scope/terminal message
uses a reset/BF16-body label; feature flags, executed source and library hashes
identify the actual tested layout. Restoration first verified every current
authored-file hash before replacing only five files with their preserved
originals. [Restoration hashes/script](restoration/) and the before/after
manifest retain that proof. Prior primary/attention/direct-reset libraries and
all component/native evidence and binaries were preserved.

The GPT-OSS/Pi checkouts and primary Metal binaries remain intact. The full
three-model 2x decode/half-TTFT goal remains unmet; the
[latest actual vLLM comparison](../selected-attention-vllm/README.md) retains
all six profiles and their remaining targets.

reports.title: Dense one-pass prefill: verified improvement, full goal still unmet
reports.report_text:
# Dense one-pass prefill: verified improvement, full goal still unmet

Text and coder first-token latency improves when their 22/26-token prompts
use one padded 32-token pass instead of two 16-token passes. Two native
ABBA runs preserve all 96 complete requests. Decode speed is essentially
unchanged. A fresh matched FP32 vLLM-Metal comparison preserves all 48
complete requests, but does not meet every 2x decode or any half-TTFT target.

## Implementation and numerical evidence

`GARNET_METAL_FLOAT_DENSE_KEY_PREFILL=ON` keeps original BF16 checkpoint bits
and decode operations. Dense prefill key projections use FP32 matrix tiles
with 64-term partial sums and a balanced reduction of up to 16 partials.
This removes the large-profile key-cache reference failure without changing
the existing acceptance thresholds. Other projections retain their current
implementation. The option defaults OFF.

The earlier 128-term candidate passes ordinary tests but fails an extended
Qwen3 batch-2, chunk-64 case; its source and failure are saved under
`rejected-128/`. The 64-term candidate passes 144 exact dyadic kernel cases,
all 11 ordinary handoff checks, and 48 independent numerical comparisons:
both models, first/last layers, batches 1/2, chunks 32/64 and three state-carry
steps. These cover inactive rows, partial tails, duplicate/backward slots,
invalid controls, unchanged state after rejected input, reset, closed graphs
and exact resident/explicit agreement. Worst normalized error is 0.992665,
below the existing threshold of 1. The reference uses wider dot accumulation;
NumPy vectorizes acceptance checks while preserving the scalar rules.

`DenseMetalDecoder.enable_prefill(32, 'shared')` and chunk 64 require the
native `dense_key_split_k` capability and hidden size <=1024. Older builds
still reject these profiles before changing decoder state. Twelve actual
old-build requests confirm rejection and preserve their complete outputs.
Default profiles and the MPS projection policy retain their previous limits.

## Repeat native evidence

Each ABBA run uses two fresh processes per policy/profile, three requests
per process and the four non-first requests for warm means. All output IDs,
finished flags and prompt IDs match the frozen prior result. The worker
verifies actual chunk plans `[32]` and `[16,16]`.

| Model | Batch | First run TTFT reduction | Confirmation TTFT reduction | Confirmation decode ratio |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Qwen3-0.6B | 1 | 24.35% | 22.34% | 0.998 |
| Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct | 1 | 28.39% | 27.58% | 0.997 |
| Qwen3-0.6B | 2 | 16.26% | 16.60% | 0.999 |
| Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct | 2 | 16.99% | 17.25% | 0.999 |

Native confirmation first-use TTFT is approximately 165/223 ms for text
and 137/155 ms for coder, batches 1/2. Initialization is measured separately.
Text batch-2 peak child RSS rises about 54 MiB; other profiles stay near or
below their controls. RSS is not aggregate or unique GPU-memory accounting.

## Fresh matched comparison

Both runtimes use the same M4 / 16 GiB Mac mini, learned values, prompts,
stop rules, output caps and batch sizes, with FP32 operations/activations/KV.
Garnet stores original BF16 weights; vLLM-Metal uses the previously verified
lossless FP32-expanded checkpoints. Exact-value proofs and asset hashes are
checked before execution. This is the additional FP32 study:
`counts_as_default_bf16_speedup=false`. Stock BF16 results remain separate.

| Model | Batch | Garnet tokens/s/sequence | vLLM tokens/s/sequence | Decode ratio | Garnet TTFT ms | vLLM TTFT ms |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Text | 1 | 55.97 | 37.05 | 1.51 | 54.34 | 86.31 |
| Coder | 1 | 71.68 | 46.54 | 1.54 | 39.73 | 62.26 |
| Text | 2 | 51.51 | 26.42 | 1.95 | 97.45 | 97.75 |
| Coder | 2 | 69.49 | 29.29 | 2.37 | 61.54 | 84.31 |

Four warm samples per runtime/profile are averaged. Prefix reuse and
speculation are disabled; runtimes run sequentially and shut down between
workers. The unchanged WorldSense service is allowed only after source/
launcher fingerprints and loaded libraries establish that it runs no
inference. Commands, terminal statuses, process checks, clocks, phase
counters, initialization, first use and RSS are retained under `completed/`.

The measured candidate library SHA256 is
`c0917b8369f89dde5b7688eb3df800905822aba52b1d0d5562f322f5cab2f36d`.
The prior selected library remains unchanged at
`26f2120c3570a28607969f855f6950d626372b388361325ac49096eb30d60671`.
The completed evidence archive SHA256 is
`83a33ccb27d54ececc9c04a9e58b71c5afa0b5febe83fb733ecd69211da87829`.

The result is limited to the actual short prompts and batches measured;
text/coder answers contain 8/17 tokens including stop. VL was not changed
or re-benchmarked in this dense comparison. Its buffer-copy experiment is
separate and is not counted as an achieved speedup here. The full three-model
2x/half-TTFT goal remains active.

reports.title: Direct resident-state reset: repeated latency gains and a decode tradeoff
reports.report_text:
# Direct resident-state reset: repeated latency gains and a decode tradeoff

The optional direct reset removes temporary zero-filled CPU vectors and their
copies into shared Metal state buffers. Two complete native ABBA runs preserve
144 full output sequences, and all 19 validation stages pass. Warm text TTFT
improves in both runs, but text batch-2 decode is 1.7–2.4% slower. The full
2x-vLLM/half-TTFT goal remains unmet; this is not a new vLLM comparison.

The `GARNET_METAL_DIRECT_STATE_ZERO` option defaults OFF. The candidate clears
logical float elements in existing buffers, preserving row padding, positive
zero, allocation identity, readiness rules and the closed-command requirement.
Decode arithmetic, checkpoint precision and graph scheduling are unchanged.
The primary serving library and GPT-OSS/Pi checkouts are untouched.

## Actual full-request results

Four warm requests per build/profile per run, from two fresh workers with
three requests each. First requests are excluded. Both builds have the same
attention-prefix policy; direct reset is the tested difference. Runtimes run
sequentially under the existing conflict guards. Prompts, stop rules, output
caps, chunk plans and actual image bytes match; images are freshly encoded.

| Model | Batch | Initial TTFT control → candidate ms | Initial reduction | Confirmation TTFT control → candidate ms | Confirmation reduction | Decode candidate/control initial / confirmation |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Qwen3-0.6B | 1 | 52.90 → 50.35 | 4.83% | 53.67 → 48.91 | 8.86% | 1.0038 / 0.9900 |
| Qwen3-0.6B | 2 | 87.38 → 75.95 | 13.08% | 87.38 → 73.20 | 16.22% | 0.9762 / 0.9827 |
| Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct | 1 | 36.10 → 36.18 | -0.22% | 35.89 → 34.88 | 2.81% | 1.0077 / 1.0004 |
| Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct | 2 | 56.85 → 55.80 | 1.84% | 56.78 → 55.09 | 2.97% | 1.0003 / 0.9954 |
| Qwen3.5-0.8B VL | 1 | 216.11 → 218.19 | -0.96% | 216.46 → 213.25 | 1.48% | 1.0212 / 1.0044 |
| Qwen3.5-0.8B VL | 2 | 380.23 → 376.64 | 0.94% | 379.81 → 377.50 | 0.61% | 1.0064 / 0.9959 |

Text TTFT gains repeat, and coder B2 has a smaller repeated signal. VL B2's
sub-1% signal is too small to establish a practically useful gain here.
Coder B1 and VL B1 warm gains do not repeat. No decode improvement is proven;
text B2's repeated slowdown is a material tradeoff, without an established
cause. Retain the option for investigation, with no uniform serving promotion.
Do not mix these candidate timings with an older vLLM run to claim new ratios.

## Reset, first use and memory

Reset remains inside TTFT on both sides. Confirmation warm reset means:

| Model | Batch | Control reset ms | Direct reset ms |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Text | 1 | 7.207 | 2.975 |
| Text | 2 | 23.676 | 5.096 |
| Coder | 1 | 0.863 | 0.417 |
| Coder | 2 | 1.736 | 0.708 |
| VL | 1 | 3.900 | 1.601 |
| VL | 2 | 11.014 | 3.660 |

All reset means also fall in the initial run. This supports the intended
mechanism, but reset savings are not identical to full-request savings.
The existing VL `vision_seconds` interval includes reset; the new separate
`reset_seconds` field permits distinguishing it without changing TTFT scope.

First-request TTFT after initialization improves in both runs for text/VL;
coder B1 is slower in both, and coder B2 is mixed. Confirmation first-request
means in milliseconds (control → candidate): text B1 155.44 → 149.71,
text B2 187.99 → 170.20, coder B1 122.28 → 125.43, coder B2 136.19 → 142.88,
VL B1 350.43 → 334.25, VL B2 565.69 → 551.97. Initialization is separately
recorded in [summary.json](summary.json). OS/driver caches were not flushed;
no sum is presented as an observed hardware-cold end-to-end TTFT.

Although temporary allocations are removed, measured peak RSS changes are
small/mixed (about -14.7 to +7.8 MiB across both runs); no peak-memory saving
is established. The largest confirmation text reset still takes 5.1 ms.
A subsequent [GPU buffer-fill component test](../state-zero-gpu/README.md)
is slower than direct CPU clear in both tested input conditions and is
rejected for integration. It does not change this native comparison's results.

## Validation and evidence

Actual M4 build and both CTest references pass. The direct-zero test checks
36 repeated nonzero-to-positive-zero transitions, padded shapes and actual
GPU consumption, plus empty-buffer and open-command rejection. The remaining
stages include 48 exact-tail comparisons, 24 private-cache profiles with
session isolation/reset checks, standard serving/image/trained-layer/head/
vision suites and 36 extended Qwen3.5 prefill comparisons. Existing numerical
bounds are unchanged. Two native ABBA runs cover all six model/batch profiles
with 144 matching complete token/prompt sequences, stopping flags and plans.

Owned root: `/Users/zsdx/garnet-metal-investigation`. Original files were
preserved before installing ten sources with verified identities. The local
[source manifest](source-manifest.json) and archived originals retain the
before/after hashes. All durable jobs are terminal exit 0: checks PID 6169,
initial inference PID 8442, confirmation PID 27472. No live job was restarted
because an observation timed out; no unrelated process was stopped.

Exact absolute commands, installed/generated runner sources, reference
scripts, build flags, library/model hashes, monitors, timings, reset telemetry,
complete outputs and exits are in [evidence](evidence/). The executed comparator
inherits an older template's BF16-body scope label; actual build hashes,
`direct_state_zero_enabled` and `attention_prefix_enabled` fields identify the
reset experiment. That label does not alter the executed work or its scope.

```text
python test2026/metal/verify_direct_state_zero.py results/20261013/direct-state-zero
```

The verifier checks 677 file hashes, installed/original/reference identities,
19 terminal validation stages, explicit check counts, both library identities,
144 complete outputs, runtime flags, fresh frames, timing arithmetic and all
48 monitored worker exits. Raw bytes are preserved by `.gitattributes`.

- Candidate library SHA256: `b33ee094e60efb1fa57de7b6141cb2b2650509f44cd218c77844b3b94c2ec451`.
- Native comparison control: `f2c5c448ec4f3c8431be37b48a2634d8fa4cc31de4aa163ec367a319c9263088`.
- Unchanged primary library: `73c10e5dc62eb97607e9ded9a1df8bb6702d87375620bd5dc160d8b871f78ce2`.
- Source bundle: `8941aa256fc62380accf5db9ad90ffa0da0bff206d742a055e657a9712e4a710`.
- Evidence archive: `82ed28a3c4e45c1fd00ff0980239bffe4a64584cb1545e6ee2ac5788b530e008`.

VL B2's attention-prefix control here isolates reset and does not promote
the otherwise inconclusive attention-prefix VL B2 policy. The latest
[actual vLLM comparison](../selected-attention-vllm/README.md) remains the
authoritative six-profile comparator result, with all unmet targets recorded.

# Bounded dual-accumulator text head: rejected after real model execution

The two-accumulator / 64-thread vocabulary-head component improved text
batch 1 by 7.3% initially and 8.6% in its component repeat. This prototype
tested that exact algorithm inside Garnet, only for one-row, 1024-input,
151936-output BF16 projections. Other shapes and batch 2 retained the
existing dispatch. The experimental build option defaulted OFF. Original
BF16 learned values and FP32 inputs/accumulation/output remained; summation
order changed. There was no quantization or reuse shortcut.

All eleven standard stages passed: CTest, serving, mixed-image pipeline,
Qwen3.5 layer references, both dense-model layer references, all three full
vocabulary references at batches 1/2, and small/pretrained vision references.
All three private-cache suites also passed, covering 24 cache profiles.
Existing numerical bounds were not widened. The vocabulary references
include actual normalization and full logits, with matching greedy IDs.

The subsequent sequential native ABBA suite preserved all 72 complete
requests, prompt IDs, finished flags and fresh-image identities. Each
runtime/policy/profile has two fresh workers, three requests per worker and
four non-first requests in the warm mean. The same M4/16 GiB Mac mini,
checkpoints, capacities, prompts, output limits and stop rules are retained.
Both policies use 24 slots for text batch 1, 22 for text batch 2, 26 for
coder, and VL plans 80 / 32+32+16. No inference runtimes run in parallel.

| Model | Batch | Candidate/control decode ratio | Candidate/control TTFT fraction |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Qwen3-0.6B | 1 | 0.99867 | 1.00001 |
| Qwen3-0.6B | 2 | 1.01767 | 0.99756 |
| Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct | 1 | 0.99482 | 0.98098 |
| Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct | 2 | 0.98959 | 1.00248 |
| Qwen3.5-0.8B | 1 | 0.99974 | 0.98987 |
| Qwen3.5-0.8B | 2 | 0.99429 | 1.00022 |

The affected text batch-1 model shows no gain. Apparent timing changes in
profiles whose head dispatch is unchanged do not establish an algorithm
benefit. No additional confirmation or fresh vLLM study is warranted.
The component timing is not a whole-model speed claim. The prototype is
rejected; all four edited production/worker files were restored byte-for-byte
on Windows and the isolated Mac source. Experimental binary and evidence
remain for audit. No changes were made to the GPT-OSS or Pi checkouts.

Selected control library SHA256:
`73c10e5dc62eb97607e9ded9a1df8bb6702d87375620bd5dc160d8b871f78ce2`.
Rejected candidate library SHA256:
`80fa97a68f83eb069279c4d634704875495feae115bbf7e6aa4a9bfcd9c4cffc`.
Archive SHA256:
`8b05c5608df3b11ebb8232bb5df8e0ee7d0ade1f4798a19bfddb6f54d29a79e4`.

## Actual commands and provenance


Exact build/runtime commands, CMake options, library/source/checkpoint hashes,
all timing/output records, numerical checks and 0.5-second process monitors
are in `evidence/`. Only the owned worker group is exempt during monitoring
and only owned processes may be terminated. Sampling cannot prove absence
of arbitrarily short external jobs between polls. Fresh processes do not
establish cold hardware; initialization and first-use requests are retained
separately and filesystem/driver caches were not flushed.

Original and candidate source bytes are both archived. Fresh image tensors
and RGB files are omitted from Git with identity hashes/sizes retained.
`evidence-proof.json` verifies the successful stages, 72 selected requests,

reports.title: Exact-value FP32 precision study; full goal still unmet
reports.report_text:
# Exact-value FP32 precision study; full goal still unmet

This additional comparison aligns arithmetic precision instead of relying
on the comparator's configured dtype label. All 72 requests have matching
complete generated token IDs. At batch 2, Garnet exceeds 2× the FP32
comparator's decode throughput for coder and VL. No workload reaches half
the comparator's TTFT, and text decode remains below 2×. These results do
not establish a 2× speedup over the default BF16 comparator; its prior
results remain separate and unchanged.

No new native optimization is selected in this experiment. Garnet uses the
existing validated MPS-score library, original BF16 checkpoint storage and
FP32 activations/KV. Its exact-scaled FP16 prefill cache preserves original
weight values. The comparator uses separate, exactly expanded F32 versions
of those values and verified FP32 weights, activations and KV. File hashes
and storage sizes differ; learned numerical values are identical.

## Exact value and actual runtime verification

The source models are read-only. A streaming converter expands each finite
BF16 bit pattern to its exact F32 representation (`uint32(bits) << 16`),
preserves any existing F32 bits, and verifies every destination value and
per-tensor SHA before publishing the new file. It updates only dtype config
fields; tokenizers, generation and image-processing assets are copied.

| Model | Serialized tensors | Values verified bit-exact |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Qwen3-0.6B | 311 | 751,632,384 |
| Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct | 290 | 494,032,768 |
| Qwen3.5-0.8B | 488 | 873,438,784 |

Serialized counts include entries not used by the runtime, such as redundant
tied heads; actual loaded-module counts are recorded separately. Three GPU
worker audits find all 310 / 290 / 473 loaded parameter tensors FP32, including
private paged-attention owners. Embedding, first norm and attention projection
outputs and KV dtypes are also FP32. Merely requesting `dtype=float32` with
the original BF16 files does not accomplish this, as the prior dtype audit
demonstrates.

The FP32 VL model failed at the original 0.30 memory fraction before cache
initialization. The final study uses 0.45 for VL and retains 0.30 for dense
models. Actual model length remains 256 and batch 1/2; the larger allowance
permits the FP32 model/cache to fit and is explicitly recorded. No inference
math, comparator loaders or security settings are patched for this study.
FP32 follows the installed comparator's normal dtype-dependent dispatch,
which differs from its optimized BF16 paths. Treat this as a separate
precision configuration, not an improvement over the default BF16 baseline.

## Actual sequential warm measurements

Same M4 / 16 GiB, same learned weights, prompt IDs, greedy sampling, batch,
context cap and output cap. No prefix, encoder-cache or speculative reuse.
One runtime exits before the next starts. Each configuration has two fresh
processes, each serving three requests; warm means exclude first requests.
Throughput is decode steps per second per row, including the full wall
interval between first and final prediction.

| Model | Batch | Garnet tokens/s/row | FP32 vLLM tokens/s/row | Decode ratio | Garnet TTFT | FP32 vLLM TTFT |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Qwen3-0.6B | 1 | 57.07 | 37.27 | 1.53× | 69.98 ms | 83.79 ms |
| Qwen3-0.6B | 2 | 52.01 | 29.29 | 1.78× | 115.29 ms | 111.27 ms |
| Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct | 1 | 72.36 | 47.29 | 1.53× | 55.05 ms | 62.20 ms |
| Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct | 2 | 69.91 | 29.64 | 2.36× | 73.90 ms | 84.09 ms |
| Qwen3.5-0.8B image | 1 | 47.21 | 26.91 | 1.75× | 547.89 ms | 252.79 ms |
| Qwen3.5-0.8B image | 2 | 42.81 | 16.62 | 2.58× | 760.50 ms | 438.50 ms |

All 48 text/coder and 24 image requests match outputs and finish. The FP32
batch-2 image outputs match the native 28-token caption; the older BF16
comparator batch-2 result did not match and reached the cap. Text/coder
generate 8/17 tokens including stop under a 64-token cap. VL uses the same
288×192 RGB image, 54 visual tokens, 79 prompt IDs and 32-token cap. Results
are limited to these agreed prompts; they do not prove model-wide speed.

Initialization, first-use requests and individual-process high-water RSS are
retained separately in raw records. Filesystem/shader caches are not flushed,
so first-use measurements are not cold boots; RSS is not unique unified GPU
allocation or aggregate multi-process memory.

## Evidence and target audit

`study-source/` retains actual helpers and historical failed-audit sources.
`equivalent-model-metadata/` contains configs, asset identity and complete
per-tensor equivalence proofs. Commands, successful and failed exits, process
guards, library/model hashes, versions, request IDs and all timings/tokens
are saved. Models and raw image buffers are excluded. Original and expanded
checkpoint hashes were revalidated when archiving.

`exact-f32-actual-dtypes-fit-20261013/jobs/summary.json` proves actual FP32
loading and activation probes. `equivalent-f32-text-20261013/jobs/summary.json`
and `equivalent-f32-vl-20261013/jobs/frame_summary.json` are the performance
summaries. Both explicitly set `counts_as_default_bf16_speedup=false`.

All six half-TTFT gates fail; four of six FP32 decode gates also fail.
The default BF16 2× target is unchanged and unmet. The full goal stays active;
no claim of completion or general 2× acceleration is justified.

reports.title: Selected recurrent chunk build: current matched FP32 comparison
reports.report_text:
# Selected recurrent chunk build: current matched FP32 comparison

The selected Garnet build still falls short of the full 2× decode /
half-TTFT goal. Actual repeated comparisons confirm batch-2 coder and VL
decode ratios above 2×, but all first-token targets and the other decode
profiles remain unmet. No target is inferred from a different batch or model.

## Precision and workload

Native original BF16 storage and FP32 operations are compared with the
previously verified lossless FP32-expanded checkpoints and FP32 vLLM-Metal
model/KV arithmetic. Every learned value is identical, even though serialized
file bytes and weight-storage width differ. Original checkpoint assets and
the full equivalent checkpoint hashes are checked before execution, and the
exact-value proofs are retained. Earlier loaded-parameter audits demonstrate
the comparator actually loads FP32 tensors from these expanded files.

This is an additional FP32 comparison, not a replacement for stock BF16
vLLM-Metal results. `counts_as_default_bf16_speedup` remains false. There is
no quantization, prefix reuse, speculative decoding or simultaneous
inference runtime execution. Both use the same M4 / 16 GiB Mac mini, prompt
IDs, stop rules, caps, batch sizes and input images. All 72 requests match
complete normalized output IDs and finished flags.

Dense text/coder use chunk 16, capacity 256 and cap 64. Their prompts contain
22 and 26 IDs, respectively, and produce 8 and 17 output tokens including
stop. VL uses the retained batched recurrent output projection, chunk 64
for batch 1 or chunk 32 for batch 2 with adaptive 16-token tails. Each fresh
288×192 frame has 54 visual tokens and 79 prompt IDs; cap 32 yields complete
28-token captions. Input RGB/patch hashes match and comparator encoder-cache
identities are unique per row/frame.

## Actual warm measurements

Two fresh workers per runtime/profile each make three requests. Means use
the four non-first requests per runtime/profile. Every runtime shuts down
before the next starts; actual commands, statuses and process checks are saved.

| Model | Batch | Garnet tokens/s/row | vLLM FP32 tokens/s/row | Decode ratio | Garnet TTFT ms | vLLM TTFT ms |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Qwen3-0.6B | 1 | 56.62 | 38.11 | 1.49 | 70.82 | 79.64 |
| Qwen3-0.6B | 2 | 51.76 | 26.85 | 1.93 | 120.40 | 97.64 |
| Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct | 1 | 72.32 | 47.23 | 1.53 | 54.85 | 61.62 |
| Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct | 2 | 69.90 | 29.57 | 2.36 | 74.62 | 84.82 |
| Qwen3.5-0.8B VL | 1 | 47.99 | 26.65 | 1.80 | 364.27 | 266.52 |
| Qwen3.5-0.8B VL | 2 | 42.76 | 16.64 | 2.57 | 609.65 | 438.67 |

The earlier observed text batch-2 ratio above 2× is not reproduced here;
its current ratio is 1.93. It is not reported as an achieved target. The
new recurrent projection reduces native VL latency versus its earlier
native control, but the comparator is still faster to the first word.

## Initialization and first use

These are separate measured intervals, not included in the warm means.
Filesystem and driver caches were not flushed. vLLM may perform preparation
during initialization, so first-use TTFT alone is not a complete startup cost.

| Model | Batch | Garnet initialization s | vLLM initialization s | Garnet first-use TTFT ms | vLLM first-use TTFT ms |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Text | 1 | 1.94 | 18.34 | 183.05 | 68.55 |
| Text | 2 | 2.60 | 17.04 | 228.64 | 105.17 |
| Coder | 1 | 2.14 | 16.62 | 157.20 | 62.34 |
| Coder | 2 | 2.13 | 16.60 | 177.80 | 94.14 |
| VL | 1 | 4.00 | 33.93 | 904.38 | 310.09 |
| VL | 2 | 5.06 | 33.50 | 883.49 | 513.87 |

## Evidence and remaining work

The selected native library SHA256 remains
`26f2120c3570a28607969f855f6950d626372b388361325ac49096eb30d60671`.
`logs/` contains actual output sequences, warm timing records, terminal
results, resource/process checks, equivalence proofs and metadata. Scripts
record their own hashes and use the validated direct WorldSense launcher
guard. Reproducible RGB/patch bytes are omitted with sizes/SHA256 retained;
their originals remain private on the Mac. Serialized per-operation profiling
is disabled for these measurements.

The current dense prompts both span two 16-token profiles padded to 32
positions. A larger single profile could reduce repeated weight passes, but
the earlier dense key-cache reference failure must be investigated and
resolved through independent numerical evidence before such profiles are
accepted. Decode remains GPU dominated. The rejected interleaved weight
layout is not used, and no further speedup is attributed to it.

reports.title: Exact dense prefill tails: validated modest latency gains
reports.report_text:
# Exact dense prefill tails: validated modest latency gains

Dense Qwen can opt into 22- and 26-token prefill profiles to remove padding
for the existing matched text and coder prompts:

```python
decoder.enable_prefill(32, 'shared', finer_chunks=True, exact_tail=True)
```

This requires a resident split-key Metal session, shared projection and
hidden size <= 1024. The option defaults false. Existing scheduling remains
unchanged unless enabled. Switching the option closes cached prefill graphs.
Unsupported combinations reject before changing decoder state. There is no
new native kernel, precision change, checkpoint change or output shortcut.
Both A/B policies use the same private-KV library, SHA256
`73c10e5dc62eb97607e9ded9a1df8bb6702d87375620bd5dc160d8b871f78ce2`.

## Actual validation and native measurements

Independent NumPy references pass all 48 comparisons: both checkpoints,
first/last layers, batches 1/2, both chunk sizes, three carried-state steps,
inactive slots and overwrites. The worst tolerance ratio is
0.9936574155; the existing bounds were not widened. CPU admission/planning
checks pass 2,048 cases, including default scheduling, capability rejection,
state preservation and graph disposal when switching policy.

Initial sequential native ABBA measurements preserve all 48 complete
requests, prompt IDs, stop rules and chunk plans. Each policy has two fresh
processes, three requests per process and four non-first requests in its
warm mean. Original BF16 weight storage and FP32 arithmetic remain. The
hardware is the same M4 Mac mini with 16 GiB and macOS 15.6.1.

| Model | Batch | Control TTFT ms | Exact-tail TTFT ms | Reduction | Decode ratio |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Qwen3-0.6B | 1 | 52.99 | 52.85 | 0.3% | 0.997 |
| Qwen3-0.6B | 2 | 92.77 | 87.11 | 6.1% | 0.994 |
| Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct | 1 | 40.88 | 39.02 | 4.5% | 0.995 |
| Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct | 2 | 63.40 | 59.23 | 6.6% | 0.997 |

Text batch 2 has a separate clean confirmation: 91.86 -> 86.50 ms, a
5.84% reduction; decode is 58.38 -> 58.65 steps/s/row (ratio 1.0045).
All 36 confirmation requests preserve complete outputs and prompt IDs.
Text batch 1 showed no useful gain and was not repeated to seek a favorable
result. Coder confirmation reduces batch-1 TTFT from 39.30 to 38.34 ms
(2.45%) and batch-2 TTFT from 62.70 to 58.19 ms (7.18%). Their decode ratios
are 1.0004 and 0.9953. The coder latency direction repeats, with a smaller
batch-1 effect than the initial run. These are prompt-specific results;
they do not establish a benefit for arbitrary lengths or larger models.
Decode throughput is effectively unchanged in this experiment.

The confirmation manager completed with exit code 0.
Coder batch-1 attempt 0 was interrupted and discarded when a separate
release-test runtime appeared. No measurements from that attempt are used.
The external runtime finished, and the manager automatically executed the
remaining clean profiles. Failed-attempt logs are retained separately.
The external process was not stopped or exempted based on its low CPU usage.
The manager waits for a five-second clear interval, monitors workers every
0.5 seconds and has a 900-second quiet-window deadline. It retries only
contention failures. This sampling cannot prove absence of arbitrarily
short external jobs between polls.

Peak child RSS, initialization, first-use requests and phase timings are
preserved separately in the records. Filesystem/driver caches were not
flushed; fresh processes do not establish cold-hardware behavior.
This is a native A/B experiment, not a fresh vLLM-Metal comparison. It does
not establish the full 2x decode / half-TTFT goal or stock BF16 speedups.
Qwen3.5 VL is unaffected. The goal remains active and unmet.

## Commands and provenance

Public runners under `test2026/metal`:

```text
python3 test_exact_dense_tail_planning.py SOURCE_ROOT OUTPUT_DIR
python3 run_exact_dense_tail_checks.py INVESTIGATION_ROOT OUTPUT_DIR
python3 run_exact_dense_tail_profiles.py INVESTIGATION_ROOT OUTPUT_DIR
```

reports.title: Extended exact-half QKV scales: correct reconstruction, no useful speed gain
reports.report_text:
# Extended exact-half QKV scales: correct reconstruction, no useful speed gain

The retained codec rejects one of 18 Qwen3.5 linear-attention QKV matrices.
Its first-layer matrix contains 14 extremely tiny rows whose ideal scale is
138, beyond the existing +/-64 range. This experiment tests admitting those
learned values exactly, using an isolated codec range -112 through 141.
Production admission and the selected native library remain unchanged.
No weight is rounded or replaced with zero.

The first actual GPU check reconstructs every finite normal BF16 bit pattern,
plus signed zeros, using scaled half storage and `ldexp`: 65,026 values per
precise/fast-math compiler mode, zero bit mismatches. BF16 subnormal weights,
infinities and NaNs are excluded from this codec admission.

The actual first-layer QKV projection then passes the existing output bound
5e-6 + 5e-5*abs(FP32 control), but fails a deliberately stricter diagnostic
for the tiny columns. Initial and diagnostic jobs stop at 22 rows with exit
1. The independent FP64 dot reference identifies large relative errors in
the unscaled FP32 MPS control too: its intermediate terms are extremely
small. Naive half rescaling is much closer, but loses a subnormal output.
The diagnosis is consistent with intermediate/result underflow; it is not
an observation of undocumented hardware instructions.

An integer IEEE power-of-two rescaler preserves subnormal result bits,
signed zero and nearest-even underflow rounding. A separate GPU test covers
all finite BF16 patterns, including source subnormals, and FP32 exponent/
mantissa edge fixtures over 13 positive/negative scales. Its 888,420 cases
per compiler mode match host `std::ldexp` bit-for-bit, including overflow
results. This is a sampled FP32 test, not exhaustive over all 2^32 words.
It does not add BF16 subnormal weight admission to the serving codec.

Two actual projection variants use this helper: all output columns, and a
hybrid that uses it only when the column scale exceeds 64. Each passes eight
physical row shapes (22/24/26/32/44/52/64/80), output padding, unchanged
general output bounds, and the independent FP64 forward-error bound for
the 14 tiny columns. The bound is gamma(1024)*sum(abs(products)) + 1e-45,
with unit roundoff 2^-24. Agreement with the inaccurate tiny FP32 control
is retained as diagnostic data, not treated as a gold reference. Neither
the original general bound nor the independent forward-error bound is
widened to admit a candidate.

Both corrected variants have worst tiny-column forward-error ratio
0.00237020186, well within that independent bound.

The initial naive/control diagnostic failure remains in the archive. It
must not be mistaken for a failed general projection bound, a model output
change, or proof that the bit-rescaled candidate is faster.

| Physical rows | All-bit rescale component speedup | Hybrid component speedup |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| 22 | 0.824 | 0.897 |
| 24 | 0.890 | 0.911 |
| 26 | 0.862 | 0.875 |
| 32 | 0.803 | 0.832 |
| 44 | 0.956 | 0.839 |
| 52 | 0.893 | 0.898 |
| 64 | 0.857 | 0.808 |
| 80 | 0.777 | 1.003 |

Ratios are FP32 MPS control / half-plus-rescale candidate GPU time. Each
variant uses two ABBA rounds, three warmups and twelve measured samples per
window. The candidate includes rescaling; the control writes directly into
the output and is not burdened with an artificial copy. All-bit rescaling
regresses every shape; hybrid regresses most shapes and is flat at 80 rows.
The variants are separate algorithms, not repeat confirmations. There is no
useful signal warranting a serving integration or full-model speed claim.

These are component tests with sinusoidal FP32 inputs and real checkpoint
weights, not model hidden-state or complete generated-output validation.
The selected serving code is untouched. The broader three-model 2x decode /
half-TTFT objective remains active and unmet.

## Commands and evidence

```text
python3 run_extended_half_scale_gpu.py INVESTIGATION_ROOT OUTPUT_DIR
python3 run_extended_half_projection.py INVESTIGATION_ROOT OUTPUT_DIR
python3 run_scale_bits_gpu.py INVESTIGATION_ROOT OUTPUT_DIR
python3 run_extended_half_bits_projection.py INVESTIGATION_ROOT OUTPUT_DIR
python3 run_extended_half_hybrid_projection.py INVESTIGATION_ROOT OUTPUT_DIR
python3 archive_extended_half_scale.py INVESTIGATION_ROOT ARCHIVE_PATH
```

The six executed jobs are terminal: codec/bit-scaler/all-bit/hybrid exit 0;
naive projection and its diagnostic exit 1 at the explicit tiny-output gate.
`evidence/completed/` retains exact commands, compiler/macOS/Python versions,
source/checkpoint hashes, raw timing windows, output diagnostics, monitors,
terminal statuses and hashes/sizes of omitted matrices and binaries.
`source-initial/` preserves the pre-diagnostic source that matches the first
projection attempt's recorded hash. Only owned probe groups could be stopped.
Existing inference guards plus 0.5-second process samples reject competing
runtimes; arbitrarily short jobs between samples cannot be ruled out.
GPT-OSS, Pi and the Mac original checkout were not changed.

Full archive SHA256:
`ce0de60a0c3d133404cf51f56f1663da4108978524dc84fd91550e70cb061c7b`.

reports.title: Extended prefill profiles: actual tests, no 2× claim
reports.report_text:
# Extended prefill profiles: actual tests, no 2× claim

Same M4 Mac mini, Qwen3.5-0.8B checkpoint, 288×192 image, 79 prompt
tokens, capacity 256, output cap 32 and fresh image encoding per request.
Each profile uses sequential candidate/control then control/candidate
workers, with three requests per worker. Warm means exclude each worker's
first request. Complete prompt IDs, generated token IDs and finished flags
match the frozen selected control for all 48 requests in each experiment.

The fixed 32/64 profiles pass all eleven handoff jobs and independent
NumPy references for actual linear/full-attention layers, batches 1/2 and
chunks 32/64, including paused rows, partial tails and state carry. The
worst normalized reference error is below 1 at the established tolerance.

## Fixed profiles: rejected

| Batch | Chunk | Control TTFT ms | Candidate TTFT ms | Candidate/control decode ratio |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 32 | 493.85 | 507.40 | 0.995 |
| 1 | 64 | 488.82 | 597.73 | 0.999 |
| 2 | 32 | 696.99 | 741.26 | 1.005 |
| 2 | 64 | 700.40 | 938.41 | 1.003 |

Padding expands 79 tokens to 96/128 rather than the control's 80. These
profiles worsen warm and first-use latency and are not selected.

## Adaptive final chunks: candidate only

The candidate schedules 32+32+16 or 64+16, retaining 80 physical token
positions. Default profiles of 16 or fewer keep their original schedule.

| Batch | Maximum chunk | Control TTFT ms | Candidate TTFT ms | Candidate/control decode ratio |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 32 | 488.90 | 451.94 | 0.982 |
| 1 | 64 | 490.68 | 437.90 | 0.963 |
| 2 | 32 | 696.36 | 646.26 | 1.015 |
| 2 | 64 | 696.88 | 683.59 | 1.007 |

First-use candidate TTFT is 1.21/1.65 seconds for batch 1 and 1.39/1.89
seconds for batch 2, versus roughly 0.78/0.97 seconds for the controls.
Multiple graph profiles add first-use preparation. Filesystem and driver
caches were not flushed. Peak individual child RSS remains around 3.4 GiB;
it is not a measure of aggregate or unique GPU memory.

These are modest warm latency gains, with inconsistent decode behavior.
The selected control binary is preserved. Neither experiment demonstrates
the full 2× decode / half-TTFT goal or a new vLLM-Metal advantage.

## Evidence and execution limits

`fixed/` preserves exact commands, terminal results, source snapshots,
raw timing/output records and independent reference logs. Reproducible
RGB and patch bytes are omitted from Git; their individual sizes and SHA256
hashes are retained in `derived-input-sha256.json`. Full bytes remain in the
private Mac evidence directory. Source uploads were checked by bundle and
per-file hashes before atomic installation, and the candidate build was
cleanly rebuilt.

The first fixed-profile benchmark launch failed at the owned-predecessor
dependency gate before inference. Its failed log is preserved. The gate
now rechecks the authoritative terminal file after probing the PID, closing
a completion/publication race while retaining the process identity check
and failing if a predecessor disappears without publishing a result.
