# Opt-in finer dense prefill profiles

Dense Qwen can select 24/48-token profiles to reduce padding, with
`enable_prefill(32, 'shared', finer_chunks=True)`. This requires a resident
split-key Metal decoder and hidden size <= 1024. The option defaults false;
existing Qwen3.5 plans remain unchanged. No kernel or learned value changed
in this experiment. Both native A/B policies use the same small-output
decode library, SHA256 `56bc06c693f3776c994d3f4078dd2e25093b575f93f6f09c4e2087a4917ee8d4`.

The 22-token matched text prompt selects 24 instead of 32 slots. The coder's
26-token prompt still selects 32. Independent NumPy validation passes all
48 comparisons for 24/48 profiles, both real checkpoints, first/last layers,
batches 1/2, three carried-state steps, inactive slots and overwritten slots.
Worst tolerance ratio is 0.992664862 (<= 1 passes), without widening bounds.
These checks use the retained split-key/linear-delta library; the only later
library change affects one/two-row decode. Whole-request execution uses
the small-output library above.

CPU-only planning/admission checks pass 4,096 cases. Actual legacy backends
reject 24/32/48/64 and finer scheduling without changing decoder state, then
complete 12 text/coder requests with frozen exact outputs. Six fresh-image
VL requests retain their previous chunk plans and exact complete captions.
Another 24 complete longer-prompt requests (42 text / 44 coder prompt IDs)
match opt-in 48-slot outputs against 64-slot controls at batches 1/2.
This longer-prompt check is separate from the matched comparator workload.

Two sequential native ABBA runs preserve all 96 complete requests. Each
policy/profile uses two fresh processes with three requests; four non-first
requests form the warm mean. Prompt IDs, output caps, stop rules and complete
output IDs are unchanged. Original BF16 storage and FP32 arithmetic remain.

| Model | Batch | Initial TTFT reduction | Confirmation TTFT reduction | Confirmation decode ratio |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Qwen3-0.6B | 1 | 3.8% | 6.8% | 0.995 |
| Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct | 1 | 0.2% | -0.3% | 1.001 |
| Qwen3-0.6B | 2 | 5.4% | 6.1% | 0.997 |
| Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct | 2 | -0.6% | 1.6% | 1.003 |

Text warm TTFT improves modestly in both runs; decode is essentially flat.
Coder has the same plan, and its small timing changes do not establish a
benefit. Initialization, first-use TTFT, peak child RSS and GPU phases remain
in the raw records. Initial text batch-1 initialization is 2.46 s versus
1.65 s; no unverified cause is assigned. Filesystem/driver caches were not
flushed, so these fresh-process samples are not guaranteed cold hardware.
Recorded wait time overlaps GPU execution and must not be added to it.

## Fresh equivalent-FP32 comparator study

This additional study compares native original BF16 weight storage with
FP32 arithmetic against losslessly expanded, bit-equivalent learned values
in vLLM-Metal FP32 weights/activations/KV. It does not replace or establish a
default BF16 speedup. Actual output/prompt parity, stop-token accounting and
clean shutdown pass for all 48 requests. Inference is sequential on the same
M4/16 GiB Mac mini; prefix reuse and speculation are disabled.

| Model | Batch | Garnet TTFT ms | vLLM TTFT ms | Garnet steps/s | vLLM steps/s | Decode ratio | TTFT fraction |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Qwen3-0.6B | 1 | 51.20 | 85.36 | 56.17 | 37.23 | 1.509 | 0.600 |
| Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct | 1 | 41.45 | 62.84 | 72.41 | 46.96 | 1.542 | 0.660 |
| Qwen3-0.6B | 2 | 91.93 | 97.83 | 51.65 | 26.81 | 1.927 | 0.940 |
| Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct | 2 | 62.61 | 83.58 | 70.56 | 29.53 | 2.389 | 0.749 |

Steps/s is per synchronous decode step (per row at batch 2); aggregate batch-2
output throughput is twice this. Warm timing excludes initialization. No
new VL vLLM comparison ran here; six VL requests above check compatibility.

The full three-model 2x decode / half-TTFT goal remains active and unmet.
Only these measured prompts/profiles are established. The smaller padded
profile is experimental and opt-in; this is not a general production claim.

`completed/` contains source snapshots, actual commands, terminal statuses,
output IDs, timing/resource samples, guard evidence and checkpoint-equivalence
proofs. The executed guard's LF copy is preserved; its committed copy retains
the repository's CRLF style with identical Python source. Private tensor/image
bytes remain on the Mac with their hashes in `evidence-proof.json`.

reports.title: Fresh-frame copy elision: less CPU work, no clear model latency gain
reports.report_text:
# Fresh-frame copy elision: less CPU work, no clear model latency gain

The common frontend loads image data before reading orientation, applies
EXIF transforms only for orientations 2–8, and converts only non-RGB images.
Plain RGB frames avoid the two whole-image copies made by the previous
`ImageOps.exif_transpose(...).convert('RGB')` chain. Pillow bicubic resizing,
normalization, temporal/channel/merge ordering, little-endian FP32 patches,
input image bytes, resolution and token limits are unchanged.

Every request still opens and decodes its source afresh, prepares new patch/
RGB files, and runs a fresh vision encoding. This is not image/encoder/prefix
reuse. The default common frontend applies the same implementation to both
Garnet and vLLM-Metal. `frame_preprocessing_control.py` preserves the original
source byte-for-byte for A/B reproduction; an optional frontend argument to
the observed frame protocol selects `control` versus `selected`.

## Attribution and alternatives

The frozen `RealWorld-04.png` asset is actually WebP, determined from file
content and Pillow's format. Initial commentary inferred PNG from its name;
that inference was corrected. The generic attribution labels in raw data
remain decode/EXIF/convert, not a claim about a PNG decoder.
Warm CPU attribution over eleven non-first samples per batch reports:
decode/EXIF/convert 33.5 ms, resizing 11.3 ms, normalization roughly 1.2 ms,
patch layout about 0.9 ms, with total fresh preparation/write/hash roughly
53.0/56.7 ms at batches 1/2. Arrays are C-contiguous; noncontiguous element
writes were not the cause.

Two CPU ABBA scans check 384 timed records each. Borrowing RGB input instead
of making the copies reduces preparation from 49.69 -> 45.40 ms and
51.76 -> 49.72 ms initially, then 48.31 -> 45.09 ms and
51.56 -> 48.96 ms. The direction repeats; this is preprocessing, not model
TTFT or decode speed.

OpenCV 5.0.0 was already installed in the isolated environment; no packages
were changed. The initial conservative PNG-only candidate fell back on this
WebP asset, so that run does not measure OpenCV decoding. The corrected
simple-WebP candidate matches exact pixels/patches but improves little over
copy elision (44.77/47.07 ms against 48.64/50.67 ms control). It is not chosen
for the shared frontend: extra decoder selection/metadata handling is not
justified by that marginal extra signal. Production preprocessing imports
only its existing Pillow/NumPy dependencies.

The initial scan's `opencl_used` output label actually recorded configuration
state, not GPU execution; its fast decoder branch never ran. The corrected
scan explicitly disables OpenCL and names that field
`opencl_enabled_after_run`. CPU image decoding is not learned inference.

## Exactness and actual matched inference

Three compatibility passes cover 448 cases each: RGB, RGBA, L, P, I and CMYK,
four sizes, all eight orientations and no-orientation cases, plus real input
at batches 1/2. Seven PNGs place EXIF after IDAT. The later tests open control
and candidate separately for those lazy files, so control loading cannot
hide an orientation-read bug. The integrated implementation is checked
against the preserved original function. Fourteen additional conservative
CV fallback comparisons per pass also match. All RGB and patch bytes match
exactly; the frozen patch SHA256 is unchanged.

A sequential factorial ABBA run alternates frontend policy within each
runtime, at batches 1/2, using the same M4 / 16 GiB and Qwen3.5-0.8B values.
There are eight fresh persistent workers per batch, three requests each,
and four non-first samples per runtime/policy. All 48 complete normalized
token sequences, prompt IDs, finish flags and patch/RGB hashes match. Native
prefill plans remain 80 at B1 and 32+32+16 at B2. Prefix/speculative caches
are disabled; all comparator encoder identities are unique across rows and
requests within each worker. No competing inference runs simultaneously.

| Policy / batch | Garnet TTFT ms | vLLM TTFT ms | Garnet steps/s/row | vLLM steps/s/row | Decode ratio | TTFT fraction |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Original / 1 | 218.58 | 264.70 | 48.44 | 26.07 | 1.858 | 0.826 |
| Selected / 1 | 218.93 | 266.25 | 48.58 | 26.45 | 1.837 | 0.822 |
| Original / 2 | 389.63 | 443.82 | 44.75 | 17.16 | 2.608 | 0.878 |
| Selected / 2 | 387.75 | 442.68 | 44.75 | 17.12 | 2.614 | 0.876 |

All phase/worker records are in the evidence.
Selected/original TTFT fractions are 1.00158/1.00585 for Garnet/vLLM at B1,
and 0.99518/0.99743 at B2. There is no useful end-to-end gain established by
this four-sample study, despite reduced preprocessing work. Native B1
preparation falls 49.57 -> 46.67 ms; comparator 53.43 -> 49.50 ms. Other
execution variation offsets this small saving in observed first-token time.
No model gain is assigned to changing a CPU copy that runs before decode.

This is an additional matched-FP32 study, not a stock BF16 win. Native
compact BF16 storage and FP32 arithmetic versus exact F32-expanded comparator
weights retain their known storage-width caveat. Actual equivalence proofs,
versions, configured dtype and complete outputs remain. B2 aggregate
throughput is twice the per-row prediction rate; terminal prediction counts
and first prediction/prefill does not. B1 decode remains below 2x and neither
batch reaches half TTFT. The full three-model objective remains active.

The simpler copy-elision code is retained because its exact-input CPU work
reduction repeats without an added decoder dependency. GPU serving library
and learned operators are unchanged. Startup and first-use are separate in
records; OS/driver caches were not flushed. Peak child RSS is not aggregate
or unique GPU memory. No larger-model, long-context or general video-quality
claim follows from these fixed image/workload results.

## Commands and provenance

```text
python3 profile_frame_frontend.py INVESTIGATION_ROOT OUTPUT_DIR
python3 compare_frame_frontends.py INVESTIGATION_ROOT OUTPUT_DIR
python3 test_frame_frontend_exact.py INVESTIGATION_ROOT OUTPUT_DIR
python3 run_frame_frontend_inference.py INVESTIGATION_ROOT OUTPUT_DIR
python3 archive_frame_frontend.py INVESTIGATION_ROOT ARCHIVE_PATH
python3 verify_frame_frontend_evidence.py EVIDENCE_DIR PROOF_JSON
```

The first attribution job failed before timings due to a wrong case-file
path; the corrected retry exits zero. All subsequent jobs exit zero. Exact
commands, identities, equivalence proofs, versions, numerical/timing/output
records and monitors are preserved. `source-history/` retains the failed
path version, PNG-only/initial WebP candidates and pre-integration sources;
current helper imports preserve the original control for reproduction.
Raw image/patch/matrix assets are omitted with hashes/sizes retained.
Only owned workers can be stopped on error; 0.5-second monitoring cannot
exclude arbitrarily brief external tasks. Protected GPT-OSS/Pi checkouts and
the original Mac checkout are untouched.

Unchanged selected library SHA256:
`73c10e5dc62eb97607e9ded9a1df8bb6702d87375620bd5dc160d8b871f78ce2`.
Archive SHA256:
`6908f3a0c7b4be82cf47c94a0e60235d6a3dcc39e93a3f303b2babb59009dab8`.

reports.title: Exact-scaled half vision projections: rejected
reports.report_text:
# Exact-scaled half vision projections: rejected

The candidate builds and passes all eleven handoff validation jobs, including
real-model vision references and generation. It does not improve real-frame
latency or decode speed. Its four production-source changes were reverted.
The selected KV-chunk-vector library remains unchanged:
`564b515ab6b0eb68413ef5a54de6beff47d333f8f1fa6a1188562bf6e5c28ec4`.

The experiment extends the existing lossless per-output power-of-two BF16 to
FP16 storage representation to vision-block and merger matrices, using MPS
with FP32 inputs, accumulation and outputs plus inverse scale. It excludes
patch embedding, positional embeddings, norms and biases. This retains the
checkpoint values; it is not reduced-precision weight quantization.

## Actual native ABBA comparison

Same M4 16 GiB Mac mini, Qwen3.5-0.8B checkpoint, image bytes, preprocessing,
288×192 input, 54 visual tokens, 79 prompt tokens, 32-token cap, chunk 16.
Each persistent worker re-encodes every image, resets decoder state, and closes
cleanly before the next worker starts. Twelve requests per batch (24 total),
including first-use requests; warm means below exclude the first request in
each fresh process. All generated token IDs match the selected native control
and all requests finish. These are native comparisons, not new vLLM results.

No useful gain is demonstrated, so no additional confirmation or comparator
speed claim is warranted.

The separate serialized operation diagnostic executes 885 exact-half
projections, including actual 432-row vision operations. It matches the

using its GPU attribution as serving timing. Thus the failed speed result
cannot be attributed to an unexecuted candidate path.

## Evidence

and candidate/control library hashes before reverting. Each job directory
preserves actual commands, terminal exits, validation output and process

contains timings, complete token IDs and identical RGB/patch hashes.
`half-vision-profile-20261013/jobs/summary.json` contains diagnostic attribution.

vLLM-Metal decode throughput and at most half its TTFT. Existing native FP32
activation/KV arithmetic differs from the comparator's BF16 internal arithmetic;
matching checkpoint bytes alone does not establish identical precision.

reports.title: Bounded joined MPS prefill: modest warm gain, costly first use
reports.report_text:
# Bounded joined MPS prefill: modest warm gain, costly first use

The optional `GARNET_METAL_JOINED_PREFILL=ON` prototype combines adjacent
BF16 projections with the same input into one larger exact-half MPS
projection and one split-rescale kernel. Original learned values, per-row
integer scales and FP32 inputs/accumulation/outputs remain. There is no
prefix/image reuse, speculative prediction, shorter prompt or token cap.

Two component shapes had repeated signals; serving admission is limited to
44 rows / K=1024 / N=3072 (text B2) and 26 rows / K=896 / N=4864 (coder B1).
Other shapes, split-key projections, unequal strides, output aliases and
unrepresentable weights keep the existing path. Selected invalid shape/device
or pending-input/output controls reject before output mutation. Pack caches
retain their source weight owners to prevent identity reuse after disposal.
The original single command-buffer dependencies are preserved.

The flag requires exact-half prefill and defaults OFF. It is not combined
with the optional native-BF16 body decode route in these measurements. The
joined shader and graph pairing are compiled only when enabled. Session
`joined_prefill_pairs` and the prefill result dictionary expose actual
dispatch counts; unsupported profiles count zero. Serialized per-operation
diagnostics deliberately retain separate projections rather than claiming
their timings represent this serving path.

## Actual validation

Both native admission shapes pass repeated bit-exact dyadic output tests
against the original two-projection path. Tests cover output alias rejection,
invalid dimensions, uninitialized input, foreign pending output ownership,
unsupported shapes, unchanged output data and counter reset after abort.
The new test is included in CTest alongside the original kernel reference.

All eleven existing serving/numerical/head/vision stages and all three
private-cache suites (24 profiles) pass. Another 48 independent trained
first/last-layer comparisons exercise 22/26-token chunks, batches 1/2 and
three carried-state steps, including paused rows, partial tails, overwritten
slots, invalid controls, state preservation and resident/explicit equality.
Dispatch assertions prove one joined pair in each admitted single layer and
zero in unsupported cases. All 48 retain the existing error bounds; worst
observed normalized error remains 0.9936574155, below 1.

The build/check runner records 18 successful configure/build/check stages.
No numerical tolerance is widened, and benchmarks are gated on its exit 0.

## Actual native inference and memory

Same M4 / 16 GiB, frozen checkpoints, image bytes, prompts, capacities,
output caps and stopping rules. ABBA order uses two fresh persistent workers
per build and three requests per worker. Four non-first requests form each
warm mean. All 72 initial plus 24 confirmation requests preserve complete
token IDs, prompt IDs and finished flags. Every VL request freshly encodes
its image. Actual full-model counts are 28 joined pairs for text B2 and
24 for coder B1; all other profiles have zero.

| Admitted workload | Initial warm TTFT control -> candidate | Confirmation warm TTFT | Repeat reduction | Repeat decode ratio | Repeat peak RSS increase |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Text B2 | 90.47 -> 87.79 ms | 88.86 -> 86.47 ms | 2.68% | 1.0105 | 335.20 MiB |
| Coder B1 | 38.11 -> 36.84 ms | 38.94 -> 38.11 ms | 2.14% | 1.0061 | 167.18 MiB |

The warm latency direction repeats, but the whole-model effect is much
smaller than the isolated projection ratio. Decode changes are small and do
not establish a useful decode algorithm improvement. Apparent changes in
unsupported profiles, whose path is unchanged, are not attributed to this
optimization. Raw six-profile and two-profile confirmation records remain.

First-use TTFT regresses substantially in confirmation: text B2
196.66 -> 255.36 ms, and coder B1 127.94 -> 188.64 ms. Pack allocation/copy
happens lazily at first use and cached packs persist for the session's
lifetime. Initialization is separate and approximately unchanged:
text 1.685/1.683 s and coder 1.377/1.376 s (control/candidate).
`first-use-summary.json` preserves both runs and all other profiles.
OS/driver caches were not flushed; these fresh-worker samples do not prove
cold hardware or an observed combined startup-plus-first-token clock.

Peak RSS is the macOS `/usr/bin/time -l` maximum resident-set field for each
worker/process family, reported as an individual-process high-water measure
in bytes. The same peak is attached to that worker's three records; it is
not a per-request measurement, aggregate worker memory or unique GPU memory.
It includes initialization and first use. The first-use cost and higher
resident memory matter when evaluating the small warm latency reduction.

The implementation is retained as a default-OFF experimental option. The
selected serving library remains unchanged; no broad promotion is warranted
from this tradeoff. There is no fresh vLLM comparison or stock BF16 advantage
claim here. All-model 2x decode / half-TTFT remains active and unmet.

## Commands and evidence

```text
python3 run_joined_prefill_checks.py INVESTIGATION_ROOT OUTPUT_DIR
python3 run_joined_prefill_profiles.py INVESTIGATION_ROOT OUTPUT_DIR
python3 run_joined_prefill_profiles.py INVESTIGATION_ROOT OUTPUT_DIR --confirm
python3 archive_joined_prefill.py INVESTIGATION_ROOT ARCHIVE_PATH
python3 verify_joined_prefill_evidence.py EVIDENCE_DIR PROOF_JSON
python3 summarize_joined_prefill_first_use.py EVIDENCE_DIR SUMMARY_JSON
```

All three durable jobs have terminal exit 0. Numerical checks, monitored
native workers and predecessor gates prevent simultaneous competing inference.
Only created worker groups are exempt; only owned processes may be stopped.
There were no discarded/interrupted profiles in the selected runs. Monitoring
every 0.5 s cannot exclude arbitrarily short jobs between samples.

Exact compiler/runtime/time-wrapper commands, versions, all source/checkpoint/
library hashes, raw output and timing windows, dispatch counters, resource
records, process monitors and original source snapshots are in `evidence/`.
The installer checks original identities and verifies the complete staged
bundle before writing only its explicit investigation paths. Source bundles
retain both before/after identities. Matrix/RGB/patch arrays and binaries are
omitted with their sizes/hashes. GPT-OSS, Pi and the Mac original checkout
were not modified.

`cc41fde1f3905fcfb02fed6a50ab0f9d68933e94358352b92db4e44cb5f43dfe`.
Unchanged selected control:
`73c10e5dc62eb97607e9ded9a1df8bb6702d87375620bd5dc160d8b871f78ce2`.
Archive SHA256:
`c9b528fcb30f09b9c68d0eba90e314106b6da220c94a6e598f2c6076670d9c9f`.

reports.title: Batched recurrent output projections: validated latency improvement
reports.report_text:
# Batched recurrent output projections: validated latency improvement

The new optional Qwen3.5 Metal prefill path projects recurrent outputs for
all chunk tokens together. Actual repeated image inference confirms lower
first-token latency with unchanged complete caption tokens. Decode throughput
does not improve consistently. The 2× decode / half-TTFT goal remains unmet.

## Implementation

`qwen35_linear_chunk` flattens independent input projections across batch
and token rows, then runs convolution, recurrent state updates and gated
normalization in causal token order. It gathers the gated token outputs and
performs one output projection for the chunk. Paused rows preserve state;
the existing recurrent split-output optimization remains applicable.

The API opt-in is `decoder.enable_prefill(chunk, 'shared', True)` for
Qwen3.5. The matched frame worker accepts `prefill_linear_chunk: true`.
The flag defaults to false, preserving the prior path as a control.
Chunks 32/64 are available for Qwen3.5; the resident scheduler uses smaller
final chunks to avoid unnecessary padding. For this 79-token image prompt,
plans are 16×5, 32+32+16 or 64+16, each representing 80 physical positions.
No prompt reduction, image reuse, weight quantization or speculation is used.
Checkpoint weights remain BF16 with native FP32 activations and KV.

## Actual native ABBA results

Same M4 Mac mini / 16 GiB, Qwen3.5-0.8B, 288×192 source-image processing,
54 visual tokens, 79 prompt IDs, capacity 256 and output cap 32. Each of the
two independent runs uses candidate/control then control/candidate, three
requests per worker and warm means excluding each worker's first request.
All 144 requests match frozen control prompt IDs, complete token IDs and
finished flags. Competing inference runtimes never run together.

| Run | Batch | Chunk | Control TTFT ms | Candidate TTFT ms | Control tokens/s/row | Candidate tokens/s/row |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Initial | 1 | 16 | 486.51 | 401.21 | 48.17 | 48.17 |
| Confirm | 1 | 16 | 488.92 | 402.19 | 48.05 | 48.29 |
| Initial | 1 | 32 | 488.68 | 369.77 | 47.87 | 48.48 |
| Confirm | 1 | 32 | 490.72 | 368.38 | 48.24 | 48.56 |
| Initial | 1 | 64 | 491.77 | 354.39 | 48.35 | 48.20 |
| Confirm | 1 | 64 | 489.61 | 353.50 | 48.16 | 48.14 |
| Initial | 2 | 16 | 699.26 | 608.92 | 44.24 | 44.37 |
| Confirm | 2 | 16 | 698.38 | 613.20 | 44.36 | 44.09 |
| Initial | 2 | 32 | 699.74 | 597.25 | 44.24 | 42.94 |
| Confirm | 2 | 32 | 702.80 | 582.47 | 44.57 | 44.48 |
| Initial | 2 | 64 | 700.30 | 598.20 | 44.40 | 43.66 |
| Confirm | 2 | 64 | 699.62 | 596.92 | 44.22 | 44.33 |

Batch-1 chunk 64 cuts warm TTFT by about 28% in both runs and retains
roughly 48 tokens/sec/row. Batch-2 chunk 32 cuts warm TTFT by 15–17%,
but its initial decode regression is not reproduced consistently. These
profiles are optional; no batch-2 decode gain is claimed.

The confirmation run's ordinary phase counters show batch-1 chunk-64
prefill GPU time falling from 316.64 to 197.88 ms and CPU encoding from
48.98 to 34.93 ms. Batch-2 chunk-32 GPU time falls from 461.14 to 360.44 ms
and encoding from 48.96 to 38.09 ms. GPU time is inside the wait interval,
not an additive phase. Vision remains approximately 63/123 ms for batches
1/2. These counters identify remaining GPU work; further CPU-only tuning
cannot by itself meet the full target. Serialized per-operation diagnostics
were not enabled for these speed measurements.

First-use batch-1 chunk-16 TTFT falls from approximately 790 to 568 ms;
chunk-64 first use stays around 783 ms, near its control. Batch-2 chunk-16
first use falls from approximately 980 to 763 ms; chunk-32 is around
879 versus 974 ms, while chunk-64 is slower at about 1,041 versus 972 ms.
Filesystem and driver caches were not flushed. Individual child RSS stays
around 3.4 GiB; this excludes aggregate/unique GPU-memory accounting.

## Validation and limits

All eleven handoff checks pass: kernel tests, serving/reset, mixed-image
requests, existing Qwen3.5 layers, text/coder first and last layers, all
three model heads, and small/pretrained vision. Independent NumPy checks
also pass all 24 Qwen3.5 combinations: linear/full attention × batches
1/2 × chunks 2/4/8/16/32/64, three state-carry steps each, paused rows,
partial tails, duplicate/backward slots, rejected controls and reset.
Worst normalized reference error is 0.56435 against the existing threshold
of 1. Explicit and resident executions are exactly equal.

Additional extended dense checks expose a Qwen3 batch-2 chunk-32 key-cache
rotation mismatch: worst ratio 1.51658 exceeds the established tolerance.
The runner stops before the coder's extended checks. The tolerance is
unchanged, and dense text/coder adapters explicitly retain validated
profiles 2/4/8/16. The larger dense profiles are not accepted or advertised.
The failed log and subsequent rejection/state-preservation/output checks
are retained separately. This failure does not invalidate the passing
Qwen3.5 references or its complete caption comparisons.

Candidate library SHA256:
`26f2120c3570a28607969f855f6950d626372b388361325ac49096eb30d60671`.
Preserved control SHA256:
`9bbac5c9ad7486e1fe70690c526bebaed7fcfa06e4d162a3fe257af0a6faddef`.
The candidate is a clean build with exact-half prefill, MPS vision scores
and parallel delta split enabled. Source bundles and every installed file
were SHA256-verified before atomic installation.

The final C++ edits change only indentation and normalize line endings. Subsequent Mac builds
produces the byte-identical confirmed library and passes CTest again;
`final-verification/` preserves both source hashes, commands and binary proof.
After adding the dense profile guard, twelve actual text/coder requests
(both batches) preserve complete saved outputs, and rejected profiles leave
the selected chunk, graph cache and decoder slots unchanged.

`logs/` retains actual commands, process checks, raw records, terminal
results and references. `source-snapshot/` freezes the measured source.
`derived-input-sha256.json` records sizes/hashes for omitted reproducible
RGB and patch bytes, whose full originals remain on the Mac. These are
native comparisons; stock vLLM-Metal uses a different activation/KV dtype,
so these measurements are not an exact-precision vLLM speedup claim.

# Chunk convolution and preparation: verified VL prefill gain

The optional `GARNET_METAL_LINEAR_CHUNK_CONV=ON` path processes causal
convolution across a prompt chunk, writes final convolution state once and
prepares all tokens together. Each channel retains its original token order,
FP32 sum/activation and inactive-row behavior. Recurrent delta updates remain
sequential. Kernels longer than eight elements retain the existing path.
The option defaults OFF and is measured with the retained direct-write path.

All 48 convolution cases are bit-identical to the existing sequential GPU
kernel for both complete outputs and final state: batches 1/2, padded/regular
channels, kernels 1/4/8 and chunks 1/4/16/64, including pause/resume and
inactive tails. Compile flags recorded in `source-binary-proof.json` confirm
this test block is enabled. Kernel, serving and mixed-image checks pass.
All 36 real Qwen3.5 linear layer comparisons pass at batches 1/2 and chunks
2/4/8/16/32/64, with three state-carry steps and existing tolerances.

Two native ABBA runs preserve complete captions, finished flags, prompt IDs,
RGB bytes and patch bytes across all 48 requests. Images, prompt, stop rules
and cap remain the previous 288x192 / 54 visual / 79 prompt / 28 output-token
workload. Batch 1 uses chunk 64 and batch 2 chunk 32, with adaptive tails.
Every runtime exits before the next starts. Means use four warm requests per
policy/profile per ABBA run; first use and initialization remain separate.

# Persistent chunk recurrence: verified VL latency gain

state block in FP32 registers throughout a prompt chunk, emits every token's
core output and writes final state once. Gated normalization then processes
all chunk outputs together. The kernel retains the existing 128-thread /
32-lane reduction structure and per-token causal order, including inactive
rows. A barrier protects shared norm partials between tokens. No checkpoint
values, output limits, prompts, input resolution or precision are changed.

The option defaults OFF and requires chunk convolution and parallel delta
split. Unsupported key/value dimensions retain the previous path. This is
measured with the other retained investigation flags enabled.

## Validation and native confirmation

All 48 recurrence cases match the existing sequential parallel GPU kernel
bit-for-bit for both complete output sequences and final state: batches 1/2,
value dimensions 16/32/128, chunks 1/4/16/64, fresh/carried state and paused
rows/tails. Existing convolution, direct-write and matrix checks also pass.

36 real-weight linear layer comparisons pass with unchanged tolerances;
resident/explicit execution, reset and rejected-control state checks pass.

reports.title: Whole-block BF16 packing: rejected
reports.report_text:
# Whole-block BF16 packing: rejected

This exact codec stores 128-value blocks as 128 sign/mantissa bytes plus
64 exponent-tag bytes when the exponent span fits four bits. Other blocks
keep their original 256 raw bytes. One 64-bit metadata word holds each block's
offset, exponent base and compact/raw flag. Unlike earlier nibble codecs,
there are no per-value escapes, prefix sums or separate exception reads.
The original BF16 bits are reconstructed before FP32 dot products.

The isolated M4/16 GiB GPU run completes all three original checkpoints,
their complete heads and first-layer MLP down projections, batches 1/2.
All 12 projections are bit-exact. Full CPU/GPU weight reconstruction also
passes for the matrices, all 65,536 BF16 patterns, and a random 4,097-value
tail, including nonfinite payload bits without multiplying those fixtures.
Another 21 local CPU roundtrips cover arbitrary, compact and mixed inputs
and lengths around block/chunk boundaries; cpu-roundtrip-checks.json retains
the cases and codec source hash.

Packing reduces complete-head bytes by about 21.7%, including metadata.
It does not establish process-memory savings: raw and packed buffers are both
resident in this component experiment. Host packing uses bounded 262,144-value
windows. Checkpoint files and serving code are unchanged.

| Model / batch | Raw head GPU ms | Packed head GPU ms | Raw / packed ratio |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Text / 1 | 2.939 | 3.521 | 0.834 |
| Text / 2 | 2.942 | 3.616 | 0.814 |
| Coder / 1 | 2.592 | 3.144 | 0.825 |
| Coder / 2 | 2.610 | 3.105 | 0.841 |
| VL / 1 | 4.869 | 5.996 | 0.812 |
| VL / 2 | 4.877 | 5.960 | 0.818 |

Each profile has four ABBA rounds, three warmups per position, and twelve
samples per position. The table is the median of the eight position medians
per policy. Runs are sequential with before/after inference guards. Packing,
CPU validation and compilation are outside the GPU clock. Complete heads
are all slower, as are the tested down projections; no serving integration
or favorable-sample repeat is justified. These are not model TPS or TTFT.

Commands, statuses, hardware/source/checkpoint/input hashes, guards, CPU/GPU
checks and raw timing windows are in completed/. Source snapshots are in
source/ and test2026/metal/. Raw tensors/binaries remain privately on the Mac
with sizes/hashes in evidence-proof.json. Transferred archive SHA256:
7f0a58986cc4f1ab9b0bc83a48ae4b68996ea446f1cebc6d3cf7cf1f649a4564.

The selected library remains
cc5539990dcb4effbece7c611787a656df56b51271f1f40e1c3e8b5dbf90c8f8.
The three-model 2x decode / half-TTFT goal remains active and unmet.

reports.title: Dedicated MPS vector multiply: dtype limit and rejected FP32 route
reports.report_text:
# Dedicated MPS vector multiply: dtype limit and rejected FP32 route

Actual execution on the M4 establishes two results. A Float16 matrix with
FP32 input/output vectors aborts with the framework assertion `Both inputs
must use the same type.` The valid all-FP32 route passes real-weight checks
but is much slower than the compact-BF16 native control. Neither route is
integrated into serving. The full 2x decode/half-TTFT goal remains unmet.

## Actual compatibility

The dedicated `MPSMatrixVectorMultiplication` API differs from the previously
tested mixed-input `MPSMatrixMultiplication`. Each dtype combination executes
in its own guarded child process using exact dyadic values, five outputs and
37 input elements. The unsupported combination terminates only its child
with SIGABRT (exit -6); the following all-FP32 child exits 0 and matches all
five independent expected outputs exactly. The parent finishes with a status
record for both outcomes; its exit 0 does not mean both combinations passed.

This rules out directly substituting the existing exact-half weight cache
while retaining FP32 activation vectors through this API on the tested Mac.
No activation conversion, rounding or precision shortcut was introduced.
Apple's [matrix-vector API documentation](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/metalperformanceshaders/mpsmatrixvectormultiplication?language=objc)
identifies the operation; the mixed-dtype limit above is measured framework
behavior on this system, not a claim about every device or future OS.

## Real-matrix component measurements

The valid route losslessly expands original BF16 bits into FP32 matrix storage
with a bit shift, preserving every learned value. Input, result and matrix
types are FP32. Batch 2 encodes one vector operation per row into a single
command buffer. The control shares compact BF16 weights across both rows.
Weight widths and memory traffic therefore differ; this is not a comparison
with identical storage, nor a stock-runtime performance claim.

| Model | Batch | Pooled large-matrix control/candidate GPU ratio | Body-only ratio |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Qwen3-0.6B | 1 | 0.5141 | 0.5724 |
| Qwen3-0.6B | 2 | 0.2537 | 0.3365 |
| Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct | 1 | 0.4999 | 0.5557 |
| Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct | 2 | 0.2579 | 0.3119 |
| Qwen3.5-0.8B | 1 | 0.5067 | 0.7026 |
| Qwen3.5-0.8B | 2 | 0.2545 | 0.3395 |

Ratios below one mean slower. Pools sum measured GPU times once per collected
matrix/batch with more than 256 outputs; body-only also excludes vocabulary
heads. They are not weighted by model layer counts and are not decode TPS.

| Model | Batch | Control full-head GPU ms | FP32 GEMV full-head GPU ms |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Text | 1 | 3.166 | 6.276 |
| Text | 2 | 2.996 | 12.336 |
| Coder | 1 | 2.719 | 5.529 |
| Coder | 2 | 2.670 | 10.666 |
| VL | 1 | 4.993 | 10.243 |
| VL | 2 | 5.092 | 20.570 |

Every real-matrix profile passes the unchanged `5e-6+5e-5*abs(control)`
comparison and the independent FP64 envelope
`gamma(ceil(K/32)+32)*sum(abs(products))+1e-7`. Both control and candidate are
checked against FP64; worst candidate allowed-bound ratio is 0.0097090214.
All 68 matrix/batch checks pass, including first-layer projections, complete
heads, irregular tails, distinct batch inputs and output-padding preservation.
Output summation order may differ; general bit-identical output is not claimed.

Each profile has two ABBA rounds, three warm operations per window and twelve
measured operations per window. Preparation, FP32 expansion, object creation,
source compilation and numerical readbacks are outside component timing.
GPU and host wall times are retained. Wider storage and separate per-row work
may contribute to the slowdown, but DRAM traffic/cause is not independently
measured. Resident startup and peak process memory are not measured here.

This large regression rejects integration without a favorable-number repeat
or costly full-model variant. No complete generation or new vLLM comparison
was run; serving sources and primary binaries remain unchanged.

## Evidence and reproduction

Owned root: `/Users/zsdx/garnet-metal-investigation`. Compatibility PID 53831
and component PID 54260 are terminal. Conflict guards reject competing
inference/probes and enforce at least 2 GiB free space. No unrelated process
was stopped and no comparator dependencies were installed.

Commands are `run_mps_gemv_compat.py ROOT NEW_OUTPUT_DIR` and
`run_mps_gemv_probe.py ROOT NEW_OUTPUT_DIR`. Exact absolute compiler/runtime
commands, source snapshots/hashes, raw assertion, statuses, hardware, model
and matrix identities, numerical/timing windows and monitors are in
[evidence](evidence/). Raw matrices remain private and are omitted with 34
verified size/hash/checkpoint proofs; they are regenerable from the pinned
checkpoints. The source includes the lossless expansion and vector-view setup.

```text
python test2026/metal/verify_mps_gemv.py results/20261013/mps-gemv
```

The verifier checks 62 archive file hashes, actual -6/0 dtype outcomes,
source/checkpoint identities, all 68 numerical/padding checks and timing
arithmetic. Archive SHA256:
`1b06838f8dcd77658580c16619ff59a4b36af6cc5e38a319af3921ca19a75a07`.
The primary/attention libraries and GPT-OSS/Pi checkouts remain intact.
The [latest actual vLLM comparison](../selected-attention-vllm/README.md)
continues to record all six profiles and their unmet joint targets.

reports.title: Independent MPS scheduling and joined prefill projections
reports.report_text:
# Independent MPS scheduling and joined prefill projections

These component experiments address independent first-layer gate/up prefill
projections on the same M4 / 16 GiB Mac mini. They use real checkpoint BF16
weights admitted by the selected exact-half codec, FP32 inputs/accumulation/
outputs, identical per-row scales and the retained rescaling expression.
No learned values are rounded, no images or prefixes are reused, and no
serving source or selected library changes in this experiment.

## Scheduling: reject shared-event branching

The first run compares two projections/rescales in one command buffer with
two independent GPU queues. All 24 shape/model checks are bit-identical.
Static-input completion-span speedups are often 1.1–1.3, but do not include
graph producer/consumer synchronization.

The second run adds a GPU producer, independent branch queues, three shared
events and a dependent SiLU-times-up consumer. A distinct completion event
per branch avoids one branch's higher signal value prematurely satisfying
the other branch's dependency. Increasing generations and 16 alternating
GPU-produced inputs per shape verify that stale event values do not let
consumers read an old result. All 24 checks and 384 generation comparisons
are bit-identical, including output padding.

Every synchronized completion-span ratio is below 1: roughly 0.44–0.95.
Most host-wall ratios regress too. Four command buffers and event costs erase
the static pair's apparent gain. This path is rejected for serving. GPU
command-buffer interval overlap is recorded; overlapping intervals alone do
not prove simultaneous execution of individual shaders.

## Packing: joined MPS gate/up candidate

Two other runs concatenate the exact encoded gate/up weight rows and integer
scales, execute one larger MPS projection, then split/rescale into the two
existing outputs with one kernel. A producer and dependent consumer stay in
the same command buffer on both sides. The control has two MPS projections
and two rescalers. No command-queue events or intermediate host waits are
introduced. Joined packing is checked byte-for-byte against the two encoded
source rows; half-scale admission is unchanged.

Each run covers rows 22/24/26/32/44/52/64/80 for all three models: 24 shape
checks plus 384 alternating-generation comparisons. Both the gate/up outputs
and dependent consumer are bit-identical across all checked cases in both
runs. Existing bounds remain 5e-6 + 5e-5*abs(control); none is widened.
The consumer additionally checks every output for finiteness and padding.

| Serving workload's physical rows | Initial GPU completion speedup | Repeat speedup | Repeat host-wall speedup |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Text B1 / 24 | 1.130 | 0.986 | 1.039 |
| Text B2 / 44 | 1.162 | 1.295 | 1.257 |
| Coder B1 / 26 | 1.096 | 1.126 | 1.087 |
| Coder B2 / 52 | 1.042 | 0.968 | 1.005 |
| VL B1 / 80 | 1.006 | 0.781 | 0.811 |
| VL B2 chunk / 64 | 1.033 | 1.030 | 1.048 |

Ratios are control/candidate; below 1 is slower. Each timing uses two ABBA
rounds, three warmups and twelve measurements per position. Absolute GPU
times vary across scans, so each scan uses its paired control. Completion
span and host wall include producer/consumer work in the joined and event
experiments. The static experiment does not include that work.

The evidence supports investigating only a bounded full-model candidate:
text at 44 physical rows / K=1024 / N=3072, and coder at 26 rows / K=896 /
N=4864. Text B1 and coder B2 signals do not repeat; broad VL promotion would
regress its 80-row profile. VL 64-row gain is small. Packing all model layers
would allocate additional joined half buffers, and cold/first-use packing
cost is outside these component timings. Those costs require measurement
before a serving decision.

## Integration work still required

No actual model TTFT, decode TPS, model hidden-state validation or fresh
vLLM comparison is established here. Only first-layer gate/up weights and
deterministic sinusoidal inputs are used. The all-model 2x decode / half-TTFT
goal remains active and unmet.

A bounded integration should recognize adjacent BF16 projections with the
same input and distinct outputs, preserve unsupported and split-key paths,
and admit only the repeated shapes. Pack caches must retain their source
weight ownership to prevent pointer-key reuse after graph disposal. Reject
invalid shapes/devices/output aliases before output mutation. A dispatch
counter should prove the real model uses the new route. Check trained
first/last layers and carried state with the existing 22/26-token references,
then measure full native ABBA inference, memory and first-use behavior.
Component gain alone is not a serving promotion criterion.

## Commands and evidence

```text
python3 run_concurrent_mps_pair.py INVESTIGATION_ROOT OUTPUT_DIR
python3 run_concurrent_mps_dependency.py INVESTIGATION_ROOT OUTPUT_DIR
python3 run_joined_mps_pair.py INVESTIGATION_ROOT OUTPUT_DIR
python3 run_joined_mps_pair.py INVESTIGATION_ROOT CONFIRMATION_OUTPUT_DIR
python3 archive_mps_pair_probes.py INVESTIGATION_ROOT ARCHIVE_PATH
python3 verify_mps_pair_probe_evidence.py EVIDENCE_DIR PROOF_JSON
```

All four durable jobs are terminal with exit 0. The archive retains exact
compiler/GPU commands, source/checkpoint hashes, versions, all raw ABBA
windows, checks, generation counts, 0.5-second process monitors, statuses
and sizes/hashes of omitted matrix assets and binaries. Other inference
runtimes are rejected; only owned probe process groups may be terminated.
Arbitrarily short external jobs between monitor samples cannot be excluded.
Protected GPT-OSS/Pi checkouts and the Mac original source remain untouched.
The selected library is still SHA256
`73c10e5dc62eb97607e9ded9a1df8bb6702d87375620bd5dc160d8b871f78ce2`.

Archive SHA256:
`733fda3e04b54873620f03134ce2a1e4f8250b956c61ecd32d72dfe049da2742`.

# Optional FP32 MPS vision attention: validated modest latency gain

Packing query/key heads into bounded FP32 scratch and computing batched
`Q * K^T` with MPS reduces warm real-frame TTFT. It retains the existing
softmax implementation, checkpoint, input bytes, decoder and output cap.
Two native ABBA runs produce identical complete generated tokens. This
improvement is retained as `GARNET_METAL_MPS_VISION_SCORES`, OFF by default.
The 2× vLLM-Metal throughput / half-TTFT goal is still unmet in every profile.

The MPS path handles at most 1,024 flattened image rows, 512 patch tokens,
16 heads and head dimension 128. Other shapes retain the existing score
kernel. Scratch is cached by rows, tokens, hidden size and heads, reused across
vision blocks in the graph, and released with its context. Heads/batches have
separate matrices. No learned weights are changed or quantized.

## Actual native measurements

Same Apple M4 Mac mini, 16 GiB, Qwen3.5-0.8B BF16 checkpoint, 288×192 image,
54 visual tokens, 79 prompt IDs, chunk 16, capacity 256, 32-token output cap.
Every frame is freshly preprocessed and encoded; decoder state is reset.
Only one inference process runs at a time. Each ABBA run contains twelve
requests per batch, four of which are first-use requests. Warm means exclude
the first request in each fresh process.

| Run | Batch | Control TTFT | Candidate TTFT | TTFT reduction | Control tokens/s/row | Candidate tokens/s/row |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Initial | 1 | 563.48 ms | 547.55 ms | 2.83% | 47.14 | 47.04 |
| Initial | 2 | 796.18 ms | 762.26 ms | 4.26% | 43.07 | 42.98 |
| Repeat | 1 | 563.64 ms | 551.43 ms | 2.17% | 47.23 | 47.08 |
| Repeat | 2 | 792.48 ms | 765.85 ms | 3.36% | 43.04 | 43.09 |

All 48 native frame requests match complete control token IDs and finish.
Decode is essentially unchanged; no meaningful decode speedup is claimed.

Repeat first-use means, separate from warm results:

| Batch | Control model initialization | Candidate initialization | Control first TTFT | Candidate first TTFT |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 2.897 s | 2.906 s | 859.45 ms | 864.38 ms |
| 2 | 2.927 s | 2.895 s | 1,059.40 ms | 1,049.73 ms |

These are fresh processes with existing filesystem/shader caches, not cold
boots. Memory evidence remains individual-process high-water RSS, not unique
unified GPU memory; all raw process accounting is retained.

## Fresh sequential vLLM-Metal comparison

The isolated comparator and all three checkpoint paths are unchanged from
the prior investigation. Prompts, token caps, batch, image bytes and native
prompt IDs match. Prefix reuse, image encoder reuse and speculation are
disabled. These are observed same-checkpoint results: native FP32 vision,
activations and KV differ from the comparator's BF16 internal arithmetic.
That precision difference remains an acceptance limitation.

| Model | Batch | Garnet tokens/s/row | vLLM tokens/s/row | Garnet TTFT | vLLM TTFT |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Qwen3-0.6B | 1 | 56.86 | 73.99 | 70.85 ms | 51.04 ms |
| Qwen3-0.6B | 2 | 51.99 | 75.78 | 116.94 ms | 64.13 ms |
| Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct | 1 | 72.27 | 92.11 | 55.42 ms | 34.74 ms |
| Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct | 2 | 69.83 | 92.24 | 74.50 ms | 38.02 ms |
| Qwen3.5-0.8B image | 1 | 47.06 | 48.19 | 548.54 ms | 205.49 ms |
| Qwen3.5-0.8B image | 2 | 42.99 | 48.31 | 763.94 ms | 327.28 ms |

Text/coder and image batch 1 have exact generated token IDs and complete
outputs. Image batch 2 still differs: native completes its 28-token caption,
while the comparator reaches the 32-token cap. Its timing is diagnostic and
cannot establish a successful matched-output speed comparison. Text/coder
are the existing short prompts (8 and 17 generated tokens including stop),
so their throughput should not be generalized to every workload.

Every decode ratio is below 2 and every TTFT fraction exceeds 0.5. All target
flags remain false. No current result supports a 2× claim.

## Validation and reproduction

All eleven handoff jobs pass: CTest, serving/reset/shared-state checks,
mixed-image pipeline, actual Qwen3.5 and dense decoder layer references,
all three complete vocabulary heads and small/pretrained vision references.

records actual commands, exits, versions/hashes, process guards and results.
Summaries retain all token IDs and RGB/patch hashes; raw pixel buffers are
excluded. The selected prior control binary remains unchanged:
`564b515ab6b0eb68413ef5a54de6beff47d333f8f1fa6a1188562bf6e5c28ec4`.

reports.title: Native BF16 body decode: small repeated gains, latency tradeoff
reports.report_text:
# Native BF16 body decode: small repeated gains, latency tradeoff

An optional `GARNET_METAL_NATIVE_BFLOAT_BODY=ON` route loads original BF16
weight bytes through Metal's native `bfloat` type. One-row body projections
use the original serial accumulation with 64 threads; two-row body projections
use vector dot products with 128 threads. FP32 inputs, accumulation and output
remain. The vector-dot route reassociates sums; learned values are not rounded.
There is no weight repacking, prefix/encoder reuse or speculative decoding.

Admission is bounded to one/two rows, input widths divisible by four and
257 through 99,999 output columns. Small outputs and the complete vocabulary
heads keep their selected kernels. Prefill dispatch is unchanged. Native BF16
source and Metal language version 3.1 are enabled only by the opt-in build
flag. The default remains OFF and does not compile the extra kernels. Actual
compatibility/performance here is established on this M4, not all Mac GPUs.

## Component and numerical evidence

The initial real-weight component run covers four variants (serial/dot,
64/128 threads), first-layer matrices, all three complete heads, batches 1/2,
irregular input widths and padded outputs: 272 checks. A confirmation tests
serial/64 and dot/128 in 136 checks. All 408 pass the independent FP64 dot
reference, with fixed gamma(n)*sum(abs(products))+1e-7 bound and
n=ceil(inner/32)+32 using float epsilon. Worst bound ratio is 0.00997263774.
The control must pass too. Serial candidates are bit-identical; dot candidates
can differ due to summation order. No existing trained-layer bound is changed.

Initial heads mostly regress, so they are excluded from serving admission.
Large body component sum ratios repeat at roughly 1.03–1.05 for selected text
variants and 1.05 for VL batch-2 dot/128. These sums cover collected matrices
once per batch and are not weighted by layer counts or model tokens/sec.
Coder component signals are small/mixed.

The integrated build passes all eleven ordinary stages (native kernel test,
serving, mixed images, trained Qwen3.5/dense layers, all three complete heads,
small/pretrained vision), plus three private-cache suites covering 24 profiles.
Existing numerical thresholds and complete greedy output checks remain.
An additional actual GPU test verifies native BF16-to-FP32 casts for all
65,280 finite patterns, including subnormals and signed zero, under precise
and fast-math compilation: zero bit mismatches in both modes. Nonfinite
weights retain existing upload rejection.

The SDK exposes `MPSDataTypeBFloat16`, but earlier actual direct-BF16 MPS
execution on this Mac aborted. That compatibility test was not repeated;
the working exact-half prefill route remains. Native shader BF16 loads are
distinct from direct BF16 MPS matrix multiplication.

## Actual native inference results

Same M4 / 16 GiB, checkpoints, prompts, image bytes, capacities, output caps,
stop rules and retained prefill plans. Each native comparison uses ABBA build
order, two fresh persistent workers per build, three requests per worker and
four non-first requests per warm mean. Every complete sequence, prompt ID,
finished flag and VL fresh-image identity matches the frozen baseline.
There are 72 initial plus 48 confirmation requests. No runtimes run together.

| Model | Batch | Initial decode ratio | Confirmation decode ratio | Confirmation TTFT fraction |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Qwen3-0.6B | 1 | 1.01675 | 1.01016 | 1.01025 |
| Qwen3-0.6B | 2 | 1.01644 | 1.02801 | 1.02577 |
| Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct | 1 | 0.99890 | Not repeated | Not repeated |
| Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct | 2 | 0.99550 | Not repeated | Not repeated |
| Qwen3.5-0.8B | 1 | 1.00874 | 1.00488 | 1.00532 |
| Qwen3.5-0.8B | 2 | 1.01866 | 1.01588 | 1.00748 |

Ratios are candidate/control. The text decode direction repeats, about
1.0–2.8%; VL is about 0.5–1.6% in confirmation. Coder is flat and was not
repeated to seek favorable noise. Confirmation TTFT is slightly worse:
53.73 -> 54.29 ms and 90.11 -> 92.43 ms for text; 217.14 -> 218.29 ms and
387.24 -> 390.14 ms for VL. No latency benefit is established or attributed
to the decode algorithm. These are modest warm means, not a broad task suite.

The code is retained as a default-OFF experimental option. It is not selected
as the primary serving build, given the small throughput gain and latency
tradeoff. The selected control library stays byte-identical. There is no new
vLLM comparator run, stock BF16 advantage, or 2x/half-TTFT success claim.
The broader all-model goal remains active and unmet.

Counters come from the existing native decoder session. No per-operation
GPU serialization or diagnostic synchronization is enabled. Metadata is
emitted after the existing first/done markers. The added assembly timestamp

| Batch | End-to-end TTFT | Vision/reset | Prompt assembly | Prefill wall | CPU prepare | CPU encode | GPU execution | Submit/wait wall |

reports.title: Rejected interleaved BF16 decode layout
reports.report_text:
# Rejected interleaved BF16 decode layout

This candidate preserves all learned BF16 bits and the original per-output
FP32 accumulation/reduction order. Four output columns by four K terms are
stored in a contiguous 32-byte block. The GPU loads two `uint4` vectors and
reconstructs the original FP32 values. Odd K retains the original kernel.
The raw BF16 buffer remains available for prefill, fallback and control.

The candidate compiles with the optional `GARNET_METAL_PACKED_DECODE` flag.
All eleven handoff checks pass, including actual model layers/heads, serving,
mixed images and vision. Seventy-two direct GPU comparisons are bit-exact
against the original kernel, covering batches 1/2, aligned and odd K,
column tails, signed zero and small BF16 values. Actual native ABBA inference
then completes 48 text/coder requests and 24 image requests with identical
prompt IDs, complete output token IDs and finished flags.

## Actual whole-model results

Same M4 Mac mini / 16 GiB, checkpoints, prompt IDs, caps and batches. Only
one inference runtime runs at once. Candidate/control then control/candidate
workers each make three requests; warm means exclude each worker's first
request. These are native comparisons, not vLLM speed claims.

| Model | Batch | Control tokens/s/row | Candidate tokens/s/row | Decode ratio | Control TTFT ms | Candidate TTFT ms |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Qwen3-0.6B | 1 | 47.51 | 48.68 | 1.025 | 89.39 | 89.53 |
| Qwen3-0.6B | 2 | 47.77 | 48.30 | 1.011 | 133.86 | 131.62 |
| Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B | 1 | 65.66 | 66.18 | 1.008 | 71.24 | 72.13 |
| Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B | 2 | 70.11 | 69.34 | 0.989 | 75.10 | 78.48 |
| Qwen3.5-0.8B VL | 1 | 48.44 | 49.57 | 1.023 | 353.98 | 359.55 |
| Qwen3.5-0.8B VL | 2 | 44.67 | 45.99 | 1.030 | 606.70 | 607.58 |

The VLM uses the previously validated recurrent chunk path: chunk 64 with
an adaptive 16-token tail for batch 1, and chunk 16 for batch 2. Both builds
freshly encode the same 288×192 image per request, with 79 prompt IDs and
cap 32. Text/coder use chunk 16 and cap 64. No reduced prompt, image reuse,
prefix caching or speculative decoding is introduced.

Decode changes are small and mixed, while most TTFT profiles are flat or
worse. Peak individual child RSS increases from about 2.33 to 3.44 GiB
for text, 1.93 to 2.85 GiB for coder, and 3.35 to 4.75 GiB for VL batch 1.
These are high-water child RSS values, not aggregate or unique GPU memory.
Batch-1 initialization is 2.09 versus 1.94 seconds for text, 1.70 versus
1.41 seconds for coder, and 3.39 versus 3.10 seconds for VL. First-use VL
TTFT is 848 versus 777 ms. Filesystem and driver caches were not flushed.

The broad layout is rejected: it adds approximately 0.9–1.4 GiB and load
work without a useful consistent improvement across the requested models
and latency/throughput metrics. There is no confirmation or new matched
vLLM comparison of this rejected candidate. The 2× decode / half-TTFT goal
remains active and unmet.

## Environment and restoration

Recorded checkpoint/config/tokenizer assets match the prior control's
metadata. Absolute text timings differ from earlier sessions; desktop and
streaming services are present in process snapshots, so the paired control
in this run is the reference. A post-run query records no thermal/performance
warning, and swap usage is 3,109.25 MiB, equal to the observed preflight value.
This does not prove the absence of all background contention.

After the benchmarks, an unrelated release-test xlang3 process cannot be
verified by the existing ancestor-based inference guard. The rejected
restoration preflight and its evidence are retained. No further inference
was started, the guard was not relaxed, and no unrelated job was stopped.
Source-only restoration verifies all owned experiment jobs are terminal,
checks the current candidate and restored file hashes, and touches only
the four investigation source files and its created probe script.

The selected library remains byte-identical:
`26f2120c3570a28607969f855f6950d626372b388361325ac49096eb30d60671`.
The rejected private candidate remains isolated:
`6bed77dcbd5dbfe1e6bb875062bce55d42db5e819f04badaeafe701694a55ba9`.
Production source is restored locally and on the Mac. `restoration/`
preserves that proof; `source-snapshot/` and `rejected-packed-decode.diff`
preserve the actual experimental implementation. `logs/` retains exact
commands, terminal results, outputs, process snapshots and numerical checks.
Reproducible RGB/patch bytes are omitted from Git with their sizes/SHA256
retained; full originals and compiled candidates remain private on the Mac.

The later read-only launcher audit resolves the release-test service's identity
and adds exact fingerprint/library checks to the comparison guard. That
separate change and its eighteen passing checks are documented in
`../worldsense-inline-guard/`; the rejected layout stays reverted.

reports.title: Parallel recurrent reductions: validated and retained
reports.report_text:
# Parallel recurrent reductions: validated and retained

The optional `GARNET_METAL_PARALLEL_DELTA_SPLIT` kernel improves actual
Qwen3.5 image latency and decode throughput. Two native ABBA comparisons
show matching complete outputs and repeatable gains. The full 2× decode /
half-TTFT goal remains unmet. The option is OFF by default; the tested
investigation build enables it with exact-half prefill and MPS vision scores.

## Implementation and correctness

The existing recurrent kernel assigns one thread to each output value and
loops over 128 key elements serially. The candidate assigns four output
values to each SIMD group, distributes key terms over 32 lanes and uses
SIMD reductions. Each threadgroup handles 16 values. This increases useful
parallelism and shortens dependent dot-product loops. The original key-major
state layout and all learned values are retained. No weight quantization,
prefix reuse or speculation is introduced.

The fast path requires key dimension 128, value dimension divisible by 16,
and aligned state/output strides. Other shapes use the prior kernel.
Paused rows copy state bit-for-bit and produce zero output. Active FP32 dot
reductions change addition order, so their intermediate bits need not match
the old serial reduction. Independent FP64 output/state oracles use a
3e-6 absolute tolerance. Tests retain strict bitwise checks for fallback and
paused paths, pending-output rejection, abort recovery and in-place rejection.

All eleven handoff jobs pass, including actual Qwen3.5 layer/state references,
dense text/coder layer references, all three complete heads, serving/reset/
shared-state behavior and small/pretrained vision references. The option OFF
also compiles and passes CTest. All 48 requests across the two native frame
comparisons match complete control token IDs and finish.

## Actual native ABBA measurements

Same M4 / 16 GiB, Qwen3.5-0.8B, 288×192 image, 54 visual tokens, 79 prompt
IDs, chunk 16, capacity 256 and cap 32. Every frame is freshly encoded and
decoder state reset. Each run has twelve requests per batch; warm means
exclude first use in each fresh worker. Only one inference runtime runs.

| Run | Batch | Control TTFT | Candidate TTFT | TTFT reduction | Control tokens/s/row | Candidate tokens/s/row |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Initial valid | 1 | 549.54 ms | 491.62 ms | 10.54% | 47.15 | 48.06 |
| Initial valid | 2 | 760.61 ms | 700.48 ms | 7.91% | 42.93 | 44.56 |
| Confirm | 1 | 549.16 ms | 490.29 ms | 10.72% | 47.19 | 48.27 |
| Confirm | 2 | 764.32 ms | 703.32 ms | 7.98% | 43.20 | 44.41 |

Confirmation decode gains are 2.29% / 2.79%. Existing non-serialized session
counters attribute the change to GPU prefill: 374.90 → 317.97 ms at batch 1,
524.88 → 460.73 ms at batch 2. CPU encoding stays about 49 ms. No serialized
per-operation diagnostic timing is used as serving performance.

First-use confirmation measurements remain separate:

| Batch | Control initialization | Candidate initialization | Control first TTFT | Candidate first TTFT |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 3.102 s | 3.061 s | 846.23 ms | 799.57 ms |
| 2 | 3.113 s | 3.103 s | 1,047.06 ms | 980.56 ms |

These are fresh processes with existing filesystem/shader caches, not cold
boots. Individual-process RSS remains distinct from unique unified GPU
allocations and aggregate multi-process memory.

## Fresh stock BF16 comparator results

These observed same-checkpoint results retain the prior precision limitation:
native activations/KV are FP32, stock comparator activations/KV are BF16.
All stock-comparator throughput and half-TTFT gates remain false.

| Model | Batch | Garnet tokens/s/row | vLLM tokens/s/row | Garnet TTFT | vLLM TTFT |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Qwen3-0.6B | 1 | 56.76 | 74.35 | 71.34 ms | 49.76 ms |
| Qwen3-0.6B | 2 | 51.97 | 75.95 | 116.03 ms | 70.92 ms |
| Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct | 1 | 72.58 | 92.09 | 54.80 ms | 34.78 ms |
| Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct | 2 | 69.85 | 92.25 | 74.48 ms | 38.39 ms |
| Qwen3.5-0.8B image | 1 | 48.24 | 48.26 | 488.11 ms | 203.05 ms |
| Qwen3.5-0.8B image | 2 | 43.16 | 47.34 | 713.55 ms | 329.11 ms |

Stock image batch 2 still has differing outputs and comparator cap exhaustion;
it cannot establish a matched-output speed claim. Text/coder and image batch
1 outputs match. Text/coder kernels are unaffected by this recurrent change;
their timings remain close to prior native measurements.

## Separate exact-value FP32 comparison

The original learned values are compared against the previously verified
lossless F32 copies, with actual FP32 weights, tested activations and KV.
The comparator uses memory fraction 0.30 for dense models and 0.45 for VL
so the expanded model/cache fits. These are separate precision-configuration
results and do not count as beating the default BF16 baseline.

| Model | Batch | Garnet tokens/s/row | FP32 vLLM tokens/s/row | Garnet TTFT | FP32 vLLM TTFT |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Qwen3-0.6B | 1 | 57.05 | 38.05 | 70.57 ms | 79.26 ms |
| Qwen3-0.6B | 2 | 51.53 | 24.24 | 118.52 ms | 106.00 ms |
| Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct | 1 | 72.31 | 47.18 | 55.69 ms | 63.11 ms |
| Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct | 2 | 69.80 | 29.41 | 74.84 ms | 81.44 ms |
| Qwen3.5-0.8B image | 1 | 48.13 | 26.28 | 490.92 ms | 261.23 ms |
| Qwen3.5-0.8B image | 2 | 44.55 | 16.65 | 699.27 ms | 436.31 ms |

All 72 FP32 study requests match complete outputs. Coder/vision batch-2
decode ratios are 2.37× / 2.68×, while half-TTFT fails everywhere. The observed
2.13× text batch-2 ratio reflects a slower comparator than the prior run
(24.24 versus 29.29 tokens/s); native text speed did not improve. It is not
a confirmed new text acceleration and must not be used as evidence that
this recurrent optimization made dense text 2× faster.

## Transfer/rebuild provenance and evidence

The first build started before failed SSH source transfers were confirmed.
C++ compilation accepted the raw embedded string, but CTest caught its
incomplete Metal shader before any inference benchmark. The next build
reused stale objects because extracted source timestamps were older. Both
failed chains and their blocked benchmark successors are retained. A source
bundle was then uploaded in small hash-checked pieces, fully SHA-verified,
atomically installed, and rebuilt with `--clean-first`. All reported valid
measurements use that verified clean rebuild. No failed attempt supplies a
speed result, and the selected control binary was never rebuilt or modified.

`candidate-source/` contains actual source, flags, helpers, verified install
manifest, hashes, failure snapshot and CTest details. Job directories record
commands, terminal exits, process guards, all request timing/token IDs and
image/model identity. Raw image buffers are excluded. The candidate library
is `9bbac5c9ad7486e1fe70690c526bebaed7fcfa06e4d162a3fe257af0a6faddef`;
the control remains
`c9f8c76aa2657669d6a7b10eba459481ac797fc64904d25360933b565f9d77d1`.

The complete goal remains active: repeated 2× decode and half-TTFT across all
agreed models/batches with matched precision. Current measurements contradict
completion, despite a useful validated native latency improvement.

reports.title: Parallel delta GPU prototypes: rejected
reports.report_text:
# Parallel delta GPU prototypes: rejected

Two isolated GPU implementations of the validated FP32 chunk formulation
were executed sequentially on the M4/16 GiB Mac mini. Both are slower than
the retained gated_delta_chunk kernel, so neither is integrated into serving.
The selected extended-prefill library remains byte-identical:
cc5539990dcb4effbece7c611787a656df56b51271f1f40e1c3e8b5dbf90c8f8.

The first implementation uses six batched MPS FP32 products and a direct
forward substitution for the triangular recurrence. The second replaces
those products with 16x32 output tiles and 32-wide reduction tiles in Metal
SIMD-group matrix operations. Both preserve direct decay products without
clipping or division, including zero-decay and inactive tokens.

Both pass 68 output/state comparisons against the retained GPU kernel with
the unchanged 5e-6 + 5e-5*abs(reference) tolerance. The worst tolerance ratio
is 0.039274359 in each run. There are 64 synthetic cases covering batches
1/2, heads 2/16, chunks 16/32/64/80, inactive tokens, correlated keys and
zero decay. Four cases use actual trained layer 0/22 projections with
synthetic hidden inputs and prior states. These are core component checks;
they are not complete layer, model, image-caption or vLLM comparisons.

Each case runs two ABBA timing rounds, three warmups per position, and twelve
measurements per position. The table is the median GPU command-buffer time
over the four positions for each implementation. Control timings are shown
separately for each run. Encoders and matrix operations execute in one command
buffer; wall time is also retained in raw logs. Guard snapshots before and
after each run check for competing inference.

| Layer / batch / chunk | MPS-run control ms | MPS candidate ms | Tiled-run control ms | Tiled candidate ms |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 0 / 1 / 80 | 0.2776 | 0.8550 | 0.2799 | 1.0710 |
| 0 / 2 / 32 | 0.2101 | 0.6000 | 0.2137 | 0.7190 |
| 22 / 1 / 80 | 0.2787 | 0.8504 | 0.2849 | 1.1446 |
| 22 / 2 / 32 | 0.2100 | 0.5995 | 0.2084 | 0.7112 |

MPS is 2.85-3.08x slower; tiled Metal is 3.36-4.02x slower in these trained
projection cases. The additional matrix work and dispatches are a plausible
cost, but this experiment does not isolate each operation's contribution.
There is no useful speed gain to justify full-model integration or a repeat
run solely to seek a favorable sample.

Commands, terminal statuses, source hashes, assets manifests, raw numerical
checks, timing windows and summaries are in completed/. The exact standalone
sources are in source/ and test2026/metal/. Input tensors and compiled binaries
remain on the Mac; their byte sizes and hashes are in evidence-proof.json.
The transferred archive SHA256 is
78bdeb4488a408b5e8e83b88bc6f7b4dbdd57a0e591f00ef213acdb8263328b9.

The full goal of 2x vLLM-Metal decode and half first-token latency across the
three matched Qwen workloads remains active and unmet. These rejected probes
provide no end-to-end improvement and no new comparator results.

reports.title: Extended Qwen3.5 prefill: small batch-1 latency gain
reports.report_text:
# Extended Qwen3.5 prefill: small batch-1 latency gain

GARNET_METAL_QWEN35_EXTENDED_PREFILL=ON admits up to 80 prompt slots, with
an 80*1024 packed-hidden bound. The flag defaults OFF and requires retained
convolution/delta chunk kernels. The GPU shader/arithmetic are unchanged;
the C++ profile bounds and Python admission change. Default bounds remain
64 slots / 65536 packed hidden. Other model profiles remain unchanged.

MetalDecoder.enable_prefill(80, 'shared', linear_chunk=True) requires a
resident session, hidden size <= 1024 and batch*chunk <= 128. It turns this
79-token image prompt into [80] instead of [64,16] at batch 1. Two [40,40]
chunks were tested at batch 2 against [32,32,16]; they show no benefit and
are not recommended for this workload. Keep maximum 32 at batch 2.

All 36 independent real-weight comparisons pass for first/last linear and
full-attention layers, chunks 40/80 (batch 1) and 40 (batch 2), three carried
state steps, inactive tokens and overwritten slots. The original tolerance
5e-6 + 5e-5*abs(reference) is unchanged. Explicit and resident GPU results
also match exactly. Invalid controls, reset and closed-graph rejection pass.
Worst numerical tolerance ratio is 0.599987384 (<= 1 passes).

All eleven standard kernel/serving/numerical/head/vision tests pass. CPU-only
planning/admission checks pass 4,096 existing dense cases and 768 extended
Qwen3.5 cases. Actual candidate and legacy workers reject invalid profiles
without changing profile/cache/slot state, then complete image requests.

Two sequential native ABBA runs retain identical complete captions, prompt
IDs and fresh RGB/patch bytes across all 48 timed requests, with the same
32-token output cap and 28 generated IDs including stop. Each build/batch
uses two fresh workers with three requests; four non-first requests form
the warm mean. No prefix/encoder reuse or speculation is introduced.

| Batch | Initial TTFT reduction | Repeat TTFT reduction | Repeat candidate/control ms | Repeat decode ratio |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 2.7% | 4.0% | 217.38 / 226.45 | 1.002 |
| 2 | -1.0% | -0.2% | 384.03 / 383.09 | 1.006 |

The batch-1 latency gain is small and repeats; decode is effectively flat.
Batch 2 is slightly slower in both runs. Only the batch-1 80-slot policy is
selected for subsequent comparison. The 40-slot profile remains experimental.
First-use and initialization are separate from warm timing; caches were not
flushed. Peak process RSS includes initialization and is not unique GPU memory.

| Batch | Repeat first-use TTFT candidate/control ms | Repeat initialization candidate/control s |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 342.34 / 429.02 | 3.07 / 3.08 |
| 2 | 509.55 / 573.42 | 3.08 / 3.08 |

The first 80-slot test exposed the prior packed-hidden ceiling; its failure,
initial source/binary hash and retained fixture are preserved. Test cleanup
is fixed so an unsuccessful build is not masked by a session-reset error.
The corrected profile passes without altering numerical tolerances.

The WorldSense supervisor changed during validation. Read-only import/literal
audit confirms it only forwards GARNET_TRT_WEIGHT_STREAMING_BUDGET_MIB and
loads no inference libraries. Only its exact inspected source fingerprint
6ce05f32376832f579e5908399a9787d5957cc1b08bff31b6394c09fff9b80ec is added;
the existing identity/loaded-library rejections remain. All 21 guard checks
pass against the live service. Only the investigation's old preflight waiter
was stopped to load the corrected guard, before any test started. The successful
36-case numerical job is reused. External services/processes were unchanged.
Failed dependencies and the stopped preflight are distinguished from executed
numerical or benchmark failures in their saved statuses.

No 2x decode / half-TTFT achievement is established. The full three-model
goal remains active and unmet; these profiles are verified only on the
M4/16 GiB Mac mini, this checkpoint, image/prompt and batches 1/2.

Completed source, commands, statuses, outputs, profile plans, guards,
resource samples and failed/retried evidence are in completed/. Private
tensor/image bytes and binaries remain on the Mac with hashes in
evidence-proof.json. The archive verifier's first version misclassified
both native worker labels as candidates; the corrected verifier uses folder
identity and verifies each executed plan. Benchmark records were unchanged.

Candidate library SHA256: cc5539990dcb4effbece7c611787a656df56b51271f1f40e1c3e8b5dbf90c8f8.

Unchanged control library SHA256: 56bc06c693f3776c994d3f4078dd2e25093b575f93f6f09c4e2087a4917ee8d4.

Native evidence archive SHA256: 0ef070c976813fec8570645a85e0af7b2f4e9c3d1068cc37da5f8a8897a1ac3c.

## Fresh equivalent-FP32 comparator study

The subsequent comparison uses chunk 80 at batch 1 and retains chunk 32 at
batch 2. Original learned values, source RGB, prompt IDs and output cap are
matched, with sequential native/vLLM-Metal workers and no reuse/speculation.
All 24 requests pass exact output and prompt parity and fresh-encoder checks.

This additional study compares native original BF16 storage with FP32
arithmetic against losslessly expanded, bit-equivalent FP32 comparator
weights/activations/KV. It does not establish stock/default BF16 speedups.

| Batch | Garnet TTFT ms | vLLM TTFT ms | Garnet steps/s | vLLM steps/s | Decode ratio | TTFT fraction |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 221.69 | 256.38 | 48.45 | 26.75 | 1.811 | 0.865 |
| 2 | 385.08 | 447.87 | 44.91 | 16.44 | 2.732 | 0.860 |
