reports.title: Private single-slot KV writes: retained opt-in text decode improvement
reports.report_text:
# Private single-slot KV writes: retained opt-in text decode improvement

GARNET_METAL_RESIDENT_KV_INPLACE=ON writes only the newly decoded token into
each session-owned key/value cache. It replaces the full-cache copy for
eligible single-token attention graphs. The option defaults OFF. Explicit
graph calls retain their independent outputs; rank-three chunk prefill retains
the original cache path, preserving causal behavior across overwritten slots.
Learned values, FP32 arithmetic, layouts, prompts and generated tokens are
unchanged. There is no prefix/encoder reuse or speculative decoding.

Eligibility requires a fresh output storage group with exactly one KV writer,
the matching state input, and no later consumer of the old input cache. Graph
bindings are restored after encoding, under the existing graph/session locks.
The session keeps its private cache allocation; invalid controls are validated
before any encoding/state mutation. GPU failures still poison the session and
require reset. kv_inplace_updates counts selected private cache update
dispatches in the last run, including dispatches with inactive rows.

All eleven existing kernel/serving/numerical/head/vision stages pass. Another
24 real first/last-layer profiles cover all three models, batches 1/2,
capacities 8/256 and eight steps each. Their 192 steps match explicit graph
outputs/cache values exactly. Paused/all-inactive rows, boundary slots,
overwrites, rejected controls, reset, caller-owned input preservation and
shared-graph session isolation pass. Counters prove two private cache dispatches
per tested single-layer request. A separate native GPU primitive passes 16
profiles with bit-exact IEEE words, signed zero, subnormals, NaN payloads,
inactive rows, abort unreadability and recovery. The legacy control rejects
the new aliasing mode. A fresh default-OFF build passes its kernel test and
all 24 private-session profiles with zero private update dispatches.

## Sequential native comparison

Same M4/16 GiB Mac mini and frozen checkpoints/workloads. Each profile has
ABBA build order, two fresh processes per build, three requests per process,
and four non-first requests per warm mean. Every complete output, prompt ID
and finished flag matches the frozen control. VL freshly encodes the same
288x192 image and 79-token prompt, with a 32-token output cap. Text/coder
retain their prompts, 64-token caps and finer prefill policies. Per-row
decode steps/s is reported; aggregate batch-2 throughput is twice this.

| Model / batch | Control steps/s | Candidate steps/s | Decode ratio | Control TTFT ms | Candidate TTFT ms |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Text / 1 | 55.70 | 59.84 | 1.074 | 53.28 | 51.46 |
| Text / 2 | 51.25 | 58.66 | 1.144 | 93.57 | 91.74 |
| Coder / 1 | 72.29 | 71.96 | 0.996 | 40.45 | 41.07 |
| Coder / 2 | 70.03 | 71.26 | 1.018 | 63.86 | 63.23 |
| VL / 1 | 48.22 | 48.12 | 0.998 | 219.63 | 220.63 |
| VL / 2 | 44.51 | 44.99 | 1.011 | 390.93 | 390.19 |

The text gain repeats in a second full text ABBA run:

| Text batch | Control steps/s | Candidate steps/s | Decode ratio | Control TTFT ms | Candidate TTFT ms |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 55.56 | 59.81 | 1.077 | 53.59 | 50.54 |
| 2 | 51.50 | 58.52 | 1.136 | 93.07 | 90.43 |

An earlier independently completed text batch-1 profile also gives 1.074.
The retained signal is text decode: about 7.4-7.7% at batch 1 and 13.6-14.4%
at batch 2. Coder/VL changes are small and mixed; no useful gain is established
for them, and they were not repeated solely to seek a favorable sample.
First-token changes are small compared with the half-TTFT target. No new
vLLM comparison ran here, and native ratios must not be presented as vLLM
speedups or stock/default BF16 advantages.

Initialization and first-use requests remain separate in raw records.
Confirmation initialization is 1.657/1.657 seconds (candidate/control,
text batch 1), and 1.681/1.683 seconds (batch 2). Filesystem/driver caches
were not flushed. No new process-memory improvement is claimed: independent
graph cache output buffers remain allocated for explicit calls.

## Guards and retained failures

Unknown external xlang3 jobs interrupted the initial validation's post-guard
and two full-suite benchmark attempts. The initial text correctness suite
had exited zero and is reused by the successful resumed validation. Its
wrapper's guard failure remains distinct from a numerical failure. Interrupted
benchmark workers are excluded from selected results. Clean completed profiles
are reused only after checking all four worker exits and monitor records.
Native workers are monitored every 0.5 seconds; only the process group created
by this benchmark is exempt, and multiple owned native workers are rejected.
External jobs were not stopped. This samples contention; it cannot prove the
absence of arbitrarily short external jobs between polls.

The per-profile manager waits for a five-second clear guard interval before
each attempt and can retry only contention failures. Its first version failed
before inference because a guard helper needed hashlib; that source/error is
preserved alongside the corrected version. Source snapshots distinguish the
initial monitored runner, the word-check preflight version and the final
filtered profile runner. No running job was restarted because observation
timed out. The selected six-profile set plus text confirmation contains 96
clean timed requests. Other initial/failed/partial records remain separately.

completed/ contains commands, statuses, guards, monitor samples, full outputs,
numerical logs, profile means and first-use data. current-source/,
original-source/ and source-history/ retain exact code versions and transfer
manifests. Raw patch/RGB arrays and standalone binaries stay on the Mac with
sizes/hashes in evidence-proof.json. Evidence archive SHA256:
204b2ce0c0731c643dd453c95e3c26df4513903acee7f8f4a32e00e3998ab75d.

Candidate library SHA256:
73c10e5dc62eb97607e9ded9a1df8bb6702d87375620bd5dc160d8b871f78ce2.
Unchanged control:
cc5539990dcb4effbece7c611787a656df56b51271f1f40e1c3e8b5dbf90c8f8.
Default-OFF library:
092456f43ca1e96409b5d5917e861c9820b5843769a15560c4095ef6c2fee037.

The full three-model 2x vLLM-Metal decode / half-TTFT objective remains active
and unmet. The GPT-OSS and Pi checkouts are untouched.

# Fresh Garnet / vLLM-Metal comparison after private KV writes

The retained native library is compared with actual vLLM-Metal on the same
Apple M4 Mac mini, 16 GiB, macOS 15.6.1. This is an additional matched-FP32
study: native original BF16 storage with FP32 operations versus losslessly
expanded, bit-equivalent F32 learned values with FP32 comparator operations.
It does not establish stock/default BF16 speedups. All original source and
expanded checkpoint hashes and complete learned-value proofs are retained.

Fresh actual loaded-model audits verify 310 text, 290 coder and 473 VL MLX
parameter tensors are F32. Probed activations and runner KV caches are also
F32 for all three models. Configuration settings alone are not used as proof.
Comparator versions remain vLLM 0.30.0+cpu, vLLM-Metal 0.30.0, MLX 0.32.1,
MLX-LM 0.32.0, MLX-VLM 0.6.17, Torch 2.13.0 and Transformers 5.19.0.
The CPU Torch wheel hosts an actual MLX GPU execution path; the version label
is not evidence that these model computations run on the CPU.

## Actual warm results

| Model / batch | Garnet steps/s/row | vLLM steps/s/row | Decode ratio | Garnet TTFT ms | vLLM TTFT ms | TTFT fraction |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Qwen3 text / 1 | 59.78 | 37.81 | 1.581 | 51.88 | 75.07 | 0.691 |
| Qwen3 text / 2 | 58.36 | 25.96 | 2.248 | 91.29 | 97.58 | 0.936 |
| Qwen2.5 coder / 1 | 72.10 | 47.37 | 1.522 | 39.73 | 58.58 | 0.678 |
| Qwen2.5 coder / 2 | 71.61 | 28.64 | 2.500 | 64.65 | 76.36 | 0.847 |
| Qwen3.5 VL / 1 | 48.15 | 26.60 | 1.810 | 220.21 | 266.43 | 0.827 |
| Qwen3.5 VL / 2 | 44.31 | 17.30 | 2.561 | 391.57 | 432.93 | 0.904 |

Batch-2 aggregate output throughput is twice the per-row step rate. All
batch-2 decode ratios exceed 2 in this precision study. All batch-1 ratios
remain below 2, and no first-token fraction is at most 0.5. The full goal
therefore remains active and unmet; these are not default BF16 conclusions.

Each profile executes sequential Garnet / vLLM / vLLM / Garnet process order,
with two fresh persistent processes per runtime, three requests per process,
and four non-first requests per warm mean. All 72 selected requests preserve
complete normalized token IDs, prompt IDs, finished flags and one prediction
per step. The comparator's omitted terminal stop ID is restored only using
its recorded stop reason or verified default EOS. Text/coder retain the same
22/26-token prompts and cap 64. VL retains the same fresh 288x192 RGB/FP32
patch bytes, 54 visual tokens, 79-token prompt and cap 32. Native VL uses
chunk 80 at batch 1 and chunk 32 at batch 2. Every frame is freshly encoded;
comparator encoder identities are unique across rows/requests. Prefix caching
and speculative decoding are disabled and verified in actual engine records.

## Initialization and memory

| Model / batch | Garnet init s | vLLM init s | Garnet peak child RSS GiB | vLLM peak child RSS GiB |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Text / 1 | 2.53 | 18.03 | 2.276 | 3.350 |
| Text / 2 | 1.77 | 16.99 | 2.320 | 3.497 |
| Coder / 1 | 1.39 | 15.98 | 1.927 | 3.579 |
| Coder / 2 | 1.39 | 15.93 | 1.927 | 3.559 |
| VL / 1 | 4.09 | 33.73 | 3.361 | 5.521 |
| VL / 2 | 4.15 | 33.21 | 3.397 | 5.391 |

Initialization and first-use requests are saved separately from warm timing.
Filesystem/driver caches were not flushed, so fresh processes are not proof
of cold hardware. RSS is RUSAGE_CHILDREN's high-water individual child value,
not aggregate worker RSS or unique GPU memory. Peak RSS includes startup;
these figures are not pure inference allocations. Native and comparator
weight storage widths differ despite exact learned-value equivalence.

## Remaining budgets and execution guards

remaining-budgets.json derives each unmet deadline from its actual comparator
measurements and retains native phase counters. For text batch 1, the decode
target is 75.62 steps/s and TTFT target 37.53 ms. Native prefill GPU time is
37.35 ms before the other work, while CPU encoding is 5.20 ms. Decode GPU
time is 15.53 ms, with CPU preparation/encoding about 0.61 ms combined.
GPU execution remains material; removing CPU work alone would not satisfy
the requested decode target. Wait time overlaps GPU time and is not additive.

Before/after guards and 0.5-second monitors reject other inference runtimes.
Only the process group created for the current worker is exempt; unrelated
native and Python comparator processes remain visible. Four ownership tests
verify this filtering, including rejection of multiple owned native workers.
The selected runtimes never run together. One coder batch-1 attempt was
interrupted by an unknown external xlang3 process and excluded; its failure
and partial records remain. A five-second clear guard interval precedes the
retry. No external job was stopped. Sampling cannot prove the absence of
arbitrarily brief external jobs between polls.

completed/ retains exact commands/exits, monitors, guards, runtime versions,
actual dtype reports, full request records, checkpoint equivalence proofs and
warm/first-use measurements. source/ retains executed runner/worker/auditor
versions. Raw image tensors remain on the Mac with sizes/hashes in
evidence-proof.json. The native library remains
73c10e5dc62eb97607e9ded9a1df8bb6702d87375620bd5dc160d8b871f78ce2.
Transferred archive SHA256:
a36ada17e1ccd2511a84b63ab3020815e936e3fcfcf616064e0a3c33fa515c1c.

Neither the primary GPT-OSS checkout nor the Pi checkout was modified.

reports.report_text:
# Selected attention policy versus vLLM-Metal

The full goal remains unmet. A fresh sequential comparison completed three
actual GPU dtype audits, all six profiles, and 72 complete matching outputs.
All batch-2 profiles exceed 2x decode in this run; no batch-1 profile does.
No warm first-token latency reaches half of vLLM-Metal's latency.

## Warm measurements

Means of four warm requests per runtime/profile, drawn from two fresh workers.
Each worker's first request is excluded. TPS below is per row; aggregate TPS
at batch 2 is twice the displayed value because the identical rows finish
together. The first prediction is excluded from decode TPS; terminal
predictions count. TTFT includes the measured request preparation and prefill.

| Model | Batch | Garnet TPS | vLLM TPS | Decode ratio | Garnet TTFT ms | vLLM TTFT ms | TTFT fraction |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Qwen3-0.6B | 1 | 59.89 | 37.02 | 1.618 | 51.27 | 83.50 | 0.614 |
| Qwen3-0.6B | 2 | 58.62 | 28.25 | 2.075 | 86.19 | 89.81 | 0.960 |
| Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct | 1 | 72.07 | 47.19 | 1.527 | 36.83 | 58.01 | 0.635 |
| Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct | 2 | 70.70 | 28.60 | 2.472 | 56.60 | 80.16 | 0.706 |
| Qwen3.5-0.8B VL | 1 | 47.73 | 26.16 | 1.824 | 210.79 | 265.35 | 0.794 |
| Qwen3.5-0.8B VL | 2 | 44.26 | 17.34 | 2.552 | 390.23 | 438.08 | 0.891 |

Batch-1 decode still needs another 23.6% text, 30.9% coder, and 9.6% VL
speedup relative to these measurements. TTFT needs another 18.6–47.9%
reduction across the six profiles. Exact targets, aggregate TPS and separate
setup observations are in [remaining-budgets.json](remaining-budgets.json).
These measurements do not justify a completion claim or a favorable-number
repeat without a new change or an unresolved measurement concern.

The [native phase summary](native-phases.json) points to additional work
outside the measured prefill session: text B2 TTFT is 86.19 ms while the
session is 62.62 ms; text B1 is 51.27 versus 43.83 ms. This difference includes
reset, embedding assembly and wrapper work and does not attribute a cause.
Source inspection finds that resident reset creates a temporary zero-filled
CPU vector for each state and copies it into the existing shared buffer.
A bounded direct-buffer zeroing experiment is warranted; its benefit remains
unmeasured. Decode is mainly GPU work in these observations, so this experiment
cannot establish the missing decode gains. GPU and wait times overlap and
must not be added.

## Initialization and first use

These are separate measured intervals, averaged over two fresh workers.
First-request TTFT starts after initialization. OS/driver caches were not
flushed; this is not a hardware-cold end-to-end latency measurement. The
intervals are not added and presented as an observed cold TTFT.

| Model | Batch | Garnet init s | vLLM init s | Garnet first-request TTFT ms | vLLM first-request TTFT ms |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Text | 1 | 1.690 | 17.212 | 158.22 | 68.19 |
| Text | 2 | 1.884 | 16.377 | 180.19 | 107.51 |
| Coder | 1 | 1.383 | 15.964 | 119.96 | 60.46 |
| Coder | 2 | 1.391 | 16.004 | 146.03 | 96.45 |
| VL | 1 | 4.069 | 33.515 | 357.81 | 302.29 |
| VL | 2 | 4.795 | 33.150 | 571.70 | 506.80 |

Garnet initializes faster, but its first request after setup is slower in
every profile. Warm speed must not obscure this limitation.

## Scope and selected builds

This is an additional matched-FP32 study. Learned values, prompts, image
bytes, capacities, output caps, stopping rules, activations, arithmetic and
KV precision match. Garnet retains compact BF16 weight storage and exact
scaled-half prefill storage; vLLM loads losslessly expanded FP32 weights.
The weight widths and memory traffic differ. This study does not isolate
the contribution of that difference or prove a win over stock BF16 vLLM.

The optional contiguous-attention candidate is selected for text/coder B1/B2
and VL B1 after independent native confirmation. VL B2 uses the retained
control because its native gain was inconclusive. The primary serving
library is unchanged and the experiment remains default OFF.

- Candidate SHA256: `f2c5c448ec4f3c8431be37b48a2634d8fa4cc31de4aa163ec367a319c9263088`.
- Control SHA256: `73c10e5dc62eb97607e9ded9a1df8bb6702d87375620bd5dc160d8b871f78ce2`.
- Native plans: text B1 `[24]`, B2 `[22]`; coder `[26]`; VL B1 `[80]`, B2 `[32,32,16]`.

The fixed source image is `RealWorld-04.png` (WEBP bytes), RGB 1818 x 1372,
prepared at the selected 288 x 192 profile with 216 patches, 54 visual tokens,
79 prompt IDs and a 32-token output cap. Images are freshly encoded per
request. Prefix/encoder reuse and speculation are disabled. Runtimes run
sequentially under a conflict guard and a 2 GiB free-space guard. Small models,
short frozen prompts, one image and equal batch rows limit generalization;
larger models, long contexts, diverse batching and broad task quality remain
unproven.

Hardware: M4 Mac mini, 10 CPU cores (4 performance/6 efficiency), 10 GPU
cores, 16 GB unified memory, macOS 15.6.1 ARM64. Installed comparator versions:
vLLM `0.30.0+cpu` using the verified MLX GPU backend, vLLM-Metal `0.30.0`,
MLX `0.32.1`, mlx-lm `0.32.0`, mlx-vlm `0.6.17`, torch `2.13.0`,
transformers `5.19.0`, NumPy `2.3.5`, Pillow `12.3.0`. Dependencies remain
inside the isolated comparator environment.

## Reproduction and evidence

Remote root: `/Users/zsdx/garnet-metal-investigation`. The completed runner
was `run_selected_attention_vllm.py`, with logs under
`logs/selected-attention-vllm-20261013`. Its archived executed source records
the exact sequential subprocess commands, environment policy and guards.
The selected policy, checkpoint equivalence proofs, actual dtype audits,
source/library hashes, complete outputs, monitors, versions and exit codes
are retained in [evidence](evidence/).

`7dcc7ab02498e1d91ab726a1a1f6997afceadbac5224b3964793c70804c60d68`.

reports.title: Three-half activation prefill: rejected partial experiment
reports.report_text:
# Three-half activation prefill: rejected partial experiment

The isolated M4/16 GiB prototype splits each supported FP32 activation into
three FP16 components with per-row power-of-two scaling. It checks every
reconstructed input bit on the GPU, including signed zero. Each weight row
uses the existing exact BF16-to-scaled-FP16 converter. Three MPS products
produce FP32 intermediate outputs, which are combined and rescaled into FP32.
No approximate input is silently admitted. Wide-exponent inputs deliberately
fail reconstruction and require fallback; all three admission probes verify
this rejection. Metal helper shaders disable fast math for decomposition.

The control is one mixed FP32-input / exact scaled-FP16-weight MPS product
with FP32 output and rescaling, as used for compatible retained prefill
matrices. The candidate's three products reorder arithmetic; bit-exact
representations do not imply bit-exact products. The original output bound
5e-6 + 5e-5*abs(control) is unchanged. Inputs are deterministic synthetic
activations, and weights are actual first-layer checkpoint matrices.
This is not an independent full-model reference or matched vLLM comparison.

Text and coder complete 36 checks each at rows 24/32/64/80, including small
irregular matrices. VL completes eight checks before its QKV matrix reaches
a weight row outside the converter's supported range. The overall job exits
1, and is explicitly preserved as incomplete. No tolerance is widened and
no incompatible value is rounded to force acceptance. All 80 executed checks
pass, with worst tolerance ratio 0.296439417 and exact activation recovery.
The failed matrix is
model.language_model.layers.0.linear_attn.in_proj_qkv.weight.

| Tested MLP matrices | Rows | Control / candidate GPU ratio range |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Text gate/up/down | 24 | 0.341-0.392 |
| Text gate/up/down | 32 | 0.351-0.405 |
| Text gate/up/down | 64 | 0.357-0.424 |
| Text gate/up/down | 80 | 0.394-0.410 |
| Coder gate/up/down | 24 | 0.345-0.390 |
| Coder gate/up/down | 32 | 0.332-0.403 |
| Coder gate/up/down | 64 | 0.361-0.436 |
| Coder gate/up/down | 80 | 0.351-0.429 |

The candidate is about 2.3-3x slower on these MLP matrices. Each profile uses
two ABBA rounds, three warmups and twelve samples per position. GPU/wall
times include decomposition and recombination for the candidate. No other
inference runs simultaneously. There is no reason to integrate this slower
prototype, retry the unsupported VL matrix, or claim a speed improvement.

The serving source and selected library are unchanged. An encoder-reuse
change prepared locally during this investigation was discarded before
upload/build/run after the existing encoder-reuse report was found; that
prior experiment already showed negligible gain. Three local source files
were restored byte-exactly from their verified backups.

completed/ retains the terminal failure, partial records, all three admission
results, individual statuses, asset manifests and numerical/timing logs.
source/ retains the actual runner, shaders, native probe, converter and asset
collector. Raw tensors/binary remain on the Mac; hashes and sizes are in
evidence-proof.json. Transferred archive SHA256:
a5a8890cf6c328940ced2c9b736ebf51c9b7eca28a92c3d35bdf075c5a996586.

No new model performance or comparator result is established. The full
three-model 2x decode / half-TTFT objective remains active and unmet.

reports.title: GPU buffer-fill reset: rejected component variant
reports.report_text:
# GPU buffer-fill reset: rejected component variant

A synchronous Metal blit fill is slower than direct CPU clearing in all six
model/batch reset profiles, both with CPU-warmed buffers and immediately
after GPU writes. Do not integrate this variant into serving. No native
library, model precision or checkpoint changed in this experiment. The full
2x-decode/half-TTFT goal remains unmet.

## Measured reset wall time

State sizes come from the actual three checkpoint configurations at capacity
256 and batches 1/2, including full-attention KV and VL convolution/recurrent
state. Allocations use the same MPS FP32 row-stride calculation and shared
Metal storage as the native context. These are synthetic reset components,
not full model requests; their cache/resource behavior differs from serving.

Each run uses two rounds of policy order legacy/direct/GPU/GPU/direct/legacy,
three warm operations per window and eight measured operations per window.
Reported values are medians of the four window medians for each policy.
GPU reset timing includes command creation, encoding, submission and waiting
for completion. Source compilation, allocations and correctness readbacks
are excluded on all sides. In the GPU-conditioned run, a compute kernel
writes every logical state element and completes before each warm/sample
reset; that conditioning is excluded from reset time, as preceding work.

| Model | Batch | Logical MiB | CPU-warmed direct CPU ms | CPU-warmed GPU fill ms | After GPU writes: direct CPU ms | After GPU writes: GPU fill ms |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Qwen3-0.6B | 1 | 56 | 0.510 | 1.062 | 0.846 | 1.364 |
| Qwen3-0.6B | 2 | 112 | 1.750 | 2.192 | 1.353 | 1.866 |
| Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct | 1 | 6 | 0.081 | 0.656 | 0.053 | 0.329 |
| Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct | 2 | 12 | 0.110 | 0.692 | 0.196 | 0.740 |
| Qwen3.5-0.8B | 1 | 25.6875 | 0.409 | 1.262 | 0.235 | 0.531 |
| Qwen3.5-0.8B | 2 | 51.375 | 0.790 | 0.959 | 0.832 | 1.073 |

The original temporary-vector/copy control is also retained in raw results.
For example, its text B2 component times are 22.094/21.039 ms in these runs.
The padded 1,032-byte profile validates logical-element clearing without
overwriting row padding; it is not a serving performance profile.
GPU fill is about 1.29–6.24x slower than direct CPU clear in the six
GPU-conditioned profiles. The raw summary field `gpu_over_direct_cpu` means
CPU-time/GPU-time speedup; values below one indicate a slower GPU variant.

Both conditions reject the measured synchronous blit design. This does not
reject every possible GPU reset implementation or predict exact full-model
latency. In particular, the isolated direct-clear text B2 time is lower than
the 5.1 ms observed in the actual native confirmation. Buffer/driver/cache
behavior and surrounding work differ; component times must not be substituted
into full-model TTFT or mixed with vLLM throughput measurements.

## Validation and retained failures

Two terminal successful runs perform 126 nonzero-to-positive-zero checks,
verified by CPU bit inspection and a GPU verification kernel, with row padding
preserved. Checks use three different nonzero CPU patterns per policy/profile;
GPU conditioning applies to the timed windows. Seven profiles per run cover
the six model states and the deliberately padded case. There are 168 timing
windows, each with eight measured operations. Conflict guards reject other
inference/probe processes and enforce at least 2 GiB free space.

The first build failed because of a missing closing brace before any GPU
timing. Its exact source, compiler output, command and exit 1 are retained.
The corrected CPU-warmed run and the additional GPU-conditioned run exit 0.
No observation timeout caused a restart; no unrelated job was stopped.

Owned root: `/Users/zsdx/garnet-metal-investigation`. Durable jobs:
`state-zero-gpu-probe-20261013` (PID 30139, failed compile),
`state-zero-gpu-probe-retry1-20261013` (PID 30289, success), and
`state-zero-gpu-probe-conditioned-20261013` (PID 30560, success).
All are terminal. No additional inference dependencies were installed.

Apple's [buffer-fill API documentation](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/metal/mtlblitcommandencoder/fill%28buffer%3Arange%3Avalue%3A%29)
defines the byte-fill operation used by the prototype. Synchronous completion
and the real zero/padding checks are exercised on the M4, not inferred from
the API's availability.

## Reproduction and evidence

The command is `run_state_zero_gpu_probe.py ROOT NEW_OUTPUT_DIR`, with
`--gpu-conditioned` for the second condition. Exact absolute runner/compiler/
GPU commands, metadata/configurations, source hashes and snapshots, profiles,
all checks/window timings, monitors and exits are in [evidence](evidence/).

```text
python test2026/metal/verify_state_zero_gpu.py results/20261013/state-zero-gpu
```

The verifier checks 48 archived file hashes, all three source snapshots,
terminal statuses, actual profile sizes, the conditioning command, all 126
checks and timing calculations. Archive SHA256:
`9a4cc42d3746741869cb27ba227caa6fe660f23516bcc4a2bea910b3513a50d2`.
Primary libraries and GPT-OSS/Pi checkouts remain unchanged. The retained
[direct CPU reset experiment](../direct-state-zero/README.md) still has its
documented latency/decode tradeoff. Prefill and decode optimization remain
necessary; the [latest vLLM comparison](../selected-attention-vllm/README.md)
continues to record the remaining targets across all six profiles.
commands_as_documented: python test2026/metal/verify_state_zero_gpu.py results/20261013/state-zero-gpu

reports.title: MPS exact-half weight layout: no broad serving promotion
reports.report_text:
# MPS exact-half weight layout: no broad serving promotion

This component experiment stores the same exact scaled-half encoded weight
bits in K-by-N layout and uses `transposeRight:NO`, against the retained
N-by-K / `transposeRight:YES` MPS path. FP32 activations, accumulation,
outputs, column scales and rescaling remain. There is no model, precision
or learned-value change. No serving source or selected library was modified.

Two actual sequential M4 / 16 GiB runs pass 432 checks in total. Each run
covers real first-layer matrices for all three checkpoints, irregular
synthetic dimensions, padded output strides and rows 22/24/26/32/44/52/64/80.
All compared finite output values are numerically identical (maximum
absolute difference zero); encoded weights are checked bit-for-bit across
layouts. This is not a claim about signed-zero output bit identity.
The fixed output bound remains 5e-6 + 5e-5*abs(control). No tolerance is widened.
Each timing uses two ABBA rounds, three warm-ups and twelve samples per
position. Timings include MPS multiplication and identical GPU rescaling.

| Model / physical rows | Initial median MLP GPU speedup | Repeat median MLP GPU speedup |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Text / 22 | 1.040 | 0.561 |
| Text / 44 | 1.038 | 1.036 |
| Coder / 26 | 1.047 | 0.756 |
| Coder / 52 | 1.007 | 1.037 |
| VL / 80 | 1.012 | 1.043 |
| VL / 64 | 1.034 | 1.035 |

Text/coder batch-1 gains do not repeat; important matrices regress.
The small VL component signal does not establish a full-model gain and
cannot justify broadly replacing the retained path. The experiment is not
promoted to serving. No model decode rate, TTFT or vLLM speedup is claimed.

Each run explicitly excludes the first-layer VL QKV matrix because the
existing exact-half converter rejects it. Unsupported weights are not
rounded or silently admitted. A subsequent read-only admission audit covers
all 18 VL linear-attention QKV matrices: 17 meet the current integer rules.
In the first matrix, 14 of 6144 rows have extremely small BF16 weights;
14336 values lie in rows rejected by the current scale limit. Their largest
magnitude is 1.17549435e-37 and the ideal row scale reaches 138, beyond the
current +/-64 limit. Clamping that scale does not make the matrix admissible.
This diagnosis suggests testing exact extended-scale reconstruction on GPU;
it is not evidence that such a path works or improves inference.

The initial admission diagnostic incorrectly asserted that every row's
largest value satisfied the existing scale rule. It failed before writing
a report. Corrected reports record rejected rows explicitly. The public
audit reran successfully, saves its own/checkpoint hashes, and reports only
CPU integer eligibility; GPU reconstruction remains untested.

## Actual commands and evidence

```text
python3 run_transpose_half_prefill_probe.py INVESTIGATION_ROOT OUTPUT_DIR
python3 audit_exact_half_qkv_admission.py CHECKPOINT OUTPUT_DIR
```

Both GPU jobs have terminal exit code 0 and ran after the refreshed
comparator suite completed. Exact compiler/runtime commands, generated
asset identities, source hashes, raw ABBA windows, checks, exclusions and
0.5-second process monitors are under `evidence/`. Matrices and binaries are
omitted from Git with sizes/hashes retained. This remains a component study
with deterministic sinusoidal inputs, not model hidden-state validation.
The full three-model 2x decode / half-TTFT goal remains active and unmet.

Archive SHA256:
`9f9c05fab337bffeed43160e7ad4ae7d9dce571e7c2e012fe16d4bbf7aee8324`.
commands_as_documented:
python3 run_transpose_half_prefill_probe.py INVESTIGATION_ROOT OUTPUT_DIR
python3 audit_exact_half_qkv_admission.py CHECKPOINT OUTPUT_DIR

reports.title: FP32 vision softmax/value fusion: default-OFF experiment
reports.report_text:
# FP32 vision softmax/value fusion: default-OFF experiment

The optional `GARNET_METAL_FUSED_VISION_CONTEXT` route retains the selected
batched MPS Q/K scores, then computes softmax and probability × value in one
threadgroup. It avoids a device-memory probability matrix and the following
compute dispatch. The score/softmax arithmetic and serial value accumulation
remain FP32. Checkpoint weights, prompts, image resolution and decoder policy
are unchanged.

This differs from the earlier rejected MPS value-contraction experiment:
it retains the serial contraction and removes the intermediate probability
output instead of packing values into another batched matrix multiplication.
At the serving shape, eliminating 12 graph-owned probability outputs removes
25.63 MiB / 51.26 MiB of logical FP32 elements at B1/B2. Those are calculated
buffer sizes, not measured RSS or unique GPU-memory reductions.

The flag defaults OFF and requires `GARNET_METAL_MPS_VISION_SCORES`. Graph
lowering selects it only for at most 1024 flattened rows, 512 patch tokens,
16 heads and dimension 128; other shapes use the existing two operations.
The serving library remains the preserved resident-KV control.

Two sequential component runs cover 24 shapes each: batch 1/2, patch tokens
4/24/216, heads 2/12 and dimensions 8/64. Four changed-input generations,
including large score magnitudes, are bit-identical to the extracted selected
softmax/value kernels. All independent FP64 checks pass; the largest error
uses 0.023403 of the established `5e-6 + 5e-5*abs(reference)` tolerance.
Output padding is preserved. Synthetic inputs are used in this component test.

| Serving-shaped component | Initial control / fused GPU ms | Initial ratio | Confirmation control / fused GPU ms | Confirmation ratio |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| B1, 216 patches, 12 heads, dimension 64 | 1.2228 / 1.0264 | 1.1914× | 1.2238 / 1.0247 | 1.1944× |
| B2, 216 patches, 12 heads, dimension 64 | 2.2359 / 1.9719 | 1.1339× | 2.7587 / 2.4541 | 1.1241× |

The runs contain 384 ABBA timing records with 20 completed submissions per
record. These GPU command-buffer spans cover the softmax/value component,
excluding Q/K projection and scoring. They are not full-model speedups.
B2 absolute timing varies substantially between runs despite the similar
relative signal. Background guards and 0.5-second process monitors are retained.

The first two harness attempts failed before numerical checks: a missing
Objective-C++ closing brace, then an incomplete extracted struct declaration.
Both terminal failures and their source versions are preserved; corrected
component jobs complete with exit 0.

Commands and evidence are retained under `evidence/logs/`; generated execution
drivers preserve the exact standard checks and native ABBA workload. Source
snapshots and SHA-256 manifests preserve the control and candidate separately.
Initialization, first-use requests, warm requests and individual process RSS
are recorded separately. The first request in each worker is excluded from
warm means. The OS/driver caches are not flushed.

The full-frame workload uses the M4 / 16 GiB Mac mini, Qwen3.5-0.8B,
fresh 288×192 image preparation (216 patches and 54 visual tokens), the
unchanged frozen prompt and a 32-token cap. Batch 1 prefill uses `[80]`;
batch 2 uses `[32,32,16]`. Native workers run one at a time in ABBA order.
The control is the preserved selected library, not a new vLLM run.

All 18 configure/build/handoff stages pass, including native CTest, 48
exact-tail comparisons, all three private-KV suites, trained dense/recurrent
layers, output heads, synthetic vision and all 12 pretrained vision blocks.
Two native ABBA runs produce 48 complete frame outputs, all matching the
control's token IDs, stopping state, prompt IDs and exact image patch hash.

| Full-frame warm TTFT | Initial control → fused | Initial reduction | Confirmation control → fused | Confirmation reduction |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Batch 1 | 219.33 → 213.61 ms | 2.61% | 216.79 → 216.32 ms | 0.22% |
| Batch 2 | 388.28 → 383.47 ms | 1.24% | 389.20 → 383.62 ms | 1.43% |

B1's complete TTFT gain does not repeat. B2 shows a repeated modest gain,
well short of halving TTFT. Confirmation vision time is 59.44 → 58.04 ms
at B1 and 125.21 → 120.58 ms at B2. Other phases also vary; the entire TTFT
change cannot be assigned to the fused kernel alone. No further repeat is
justified solely to seek a more favorable B1 mean.

Confirmation decode throughput is 47.97 → 48.20 steps/s/row at B1 and
44.60 → 44.52 at B2. The decoder has no changed computation; these small
mixed differences do not establish a decode improvement. B2 aggregate
throughput is twice its per-row value for this equal-row workload.

Confirmation worker initialization is 2.966 → 2.953 seconds at B1 and
2.973 → 2.965 at B2. First-use frame TTFT, excluding initialization, is
340.68 → 342.66 ms and 566.42 → 564.19 ms respectively. Individual worker
peak RSS falls by 1.66 / 1.83 MiB in confirmation (7.31 / 7.44 MiB initially).
These small RSS shifts do not demonstrate the calculated logical-buffer
savings as measured unique GPU memory. RSS is from `/usr/bin/time -l`, not
an aggregate process-tree or shared-memory ownership measurement.

Decision: retain the optional route and validation helpers for further
investigation; keep it OFF and leave the primary serving library unchanged.
Its repeated component benefit and B2 frame benefit are bounded by this
fixed workload. This is not a broadly established model speedup.

The archive SHA-256 is
`a76aa5283d55e77287a6bcb636c78ae1bf0fc62fe3d0b0b06cd18fc8e7ad2be0`.
The candidate library SHA-256 is
`418985b013b9e121f23201391a754f3dfa5e548016b53237b098cca4edc91971`;
the preserved primary/control remains
`73c10e5dc62eb97607e9ded9a1df8bb6702d87375620bd5dc160d8b871f78ce2`.
`verify_vision_fused_context_evidence.py` verifies all 505 archived file hashes,
both retained harness failures, 48 shape/192 changed-input comparisons,
384 timing records, all terminal checks, actual compiler definitions,
both library identities and all 48 full-frame outputs/warm means.

The previous selected-frontend frame study measured B1 warm preprocessing
46.67 ms, vision 60.23 ms, prefill wall 108.85 ms and total TTFT 218.93 ms.
Its prefill profile reports roughly 100 ms of GPU time and 5.78 ms encoding
time for one warm request. Fusion therefore targets a limited fraction of
TTFT; prefill GPU work remains a larger optimization target. These numbers
come from the [prior frame study](../frame-frontend/README.md) and are not
measurements of this candidate.

The complete twofold decode / half-TTFT goal remains unmet. This experiment
does not establish a new vLLM-Metal comparison, stock BF16 wins, larger-model
behavior, long-context performance or general concurrent scheduling.

reports.title: Threaded fresh WebP preparation: exact inputs and repeated latency benefit
reports.report_text:
# Threaded fresh WebP preparation: exact inputs and repeated latency benefit

Two CPU scans preserve all model input bytes and reduce fresh preparation by
about 9 ms at both batches. A first matched native/vLLM run preserves 48
complete output sequences; native warm TTFT falls 2.6%/1.8% at batches 1/2.
A clean confirmation preserves another 48 outputs and reduces native TTFT
5.0%/2.1%. Retain the optional path, with the default frontend unchanged.
No decode improvement or full 2x/half-TTFT achievement is claimed.

The optional CPU bridge uses Pillow's own bundled libwebp 1.6.0 with threaded
decoding requested, RGB output and all normal filtering/upsampling options.
It accepts only a conservatively parsed static WebP container with no metadata,
animation or alpha. All other images use the unchanged selected Pillow path.
Every request rereads and decodes the source, resizes with the same Pillow
bicubic operation, normalizes/arranges identical FP32 patches and writes/hashes
fresh patch/RGB files. No image/encoder/prefix reuse or reduced pixels/tokens
is introduced. Threading is CPU preparation, not concurrent model inference.

## Actual CPU results and exactness

| Batch | Initial selected → threaded ms | Repeat selected → threaded ms |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 44.45 → 35.40 | 44.40 → 35.45 |
| 2 | 46.66 → 37.54 | 46.48 → 37.64 |

The single-threaded native RGB alternative saves only about 2.3–2.6 ms, so
threading contributes additional work reduction. Two ABBA CPU scans retain
768 timed records. Each sample includes fresh source read/decode, exact resize,
normalization, patch layout, file writes and hashes. Both threaded and native
single-threaded routes match every pixel of the actual source RGB image and
its canonical patch SHA256. These are preparation times, not model TTFT.

The standalone compatibility suite passes 956 comparisons over 239 fixtures:
RGB/RGBA/L, lossy/lossless WebP, four sizes, orientations 1–8 plus absent EXIF,
animation, PNG/JPEG/BMP fallback and PNG EXIF after IDAT. Sixteen fixtures use
the native route; full decoded RGB also matches there. All resized RGB and
patch bytes match. Alpha/animation/metadata fixtures conservatively fall back.
Control/candidate open independently, so control loading cannot hide lazy
metadata behavior.

The first standalone test failed before image checks: the original bridge
retained Pillow's wheel build-time `/DLC/PIL/.dylibs/libwebp.7.dylib` ID. It
worked in the initial scan because Pillow already loaded the actual library.
The rebuilt bridge explicitly points to the existing bundled library using
`install_name_tool`; only the new experimental bridge is changed, with no
global loader environment or installed-package modification. Both original
source/logs and the fix are retained. The standalone retry and repeated CPU
scan pass. Corrected bridge SHA256:
`3c86ac196227b3729477cd24704ea4cea4e796fe5f9933c7a5a20361a32804a3`.

The [libwebp advanced API](https://developers.google.com/speed/webp/docs/api)
documents the threading option. [Pillow 12.3's decoder source](https://github.com/python-pillow/Pillow/blob/12.3.0/src/_webp.c)
uses default animation-decoder options; actual equality and timings above
are verified on the M4 rather than inferred from API availability.

## Actual matched inference and confirmation

Fresh FP32 GPU audit, same learned values/prompts/image bytes/caps, greedy
stopping, fresh vision encoding, prefix/speculation disabled. Each runtime/
frontend has two fresh workers with three requests each, four warm samples
after excluding first use. Selected and threaded preparation apply equally
to Garnet and vLLM-Metal. Native uses the retained attention candidate at B1
and retained control at B2, identically across frontend policies.

| Batch / frontend | Garnet TTFT ms | vLLM TTFT ms | Garnet TPS/row | vLLM TPS/row | Decode ratio | TTFT fraction |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 selected | 208.20 | 262.46 | 48.25 | 26.30 | 1.834 | 0.793 |
| 1 threaded | 202.75 | 251.15 | 48.29 | 26.48 | 1.824 | 0.807 |
| 2 selected | 385.95 | 442.22 | 44.75 | 17.16 | 2.608 | 0.873 |
| 2 threaded | 378.81 | 433.75 | 44.72 | 17.07 | 2.619 | 0.873 |

Native TTFT improves less than the CPU component saving; execution/protocol
variation also affects the observed endpoint. Decode is essentially unchanged.
The initial relative TTFT fraction does not improve: this helps both runtimes
and does not establish a larger advantage over vLLM. B1 decode remains below 2x,
and neither batch reaches half TTFT. B2 aggregate TPS is twice the per-row rate
for these equal rows; terminal predictions count and the first does not.

The independent confirmation is clean, without a discarded profile:

| Batch / frontend | Garnet TTFT ms | vLLM TTFT ms | Garnet TPS/row | vLLM TPS/row |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 selected | 213.22 | 270.50 | 48.14 | 26.37 |
| 1 threaded | 202.56 | 265.85 | 48.22 | 26.18 |
| 2 selected | 387.58 | 441.85 | 44.52 | 17.09 |
| 2 threaded | 379.34 | 434.07 | 44.74 | 16.92 |

Confirmation native preparation falls 45.46 → 34.68 ms at B1 and
49.14 → 39.25 ms at B2. Native observed TTFT falls 5.00% and 2.13%;
vLLM falls 1.72% and 1.76%. The direction repeats for both runtimes and
batches, but relative-ratio changes are mixed across runs. Do not attribute
an improved model execution rate to the CPU decoder. Native decode changes
remain small (about +0.09/+0.16% at B1 and -0.05/+0.48% at B2 over the
initial/confirmation runs); no decode benefit is established.

Confirmation first-request TTFT after setup also falls: native B1
347.46 → 308.58 ms and B2 570.98 → 544.22 ms; comparator B1
303.75 → 258.37 ms and B2 516.07 → 476.15 ms. These are first requests
after worker/frontend setup, not hardware-cold end-to-end measurements.
Frontend setup is separately recorded (roughly 0.4–0.6 ms selected versus
1.6–1.8 ms threaded in confirmation); initialization and peak child RSS are
also separate. Peak-memory changes are mixed; no memory saving is claimed.
The [separate observations](confirmation/observations.json) retain all eight
run/batch/runtime groups without adding intervals into a synthetic cold TTFT.

Retain the existing optional `WebPDecoder(library).prepare(...)` path and
measured `run_webp_thread_frame_process.py` policy `threaded`. It requires
the correctly linked bridge built against the installed Pillow library.
It has only been validated on this Mac/library version; it is not a general
replacement for all image formats or platforms. The default shared Pillow
frontend and native GPU sources are unchanged.

This remains an additional matched-FP32 study: native compact BF16 weight
storage versus losslessly expanded FP32 comparator storage retains different
weight widths/traffic. It is not a stock BF16 win. The actual audit confirms
FP32 parameters/activations/KV on the GPU. Complete prompt/output IDs, stopping
flags, fresh encoder identities and patch/RGB hashes match across 48 outputs.
One B2 attempt was interrupted by the inference guard (PID 61852 later absent)
and discarded before a clean retry. No unrelated job was stopped or guard
relaxed. Interrupted timings are excluded, with raw logs retained.

Worker initialization, first requests and CPU frontend setup are separately
recorded; frontend setup includes optional bridge loading before requests.
OS/driver caches were not flushed. No sums are presented as an observed
hardware-cold end-to-end latency. Broader images/tasks, longer contexts and
peak-memory savings are not established by these results.

## Evidence and terminal jobs

Owned root: `/Users/zsdx/garnet-metal-investigation`. CPU scans and standalone
checks are terminal. Initial inference PID 57190 is terminal exit 0.
Confirmation PID 66500 was launched behind that successful predecessor and
is now terminal exit 0, with no live handle. No observation timeout caused a
restart. Its runner
is `run_webp_thread_inference.py ROOT NEW_OUTPUT_DIR`; exact commands are logged.

[CPU evidence](cpu/evidence/) verifies 53 file hashes, 768 timing records and
956 compatibility checks. CPU archive SHA256:
`45d50cb76ae3893cf92c1111dd75ed0d261b7af14d702a3a8cea170e601c0803`.
[Initial inference evidence](inference/evidence/) verifies 430 file hashes,
the same CPU proof, one actual dtype audit and 48 matched outputs. Archive:
`ba37c688d7547923d3903803935e1f560542dc4068fd0a022bb6f25bb77b0461`.
[Combined confirmation evidence](confirmation/evidence/) verifies 763 hashes,
both inference runs, two actual FP32 GPU audits and 96 complete matching
outputs, plus the 768 CPU records and 956 compatibility checks. Archive:
`1df7a5c0405d4fd1aaf0cb2438a984c76e73a772905c692037b9e4ac798174a7`.
Raw arrays/bridge binaries are omitted with size/SHA proofs; source, compile/
loader commands, library/model identities, failed attempts, timings, versions,
monitors and exact outputs are retained. Existing helper-template scope labels
still mention copy elision; executed source and frontend policy identify the
threaded experiment.

```text
python test2026/metal/verify_webp_thread.py results/20261013/webp-thread/cpu
python test2026/metal/verify_webp_thread.py results/20261013/webp-thread/inference
python test2026/metal/verify_webp_thread.py results/20261013/webp-thread/confirmation
```

# Constant-address BF16 weights: no useful native decode gain

The component changes only the original shader's weight address-space
qualifier from device-readonly to constant, including its ushort4 casts.
Weights retain the same buffer, BF16 bits and original FP32 math. Both
native small-output and regular decode kernels are tested. The initial
attempt stopped at shader compilation because vector casts still used
device space; its timings are discarded. The corrected and fresh-process
confirmation jobs (PIDs 8012 / 8994) exited 0 after 35.64 / 35.59 seconds.

Both successful runs verify all three checkpoint identities and canonical
BF16 tensor slices, covering 34 fixtures / 68 batch profiles. All 121,652
validated warm/timed executions retain complete output/padding bits with
four freshly uploaded input variants. Each run also has 272 independent
FP64 reference executions, 6,528 timed executions, and a common alternating
250 ms warm stage per profile. Worst FP64 normalized error is
0.0100017036, below 1 under the unchanged prior envelope. Encoding, wall
and GPU clocks are separate; setup/checks/input copies are outside timing.

| Model/batch | Pooled constant/device wall fraction, initial / repeat |
| --- | ---: |
| Text B1 | 0.99247 / 0.98746 |
| Text B2 | 0.98009 / 0.99249 |
| Coder B1 | 0.97987 / 0.99532 |
| Coder B2 | 1.00235 / 1.00810 |
| VL B1 | 0.93113 / 0.98917 |
| VL B2 | 1.02018 / 1.01834 |

These are components, not observed full-model TPS. Large B1 head wall
fractions in four independent ABBA rounds (initial then fresh-process
repeat) are text 0.9960/0.9773/0.9752/0.9965, coder
0.9624/0.8931/0.9586/0.9324 and VL 0.7969/0.9618/0.9439/0.9922.
Magnitude varies substantially, but the B1 head direction repeats. Body
profiles are mostly flat/mixed, and B2 does not justify broad admission.
OS caches were not flushed, GPU frequency is not pinned and the 0.5-second
guard cannot rule out arbitrary shorter external activity.

## Native experiment, not a completed speed claim

`GARNET_METAL_CONSTANT_BF16_HEAD` defaults OFF. Its candidate route keeps
the original shader code and float operations, changing the two weight
pointer qualifiers only. Admission is exactly one row with K/N equal to
896/151936, 1024/151936 or 1024/248320, matching the measured vocabulary
heads. All other cases keep the existing path. The session exposes actual
dispatch counts, reset on clear/reset/begin/abort and published only after
successful submission. Worker logs capture the feature marker and actual
last-session dispatch count after the timed request has completed.

The isolated candidate builds and passes native CTest. All 19 trained-model,
cache, vision and extended-prefill validation stages subsequently passed,
with exit 0 after 1006.73 seconds.
Candidate library SHA-256 is
`df1c1912b2daf40c86925d323747d60db6a4950723ac04562f06854da1c7aaa3`.
Owned validation PID **10827** is terminal, directory
`ROOT/logs/constant-head-checks-20261014`. Historical build/CTest snapshots
are in `native/pending`; the full remote terminal logs remain authoritative.

Owned PID **16406** verified the predecessor's successful terminal state,
then completed three sequential B1 comparisons against retained attention.
All 36 complete outputs match, and candidate dispatch counters equal 1
versus control 0. Its directory is
`ROOT/logs/constant-head-native-20261014`; its exit code is 0. Both owned
jobs are terminal and must not be restarted. Full raw native evidence is
archived in `native/evidence`; `native/initial-summary.json` captures this
initial result and `native/verification.json` independently audits it.

| Initial native B1 result | Control → candidate TPS | Control → candidate TTFT |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Text | 59.2747 → 58.9827 | 51.9618 → 52.8059 ms |
| Coder | 72.0785 → 71.3736 | 35.5724 → 36.0902 ms |
| VL | 48.0947 → 48.1353 | 209.9577 → 206.6803 ms |

The component head signal does not establish a whole-model decode gain:
text/coder regress slightly and VL decode is essentially flat. Its single
small VL latency reduction is unconfirmed. No favorable-number repeat is
warranted without a new change or a specific unresolved concern. The route
remains optional and default OFF; no runtime promotion is made.
Selected primary/attention binaries remain unchanged (73c10e5d / f2c5c448).
These are initial native comparisons, with no fresh vLLM comparison for
this candidate. The full 2x decode / half-TTFT goal remains unmet.

reports.title: Bounded cache reset: repeated component signal
reports.report_text:
# Bounded cache reset: repeated component signal

Clearing only the previously written KV prefix substantially reduces reset
cost in a synthetic component on the actual M4. This is not yet integrated
into Garnet serving and does not prove a TTFT, decode or vLLM improvement.
Selected libraries and production source remain unchanged.

The current full-request telemetry records text batch-2 reset taking about
20–25 ms. This experiment compares temporary zero-vector allocation/copy
(current baseline), full direct CPU zero, and bounded direct CPU zero. Actual
checkpoint configurations determine all state sizes at capacity 256 and B1/B2.
Each KV head retains its full allocation; only its dirty token prefix is
cleared. All convolution and recurrent state is fully cleared in every policy.
FP32 state storage, MPS row strides and padding remain unchanged.

| Model / batch, 64 dirty tokens | Initial legacy / full-direct / prefix ms | Confirmation legacy / full-direct / prefix ms |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Text / 1 | 4.437 / 0.609 / 0.138 | 4.092 / 0.703 / 0.156 |
| Text / 2 | 19.633 / 1.651 / 0.368 | 19.357 / 1.432 / 0.642 |
| Coder / 1 | 0.309 / 0.052 / 0.049 | 0.310 / 0.052 / 0.050 |
| Coder / 2 | 1.108 / 0.111 / 0.112 | 1.117 / 0.156 / 0.134 |
| VL / 1 | 2.605 / 0.447 / 0.365 | 2.862 / 0.336 / 0.251 |
| VL / 2 | 8.795 / 0.745 / 0.607 | 8.955 / 0.610 / 0.447 |

These are reset-component wall means after bounded GPU writes, not full-request
estimates. Differences between component and serving cache behavior can be
large: the earlier full direct-zero experiment reduced TTFT but slowed text
batch-2 decode by 1.7–2.4%. Bounded clearing must therefore pass native repeats
before selection; component savings must not be added to old comparison results.
Coder gains over a full direct clear are small or absent.

Both runs cover 25 profiles: all three models × B1/B2 × dirty lengths
0/1/64/256, plus a padded synthetic allocation. Each run validates 300
nonzero-to-positive-zero transitions on CPU and GPU and records 3,600 timed
resets. The prefix-zero case still clears all linear state. Full-capacity
cases exercise fallback-equivalent work. Whole logical buffers, including
unwritten regions, finish at positive zero and padding retains its sentinel.

The first run checked initialization and complete post-clear buffers but did
not separately observe the GPU producer pattern. The confirmation adds that
independent observation before every numerical clear: every dirty element
matches the known finite nonzero pattern and every unwritten element is zero.
Its local audit requires `all_gpu_dirty_patterns_observed: true`. The actual
reset policies and timing scope are unchanged. No tolerance is involved.

Each profile alternates all three policies while warming for at least 250 ms,
then runs two rounds of legacy/direct/prefix/prefix/direct/legacy. Each window
has three warm operations and twelve samples. Fresh bounded GPU writes and
completion precede every reset; their cost and correctness checks are excluded
from reset timing. Initial full initialization is excluded for every policy.
OS caches and GPU frequency are uncontrolled. The independent 0.5-second
guard rejects other inference/probe jobs and only terminates owned processes.

Initial owned PID 42202 exited 0 in 37.92 seconds. Confirmation PID 43002
started after it was terminal and exited 0 in 42.46 seconds. Each archive has
16 files, exact executed sources, compiler commands, monitors and a hash/size
proof for the omitted binary. Local audits independently reconstruct model
state sizes, all profile/check/window/sample coverage and timing means.

Archive SHA-256:

- Initial: `4bf3cb9bf30bde60a8267d1d5da71682bad35befab78c1aed9c913e1ff0ca223`
- Confirmation: `076071956340e461e6657a41f1b8062003f2b84a51477190fb0d630d59ab2850`

```text
python3 launch_dirty_prefix_reset_probe.py ROOT ROOT/logs/dirty-prefix-reset-probe-20261014
python3 launch_dirty_prefix_reset_probe.py ROOT ROOT/logs/dirty-prefix-reset-confirm-20261014
python3 archive_dirty_prefix_reset_probe.py ROOT JOB ARCHIVE
python verify_dirty_prefix_reset_probe.py RESULTS VERIFICATION_JSON
```

## Native admission requirements

Any native implementation must default off, preserve original selected builds,
and track the high-water mark of validated active KV writes independently for
each session. New buffers require full zero initialization. Generic graph
outputs, unknown state writers, unsupported cache layouts, failed commands
and poisoned state require a full reset. Inactive rows must not advance dirty
extent. Gaps and overwrites still require clearing through the highest actual
write, not merely the number of generated tokens. Extent must persist across
chunk profile changes and swaps of private cache storage. Linear state remains
fully reset. Full-cache snapshots after reset must match the original reset
bit for bit, with no reuse of prior request contents.

Validation must cover all original nineteen numerical stages, multiple
request lengths, sparse/overwritten/inactive slots, two interleaved private
sessions, failed-run recovery and full-capacity boundaries before six-profile
native ABBA timing. A repeated serving gain and fresh matched vLLM comparison
are required before any selection change. The full 2x/half-latency goal is unmet.

## Optional native implementation

`GARNET_METAL_DIRTY_PREFIX_RESET` defaults OFF and is mutually exclusive with
the earlier full direct-reset experiment. The new isolated build keeps global
half alpha enabled and all other experimental paths disabled. The three
selected libraries retain their original hashes.

Only graph outputs proved to have a single KVUpdate/KVChunk writer, the
original cache input, explicit unchanged slot/active controls and a supported
four-dimensional cache layout admit the bounded reset. Admission is computed
once per compiled graph. A session tracks the highest validated active slot
plus one across decode/chunk calls and private storage swaps. It does not
infer extent from token count or clear another session's buffers. Generic
writers invalidate the proof; poisoned requests force full reset recovery.
Every new state buffer is fully initialized. Convolution/recurrent and
unsupported state retain the original full vector-copy reset. Padding is
preserved and host clearing requires completed, initialized buffers with a
closed command batch.

Workers now record actual cleared-byte counts, bounded-state counts and full
fallback counts inside the unchanged TTFT scope. Warm profile admission
checks these against the preceding complete request, prompt length, actual
decode steps and archived model configuration. First-request counters are
checked separately, without calling initialization hardware-cold latency.

Installation verified eleven original source hashes against `4053c7d4`, saved
their exact bytes and installed twelve pinned candidate files. The candidate
library SHA-256 is
`e389fc080249301b506b84ff09b242df7d6cd63128091e1ab677b4025710491c`.
The actual M4 configure/build and both CTests pass. The new unit performs 216
whole-buffer positive-zero checks after GPU writes/consumption across rows
1/2/3, groups 1/3, capacities 1/17/256, widths 1/3/128 and dirty extents
0/1/half/full. Invalid bounds, uninitialized buffers, open commands and abort
recovery are also checked. The original numerical CTest remains intact.

Owned validation PID **44364** exited 0 in 1205.88 seconds after all nineteen
original stages. Dependent PID **45551** passed six B1/B2 real-layer recovery
gates (partial clearing, unknown writer, nonfinite-head poisoning, full recovery
and session isolation), then exited 1 in 1172.16 seconds including its wait.
The first performance profile failed the actual bounded-state count assertion.
All six completed control/candidate outputs matched, but both warm candidate
requests cleared the full 58,720,256-byte text cache and recorded zero bounded
states. These incomplete timing windows are rejected, with no speed claim.

The failure archive SHA-256 is
`a55880de3c40e979ad396f0d564ab8e200edb3d37a65ee7a1204146aba16ec9f`.
`native/failure-verification.json` verifies all 461 archived files, original
nineteen stages, six recovery checks, six completed matching outputs, actual
fallback byte counts, exact source and preserved terminal failure. Evidence is
under `native/failed`; the original first candidate binary remains intact.

`native/pending` is a historical bounded snapshot of actual owned handles,
source hashes, library identities, successful configure/build/CTest stages and
the real unit output. It is not evidence that the remaining full-model/session
gates or serving measurements are complete. Preserve current source/binaries
until their terminal records and exact executed-source archives are collected.
No native TTFT/TPS gain or new vLLM comparison is claimed yet.

## Completed cache-copy admission repair

Prefill returns its cache through a fresh `Layout` reshape copy. The first
admission check expected the final writer itself to be KVUpdate/KVChunk and
conservatively invalidated tracking. The repair traces a sole resident writer
through complete row-preserving Layout copies, with unchanged rows/columns,
zero layout operation, no auxiliary output and cycle detection. It must still
end at the validated KV writer with the original cache/slot/active inputs and
matching head/capacity/dimension metadata. Add, mask, reorder, partial copy and
unknown producers remain ineligible. The numerical kernels are unchanged.

All twelve prior source hashes were pinned against `32b90ea8` and saved before
installation. A separate repaired build preserves the original candidate and
all selected binaries. Repaired library SHA-256:
`b5614830b706e3ae8bf8ca3333f492b7b79e47e1bca289041267d0fb706efaee`.
Configure/build and both CTests pass. Six new actual trained chunk-prefill
checks also pass, covering all three models and B1/B2. Sparse active slots
0/3 clear only extent 4 at capacity 8; an inactive slot 7 must not enlarge it.
Repeated full-cache snapshots verify all zero and preserve another session.
These tests specifically detect the first implementation's fallback bug.

Owned repair validation PID **66790** exited 0 in 1224.31 seconds after all
22 stages: the original nineteen gates plus three model-specific copy stages.
Dependent PID **68433** exited 0 in 1299.91 seconds including its validation
wait, passing six recovery gates and all six native ABBA profiles (72 complete
requests). Fresh confirmation PID **91803** exited 0 in 151.33 seconds after
six more recovery gates and another 72 complete requests. The second run
starts after the first is terminal. Actual cleared-byte/state/fallback counts
match archived checkpoint configuration, prompt length and preceding decode
steps for every request, including separate first-request accounting.

| Model / batch | Initial TTFT control → candidate ms | Repeat TTFT control → candidate ms | Decode candidate/control initial / repeat |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Text / 1 | 50.979 → 44.536 | 48.678 → 43.907 | 1.0081 / 0.9846 |
| Text / 2 | 82.604 → 66.170 | 80.444 → 66.484 | 0.9778 / 0.9831 |
| Coder / 1 | 31.620 → 32.397 | 32.617 → 32.161 | 1.0053 / 0.9934 |
| Coder / 2 | 52.059 → 50.959 | 51.434 → 49.430 | 1.0021 / 0.9985 |
| VL / 1 | 196.462 → 192.869 | 195.229 → 194.557 | 0.9949 / 0.9942 |
| VL / 2 | 359.408 → 355.739 | 360.893 → 357.563 | 0.9955 / 1.0055 |

Text TTFT reductions repeat at 12.6% / 9.8% for B1 and 19.9% / 17.4% for
B2. Text B2 decode decreases 2.2% / 1.7%; B1 throughput direction changes.
Coder B2 TTFT improves 2.1% / 3.9% with essentially flat decode. Coder B1
latency direction changes. VL warm gains are small, with no repeatable decode
improvement. This remains an optional latency/throughput tradeoff; it is not
selected as a uniform policy for the objective that requires both metrics.
No favorable-sample rerun or new vLLM speed claim follows these results.

Repeat text reset falls from 5.611 to 1.226 ms at B1 and 20.144 to 2.277 ms
at B2. Actual candidate clearing is 6,651,904 / 13,303,808 bytes; the control
library is not instrumented, so its recorded zero counters are unavailable
instrumentation, not an absence of reset. Phase reports use null for them.
Reset savings do not exactly equal full TTFT savings. The cause of the decode
tradeoff is not independently established. GPU/wait intervals overlap.

First request after initialization on repeat is 154.500 → 149.482 ms for
text B1 and 188.011 → 166.792 ms for text B2. Initialization is separately
reported and essentially unchanged. OS/driver caches were not flushed; these
are not hardware-cold end-to-end measurements. Other first-use phases and

reports.title: Global lossless half scale through MPS alpha: trained components pass, native validation running
reports.report_text:
# Global lossless half scale through MPS alpha: trained components pass, native validation running

Native exact-half prefill currently chooses each output row's lossless scale,
runs mixed-storage MPS multiplication, then launches a separate rescale kernel.
This investigation asks whether one exact common matrix scale can place the
inverse power of two in MPS's alpha coefficient, avoiding the temporary and
rescale dispatch. Learned values and FP32 activations/output remain the same.
The optional native experiment described below now implements this route.

A CPU-only audit of 22 sampled layer-zero body matrices finds 20 with a common
exact scale: text 7/7, coder 7/7 and VL 6/8. Every accepted encoded value restores
the original BF16-expanded FP32 bits exactly. VL in_proj_qkv and in_proj_z have
unrepresentable values under the common scale and must retain fallback paths.
This is eligibility evidence, not GPU model compatibility or performance.

Owned toy gate PID 5180 exited 0 after 3.67 seconds on Apple M4. Real execution
uses FP32 inputs, exact scaled FP16 weights and FP32 output with alpha 2^-16,
without a separate rescale. Shapes (M/K/N) 3/7/5 and 16/1024/64 pass independent
FP64 checks under 5e-6 + 5e-5*abs(reference); maximum absolute errors are
4.38558e-9 and 2.45605e-7. The weights round-trip bit for bit. No trained GPU
projection, native full-model inference or speed claim is established yet.

## Trained projection evidence

Initial projection PID **6347** and fresh-process confirmation **9473** exited
0 after 152.88 / 148.48 seconds. Each covers 20 admitted trained body matrices
at 13 row counts: 8/16/22/24/26/32/44/48/52/64/80/128/160. Two VL matrices are
excluded for inexact common-scale storage. Every accepted weight restores the
original learned bits. All output elements and padding are checked with four
fresh power-of-two input variants, alternating warming of at least 250 ms and
two ABBA rounds per profile. Full independent FP64 projections verify both
routes under the unchanged 5e-6 + 5e-5*abs(reference) envelope.

All **212,350** validated executions across both successful runs have zero
numerical difference from the row-scaled control. This is numerical equality,
not a signed-zero bit identity claim. Each run contains 260 checked profiles /
2,080 timing windows. Worst normalized candidate FP64 error is 0.514653261,
below 1. Setup, uploads and validation are outside the recorded clocks.

| Model | Mean per-profile GPU fraction, initial / repeat | Wall fraction, initial / repeat |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Text | 0.8189 / 0.8142 | 0.9357 / 0.9298 |
| Coder | 0.8044 / 0.8177 | 0.9428 / 0.9544 |
| VL | 0.8380 / 0.8617 | 0.9406 / 0.9527 |

Encoding duration increases roughly 8%; GPU and wall durations decrease.
These are component clocks, not whole-model TPS or TTFT. Full precision data
and excluded cases are in `projections/summary.json` and
`projections/confirmation.json`. OS caches/GPU frequency are uncontrolled, and
0.5-second guarding cannot exclude arbitrary shorter external activity.

## Optional native experiment

`GARNET_METAL_GLOBAL_HALF_ALPHA` defaults OFF and requires exact-half prefill.
Only modest body matrices with entirely exact common-scale encoding use it.
The existing raw BF16 decode buffer stays intact. Inexact common-scale matrices
retain the prior per-row representation or existing FP32 fallback. The route
uses the existing half buffer and writes directly to the FP32 output, avoiding
the explicit rescale encoder and intermediate result matrix. Internal MPS
dispatch counts are not claimed. The MPS cache key includes the common scale
as well as shape, preventing reuse of a product with an incorrect alpha.

Counters reset on Begin/Abort/session reset/clear/run and publish after a
successful GPU submission. Adapters record aggregate actual prefill dispatches
only when the backend marker is present. Benchmark comparisons require positive
actual candidate counts and zero in the control. Other experimental norm/head/
joined/reset flags remain OFF in this candidate.

The twelve prior source hashes matched before installation; exact originals
are preserved at `ROOT/logs/global-half-alpha-original-source-20261014`.
The isolated candidate builds and passes native CTest, including differently
scaled same-shape cache entries, independent FP64 checks, counter resets and
common-scale rejection with lossless row-scale fallback. Library SHA-256 is
`887b70f521d5af7f948bcb32a2cf94842377e2ecb828bc9280ffb38af6fe058f`.

Validation PID **12334** completed successfully in 1203.47 seconds. All 19
model/cache/vision/prefill stages passed, including all eight complete dense-tail
fixtures per dense model with their original random sequence and coverage.
Dependent benchmark PID **15843** completed all six sequential native profiles.
The local verifier checked 641 archived files, all 72 complete output requests,
actual positive global-alpha counters versus zero control counters, source and
library identities, contention monitors, fresh image preprocessing and independently
recomputed warm means. Historical pending snapshots remain in `native/pending`.

reports.report_text:
# Recorded real BF16 projections: no broad speed benefit

This component probe uses the current Garnet `bf16_decode` and
`bf16_decode_small` shader source, preserving the selected small-output
policy (N <= 256), original compact BF16 learned values and FP32 math.
It compares the normal native pipeline/direct encoding against a recorded
one-command indirect buffer. A second direct control enables indirect
support on the pipeline, isolating the support flag from replay.

Actual execution on the Apple M4 / 16 GiB, macOS 15.6.1 (24G90), exited
0. Source snapshots, extracted shader, compiler version, binary identity,
guarded process monitoring, commands and terminal states are archived.
The owning durable PID 98061 completed in 22.82 seconds; no probe remains
running. The selected native serving libraries are unchanged.

Coverage is 34 matrix fixtures across 68 batch profiles (rows 1/2):
25 trained first-layer/body/head matrices and nine synthetic tail
fixtures, with the three tail shapes repeated for each model. The three
Qwen checkpoint hashes, fixture hashes, BF16 dtypes, shapes and actual
checkpoint tensor slices were verified before execution. An earlier
progress update called these 68 matrices; 68 is the batch-profile count.

Four fresh input variants (original, negated, half and double) are
independently prepared. All 16,320 subsequent GPU executions, including
warmups, match the current native reference bit for bit, with unchanged
output padding. The 272 reference executions retain the prior independent
FP64 gamma(ceil(K/32)+32)*sumabs+1e-7 envelope; the worst normalized error
is 0.0100017036, below 1. This tests actual updated input reads, rather
than reusing previous prediction results.

Two ABBA rounds per control/profile retain 1,088 windows with twelve raw
encoding/wall/GPU samples each, totaling 13,056 timed executions. Input
updates and output checks are outside the timing interval for every
policy. Recording/setup time is separate. GPU, encoding and wall clocks
overlap and are not added. Each sample uses a fresh command buffer and
waits for completion; competing inference runtimes never run together.

| Comparison: indirect / direct, ratio of pooled means | Encoding | Wall | GPU |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Normal native pipeline | 1.14106 | 0.99634 | 0.97472 |
| Direct pipeline with indirect support | 1.15862 | 1.02070 | 1.00451 |

Median per-profile wall ratios are 1.03197 and 1.03591 respectively.
The small pooled GPU difference does not establish a broad wall-time gain;
CPU resource declarations cost more than this single-dispatch replay
saves. These are projection components, not full-model TPS or TTFT,
and cache behavior differs from traversing all model layers. No fresh
vLLM run or stock-BF16 advantage is claimed.

The gate does not justify replacing every individual projection with an
indirect buffer. A separately validated multi-operation MLP sequence may
amortize encoding differently; this report provides no evidence about
that untested sequence. The full 2x decode / half-TTFT target remains unmet.

identities, four terminal stages, fixture coverage, exact/padding and
FP64 gates, monitored samples, all sample counts and recomputed means.
The initial summarizer expected twice the actual fixture count; that
postprocessing assertion was corrected to the authoritative manifests,
without changing or rerunning the measurements. The successful derived
report is `summary.json`. Raw measurements retain their byte identities.

# Recorded compute commands: lower CPU encoding, no broad wall-time gain

This new component probe records a dependent FP32 addition chain into a
Metal indirect command buffer once, then executes it with fresh input
values on every request. Commands retain buffer bindings and parameter
buffers, declare resource usage and use an explicit barrier after each
dispatch. The same shader, buffers and arithmetic serve three controls:
separate direct encoders, one direct encoder with buffer barriers, and
recorded indirect commands. There is no output, prefix or encoder-result
reuse. This is a synthetic command-encoding gate, not Qwen inference.

Actual execution on the M4/macOS 15.6.1 passed. The shader compiles with
fast math disabled and actual indirect-pipeline support enabled. Nine
profiles cover 896/1024/2048 elements and 16/64/256 dependent dispatches.
Two rounds use direct/indirect ABBA and single/indirect ABBA windows,
three untimed warmups and twelve timed samples per window. All 2,160
complete outputs match the CPU dyadic reference bit for bit, including
warmups and changing inputs; 1,728 timing records remain. Compilation
and the guarded child exited 0. Owned durable PID 96760 completed after
4.16 seconds; no probe from this job remains running.

Across all component profiles/rounds, the ratio of pooled means is
0.21746 for CPU encoding time, 1.08386 for wall time and 1.53763 for GPU
time (indirect/direct). Encoding improves about 78%, but mean wall time
is about 8% worse. Individual wall-time ratios are mixed; 64/256-dispatch
chains are mostly slower. The repeated 1024-element/16-dispatch case
improves 5.4%, while many other repeats regress. The one-encoder control
is generally faster than indirect execution as well. Encoding, GPU and
wall clocks are separate, overlapping observations and are not added.
Recording/setup time is separate in the raw log.

This gate does not justify broad native integration. The addition chain
does not prove behavior or performance of real BF16 matvec, MPS prefill,
attention, KV writes or mixed MPS/custom-kernel graphs. A future realistic
kernel experiment would need actual numerical and wall-time evidence;
the CPU encoding reduction alone is insufficient. Selected Garnet
libraries are unchanged, and no fresh vLLM comparison is claimed.
The full 2x decode / half-TTFT goal remains unmet.

The source uses the actual installed SDK declarations for
`MTLIndirectComputeCommand`, `setBarrier`, `setKernelBuffer`,
`concurrentDispatchThreads`, `executeCommandsInBuffer` and pipeline
`supportIndirectCommandBuffers`. Apple documents [indirect compute
commands](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/metal/mtlindirectcomputecommand)
and [barriers](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/metal/mtlindirectcomputecommand/setbarrier()).
Actual pipeline creation and execution, rather than SDK declarations
alone, establish compatibility on this Mac.

# Recorded four-kernel MLP: clean numerics, unstable wall-time gains

This probe records the original gate projection, up projection, SiLU
multiply and down projection into one GPU indirect-command plan. The
learned BF16 weights, FP32 math, original shaders and dispatch widths
remain. One plan orders all four kernels; another permits independent
gate/up overlap and explicitly waits for both before SiLU, then waits
for SiLU before down. Barrier flags are set before command encoding,
following Apple's documented before-command ordering. A direct control
with indirect pipeline support separates that flag from replay.

Actual initial and fresh-process confirmation jobs (PIDs 99355 / 99806)
completed with exit 0 in 8.41 / 8.40 seconds. Both cover all three frozen
Qwen checkpoints and batch 1/2, using the first trained MLP layer.
Checkpoint hashes, BF16 tensor shapes, fixture hashes and exact canonical
tensor slices were verified. Inputs are freshly uploaded in four variants
(original, negated, half and double). Both runs retain all four intermediate
buffers, complete outputs and padding bit for bit in 4,320 total validated
executions. Independent FP64 projections and a double-precision SiLU
reference keep the existing bounds; worst normalized errors are
0.00324921315 / 0.00217654517 respectively. No tolerance is widened.

Each run has 24 separately checked reference executions and 1,728 timed
executions in 144 ABBA windows. Two rounds and two windows per policy
provide 48 timed samples per model/batch/comparison. CPU input updates and
output checks are outside the measured encoding/wall/GPU clocks for both
policies. Recording/setup is separate; overlapping clocks are not added.
