# One joined product for lossless input components: rejected

The M4 component preserves every supported FP32 input bit through three
scaled FP16 components, joins them as 3×B rows and encodes one MPS matrix
product. FP32 partial results are recombined and rescaled. All eligible
numerical checks pass, but the candidate is slower across all six unweighted
large-matrix pools. It is rejected for serving integration; no full inference
or vLLM gain is claimed. No serving source or selected library changes.

The earlier three-product prefill method was substantially slower. This new
trial tests B1/B2 decode with one joined product against the exact original
native BF16 shader, including its selected small-output policy. The control
uses its original default compiler options; decomposition/recombination
disable fast math. Learned BF16 values restore bitwise from scaled-half
storage, and GPU reconstruction checks every FP32 input bit, including signed
zero. Arithmetic order changes. FP32 result buffers alone are not proof of
an internal accumulation implementation; independent FP64 and unchanged
control bounds gate all outputs. No approximation or wider tolerance is used.

The successful run validates 64 matrix/batch profiles from the three frozen
checkpoints, including trained first-layer products, complete eligible heads
and irregular synthetic cases. It performs **51,750 validated executions**
and **6,144 timed executions**. Four fresh power-of-two input variants and
output padding are checked. Worst candidate FP64 normalized error is
0.0075366 under the original `gamma(ceil(K/32)+32)*sumabs+1e-7` envelope.
Worst control-comparison ratio is 0.0686387 under `5e-6+5e-5*abs(control)`.
Wide-exponent input rejection passes separately for every model.

| Unweighted trained large-matrix pool | Batch | Candidate/control GPU fraction | Wall fraction |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Text | 1 | 1.1685 | 1.1316 |
| Text | 2 | 1.2031 | 1.1466 |
| Coder | 1 | 1.1032 | 1.0975 |
| Coder | 2 | 1.1650 | 1.1473 |
| VL | 1 | 1.1075 | 1.1189 |
| VL | 2 | 1.1038 | 1.0896 |

Fractions above one are slower. Pools sum measured times once per collected
trained matrix with N>256; they are not full-model layer-weighted estimates
or tokens/sec. A small coder up-projection GPU signal has essentially flat
wall time and does not justify a favorable-number repeat. No DRAM traffic or
internal MPS kernel count is inferred merely from using one API operation.

Two weight matrices fail exact-half admission: Qwen3's vocabulary embedding
head (`matrix-0`) and Qwen3.5 layer-0 QKV (`matrix-3`). They are explicitly
excluded and would require the original native fallback. No row is rounded,
clamped or silently forced into the candidate. Every eligible result is
checked, with all weights/matrix identities pinned to the original checkpoint.
These are deterministic synthetic activations, not model hidden-state evidence.

Every eligible profile alternates common warming for at least 250 ms, then
two ABBA rounds with three warm operations and twelve measured samples per
window. Timers include GPU decomposition, MPS product and recombination, plus
separate host encoding/wall intervals. Setup, uploads and numerical readbacks
are excluded equally. Native reset initial/confirmation jobs were both
terminal before this trial; guards reject other inference/probe jobs every
0.5 seconds and only stop owned processes. Caches/frequency are uncontrolled.

unsafe-input fixture used index 101, absent from the first eligible short
matrix. The repaired rejection-only branch injects 2^-60 at index 1. Timed
inputs, numeric kernels and tolerances remain unchanged; the independent audit
verifies the one-line source difference. Repaired PID 95450 exits 0 in
46.69 seconds, including all three rejection gates and all eligible profiles.
Both terminal runs, exact executed sources, commands, monitors and omitted
binary hashes are archived. No favorable performance sample was selected.

# Optional joined global MLP native trial

The overall 2x decode / half-TTFT goal remains unmet. This optional experiment
passes the full numerical suite and complete-output comparison, but is not
selected: only text B2 shows repeated warm latency improvement, first-use
latency regresses substantially, and there is no established decode gain.

`GARNET_METAL_JOINED_GLOBAL_MLP` defaults OFF and requires global half alpha.
It recognizes adjacent BF16 gate/up products followed by SiLU. Eligible pairs
use one common-alpha MPS product, followed by a split-SiLU encoder writing all
three existing independent gate/up/activation buffers. Public outputs retain
zero offsets, their own strides, readiness and ownership. This differs from
the preceding component probe's shared output views because native custom
kernels currently assume zero buffer offsets. No internal MPS kernel count is
claimed. The same FP32 SiLU expression is retained.

Only the tested text physical rows 24/44, coder rows 26 and VL rows 32 are
considered. Both weights must already have identical exact common scales;
other pairs fall back. The packed half weights replace the individual half
allocations using MPS subviews, while raw BF16 decode buffers and learned
values remain unchanged. Cache owners retain both weights. Begin/Abort and
session clear/reset/run/failure reset the counter; the session publishes it
only after successful submission. Adapters record actual prefill block counts.

The sampled VL layer-0 gate/up scales are 18/19. Although the component can
encode their union exactly, this conservative native version does not reencode
different scales and has **zero actual VL coverage** in both frozen profiles.

# Packed Add/Layout/RMS fusion: small native latency benefit, no promotion

The prior adjacent Add/Norm trial produced no useful native decode gain and
did not cover prefill's intervening reshape. This method combines prefill's
three original dispatches while preserving all three outputs: packed residual,
reshaped residual and normalized result. The same rounded FP32 addition,
128-thread RMS reduction, learned values, epsilon and weight offset are used.
Padded packed and normalized strides remain independent. No precision, batch,
model values, output caps, image bytes or cached results change.

Initial component PID 56946 exited 0 after 89.52 seconds. It covers six trained
layer-zero normalization weights across all three models, batch 1/2 and chunks
8/16/22/26/32/64/80. All **29,730** fresh-input executions retain all three
outputs and padding bit for bit, with four input variants and independent FP64
normalization checks. Each profile has two ABBA rounds, 192 timed executions
and at least 250 ms alternating common warm-up. Setup, input copies and checks
are outside the recorded clocks.

Confirmation 58492 was interrupted by an unrelated xlang3 runtime and is
discarded. Quiet-launch retry 59605 failed before inference because its guard
lacked the `output` variable; the corrected retry 59985 was also interrupted
by an unrelated runtime. No unknown actor was excluded or stopped. Their
observations are preserved, but none contribute to speed claims. The quiet
guard and 0.5-second monitoring remain mandatory; shorter external activity
cannot be categorically excluded.

Grouped retry PID **61209** exited 0 after 434.38 seconds. Every group waits for
five quiet seconds and runs one trained norm in a fresh process. Only an
interrupted group is discarded/retried. All 12 clean groups passed: six repeat
groups for the original 84 profiles, plus six groups covering chunks 2/4/24/48.
Chunk 24 is required by the frozen text-B1 workload. The grouped result covers

reports.report_text:
# GPU-private BF16 weights: compatible, no repeated broad speed gain

The probe keeps the original Garnet shaders, BF16 learned values and FP32
inputs/math/outputs, and changes only weight storage from shared to private.
Rounded staging bytes are uploaded by GPU blit and copied back for exact
comparison, including padding. Each successful profile reports actual
storage mode 2. Both batches preserve the existing small-output kernel
selection. Private upload/readback setup is outside projection timing.

The first attempt exited 1 after the trained text matrices: an additional
assertion incorrectly expected every private buffer's CPU pointer to be
null. A read-only allocation diagnostic showed private mode 2 at 1,408,
8,192 and 1,048,576 bytes; the two smaller buffers expose a non-null
pointer on this Mac. No private-pointer data access is used. The corrected
gate checks actual storage mode and exact GPU-copy readback. The failed
attempt's timings are discarded.

The corrected initial run (PID 1966) exited 0 after 37.56 seconds. Both
successful runs cover 34 fixtures / 68 batch profiles: 25 trained matrices
and nine repeated synthetic tail fixtures. Checkpoint hashes, raw fixture
hashes, BF16 dtypes, shapes and actual tensor slices are verified. Original,
negated, half and double inputs are freshly uploaded; output/padding data
is reset and checked on every warm or timed execution. Each profile adds
an alternating 250 ms common warm stage before its two ABBA rounds. This
is deliberately common to both policies, not proven GPU-frequency pinning.

The first confirmation (PID 3993) exited 1 in preflight when the guard saw
unrecognized XLang processes. A queued preflight waiter (PID 4319) was
superseded and terminated only after its exact owned command identity and
`benchmark_started=false` state were verified. No user process was stopped.
The read-only audit identified PIDs 2897 / 2985 as WorldSense CPU HTTP
services with exact supervisor/launcher identity and no inference or GPU
libraries loaded. The only inference keyword in the new supervisor is the
existing forwarded TRT-budget environment name. Imports and call symbols
were reviewed without exposing arguments, constants, credentials or
library paths. Supervisor fingerprint
`2568b1d1cefdf20d5610393c463169a3b4b2a490e2680dc3b0ca73e0ae1a84f7`
is now pinned for that literal exclusion; ancestor/inline identity,
launcher fingerprint and library checks remain. Unknown workers or loaded
inference libraries still reject.

The verified confirmation (PID 5640) waited for a five-second guarded quiet
interval and completed with exit 0 after 44.61 seconds, including preflight.
No investigation probe or waiter from these jobs remains running.

## Actual results

Across the two successful runs, all 122,898 warm/timed validation executions
match the current native outputs bit for bit. Each run includes 272 separate
FP64-envelope reference executions and 6,528 timed executions. Maximum
normalized FP64 error is 0.0100017036, within the unchanged prior bound.
Two rounds and two windows per policy give 48 timed samples per matrix/batch
and policy. Failed/preflight attempts contribute no averages.

| Model / batch | Private/shared pooled wall fraction, initial / confirmation |
| --- | ---: |
| Text B1 | 1.02688 / 0.99111 |
| Text B2 | 1.00647 / 0.99628 |
| Coder B1 | 0.94592 / 1.07914 |
| Coder B2 | 0.99176 / 0.99788 |
| VL B1 | 0.97138 / 1.01303 |
| VL B2 | 0.98141 / 0.99191 |

Smaller is faster; these are ratios of pooled component means, not whole
model TPS. The apparent initial coder/VL B1 benefit reverses. Small B2
reductions do not establish a useful broad algorithm improvement. Large
head results also vary by round. CPU encoding, wall and GPU clocks remain
separate and overlapping. Hardware frequency is not fixed, OS/driver caches
are not flushed and CPU-service load remains present. The 0.5-second guard
cannot exclude arbitrary shorter external activity.

No runtime integration is admitted. Selected native libraries, learned
values, precision, prompts, limits and protected checkouts are unchanged.
This is an allocation/projection component experiment with no fresh vLLM
comparison or model-output claim. The full 2x decode / half-TTFT goal remains
unmet.

(82 files), including all terminal attempts and the sanitized CPU audit.
Local verification checks file/binary/source/shader hashes, terminal stages,
fixture coverage, private mode and byte readback, common warm duration,

counts and recomputed timings. Raw evidence keeps its recorded byte

# Residual addition plus RMS normalization: no useful native decode gain

This experiment combines two adjacent dispatches while preserving both the
rounded FP32 residual and normalized output. The original 128-thread RMS
reduction, learned weights, epsilon, weight offset and float operations remain
the same. A device/threadgroup barrier makes the rounded residual available to
normalization. There is no reduced precision, cached result or changed batch.

The first setup job (PID 33876) exited 1 before timing because the checkpoint
selector also matched Qwen3.5's MTP tensors. Restricting selection to `model.`
fixed it. The corrected job 33973 and fresh-process confirmation 34552 exited
0 after 32.35 / 32.39 seconds. Each covers six canonical trained layer-zero
normalization weights across three models, with rows 1, 2, 16, 32 and 64.

All **42,588** validated executions across both successful runs match both
original outputs and padding bit for bit, using four freshly uploaded input
variants. Independent FP64 normalization checks have worst normalized error
0.00351983185 under the unchanged 5e-6 + 5e-5*abs(reference) envelope. Each run
has 360 ABBA timing windows and 8,640 timed executions, with a shared alternating
warm loop of at least 250 ms per profile. Input copying and validation are
outside the recorded timing. Sources and raw observations are frozen locally.

GPU duration is lower in every pooled component profile in both runs; the
confirmation reductions range approximately 4–48%. Wall duration is mixed,
including regressions; isolated command submission overhead is substantial.
These are component measurements, not observed whole-model TPS or TTFT.
Full precision means and individual rounds are in `summary.json` and
`confirmation.json`. OS caches and GPU frequency are uncontrolled, and the
0.5-second process guard cannot exclude arbitrary shorter external activity.

## Optional native trial

`GARNET_METAL_RESIDUAL_NORM` defaults OFF. Graph encoding admits only adjacent
Add -> Norm operations with identical activation layouts, and writes both
existing output allocations. Resident execution requires both operations to
be selected. Profiling mode retains separate operations. Inputs must be ready
or produced in the current batch; output/input aliases, output/output aliases,
invalid epsilon, incompatible layouts and foreign batches are rejected.

The current matcher covers decode's adjacent Add -> Norm. Prefill adapters
reshape the packed residual through an explicit Layout operation, giving
Add -> Layout -> Norm; that sequence is not admitted by this candidate.
The component's prefill-sized speed reductions therefore cannot be attributed
to this native prefill path. Supporting and validating all three operations
together is a separate follow-up needed to pursue the remaining TTFT targets.

Actual dispatch counters reset on Begin/Abort and session clear/reset/run;
the session publishes them only after successful GPU submission. Worker logs
record the feature marker and last-session count after the timed request.
Native CTest covers bitwise outputs, downstream consumers, both offsets,
odd/tail widths, four input scales, batches/prefill rows, rejected aliases,
uninitialized inputs, invalid parameters/layouts and counter reset.

The isolated candidate has built and passed CTest. Owned numerical validation
uses library SHA-256
`409246a7ab8e069d048177eb490fdf34cd354c8f4e2cb4b718ceead32c49d2ce`.
Snapshots in `native/pending` are historical observations, not terminal proof.
Owned numerical validation PID **35350**, directory
`ROOT/logs/residual-norm-checks-20261014`, exited 0 after 1007.65 seconds with
all 19 model/vision/cache/prefill stages passed. Dependency PID **36987**,
directory `ROOT/logs/residual-norm-native-20261014`, verified that exact live
validation process, then completed all six sequential ABBA profiles after
validation succeeded. It exited 0 after 1073.79 seconds including waiting.
Both jobs are terminal and must not be restarted.

All **72** complete generated outputs match their frozen references, including
prompt IDs and finished flags. Actual last-session fusion counts are 28 for
text and 24 for coder/VL in both batches, versus zero in the control. Every
image request freshly re-encodes the same image and matches its patch hash.

| Native profile | Control -> candidate row TPS | Control -> candidate warm TTFT |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Text B1 | 58.8862 -> 58.5137 | 52.9490 -> 51.1108 ms |
| Text B2 | 57.4610 -> 57.3060 | 86.6573 -> 87.3352 ms |
| Coder B1 | 71.7284 -> 71.8605 | 35.5821 -> 36.2782 ms |
| Coder B2 | 70.5903 -> 69.7342 | 56.7633 -> 59.6107 ms |
| VL B1 | 47.3199 -> 46.7115 | 215.4341 -> 210.2973 ms |
| VL B2 | 43.8902 -> 43.5855 | 385.1809 -> 385.9222 ms |

Full precision values are authoritative in `native/verification.json`. Decode

establish a useful gain; favorable individual TTFT changes are unconfirmed and
mixed, with no admitted prefill fusion. No unchanged-candidate repeat or runtime

encoding changes are mixed; `native/decode-phases.json` records these separately.
The optional primitive stays default OFF for follow-up investigations.

reports.report_text:
# Optional single-row coder vocabulary kernel

The full 2x decode / half-TTFT goal remains unmet. This native experiment is
default OFF and is not selected: actual coder serving throughput is flat and
first-token latency is slightly worse. It follows the preceding
single-row BF16 component trials: the coder head direction repeats across four
ABBA rounds, while other head/body directions are mixed. Component timing is
not inference throughput.

Latest selected-bundle telemetry records coder B1 decode GPU time 12.6723 ms
and CPU encoding 0.4893 ms per step. GPU and wait overlap and are not added.
The candidate therefore tests a GPU vocabulary projection rather than inferring
a large serving benefit from command-encoding savings.

`GARNET_METAL_SINGLE_CODER_HEAD` creates a second pipeline from the original
`bf16_decode` shader with only `p.rows==2` replaced by compile-time false.
Original first-row float operations, raw BF16 learned bytes, address space,
128 threads and 16 outputs/group stay unchanged. Only rows=1, K=896,
N=151936 select it. Batch two, text/VL and body shapes retain their original
routes. Constant-address head is a separate incompatible option. Joined MLP,
residual/packed norm and reset experiments are disabled in this trial.

Context Begin/Abort and session clear/reset/run/failure reset the new counter.
The session publishes it after successful GPU submission. Dense workers record
actual counts for the prefill prediction and every subsequent decode prediction;
the VL worker checks its final zero count for its different head shape. The
future native comparison requires count=1 only for candidate coder B1, count=0
elsewhere, complete sequence parity and unchanged fresh-image identities.

## Actual build, validation and native performance

Fourteen candidate files were installed only after thirteen prior source hashes
matched branch base `fc653485`; all originals remain preserved. The initial
build failed on a C++ test declaration that grouped `MetalBF16Weight` and
`MetalMatrix` under one `auto`. Initial PID 79789 exits 1 after 26.25 seconds.
No numerical result or benchmark is claimed from that failed attempt.

The repair splits that single declaration. Its fourteen prior source identities
match the failed candidate; no kernel, input, numerical bound or assertion
changes. A fresh directory preserves the failed build. The repaired candidate
`build-single-coder-head-repaired/libgarnet.dylib` SHA-256 is
`ec927190e2830e0e8045fd6f18e74a1d90373d21fc6165355b2fe0a16e8abde0`.

The repaired build and both CTests pass on the actual M4. The new test exercises
the complete 151,936-column output with four fresh input variants, bit parity
with the original batch-two first row, lowest-index argmax, independent FP64
gamma(ceil(K/32)+32)*sumabs+1e-7 bounds, original batch-two/body fallback,
Begin/Abort/readiness and recovery. Seventeen exact synthetic row patterns
permit reuse of independently computed FP64 references while checking every
GPU output; trained checkpoint coverage remains required in the broader suite.

Owned PID **80953** completed the full nineteen-stage original validation at
`ROOT/logs/single-coder-head-repair-checks-20261014`, exiting 0 in 1198.86 seconds.
All eight complete original dense-tail fixtures per dense model, all three
private-KV suites, serving/images, all model layers and heads, vision and
extended prefill passed. Historical partial snapshots remain preserved.

Dependent PID **86463**, directory `ROOT/logs/single-coder-head-native-20261014`,
verified that exact owned validation PID/command before waiting and started
all six sequential native ABBA profiles only after terminal validation exit 0.
It completed successfully in 1043.69 seconds including that dependency wait.

# Vision FP32 products versus exact common half alpha

The component experiment preserves learned values and gives repeated GPU
reductions for vision-block projections. Full native image trials now pass
nineteen numerical stages and 96 complete requests, including a fresh repeat.
Warm TTFT decreases modestly, while decode throughput remains essentially flat.
The optional integration stays disabled in the selected comparison bundle;
there is no fresh vLLM comparison for it and the overall goal remains unmet.

The earlier per-row-scaled half vision trial failed to improve serving latency.
This trial instead compares the current expanded-FP32 MPS product against one
exact common-scale half-storage product with the inverse power of two in MPS
alpha. Both take FP32 inputs and produce FP32 outputs. There is no rescale
encoder or intermediate result matrix. Raw BF16 values restore bitwise from
the encoded half representation; there is no rounding or clipping of weights.
Internal MPS kernel counts are not claimed.

The real M4 trials cover all **50** trained 2D block/merger projection matrices
from the frozen Qwen3.5-0.8B checkpoint: 48 block products and two merger
products. Patch embedding, positional embeddings, norms and biases keep their
existing paths. Matrix slices and the complete checkpoint SHA-256 are checked
before running. Block products use actual physical row counts 216/432;
merger products use 54/108. These correspond to the unchanged batch-1/2
288x192 image grid, 216 patches and 54 visual tokens per image.

All 50 matrices admit an exact common half scale, with no exclusions. Across
both successful runs, **36,890 validated GPU executions** have zero numerical
difference from the FP32 control and satisfy the independent unchanged
`5e-6 + 5e-5*abs(reference)` FP64 envelope. Worst normalized FP64 error is
0.433996587, below 1. Numerical equality is not a signed-zero bit-identity
claim. Every eligible output and padding element is checked. Fresh inputs are
deterministic sine vectors scaled by four exact power-of-two variants; actual
image-dependent activations are covered separately by the native trials below.

Each run contains 100 matrix/row profiles and 9,600 timed executions. Each
profile alternates common warming for at least 250 ms, then two ABBA rounds,
four windows/round and twelve samples/window. Setup, uploads, allocation and
validation are outside the recorded encoding, GPU and wall clocks.

| Product group / rows | Mean per-profile GPU fraction, initial / repeat | Wall fraction, initial / repeat | Encoding fraction, initial / repeat |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Blocks / 216 | 0.9168 / 0.9192 | 0.9759 / 0.9761 | 1.1062 / 1.1084 |
| Blocks / 432 | 0.9398 / 0.9346 | 0.9789 / 0.9775 | 1.1033 / 1.0820 |
| Merger / 54 | 0.9518 / 0.8976 | 1.0133 / 0.9814 | 1.1220 / 1.1455 |
| Merger / 108 | 0.8339 / 1.0012 | 0.9202 / 1.0207 | 1.1061 / 1.0969 |

Fractions are candidate/control; means above average the independently
recomputed per-profile fractions. Block GPU improvements repeat at about
8.1% for B1 and 6.5% for B2, with only 2.2–2.4% component wall reductions.
Encoding costs rise. Merger directions are inconsistent. A native experiment
should therefore initially retain FP32 merger products and test only block
products, with full bounds, fallback and ownership validation. No benefit for
full image-to-first-token latency can be inferred from these component ratios.

## Optional native integration

`GARNET_METAL_VISION_GLOBAL_ALPHA` defaults OFF and requires global half alpha.
Only BF16 2D block QKV, attention output and MLP projection weights are selected.
Norms, biases, patch/position embeddings and both merger products retain their
existing FP32 path. Inexact common scales also fall back to the original FP32
matrix. A separate shared-weight cache key preserves the vision role.

Tagged vision weights use the existing lossless representation but always
take the MPS common-alpha route, including tiny grids with one or two rows.
Vision-only rows up to the existing grid limit are supported, while decoder
weights retain their original 128-row limit. Learned BF16 buffers, precision,
shape/device checks, alias guards and output ownership remain intact. Context
Begin/Abort and graph clear/run reset a separate counter; graph Run publishes
it after successful GPU submission. Image workers report actual per-image
counts, rather than relying on the enabled feature marker.

Installation matched all fifteen original source hashes against branch base
`2394abcb` and preserved their exact bytes before installing sixteen candidate
files. The isolated candidate builds and both CTests pass on the actual M4.
The new test checks rows 1/2/54/108/216/432 against original FP32 MPS and
independent FP64 references with four fresh inputs, unchanged decoder limits,
inexact-scale fallback representation, out-of-profile rows and Begin/Abort/
readiness recovery. Candidate library SHA-256:
`0997e2ba00ce52766b0e8b1fa0b46f44bcff6b081883e9a8c7ba93c2f3635d23`.

Owned validation PID **13040** exited 0 in 1201.13 seconds, passing all nineteen
original full-model/cache/image/head/prefill stages. Dependent PID **16264**
exited 0 in 1178.98 seconds including its validation wait, completing all six
native ABBA profiles (72 requests). Fresh VL confirmation PID **40142** exited
0 in 69.25 seconds (24 requests). Every candidate VL request records 48 actual
block-product dispatches; controls and text/coder record zero. Frozen complete
outputs and fresh image identities match. Other experimental paths stay off.

reports.report_text:
# Body-only fixed-shape serving experiment

Status: fresh build, standard Metal MPS CTest, all 19 original numerical stages,
six trained session/recovery cases and all six native ABBA profiles passed.
Independent verification covers 1594 archived files and 144 complete matching
requests, exact body dispatch counts, zero fallback misses, zero specialization
in the frozen prefill profiles, and bounded eager pipeline caches. Initial
decode gains are small and broad, and persist in a second six-profile trial.
Batch-2 TTFT is higher in both trials, so the default remains OFF.
The full 2x/half-TTFT goal remains unmet. No fresh vLLM ratio is claimed.

The preceding two component trials found repeated small body gains for coder B2
and VL, while text/coder vocabulary-head specialization consistently slowed
those heads. This candidate tests whether body gains survive real graphs while
the agreed models' original heads remain unchanged. It does not enable the
reset, streaming, fused-head, concurrent-pass, or native-bfloat experiments.

`GARNET_METAL_BODY_SHAPE` defaults OFF. It retains original BF16 learned bytes
and FP32 arithmetic/inputs/outputs. Graph initialization prepares pipelines for
physical rows 1 or 2 and output width below 100000. All three frozen Qwen
vocabulary heads exceed this width and retain their original route. Larger
prefill matrices use the existing MPS path. Tiny prefill profiles with at most
two physical rows are also eligible by shape; the six frozen benchmark prefill
plans all have more than two physical rows.

Each specialized pipeline fixes dimensions and physical strides. Tail branches
are removed only for complete output tiles. A shared, mutex-protected cache is
bounded to 128 profile entries and releases with the last owning context.
Compilation occurs before a graph becomes ready and contributes to model init.
Decode performs a lookup and does not compile lazily. Missing/unsupported
entries retain original dispatch; benchmark admission requires zero misses.

Workers record the count after prefill and every decode call. Dense layers
must use seven specialized body projections and VL linear layers eight. The
frozen prefill count must be zero, all decode counts must equal the exact layer
configuration total, and the bounded cache count must be positive. Every

# Exact coalesced BF16 block storage: repeated component signal

Compact blocks contain four output channels by128 K terms. Each stores512
sign/mantissa bytes and256 four-bit exponent-tag bytes plus a32-bit exponent
base/compact flag. When the exponent range exceeds15, the entire SIMD group
uses the original four-output raw BF16 buffer. Compact payload has fixed pitch
and coalesced vector loads. There are no per-value escapes or prefix sums.
Original BF16 bits are reconstructed before the original FP32 arithmetic and
SIMD reduction. This is lossless storage, not a reduced-precision model.

This differs from the earlier one-output nibble/whole-block candidates in its
four-output vector loading, fixed byte-plane addresses and uniform block
fallback. The original master and raw four-output storage remain resident;
the experiment does not establish process-memory savings. Added payload and
CPU packing costs are outside component timing and must be measured at model
initialization before any deployment decision.

Independent CPU admission checks original checkpoint slices and reports20
eligible first-layer matrices:6 text,3 coder and11 VL. Approximately96.5% of
their blocks fit the compact payload. This is not full-model compression
coverage. The CPU report/source are frozen alongside GPU evidence; the native
context additionally packs real byte/nibble planes and checks every recovered
original weight bit before uploading any compact buffer.

PID87646 exited0 in20.5991s. After independent audit, confirmation PID88145
exited0 in20.5885s. Combined independent verification checks89 archived files,
144 numerical cases,378 safety profiles and2304 timed submissions. All
candidate outputs are bit-exact against the current native four-output body
and meet the unchanged FP64 envelope. Runtime packing counts match the
independent CPU report. All original matrices, unsupported routes and the
special float-key policy remain in the workload.

The selected64-thread policy is fixed across all model/batch profiles:

| Model / batch | Initial GPU / wall fraction | Repeat GPU / wall fraction |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Text / 1 | 0.8644 / 0.9228 | 0.8361 / 0.9131 |

| Coder / 1 | 0.8379 / 0.9107 | 0.8356 / 0.8797 |

| VL / 1 | 0.9660 / 0.9811 | 0.9552 / 0.9817 |
| VL / 2 | 0.8112 / 0.8577 | 0.8271 / 0.8966 |

Fractions are candidate/control; below1 is faster. All64/128/256-thread raw
windows remain available. The common64-thread choice improves all six groups
in both trials, avoiding a per-model dispatch policy selected from individual
best samples. Some other variants regress. Every profile uses two ABBA rounds
and eight samples per position, after common warmup. Resource guards exclude
competing inference. These are independent first-layer projections streamed
in one submission, not complete-model execution or a vLLM comparison.

A native OFF-default integration is warranted for full validation. Whole-model
outputs, decode throughput, TTFT, initialization and memory costs remain

# Compact eight-output decode: initial exact-bit rejection; lexical follow-up

Hypothesis: share each activation float4 across two adjacent original
four-output compact BF16 blocks, reducing activation loads and scheduling
overhead without changing weight bits, packing, or each output's FP32
accumulation order. This differs from the earlier
[raw eight-output layout](../wide-body-decode/README.md), which changed storage
and gave mixed/regressive results. Neither that experiment nor the retained
four-output block gains establish a gain for this new kernel.

The control is the current compact four-output kernel at 64 threads, not the
older raw BF16 layout. Candidate policies use 64/128/256 threads and eight
outputs per SIMD group. Both policies share the existing payload, raw
fallback, matrix admission threshold and weight allocations. Candidate-only
dispatch counters are asserted in the generated harness. Decode only; no
native source or serving default changes. The source factory generates a
private context/header and harness, leaving the live MLP validation untouched.

Current status, 2026-10-15: the initial trial compiled and executed on the Mac,
with72 numerical records and189 safety profiles. Every numerical-bound check
passed, but54 records differed from control output bits. All18 model/batch/
policy profiles were rejected; zero timing samples were admitted. The lexical
follow-up has the same54 exact-bit failures and is also rejected. No kernel or
full-model speed gain is claimed.

Planned gates preserve all 29 original trained projection matrices (7 text,
7 coder, 15 VL), four input patterns, batch 1/2, exact native output bits,
the original FP64 gamma envelope and the existing native-comparison bound.
The tail/fallback/prefill, pending-output, foreign-writer, uninitialized-read,
abort and recovery cases remain. An independent frozen CPU packing audit is
reused only after original asset/checkpoint hash agreement. Reusing that audit
does not constitute another CPU replication.

Expected maximum coverage is 72 numerical records, 189 repeated safety
profiles and 1,152 timed submissions; none is an executed count yet. Only
policies passing every numerical gate may enter two ABBA rounds with eight
samples per position. One submission covers the entire independent projection
set. Common allocation/packing/input upload is outside timing. Extra compiled
pipeline/setup costs, first-call costs and process RSS are not measured by
these component wall/GPU clocks. No memory-saving claim follows from retaining
the same weight buffers.

```text

# and its evidence archived; no inference/validation may overlap this probe.
python3 run_coalesced_eight_body.py ROOT ROOT/logs/coalesced-eight-body-20261015/jobs
python3 archive_coalesced_eight_body.py ROOT ARCHIVE
python -X utf8 test2026/metal/verify_coalesced_eight_body.py RESULTS RESULTS/verification.json
```

A clean launcher/resource guard is required before executing this invocation
template. Selection requires repeated component evidence, unchanged original
model gates, full generated-output comparison and fresh repeated matched vLLM
measurements. The full 2x decode/half-TTFT goal remains unmet.

Controller PID88447 at `ROOT/logs/mlp-prefill-native-and-eight-finalize-20261015`
waits for exact upstream controller82980, then the actual native comparison PID
recorded by that controller. It archives the terminal native comparison and
requires the separate 72-complete-output audit before launching this probe.
Any upstream or audit failure stops dispatch. Native and component GPU work
cannot overlap through this sequence. Controller exit0 means probe dispatched,
not a successful probe or performance result. The probe's own quiet guard and
original numerical/timing admission checks remain mandatory.

```text
python3 finalize_mlp_profiles_and_launch_eight.py ROOT ROOT/logs/mlp-prefill-native-and-eight-finalize-20261015
```

## Executed initial trial and follow-up — 2026-10-15

The controller88447 sequence above stopped after the upstream27/28 coverage
audit failure. The later controller99421 sequence archived native PID99045
but stopped on an omitted-source archive error. The completed native
comparison was separately repaired and strictly audited before dispatching
this probe; see the [native report](../mlp-prefill-native/README.md).

PID3818 exited0 in19.352752s after its five-second quiet guard. Its private
Objective-C++ context and runtime Metal shader compiled and executed all
three original trained projection sets. The [independent audit](initial/verification.json)
verifies49 files,72 numerical records,189 safety profiles and **zero timed
executions**. Worst FP64-bound ratio0.00720305 and original-control envelope
ratio0.181313 are below1, but only18 records are bitwise equal (one-hot input
pattern);54 are unequal. Every policy has an unequal required pattern and
is excluded from timing. No tolerance or exact-bit requirement was relaxed.
The existing original-checkpoint CPU packing audit is reused, not rerun.
Archive SHA256:
`d2be45e8cf1bf01199c476e7f97393c067e1c562f2d1bcce3d6926a260557346`.

The indexed accumulator arrays may alter compiler arithmetic; that is an
unproven explanation. A follow-up duplicates the original lexical four-output
block body twice within the same K loop, with separately named accumulators
and shared activation loads. Control, assets, four patterns, thread policies,
numerical envelopes and mandatory exact bits stay the same. The generator
`make_unrolled_coalesced_eight_shader.py` is preserved in each source snapshot.

First follow-up PID4314 exited1 in11.658886s: the generated shader referred
to an undefined accumulator because sequential textual name replacements
rewrote a newly generated name a second time. The runtime compile failed
before numerical/timing records. It was archived before any source repair:
`7e28e46398ac77f619753dc800e497672667e50351a959aa7f137669d704ac7b`.
The factory now substitutes whole tokens once and checks that generated
accumulator identifiers are exactly the four declared names. This fixes a
generator bug; it does not explain the initial exact-bit differences.

Fresh PID4586 at `ROOT/logs/coalesced-eight-body-unrolled-fixed-20261015`
exited0 in19.247992s. The [50-file independent audit](unrolled/verification.json)
verifies72 numerical records,189 safety profiles and zero timed executions.
Again18 records are bitwise equal and54 unequal, so all18 profiles are excluded
from timing. Worst FP64-bound ratio0.00720305 and original-control envelope
ratio0.141144 remain below1. Removing the indexed accumulator array did not
restore exact bits; indexing alone is not an established cause. Reject both
variants for promotion without relaxing the gate. Corrected follow-up archive:
`bf10548d6e55ef01d8299e956fa1d9039519d98a66a026d07fe09bb8057c572f`.
Both shaders remain private. Native serving code/defaults are unchanged;
full goal unmet. The next TTFT experiment changes graph scheduling rather
than pursuing an unmeasured speed claim for these rejected kernels.

# Independent native projections in one compute pass: mixed results

The actual two sequential component trials passed every complete output-bit,
padding, fresh-input and original FP64 check. The independent audit verified
48 archived files, 32 group/batch configurations across the two trials, 30,595
validated executions and 6,144 timed executions. A concurrent pass does not
produce a broad repeated gain, so this is not enabled in serving. No new
whole-model or vLLM speed ratio is claimed. The full goal remains unmet.

The preceding native inference telemetry places text/coder warm decode host
preparation around 0.13–0.16 ms and encoding around 0.48–0.55 ms, compared with
12.6–16.0 ms observed GPU spans. These clocks overlap and must not be added.
This motivates testing GPU scheduling before spending effort on host-list or
control-upload changes. The source data is the control records in
`../reused-zero-source-inference/evidence/logs/reused-zero-source-confirm-native-20261015/jobs`.

This component preserves the exact current native BF16 decode shaders and
default compiler options. It changes only compute-pass scheduling for independent
learned gate/up pairs and dense Q/K/V groups, plus an irregular synthetic
read-only-input pair. VL layer 0 already has a combined QKV projection, so it
has no separate Q/K/V group in this test. B1 and B2 use fresh original, negated,
half and doubled FP32 inputs with negative-zero elements. All outputs are
separate allocations; there are no dependencies among dispatches in a group.

The control uses one serial encoder per projection. Mode 1 uses one serial
encoder for the group, isolating encoder reuse. Mode 2 requests one concurrent
encoder for the group. The API allows concurrent compute commands; requesting
it does not prove hardware overlap. Dependencies on later consumers would still
need correct synchronization in any future integration. See Apple's
[resource synchronization documentation](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/metal/resource-synchronization?language=objc).

Candidate/control component wall-time fractions below 1 are faster. These
are full grouped-projection wall intervals including encode/submit/wait,
not model TPS or TTFT. All raw per-window GPU and encoding times are preserved.

# Compute-pass GPU timestamps: validated diagnostic, substantial overhead

This adds evidence for choosing the next optimization; it establishes no new
serving speed gain. Production sources and selected libraries are unchanged.
The original source SHA-256 is
`b0cf78db529b4837022a66ac06db879774e114a73285d43065582124b505f480`.
One generated diagnostic source instruments twelve encoder sites in a
separate source/build tree, with the selected global-alpha options and both
dirty-prefix reset and streaming off. Independent verification proves all
raw Metal shader payloads unchanged.

The actual Apple M4 supports stage-boundary timestamps, but does not support
dispatch- or blit-boundary sampling. Capability PID **56549** exited 0 after
2.36 seconds. Two dependent compute passes produced 4096 bit-exact values and
four nonzero, within-pass monotonic timestamps in one command buffer. Apple's
[sampling documentation](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/metal/sampling-gpu-data-into-counter-sample-buffers)
requires checking supported sampling boundaries. Its
[counter documentation](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/metal/gpu-counters-and-counter-sample-buffers)
describes resolving counter buffers and clock conversion; recorded raw ticks
are not assumed to be milliseconds.

Initial diagnostic PID **57117** exited 1 after 21.27 seconds. Generation,
configure, build, numeric CTest and the first two native workers exited 0,
but trace stderr interleaved inside result stdout JSON. The strict parser
rejected it. `failed/` and `failure-verification.json` preserve 202 verified
files, the successful capability/CTest and three complete quiet outputs.
Traced outputs from that failed run remain unverified. Failure archive SHA-256:
`c907051262a914a881f254e786ff85ecb8d3361b729922ed2ebbc74c5e2f4b37`.

The repair writes traces to an owned, separate file with a process-wide mutex
and explicit flush, closes streams at context destruction, and leaves old
source/build artifacts intact. No parser tolerance was introduced. Repaired
PID **58044** exited 0 after 133.99 seconds. All six model/batch profiles ran
sequential quiet/traced/traced/quiet fresh workers, each with three original
requests. Independent `verification.json` checks 434 archived files, all 28
terminal stages, all 72 complete token/prompt/finished outputs and fresh frame
hashes, 358872 counter samples and 660 command summaries. Sample indices are
contiguous and timestamps valid. Counter records explicitly reject serialized
operation profiling and partial submissions. Checkpoint/config/tokenizer
hashes match the frozen comparison assets.

Successful archive SHA-256:
`0180f78d95067cef01bec0c463514962565cd8b83086a072727bbb02ae67c978`.
The generated source SHA-256 is
`f63adc3aaf44e3dd8c13f366ed2e33b8d7d1462b7f75d90e6057e2cc6f8315ec`.
The exact compiled library identity is archived in metadata and manifest.

`shape-ranking.json` groups observed decode-width head commands by operation
and shape. Text/coder MLP gate/up projections lead; VL's vocabulary head leads,
followed by MLP gate/up and QKV projections. BF16 projection passes account

percentages of full serving time: intervals overlap, internal MPS passes are
unmeasured, and the selection uses observed shapes rather than request/phase
markers. The report explicitly permits final prefill heads and small physical
tails and includes first and warm requests. Never add the sample durations
to infer command wall time or claim isolated warm throughput.

Instrumentation materially changes end-to-end clocks. Four warm requests per

VL B1 47.61→34.29 and VL B2 44.18→31.97 tokens/s per row. This is diagnostic

# Eight-lane FP32 decode: numerically valid, slower, rejected

The full optimization goal still needs batch-1 decode speed, particularly for
text and coder. This isolated experiment tests four independent eight-lane
groups per SIMD, each calculating two outputs with FP32 input, multiplication
and accumulation. It retains native BF16 learned values and their exact FP32
expansion. It changes reduction order and per-thread work distribution; it
does not claim bit equality or model-level correctness before execution.

This differs from the rejected sixteen-lane/four-output implementation that
retained two original partial accumulators per thread. The new kernel uses
one two-output accumulator per row, aiming to reduce register demand while
processing eight outputs per SIMD. Actual component performance was slower.
It tests 64- and 128-thread groups, B1/B2, real first-layer and full-head
checkpoint matrices, plus the established irregular tail and stride cases.
The control selects the existing small-output kernel for N≤256 and the
selected general kernel otherwise.

The established independent FP64 and control-comparison bounds remain
unchanged: both policies must satisfy
`gamma(ceil(K/32)+32)*sumabs+1e-7` against FP64, and the candidate must satisfy
`5e-6+5e-5*abs(control)` against native control. Padding and finite values are
checked before timing. A longer per-lane sum does not justify relaxing those
bounds. A failure rejects the experiment. A component gain still requires
complete model/cache/head/image validation and complete generated outputs
before any integration or end-to-end speed claim.

Owned queue PID **33256** was launched at
`ROOT/logs/decode-eight-lane-20261015`. It verifies exact owned dependency
**27124**, waits for its actual terminal exit 0, archives combined evidence,
then invokes one guarded component runner. The queue itself runs no inference
or GPU probe while waiting. Guards sample every 0.5 seconds and reject other
inference/probe jobs; no timed runtimes are intentionally overlapped.

PID **33256** exited 0 after 1082.43 seconds including the dependency wait.
Actual Mac compilation and all 136 matrix/batch/variant checks passed within
the unchanged bounds. Worst FP64 envelope fraction is 0.009709; worst native
comparison envelope fraction is 0.072507. Independent verification checked
53 archived files and 34 omitted raw-matrix identities.

For large trained matrices, unweighted sum-of-median GPU speedups are
0.87–0.93x across all model/batch/variant groups; corresponding wall speedups
are 0.91–0.99x. GPU time is about 7–15% longer and wall time 1–10% longer.
`component-by-batch.json` retains B1/B2 separately and both GPU and wall
clocks. This pooling is not weighted by layer count and is not a full-model
measurement. No favorable repeat, production integration or serving-speed
claim follows this broad regression. Production sources and retained
libraries are unchanged. The full optimization goal remains active and unmet.

`f56694dab8c65f81862fa79b12b670fb85f942f648c46e0e58bbde34d2d56f30`.

# Decode-only fused head: repeated full runs verified

The all-head variant repeated a 0.39–2.26% whole-model decode improvement,
but text B2 first-token latency regressed in both runs. This experiment keeps
the existing projection/argmax path when the session's physical chunk is
larger than one, and fuses only single-token runs. Agreed serving prefill
profiles use chunks of at least two; a direct single-token prefill API call
would use fusion as well. No precision, checkpoint, resolution, prompt, output
cap, request cache or prediction semantics are changed.

`GARNET_METAL_FUSED_HEAD_DECODE_ONLY` is OFF by default and requires the existing
optional fused-head flag. The previous candidate library and archived results
are preserved. Five route/measurement files are installed only after verifying
their exact original hashes. Raw fused shader arithmetic is unchanged.

Fresh build `build-decode-only-head` passed both actual CTests, including
the full-bit/FP64 fused-kernel, layout, ownership and recovery checks. All
original 19 model stages completed at PID 96768, exit 0 in 1201.70 seconds.
PID 98218 then completed six trained session/fallback/recovery cases and all
six matched native ABBA profiles, exit 0 in 1302.31 seconds including its
dependency wait. Independent verification covers 1,225 files and 72 complete
matching requests. The route counts are verified in every complete record.

The benchmark asserts zero fused dispatches for prefill's first prediction
and exactly one for each subsequent decode prediction. Every complete output,
prompt ID and finished flag must match; images must be freshly encoded. All
three models and both batches remain in scope. Initial whole-model measurements
are below; they are native control/candidate results, not new vLLM ratios.

# FP32 split-K decode: no broad gain, rejected for general dispatch

This experiment divides each learned BF16-weight dot product into two or four
parallel FP32 partial sums, then reduces them in FP32. It retains exact native
BF16 expansion and FP32 activations/output; reduction order changes. The
first kernel uses the original 32-lane/four-output layout. The second kernel
reads only complete partial sums and writes logical outputs, preserving row
padding. Both encoders share one tracked command buffer; GPU span and wall
time include both kernels and their dependency.

The control remains the selected small-output kernel for N≤256 and the native
general kernel otherwise. Tests retain all original real first-layer/full-head
matrices, B1/B2, synthetic irregular K/N tails and padded input/output strides.
Both policies must meet the unchanged independent FP64 envelope
`gamma(ceil(K/32)+32)*sumabs+1e-7`; candidate-versus-control remains
`5e-6+5e-5*abs(control)`. A failure rejects the method. Component timing alone
does not establish complete model correctness or serving throughput.

Owned PID **55556** started at `ROOT/logs/decode-splitk-20261015` only after
initial combined run, its repeat and the eight-lane queue all reached terminal
exit 0. The earlier evidence is archived and independently verified. Existing
0.5-second guards remain intact and reject other inference/probe jobs. No
competing runtime is deliberately run simultaneously.

PID **55556** exited 0 after 42.07 seconds. Actual Mac compilation and all 136
matrix/batch/variant checks passed within the unchanged numerical bounds.
Independent verification checked 55 archived files and 34 omitted raw-matrix
identities. Worst FP64 envelope fraction is 0.009973; worst native comparison
envelope fraction is 0.044918. Full generated outputs were not tested because
the component did not justify general production integration.

For large trained matrices, two-part unweighted GPU speedups are text
0.986/0.969, coder 0.996/0.941 and VL 1.007/0.983 for B1/B2 respectively.
Four-part variants are slower in all six groups (GPU speedups 0.916–0.944).
Wall results also fail to establish a broad gain; the only pooled positive
direction is VL B1 two-part at 1.009x. `component-by-batch.json` retains both
GPU and wall clocks, by batch and variant. Pooling distinct matrices is not
weighted by layer count and does not establish serving tokens/sec.

The individual VL B2 MLP down projection is an exception: two/four-part GPU
speedups 1.103/1.133 and wall speedups 1.035/1.037. This does not address the
unmet B1 throughput target and is not presented as a whole-model gain. Reject
general split-K dispatch; preserve this isolated shape observation for later
profiling rather than integrating a broad regression. No favorable full-model
claim or repeat follows the general candidate's result.

reports.title: Deferred request-state zero: repeated full-model latency tradeoff
reports.report_text:
# Deferred request-state zero: repeated full-model latency tradeoff

The optional `GARNET_METAL_DEFERRED_STATE_ZERO` reset queues each private state
matrix for row-preserving GPU blit fills at the start of the first inference
command buffer. No separate reset submission/wait is added. Owner snapshots
still return logical positive-zero values immediately; other contexts cannot
read or modify the stale physical allocation while its clear is queued.

Correctly sized host updates and direct zeros cancel a queued clear. Invalid
updates preserve it. Begin transfers ownership into the existing pending-output
set, so all GPU consumers are ordered after the fills and buffers survive until
completion. Abort/destruction invalidate pending/queued contents. Reset after
a poisoned session requeues every state. Logical row padding is preserved,
and actual materialized byte/state counts are recorded in the prefill profile.
No clears are expected on subsequent decode commands.

The feature is OFF by default and cannot be combined with the older direct-
zero or dirty-prefix reset policies. This experiment uses the selected global-
alpha compute options with fused-head variants disabled, isolating reset work.
Checkpoints, FP32 state/math, prompts, output caps, batches and images are frozen.

Fresh build `build-deferred-state-zero` passed both actual CTests in 2.43 seconds.
The new test verifies 45 nonzero/NaN/infinity transitions at B1/B2/padded B3,
positive-zero snapshots and GPU reads, ownership, duplicate resets, host-write
cancellation, invalid input handling, later-command clear elision, queued and
submitted abort recovery, partial submissions and owner destruction.

Owned validation PID 26187 passed all original 19 model gates, exit 0 in
1238.93 seconds. Two interrupted attempts were discarded when an unverified
runtime appeared; only complete clean cases are accepted. Guards are unchanged.
PID 31105 completed six trained session/recovery cases and 72 exact matching
requests in six native ABBA profiles, exit 0 in 1166.84 seconds including its

reports.report_text:
# Complete dependent MLP graph: audited stress experiment

Owned PID52062 waits for exact core graph PID50246 to be terminal, then a
five-second quiet interval. It compiled successfully and is running the three
models sequentially. No competing inference or GPU component may overlap.

The workload preserves a real MLP dependency chain: two gate/up projections,
(gate / (1 + exp(-gate))) * up, then the down projection. It uses checkpoint
MLPs at text/coder layer0 and VL layers0/3 (four blocks,12 trained matrices).
VL blocks use separate graph objects and sequential calls; no operations are
fused across actual attention/layer boundaries. Each block uses one native
submission or one synchronous graph call. Set wall time includes every block.

Native execution uses the current retained c186 library and its existing
BF16-storage/FP32-arithmetic MLP operations. Graph tensors and learned values
are FP32, with lossless expansion of original BF16 weights. Policy1 supplies
weight placeholders; policy2 embeds constants. Gate/up share the actual MLP
input, and graph intermediates follow the original dependency chain.
Only final outputs are graph targets, allowing legitimate internal fusion.

Four original input patterns are tested at physical rows24/44,26/52,80/160.
CPU FP64 computes the complete gate/up, nonlinear activation and down result.
Both native and graph final outputs must meet the existing trained-reference
envelope5e-6+5e-5*abs(reference); graph/native differences must meet the same
unchanged native-comparison envelope. This compound reference differs from
the earlier isolated-matmul gamma bound; it is not a widened tolerance.
Any failed native or graph profile has no timing windows. No failed input is
removed or adjusted to obtain a performance result.

Expected coverage is48 aggregate checks,12 first graph-set calls and up to12
admitted timing profiles with768 submissions. These are expected counts,
not audited results yet. Every admitted profile uses two ABBA rounds and
eight samples/position after common warming. First/setup costs are separate.

This remains an isolated MLP test. It does not include a full transformer
layer, attention, norm/residual operations, pending-input native/graph command
interoperability, complete generated outputs, model TTFT or a vLLM result.
Integration still requires ownership/abort/recovery, trained-model validation,
full-model repeats and a fresh matched comparator. The full goal is unmet.

```text
# Only after the exact job is terminal:
python3 archive_dependent_mlp_graph.py ROOT ARCHIVE
python -X utf8 test2026/metal/verify_dependent_mlp_graph.py RESULTS RESULTS/verification.json
```

## Audited outcome and reference correction — 2026-10-15

The launch-time protocol above is preserved as history. PID52062 is terminal
exit 0 (38.668088 s). Independent verification covers 30 archived files,
48 numerical records, 12 first graph calls and 256 admitted timed submissions.
Eight text/coder model/batch/policy profiles fail the compound CPU reference
on pattern 1 in BOTH the unchanged native control and graph candidate. These
profiles have no timing windows. All 48 graph/native comparisons pass the
unchanged comparison envelope. Process exit 0 does not mean all gates passed.

Reference-design correction: the initial whole-chain FP64 computation does
not reproduce the existing trained reference's FP32 rounding after each
projection and activation. Its bounds had been described as the existing
trained-reference test too broadly. Preserve this experiment as a stress
test; it cannot establish equivalence to that existing reference. The
[stage-rounded follow-up](../stage-rounded-mlp-graph/README.md) changes only
CPU reference rounding. It is a distinct experiment, not a replicate, and
does not erase these failures or relax tolerance coefficients.

Only VL profiles were admitted to timing in this experiment:

| Model / batch | Weight policy | Native wall ms | Graph wall ms | Graph/native wall |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Qwen3.5-0.8B / 1 | placeholder | 3.780941 | 3.574172 | 0.945313 |

| Qwen3.5-0.8B / 2 | constant | 4.791042 | 4.255926 | 0.888309 |

These are component wall means, not model TTFT, decode throughput or an
independent repeat. The first-call/setup records remain separate. Peak RSS
and isolated graph compilation time were not measured in this component
study. No production or whole-model claim follows.

reports.title: Single-dispatch independent projections
reports.report_text:
# Single-dispatch independent projections

This component experiment preserves the native BF16 projection dot products and
places independent projections in disjoint ranges of one GPU dispatch. It is
distinct from the earlier serial/concurrent compute-pass study, which retained
multiple dispatches, and from gate/up/SiLU fusion, which changed the operation
boundary. There is no serving integration or speedup claim yet.

The generator retains the original two-/four-output dot-product bodies and
passes the original parameters, input, weights and separate outputs to them.
One grid covers the sum of the projection grids. A group-uniform branch selects
the projection and adjusts its group index. The combined dispatch uses 128
threads; small projections retain only their original two active SIMD groups.
No learned weight is repacked, no sum is split, and precision is unchanged.

The experiment covers actual layer-zero learned MLP gate/up pairs for all three
models, separate dense Q/K/V projections for text and coder, and irregular
synthetic read-only-input pairs, at B1/B2. The harness requires complete output
and padding bits to match the original kernels for fresh original, negated,
halved and doubled inputs, including negative-zero values. The original FP64
gamma(ceil(K/32)+32)*sumabs+1e-7 envelope remains unchanged. Timing uses common
250 ms warmup and two ABBA rounds, twelve samples per window. Compile and kernel
pipeline creation are outside component execution timing.

Owned queue PID 47884 waits for exact owned inference PID 43673 at
`logs/threaded-striped-inference-20261015` to terminate successfully before it
compiles or uses the GPU. Its destination is
`logs/fused-projection-groups-20261015`. The same exclusive-process, disk-space
and 0.5 s monitor guards apply. Neither a queue record nor generated code proves
successful execution; actual terminal evidence and independent audit are required.

The unchanged original encoder path is the control. Component timing includes
encode, submission and wait, so it cannot establish a model TPS or TTFT gain.
Repeated component benefit would only justify considering a separate full-model
integration and output-validation study. The full goal remains unmet and active.

## Actual initial result: mixed; not integrated

PID 47884 terminated exit 0 after 243.8145 seconds, including its dependency
wait. The independent audit verified 30 archived files, 16 group/batch checks,
12,738 complete-output validated executions and 1,536 timed executions. Every
candidate output and padding bit matches; the worst original FP64 envelope
ratio is 0.0090262. Compilation and all three model stages passed their exclusive
guards. Thus the dispatch is compatible, but compatibility is not a speed win.

| Model | Batch | Group | Component wall fraction | GPU fraction |
| --- | ---: | --- | ---: | ---: |
| Text | 1 | gate/up | 1.01 | 0.99 |
| Text | 2 | gate/up | 0.98 | 0.99 |
| Text | 1 | Q/K/V | 1.01 | 0.96 |
| Text | 2 | Q/K/V | 0.90 | 0.91 |
| Coder | 1 | gate/up | 0.96 | 0.91 |
| Coder | 2 | gate/up | 1.06 | 1.07 |
| Coder | 1 | Q/K/V | 1.05 | 1.03 |
| Coder | 2 | Q/K/V | 0.97 | 0.91 |
| VL | 1 | gate/up | 1.09 | 1.05 |
| VL | 2 | gate/up | 1.03 | 1.00 |

Fractions below one are faster. These rounded component values are not whole
model TPS/TTFT. Text B2 Q/K/V improves, but VL gate/up and several coder groups
regress. The initial mixed result does not justify a blanket serving change.
There is no second trial or full inference integration for this candidate.
Irregular-pair results and full precision values remain in `verification.json`.

`4bcce4ed75a37c04ab4f7c9b7f38579a44a4bec65f8121a62ca45fdd3d600da5`.


# Isolated interleaved BF16 decoder body component

Both component trials passed and have some promising timings. The large-matrix
policy improved all six wall-time profiles in both trials. This is not a
complete-model speed improvement. The full 2x decode /
half-TTFT target remains unmet.

The private generator copies the current native context and header into the
job directory. It stores groups of four output columns together at each input
coordinate and checks every packed BF16 value and padded zero against the
original bytes before publication. The candidate shader loads two uint4
vectors per four input coordinates instead of four separate ushort4 vectors.
The original FP32 multiply/add order and SIMD reduction remain unchanged.
Original BF16 masters and the existing prefill representations remain present.
Only matrices with 256 < output width <= 8192 and input width divisible by four
receive the private layout. Small-output, odd-width and vocabulary paths keep
their original route. Production source files are not rewritten.

The queued test uses the 29 checkpoint-verified first-layer projections across
Qwen3-0.6B, Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct and Qwen3.5-0.8B, B1/B2. Four input
patterns must match the original native outputs bit for bit and remain inside
the unchanged independent FP64 envelope. Three static selection policies test
all admitted matrices, MLP only, and matrices of at least one million values.
The independent projections share one command submission. Their timings are
component measurements, not complete transformer execution or generation.

The harness also checks tail padding, fallback geometry, pending/foreign
command ownership, uninitialized input rejection, abort and recovery. Actual
private-layout dispatch counts must agree with the selected projections.
Only after numerical gates pass does it time two ABBA rounds per model/batch/
policy, with eight measurements per window. Packing and initialization are
outside these steady-state component intervals and cannot be advertised as
end-to-end gains.

# Native interleaved screening index: profile-dependent tradeoffs

The lossless index layout passes all native gates and 144 complete outputs
across two six-profile trials. VL decode improves about 3%, and coder B1
decode / coder TTFT improve in both runs. Text B1 decode regresses twice;
text TTFT and VL B1 TTFT worsen twice. Initialization is longer. This is
not a general serving improvement, so the option remains OFF by default.
The 2x-decode/half-TTFT goal remains unmet, with no fresh vLLM ratio here.

Both policies enable the same 1024-row exact seed, screened original BF16
refinement, ordered prefill streaming, partial reset and serial vision
prefetch. Only index layout and observation counters differ. Every derived
index value is checked through its four-column permutation before native
publication; the padded final group is zero. The macro-selected Metal body
matches the audited component functions. Index values, original learned
BF16 values, FP32 operation order, bounds, images, prompt IDs, output limits,
stop semantics and complete normalized outputs remain unchanged.

Validation PID 33362 exited 0 in 1312.2053 s. All 27 stages pass: original
19 model/cache/vision/prefill stages, trained full-grid vision, 51 trained
head queries and six recovery stage suites. Synthetic CTest uses vocabulary
8209 to exercise the partial four-column group, outside-seed lowest ties,
bounded/nonfinite/mixed fallback, ownership and Begin/Abort. Trained heads
check every original rejected score and retained score bits. Trained session
tests observe actual layout counts through normal prediction, float-head
fallback, generic logits, nonfinite poison, reset, close/rebuild and isolation.
Every serving candidate prediction records actual layout dispatch count 1;
legacy controls report the frozen row-major configuration. Both policies
record seed width 1024, one screened head per prediction and 12 vision
prefetch dispatches per freshly encoded image request.

Initial native PID 33417 exited 0 in 1470.9927 s including the dependency
wait. Fresh repeat PID 59868 exited 0 in 160.0026 s. Independent audits check
1,861 archived files and 144 complete requests. Each profile uses fresh
sequential control/candidate/candidate/control workers, three requests per
worker. The first request is separate; four warm requests per policy form
each mean. No competing inference runtime is intentionally run; guards sample
every 0.5 s. Both image policies use the same combined threaded decode /
exact striped resize and fresh encoding without prefix/encoder reuse.

| Model / batch | Initial decode control / candidate tokens/s per row | Repeat decode control / candidate tokens/s per row |
| --- | ---: | ---: |

VL B1/B2 decode gains are 2.94% / 3.07% initially and 3.44% / 3.50% on
repeat. Coder B1 gains 1.37% / 1.73%. Text B1 loses 2.14% / 2.79%.

# Lossless four-column screening index: repeated component gain

Two actual same-process trials reduce component GPU and wall time while
preserving every sampled masked score and flag bit. Four output columns are
stored together so the shader uses one uint4 vector load for their four-key
tile instead of four separate char4 loads. Index values, FP32 FMA order,
SIMD reductions, bounds, seed and original BF16/FP32 refinement are unchanged.
This is a derived screening-index layout change, not model quantization.

Both policies use an exact 1024-row seed. Before timing, the raw original
head must match captured complete logits bit for bit. Each policy checks all
retained scores, every sampled rejection against full original scores, and
greedy output. Candidate and control additionally match all masked output
bits and both visit/keep flag arrays. The existing candidate unsafe-input
tests exercise zero/tiny/large/NaN/Inf/mixed rows and full-refinement fallback.
No bounds were widened. The sampled gates are not certification for all
future inputs.

The complete byte permutation roundtrips all 155,582,464 / 136,134,656 /
254,279,680 derived index values for text, coder and VL, respectively, in
each trial. Physical row count rounds up to a four-column group; padded
entries are zero. The original index byte hashes and all learned input/head
hashes are verified before use. All original BF16 weights remain authoritative.

Initial PID 30117 exited 0 in 38.2029 s. Independent repeat PID 30957 exited
0 in 38.1735 s. The audit checks 84 archived files, six complete index
roundtrips, 102 captured-query pairs, 156 row states per policy, 66 candidate
unsafe-input cases, 6,528 raw timed executions, guards and ABBA ordering.
Each query has at least 250 ms common warming, then two ABBA rounds with
eight samples per window. Timed intervals include exact seed, bounds,
screen/refine and argmax in one command buffer. Only one probe runs at a time.

Fractions below average ordinary captured steps and exclude the separate
mixed-row fixture. Candidate/control below 1 means faster.

reports.report_text:
# Reset and dependent GPU read in one command buffer: repeated component signal

Two actual exclusive M4 runs exited 0 in 9.23 and 9.16 seconds. Independent
verification covers 35 archived files, 126 CPU/GPU positive-zero and padding
checks, and 1,344 timed executions. All six actual-config model/batch profiles
improve over the legacy zero-vector allocation/copy plus dependent GPU read.
This is not a measured TTFT or full-model gain.

The previous GPU-clear experiment submitted and waited for a reset command
separately. Here the candidate puts row-preserving blit fills and a dependent
GPU read in the same command buffer. The control performs the current CPU
allocation/copy reset before the same read. Both observed wall clocks include
reset work, read encoding, submission and completion. GPU conditioning writes
and waits happen before each sample and are excluded, as is CPU validation.
The GPU read checks positive-zero bits across every logical state element;
it is a synthetic dependent read, not a trained inference operation.

| Model / batch | Initial legacy → joint wall ms | Repeat legacy → joint wall ms | Repeat joint / legacy |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Text / 1 | 5.2963 → 1.6588 | 5.0763 → 2.1955 | 0.4325 |
| Text / 2 | 23.6289 → 3.7592 | 22.8792 → 4.0736 | 0.1780 |
| Coder / 1 | 1.0304 → 0.7649 | 0.7319 → 0.5124 | 0.7001 |
| Coder / 2 | 2.3989 → 1.3672 | 1.7197 → 0.7415 | 0.4312 |
| VL / 1 | 4.3236 → 1.3616 | 3.7643 → 0.9833 | 0.2612 |
| VL / 2 | 10.4411 → 2.4609 | 10.4529 → 2.7948 | 0.2674 |

Actual checkpoint configuration hashes determine all FP32 state shapes at
capacity 256 and B1/B2, including convolution/recurrent state. A padded 3-row
synthetic case preserves every padding byte but has mixed performance
(0.9291 / 1.1018 wall fractions); this is not a universal small-buffer win.
Direct CPU memset is recorded as a third diagnostic policy and can beat the
joint candidate in several profiles. GPU spans increase with the added fill
work; reduced total wall time does not imply a faster GPU read kernel.

Each profile uses at least 250 ms paired warm-up, then two balanced
legacy/direct/joint/joint/direct/legacy rounds, eight samples per window.
The source, raw configs/profiles, commands, exclusive guards, all windows,
omitted binary hashes and independent calculations are in `evidence/`.

configure, build, CTest, vision-full-grid and screened-real-heads completed;
text exact-tail checks are progressing. No terminal record has been observed.
This is not a final archive, an independent validation audit, a performance
measurement or a claim that the entire suite passed. Read later dated journal
entries for subsequent state. No source consumed by this job may change
until terminal status and archival.

Hypothesis: replace the consecutive native gate/up projections, SiLU product
and down projection with one complete FP32 MPSGraph, targeting only the final
output, to reduce prefill submissions and intermediate handling. New option
`GARNET_METAL_MLP_PREFILL_GRAPH` defaults OFF. Decode is unchanged. The route
admits supported prefill shapes, uses FP32 placeholders and losslessly expands
the original BF16 weight bits; it adds real weight-storage/cache costs.

prototype and repaired guard. The initial 17-file manifest is preserved in
the first failed archive. Native numerical sources are unchanged by the
guard and retry repairs. Eleven original files were backed up initially;

on the same Metal queue with explicit completion/error handling. Output remains
logically pending until native completion. This preserves simple ordering and
abort safety but introduces a CPU wait per MLP, which may erase component
gains. Graph creation is lazy: first-request compilation and extra FP32 weight
memory must be reported separately. The graph cache is capped at 256 entries.

The validation driver retains the original 28 numerical/recovery stages and
adds a primitive CTest covering pending inputs, foreign writers, uninitialized
reads, alias rejection, abort invalidation/recovery and row fallbacks. Expected
test coverage is not an executed passing count. No tolerance coefficients

must be reconciled against independently expected model/chunk counts.

# MPS-derived screening dot products: rejected

Actual PID 31751 exited 0 in 43.3903 s. All numerical and input/fallback
checks pass, but every model/batch component is slower. No native integration
or serving gain is claimed. The general speed/TTFT goal remains unmet.

This separates index dot products from original BF16 refinement. The control
uses the current strict INT8 screening kernel. The candidate converts every
derived signed INT8 index value exactly to FP16 storage, then uses MPS with
FP32 query matrices, exact integer-valued FP16 index matrices and FP32 score
matrices. The unchanged strict filter applies original metadata/bounds to
those scores, and retained final logits still use original BF16 weights and
FP32 refinement. Both policies use the same exact 1024-row seed.

Every converted index value roundtrips exactly for all three complete heads.
The raw original head matches captured full-logit bits before admission.
Each policy checks retained final-score bits, every sampled rejection versus
the original full logits, greedy prediction and error semantics. Existing
candidate zero/tiny/large/NaN/Inf/mixed full-refinement fallback checks pass.
Filter sums and retention masks are not claimed bit-identical across MPS
and original dot-product reduction orders. No allowances were widened, and
the sampled checks do not certify all future inputs.

The independent audit checks 42 files, three complete index roundtrips,
51 captured-query pairs / 78 row states per policy, 33 unsafe-input cases,
3,264 raw timed executions, exact generated source, original asset hashes,
guards and both ABBA rounds. Common warmup is at least 250 ms per query;
two ABBA rounds use eight samples/window. Timings include the MPS product,
seed, bounds, screen/refine and original argmax in one command buffer. The
comparison runs after all native work and layout trials are terminal; no
other inference runtime is intentionally run simultaneously.

These means average ordinary captured steps, excluding the separate
mixed-row fixture. Fractions are candidate/control; above 1 is slower.

| Model / batch | GPU fraction | Wall fraction |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Qwen3-0.6B / 1 | 1.639805 | 1.562344 |
| Qwen3-0.6B / 2 | 1.676422 | 1.577403 |
| Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct / 1 | 1.662939 | 1.566295 |
| Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct / 2 | 1.635924 | 1.531293 |
| Qwen3.5-0.8B VL / 1 | 1.643010 | 1.589446 |
| Qwen3.5-0.8B VL / 2 | 1.696898 | 1.634038 |

The candidate doubles index element storage from one byte to two and adds
an MPS product / score matrix before refinement. These are implementation
differences, not a measured attribution of the entire slowdown. The 53–63%
wall penalty in every group is sufficient to reject this tested policy;
there is no positive result requiring a full-model integration or repeat.
The separate [lossless interleaved index](../interleaved-screen-index/README.md)
preserves the original dot arithmetic and gives repeated component gains.

The Objective-C++ harness compiles on the M4. The offline Metal compiler
