# MPSGraph FP32 prefill: actual component results, no broad promotion

The repaired owned PID84919 exited0 in81.7607s. This is an independent
projection component against Garnet's current native common-alpha MPS
prefill. It uses the same M4/16 GiB Mac, original first-layer learned matrices,
physical rows24/44 text,26/52 coder and80/160 VL, and four input patterns.
Graph matmul inputs, product and outputs are FP32, with runtime tensor dtype
assertions. Original numerical bounds are unchanged.

Policy1 supplies original BF16 values losslessly expanded into FP32 weight
storage. Policy2 supplies the current lossless common-scale FP16 weight
storage, explicitly casts it to FP32 before matrix multiplication and applies
the exact power-of-two alpha in FP32. CPU conversion checks every recovered
original learned-value bit. Both policies preserve original FP32 activations;
there is no approximate activation conversion or reduced-precision matmul
requested. The SDK default graph optimization level is1.

Independent audit verifies28 archived files,400 numerical checks,100 separate
first graph executions,100 admitted matrix/batch/policy timing profiles and
6400 timed submissions. All numerical checks pass the original FP64 envelope
and5e-6+5e-5*abs(native) comparison. Four matrices retain their native routes
and are skipped: the two special text/coder keys and two VL matrices without
the control's common-alpha representation. The archived proof independently
derives this admission from hashed raw BF16 tensors using the original integer
converter's rules. Actual checkpoints and every cached raw matrix are rehashed
and checked against checkpoint tensor slices by the executed runner.

Fractions divide sums of candidate component wall means by sums of control
means over the admitted matrices. Values above1 are slower. These are not
weighted by the models' layer counts or end-to-end inference frequencies.

| Model / batch | FP32 weight graph wall fraction | Cast-half weight graph wall fraction |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Text / 1 | 1.0035 | 1.4047 |
| Text / 2 | 0.9402 | 1.2458 |
| Coder / 1 | 1.0597 | 1.4443 |
| Coder / 2 | 0.9937 | 1.3580 |
| VL / 1 | 0.9758 | 1.2339 |
| VL / 2 | 0.9575 | 1.1556 |

The cast-half policy is slower in all groups. The FP32-storage policy has a
small2–6% signal for text B2 and VL, but doubles weight storage/traffic and
does not improve text/coder B1. It does not justify broadly replacing native
prefill. Full-model memory and latency gains have not been demonstrated.
No selected serving library or production source is changed.

Each native product and graph product runs sequentially and synchronizes
before the next. There is one projection per submission; this is not a whole
layer graph or fused MLP. Timings are wall latency only: native command-buffer
GPU span is never substituted for graph GPU time. Allocations/uploads and
first graph execution are excluded from warm windows. Each admitted profile
has two ABBA rounds, two warmups and eight samples per position, with250ms
common warmup. First graph execution, which includes compile/setup and GPU
work, spans3.13–159.11ms (median32.27ms); it is recorded separately, not added
to an invented hardware-cold result.

The initial owned PID84671 failed compilation in6.8532s because an execution
descriptor property was assigned to MPSGraph. No inference ran. Its17-file
archive is preserved under `failed/`; the SDK-default optimized synchronous
call repaired the API use only after that process was terminal and archived.

# Parallel FP32 vision value contraction

Status: native integration is rejected by the unchanged trained full-grid
embedding bound. The original nineteen stages passed, but five batch-1
embedding values exceed the added gate's tolerance. No serving benchmark ran.

Two actual component trials pass the original numerical envelopes and show
lower time at the frozen 216-token, 12-head, 64-dimension shape. Independent
audit covers 42 archived files, 48 shape checks and 7680 timed submissions.
This does not establish whole-image TTFT, generated-output compatibility or
the full optimization goal.

The selected global-alpha library uses separate softmax and value operations;
its `GARNET_METAL_FUSED_VISION_CONTEXT` cache flag is OFF. The component control
is the earlier optional fused kernel, not that selected library. It retains
the serial 216-key FP32 contraction after the original SIMD softmax. The new
candidate splits the key range across four SIMD groups, stores FP32 partials
in 2048 bytes of threadgroup memory and combines them in FP32. Softmax,
normalization, input scores/values and output storage remain unchanged. This
changes summation order, so numerical compatibility does not mean bit identity.

| Batch, frozen shape | GPU fraction initial / repeat | Wall fraction initial / repeat |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 0.87985 / 0.83225 | 0.92502 / 0.87337 |
| 2 | 0.89172 / 0.90042 | 0.90058 / 0.91143 |

Fractions below one are faster. Each trial covers B1/B2, 4/24/216 tokens,
2/12 heads and dimensions 8/64, with four fresh input generations including
large score magnitudes. Every output and padding element is checked. Both
original and candidate satisfy the existing independent FP64 envelope
`5e-6 + 5e-5*abs(reference)`; candidate/control differences satisfy the same
existing envelope. No tolerance, arithmetic precision or model weight changes.
The frozen candidate's worst FP64 ratios are 0.0117424 and 0.0130210, below 1.
The changed results are not bit-identical. Component inputs are synthetic;
trained full-grid image embeddings are a separate required gate.

Each shape has common alternating warmup of at least 250 ms, two ABBA rounds,
three per-window warmups and 20 raw timed submissions per window. Shader and
pipeline compilation, allocation and validation are outside component timing.
Raw GPU/wall observations, original control source, generated candidate source,
compiler/macOS versions, process guards and recomputed means remain in evidence.
OS/driver caches were not flushed.

Owned component PIDs 60423 and 60805 terminated exit 0 after 13.2153 and
13.1141 seconds. They waited for the exact owned frontend confirmation and
never overlapped inference. Initial archive SHA-256:
`859ad5a3b03e5c730c12e8bfc80e51999e67fc72bcc1c667c6ea3c3b9f51224a`.
Combined archive SHA-256:
`0176cc262ae83d4288e2d15bdd3eaf8d6e623f63223bbd9279333f6c4b9d36ca`.

## Optional native integration: rejected

`GARNET_METAL_PARALLEL_VISION_CONTEXT` defaults OFF and requires the existing
fused context and MPS score flags. It embeds the independently measured shader
body. Routing admits only 216 patch tokens, hidden width 768, 12 heads and
216/432 physical rows, with 32-lane SIMD, 128-thread and threadgroup-memory
checks. Other shapes or an unavailable pipeline retain the prior path. The

reports.title: Ordered partial prefill submissions: repeated latency tradeoff
reports.report_text:
# Ordered partial prefill submissions: repeated latency tradeoff

This optional experiment starts GPU prefill work while the CPU encodes later
layers. Existing telemetry records about 5–6 ms host prefill encoding before
the original single command buffer is submitted. The experiment aims to
overlap that work. Two actual native ABBA runs reduce warm first-token latency
in all six profiles, but do not establish a decode speed gain. Keep this
experiment optional and default OFF. There is no fresh vLLM comparison.

`GARNET_METAL_PREFILL_STREAM` defaults OFF. Only resident prefill with chunk
greater than one submits after each four layers, excluding the last boundary.
Single-token decode keeps one submission. Model kernels, learned values,
precision, prompts, image bytes/resolution, caps, stopping rules and frozen
chunk plans remain unchanged. The candidate retains global half alpha; dirty
prefix reset, vision alpha and other experimental optimizations remain off.

MetalContext retains every submitted command and all pending output owners.
Pending values are usable by their producing context but unavailable for host
readback/update. Final submission waits for all command buffers and checks
every status before publishing readiness. Abort drains submitted work, drops
the uncommitted continuation and invalidates all produced outputs before
reuse. Session graph locks remain held through completion. Actual partial
submission counts are published only after a successful full operation.

The design uses one queue and tracked shared resources. Apple's documentation
describes [command ordering](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/metal/mtlcommandbuffer)
and [automatic resource synchronization](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/metal/resource-synchronization).
No kernel is reordered within the logical dependent sequence. GPU telemetry
reports the earliest GPU start to latest GPU end across the command group,
including inter-command gaps; it does not sum potentially overlapping spans.
GPU time can overlap both CPU encoding and CPU waiting. Phase intervals must
not be added to infer end-to-end latency or isolated kernel work.

Installation pinned nine exact original sources against `cfc051a6`, preserved
their bytes and installed ten candidate files. Isolated candidate library
SHA-256 is
`bad8c5db120df0e6ac107a0fabc6b19708a379f36785b7b5c8869a30fd14534b`.
Configure/build and both CTests pass on the actual M4. The new unit checks 27
chains across rows 1/2/3, columns 1/17/1024 and 1/3/7 partial submissions,
with whole-output bit equality against one command. It verifies pending host
access rejection, ownership retention, abort draining and buffer reuse, count
reset and a real MPS-to-compute dependency across multiple submissions. The
original numerical CTest remains unchanged.

Validation PID **98669** exited 0 after 1201.14 seconds: all nineteen original
model/cache/head/image/prefill gates and both CTests passed. Dependent PID
**3161** exited 1 before any inference request because its helper looked up
the validation metadata under date 20261014 instead of 20261015. Preserve
that failure in `failed/` and `failure-verification.json` (351 verified files,
zero native requests). The repair changed only the comparator metadata path;
the candidate binary, kernels and numerical gates were unchanged.

Repaired PID **20856** exited 0 after 145.01 seconds; repeat PID **23797**
exited 0 after 144.83 seconds. Each ran all six sequential native ABBA
profiles with 72 complete requests and four warm requests per policy/profile
from two fresh workers, excluding each first request. Independent audits
verify 941 combined archive files, all nineteen gates and all 144 complete
matching serving outputs. Fresh frame hashes, prompt IDs and finished flags
match. Actual candidate partial counts are 6 for text, 5 for coder and VL B1,
and 15 for VL B2; control and decode counts are zero. Guards reject competing
inference/probe jobs and only stop owned work.

| Model / batch | Initial TTFT control → candidate ms | Repeat TTFT control → candidate ms | Decode candidate/control initial / repeat |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Text / 1 | 49.508 → 45.158 | 50.380 → 44.506 | 1.0107 / 0.9851 |
| Text / 2 | 79.009 → 76.574 | 82.105 → 77.731 | 1.0019 / 0.9913 |
| Coder / 1 | 33.118 → 29.339 | 32.709 → 28.659 | 0.9822 / 0.9950 |
| Coder / 2 | 51.857 → 46.119 | 50.984 → 46.657 | 0.9855 / 0.9946 |
| VL / 1 | 201.617 → 190.993 | 197.364 → 190.522 | 0.9997 / 0.9977 |
| VL / 2 | 359.370 → 348.868 | 360.874 → 350.313 | 1.0032 / 0.9985 |

Repeated warm TTFT reductions are 11.7%, 5.3%, 12.4%, 8.5%, 3.5% and 2.9%.
Decode is 0.1–1.5% slower in the repeat; text's initial positive direction did
not repeat. The method is a latency tradeoff, not a throughput optimization.
The independently derived `decode-time-share.json` uses the repeat's native
control only. Across text/coder B1/B2, GPU spans account for 91.3–92.7% of
observed decode wall time, while host encoding is 2.8–3.7%. These overlapping
clocks support prioritizing GPU decode work; they do not isolate matrix
kernels, prove bandwidth saturation, or establish a hypothetical speedup.
VL workers did not save individual decode phase clocks, so their GPU and host
shares are explicitly null rather than inferred from text/coder.
Repeat first request AFTER initialization improves in every profile (text
158.518→129.841 / 188.769→165.571 ms; coder 127.850→106.672 /
139.929→116.341 ms; VL 335.761→316.931 / 563.676→528.435 ms).
Initialization is recorded separately and OS/driver caches are not flushed.

`phases.json` and `confirmation-phases.json` retain the actual clocks. Repeat
text B1 prefill falls 42.366→37.038 ms while GPU span is 34.775→34.988 ms;
host wait falls 35.764→30.563 ms. This supports overlapping host encoding,
not a claim of faster matrix kernels. Reset remains unchanged by this method.
Do not add independent dirty-prefix-reset gains to these measurements; a
combined build requires its own numerical, recovery and serving evidence.

Combined archive SHA-256:
`23994803ed9d97238b0b870a82880e98520fc299dbba6116166d7ec1816850a0`.
Initial-only archive SHA-256:
`2bf7fe3e9d5994b456d4fcb429f448a3b8c46deebf0429373f9fe03934393e89`.
Failed archive SHA-256:
`320b263e883fa44f2e54436f853e85cb4fe3519d8247cbfb1870c41e60c3c0a4`.

`pending/` is a historical bounded snapshot of actual handles, source and
library hashes, successful build/CTest stages and real unit stdout. Remaining
full-model validation and serving timings are now terminal and archived in
`evidence/`, `verification.json` and `confirmation-verification.json`.
The original selected libraries and GPT-OSS/Pi checkouts remain untouched.
The full three-model 2x decode / half-TTFT goal remains active and unmet.

# Retuned native VL B2 prefill on the same library

The 64-token internal maximum gives a small repeated warm-TTFT reduction;
16 tokens is slower and rejected. This changes the internal native schedule
while preserving all 79 logical prompt tokens, 80 total physical positions,
batch 2, fresh 288x192 image encoding, checkpoint values, precision, capacity
256, output cap 32, stops and complete outputs. It is a separate native study,
not an update to frozen-profile native/vLLM ratios. The full goal remains unmet.

Both timed policies use exactly the same native library, SHA-256
`837d6f3a55598b3169be7569a00a2ab5935fd60e4643546131790a2e654e4471`.
The library's original 27 stages and 144 complete outputs already passed
in [the layout study](../interleaved-head-native/README.md). Both policies
keep the same interleaved screening index, exact 1024 seed, streaming,
partial reset, serial vision prefetch and combined threaded/striped frontend.
The only case-field difference is `chunk`. The actual plans are control
`[32,32,16]`, rejected candidate `[16,16,16,16,16]`, and candidate `[64,16]`.

Before timing, independent NumPy references exercise first/last trained
linear and full-attention layers at chunks 16/32/64 and batch 2. Twelve
profiles and 36 carried-state steps pass the unchanged
`5e-6 + 5e-5*abs(reference)` envelope. Worst normalized error is
0.6186854863, below 1. Explicit and resident outputs are exactly equal.
Inactive tokens, overwritten slots, invalid controls, rejected-state
preservation, reset and closed-graph rejection checks also pass.

All passing fixtures are saved, including their input/expected-array sizes
and hashes. Raw float arrays remain on the Mac and are omitted from Git.
The 64-token repeat reuses these immutable passed references only after
source, library/runtime identities and the first audit are checked. The final
independent audit verifies that every comparison's checkpoint, config and
tokenizer hashes match across all trials and the frozen checkpoint/config.
It still uses new sequential serving workers and freshly encodes every image.
No numerical allowances or logical workloads were changed to obtain a gain.

Initial PID 63436 exited 0 in 244.2474 s, including the reference gate and
both profile comparisons. Repeat PID 68104 exited 0 in 38.6424 s. The audit
checks 406 archived files, all reference/profile shapes, original-bound logs,
36 complete requests and recomputed raw means. Each comparison uses fresh
control/candidate/candidate/control workers with three requests each. Four
warm requests per policy exclude first use after initialization. Inference
runtimes do not intentionally overlap, and guards sample every 0.5 s.

| Internal maximum / trial | TTFT control / candidate ms | TTFT change | Decode control / candidate tokens/s per row |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 16 / initial | 321.256 / 355.937 | +10.80% | 50.098 / 49.928 |
| 64 / initial | 320.642 / 314.553 | -1.90% | 50.137 / 50.120 |
| 64 / repeat | 319.148 / 309.454 | -3.04% | 49.919 / 50.259 |

The 64-token plan reduces actual streaming partial submissions from 15 to 10
per prefill; the 16-token plan uses 25. These are implementation differences,
not isolated attribution of the entire latency change. Decode is effectively
flat: -0.03% / +0.68% for the 64-token candidate. The candidate is retained
for subsequent latency investigation; it does not silently replace the
frozen benchmark plan or establish a new comparator advantage.

Initialization, first request after initialization, separate image/prefill
clocks and peak individual child RSS are retained in raw worker records.
Caches were not flushed. Overlapping clocks must not be summed, and peak
RSS is not unique Metal memory. No observed hardware-cold end-to-end claim
is made by combining separate clocks.

The current decoder projection admission is at most 128 rows. Batch 2 with
80 prompt positions would require 160 rows and is not currently admitted;
there is no result for that profile here. A separate bounded implementation
and original-envelope numerical/serving validation would be required before
testing it. Current 16/32/64 plans all stay within the existing 128-row guard.

Initial archive SHA-256:
`c1e015b90e8c94fb84a18c2027bf989b546892815b2f6009a8730ee2f1005cae`.
Combined archive SHA-256:
`8ce7bd7387e3c085524260ae7a62c15f8f7a50dc142ba5088365cd3b4bca940f`.

# Retained CPU zero source: repeated component signal

Two actual exclusive M4 runs exited 0 in 9.28 and 9.19 seconds. Independent
verification covers 41 archived files, 126 positive-zero/padding checks and
1,344 timed executions. A retained zero vector reduces reset-plus-dependent-
GPU-read wall time against the current temporary-allocation/copy path in all
six actual-config model/batch profiles. No full-model latency or decode gain
has been measured for this policy.

Only the CPU reset source changes: one FP32 zero vector sized for the largest
state is allocated per profile before timing and reused by the existing row-
preserving memcpy loop. The GPU reader and all numeric/padding gates remain
unchanged. The initial retained-source allocation is excluded from component
timing; a serving implementation must account for it in initialization.

| Model / batch | Initial legacy → retained source ms | Repeat legacy → retained source ms | Repeat fraction |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Text / 1 | 5.4990 → 2.8531 | 4.9615 → 3.3401 | 0.6732 |
| Text / 2 | 24.8753 → 6.3341 | 22.1480 → 6.8148 | 0.3077 |
| Coder / 1 | 0.7284 → 0.5552 | 0.8694 → 0.6924 | 0.7965 |
| Coder / 2 | 2.3387 → 1.3562 | 2.1763 → 1.1828 | 0.5435 |
| VL / 1 | 4.2853 → 1.8704 | 3.7536 → 1.6714 | 0.4453 |
| VL / 2 | 9.9708 → 3.6501 | 9.4907 → 3.6834 | 0.3881 |

Both runs reduce wall time by 20.4–74.5% over model-sized profiles. A tiny
padded case is mixed (1.0792 / 0.9033 fractions), so no universal small-buffer
claim is made. Same-command GPU clearing remains the third diagnostic policy;
its results do not establish inference behavior for this CPU source policy.

Actual checkpoint configs determine all FP32 state sizes at capacity 256 and
B1/B2. GPU conditioning writes/waits occur before each sample and are excluded.
Wall timing includes reset work, dependent GPU-read encoding, submission and
completion; CPU validation is outside. Every logical element is checked for
positive-zero bits on CPU/GPU, and padding retains its sentinel. Each profile
has a 250 ms minimum warm-up, then two balanced three-policy forward/reverse
rounds of eight samples/window. Raw commands, configs, source generation,
compiled-binary omissions/hashes, guards and all windows are in `evidence/`.

Archive SHA-256:
`df2f292b28660d660f38496dd1f170b63914e450389db992ef2d01eca4dcb8a7`.

the original CPU copy and reset/snapshot semantics. Validate initialization,
rebuild/close and private-session ownership, then all original model gates and

reports.report_text:
# Retained CPU zero source: full-model investigation

Status: actual fresh candidate build, standard MPS CTest, all 19 original
model-validation stages, six trained lifecycle/recovery cases, and two complete
six-profile native ABBA trials passed. Independent audits verified 1560 archived
files and 144 complete matching requests. The candidate is not selected:
text B2 TTFT improves in both runs, but decode slows in both runs.
The overall 2x/half-TTFT goal remains unmet. No new vLLM ratio is claimed.

The repeated component study in `../reused-zero-source/README.md` found lower
reset-plus-dependent-read wall times with a retained CPU zero vector. That does
not prove an inference gain. Earlier direct, dirty-prefix, and deferred GPU
reset policies improved some TTFT profiles but slowed decode, particularly text
batch 2. This experiment retains the original CPU copy operation and removes
the allocation/initialization of a temporary vector for each state reset.

`GARNET_METAL_REUSED_ZERO_SOURCE` is optional and defaults OFF. Each session
allocates one positive-zero FP32 source sized for its largest private state
matrix. Build initialization includes this allocation. Reset immediately copies
all logical elements into every private state matrix through the existing
MetalContext Update operation. It does not defer clearing or reuse inference
state. Rebuild and close release the source; failed reset leaves the session
poisoned. Source bytes, copied bytes, and copied-state counts are exposed to the
measurement workers. Three alternative reset flags are mutually exclusive.

The six frozen profiles remain Qwen3-0.6B, Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct, and
Qwen3.5-0.8B VL, each at B1 and B2. Native control is the selected global-alpha
library. Checkpoints, output caps, stops, prompts, image bytes/resolution,
arithmetic precision, and fresh per-request image encoding are unchanged.
The comparator is not running alongside this study. Inference guards retain
their 0.5-second sampling and whole-case contention rejection.

Actual owned jobs on `/Users/zsdx/garnet-metal-investigation`:

| Job | PID | Directory |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Fresh build and original 19 gates | 55933 | logs/reused-zero-source-checks-20261015 |
| Dependency wait, lifecycle cases, native ABBA | 57066 | logs/reused-zero-source-native-20261015 |

Both jobs terminated with exit 0: validation took 1198.6444 seconds; the queue
took 1317.7301 seconds including its dependency wait. The queue checked the
exact dependency, all 19 stage exits, and the
installed source manifest before executing recovery or measurements. Session
cases cover all three trained attention/head fixtures at B1/B2, full-logit
greedy parity, immediate snapshots, private-session isolation, repeated reset,
nonfinite poisoning/recovery, rebuild, close, and reuse after close.

Fresh candidate dylib SHA-256:
`c54ff5a158ce48bce8dd36e8eec6c2e59049013d13fbdf4db22233fb4476d6ac`.
This identifies the built artifact; it is not a correctness or performance claim.

Commands (run from the investigation source's test2026/metal directory):

```text

python3 launch_reused_zero_source_checks.py ROOT ROOT/logs/reused-zero-source-checks-20261015 checks
python3 queue_reused_zero_source_profiles.py ROOT ROOT/logs/reused-zero-source-native-20261015
```

After both jobs terminate successfully, archive with
`archive_reused_zero_source_inference.py`, extract into an evidence directory,
and independently run `verify_reused_zero_source_inference.py`. The verifier
checks raw-file hashes, original/candidate identities, all original stages,
six lifecycle cases, 72 complete matching outputs, fresh VL image encoding,
and exact source/copy counts calculated from the archived model configs. Warm
means exclude each fresh worker's first request. Initialization and first
request after initialization remain separate; caches are not flushed.

Require a second successful native ABBA run before selecting this policy.
Only after a useful candidate is selected should a fresh sequential vLLM-Metal
comparison establish updated runtime ratios. Do not combine new native numbers
with the older vLLM measurements as a fresh comparison.

## Actual initial results

Warm means from four requests per policy/profile, two fresh workers per
policy. Decode is tokens/s per row; B2 aggregate throughput is twice that rate.
These are native candidate versus native control, not a new vLLM comparison.

| Model | Batch | Control TTFT ms | Retained TTFT ms | Control decode | Retained decode | Decode ratio |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Qwen3-0.6B | 1 | 50.2961 | 47.3443 | 59.0259 | 59.1685 | 1.00242 |
| Qwen3-0.6B | 2 | 80.2221 | 68.6400 | 57.6058 | 56.6991 | 0.98426 |
| Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct | 1 | 32.6529 | 32.7672 | 72.6085 | 71.8103 | 0.98901 |
| Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct | 2 | 51.6816 | 50.9187 | 70.5768 | 70.7882 | 1.00300 |
| Qwen3.5-0.8B VL | 1 | 194.8253 | 192.2141 | 48.0711 | 47.8404 | 0.99520 |
| Qwen3.5-0.8B VL | 2 | 359.7486 | 356.6088 | 44.3280 | 44.2987 | 0.99934 |

Text B2 reset-call time falls from 21.6026 to 7.0560 ms, but observed prefill
inference rises from 57.0799 to 59.7889 ms and decode falls 1.57%. Faster reset
does not imply faster decode. Scratch overhead per session is 1/2 MiB for
text and VL B1/B2, and 128/256 KiB for coder. All reset source, copied-byte,
and state counts matched the archived model configs. Full initialization,
first request after initialization, and separate observed clocks are saved in
`verification.json` and `phases.json`; overlapping clocks must not be added.

Initial archive SHA-256:
`8e12b1d61004980674545d8cccdc6669fe5c0b31a2e2bf08b9cb73f9f382a106`.

The initial independent audit was uploaded before launching confirmation
PID 80622 at `logs/reused-zero-source-confirm-native-20261015`. Confirmation
pinned the exact candidate dylib and installed source manifest, retained the
same exclusive inference guards, and exited 0 after 144.6076 seconds. Both
trials completed all six profiles on attempt 0.

## Confirmation and decision

| Model | Batch | Control TTFT ms | Retained TTFT ms | Control decode | Retained decode | Decode ratio |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Qwen3-0.6B | 1 | 48.2805 | 46.4865 | 58.4147 | 59.3680 | 1.01632 |

reports.title: Captured-query greedy head screening
reports.report_text:
# Captured-query greedy head screening

Two actual eight-bit screening trials preserve the sampled original GPU
logits/predictions and reduce head-component time across all three models at
B1/B2. The four-bit variant also passes sampled correctness but regresses
several timings, so retain the eight-bit candidate for further investigation.
An optional native integration is now under validation. No complete-generation
speedup or fresh vLLM comparison has been established for it. The full
optimization goal remains active and unmet.

## Method and precision

The original BF16 checkpoint remains the model. A derived integer index
approximates each vocabulary row using an exact power-of-two scale. CPU FP64
calculations form inflated, upward-stored residual/original/reconstructed L2
norms. Each request computes an exact 8192-row native seed and its actual
maximum, then FP32 query norms. Screening dots plus error allowances reject
rows below that seed threshold. Every retained row is recomputed from the
unchanged original BF16 bits with the original FP32 accumulation/reduction;
the native argmax runs over retained/seed values and finite private sentinels.

The public complete-logit API is unchanged. The component requires every raw
control logit to match the previously captured native GPU bits, every retained
logit to match those bits, every rejected actual logit to be strictly below
its actual seed threshold, and each selected token/nonfinite flag to match.
This establishes the sampled queries only. The inflated screening allowances
are not certified for all future input magnitudes, and no production safety
or full-model precision claim follows from these component checks.

Each model uses eight captured real native normalized states at B1, eight at
B2, and a B2 pair combining different actual states. Checkpoint/header/head
selection, original matrix bytes, captures and every input/reference digest
are checked. Heads follow runtime selection, including the coder tied embedding
and VL language embedding. No answer, prefix or image-encoder cache is used.

## Eight-bit initial and fresh-process confirmation

Numbers below average the paired per-query fractions for the eight ordinary
states per model/batch. Mixed-state correctness and timings remain in the raw
audit. Fractions below one are faster. These are complete head-component
intervals, including exact seed, bounds, screening/refinement and argmax;
normalization common to both policies is outside this component.

| Model / batch | GPU fraction initial / repeat | Wall fraction initial / repeat |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Text / 1 | 0.74775 / 0.76074 | 0.78266 / 0.79455 |
| Text / 2 | 0.74695 / 0.74779 | 0.78369 / 0.78493 |
| Coder / 1 | 0.73408 / 0.71047 | 0.76705 / 0.74801 |
| Coder / 2 | 0.76539 / 0.75085 | 0.80220 / 0.78923 |
| VL / 1 | 0.76687 / 0.77344 | 0.78759 / 0.79658 |
| VL / 2 | 0.76254 / 0.75894 | 0.78764 / 0.78487 |

The repeated GPU reduction is about 23–29%; wall reduction is about 20–25%.
These are head-only observations, not model decode TPS or TTFT. Each query
has at least 250 ms alternating warmup, two ABBA rounds, two per-window warmups
and eight raw timed submissions per window. Compilation, index preparation,
allocation, normalization and CPU validation/readback are outside timing.
No competing inference runtime or GPU probe intentionally runs simultaneously;
the existing 0.5 s guards and disk-space checks apply. Caches were not flushed.

The initial owned job 83447 exited 0 in 58.6883 s including preparation;
confirmation 84995 exited 0 in 40.1560 s, reusing only byte-verified immutable
weight/index/input assets. It still executes every GPU seed, screening,
refinement and argmax anew. Independent eight-bit audit covers 73 files,
102 query checks / 156 row-state checks and 6528 timed submissions. The earlier
queue 81590 exited 1 on the vision dependency and executed zero queries; that
failure is preserved separately from the successful trials.

Counted weight-byte fractions, including the index and seed/refinement original
weights, are about 0.527 for text/coder and 0.516 for VL. These are algorithmic
visit counts, excluding metadata, activations and cache/prefetch effects, not
measured DRAM bandwidth or total memory. The index adds one byte per original
head element; original weights remain allocated.

Initial archive SHA-256:
`99fa00cd6acb33b245fd325f423919d1596d9f0904823ec49a3b1cb206fac6fb`.
Two-trial eight-bit archive SHA-256:
`206ee8db14f84d8660f306a050994871029df5c82de6b0dbac1afc84c20f9a2b`.

## Four-bit trial: not selected

Owned PID 85879 terminated exit 0 in 54.0472 s. Its packed derived index uses
half a byte per original weight, but larger residual bounds retain many more
rows for original projection. Counted weight-byte fractions rise to 0.649–0.690.
All 51 queries / 78 row states pass the same complete-logit, every-rejection
and greedy checks; that compatibility does not make it a better optimization.

| Model / batch | GPU fraction | Wall fraction |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Text / 1 | 0.99032 | 1.01114 |
| Text / 2 | 1.02273 | 1.04624 |
| Coder / 1 | 0.92705 | 0.94578 |
| Coder / 2 | 0.96257 | 0.97669 |
| VL / 1 | 1.04333 | 1.05191 |
| VL / 2 | 1.07019 | 1.08451 |

The combined audit now verifies 112 archived files, 153 query checks / 234
row-state checks and 9792 timed submissions across the three successful trials.
Its scope separates index widths and preserves the unexecuted dependency job.
Combined archive SHA-256:
`617d07d759ee006b58ff00b3e43b7de3ba93cd7aff8c72a814bec0f2749bd67f`.

## Six-bit trial: not selected

Owned PID 87355 at `logs/screened-head-int6-20261015` terminated exit 0 after
63.9366 s, following all prior terminal trials and their independent audit. A
pre-timing GPU roundtrip reconstructed every derived index element exactly
against CPU rounding of the original weight/scale, covering packed-word
boundaries as well as the captured-query checks. All 51 queries pass again.

| Model / batch | GPU fraction | Wall fraction |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Text / 1 | 0.99977 | 1.03024 |
| Text / 2 | 1.01413 | 1.04459 |
| Coder / 1 | 0.99411 | 1.02326 |
| Coder / 2 | 1.01995 | 1.04732 |
| VL / 1 | 1.02168 | 1.04022 |
| VL / 2 | 1.03611 | 1.05730 |

Counted weight-byte fractions fall to 0.396–0.411, while wall time is 2.3–5.7%
higher than the original complete head. Reduced byte visits alone do not prove
a faster kernel. This six-bit layout is rejected for integration without
seeking a favorable repeat. The eight-bit route remains the repeated candidate.

The final audit verifies 151 archived files, four successful trials, 204 query
checks / 312 row-state checks and 13,056 timed submissions. Every complete
six-bit index reconstruction is recorded separately. All original/generated
sources and input/index/reference identities remain preserved by trial.
All-width archive SHA-256:
`6a2ce969d7ed032e0b28b74989285c50923bc82a852b7052ba7f4a0f878fe419`.

## Bounded strict-math eight-bit trial

Owned PID 89166 exited 0 after 40.9025 s. Screening now uses a separate
`fastMathEnabled=NO` Metal library; the original full/seed projection retains
its original math policy. Nonfinite inputs, absolute input values above 1e6,
and norms outside [1e-10, 1e10] force full original-row refinement. Metadata
must be finite and bounded. This limits screening admission; it does not
establish a universal numerical proof for all possible admitted queries.

All 51 captured queries pass retained-bit, every-rejection and greedy checks.
Another 33 cases check zero, tiny, large, NaN, infinity and mixed safe/unsafe
batch rows against the original full projection and its error flags.

| Model / batch | GPU fraction | Wall fraction |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Text / 1 | 0.74387 | 0.78045 |
| Text / 2 | 0.77047 | 0.81050 |
| Coder / 1 | 0.73468 | 0.77126 |
| Coder / 2 | 0.76899 | 0.80989 |
| VL / 1 | 0.77382 | 0.79698 |
| VL / 2 | 0.77270 | 0.79872 |

These are head-component intervals, not whole-model TPS or TTFT. Combined
component audit: 187 archived files, five successful trials, 255 query checks,
390 row states, 16,320 timed submissions and the 33 fallback checks.
Archive SHA-256:
`533e97172600b595df9f63f3ad02e6e6412d4f6ed944b2758f6dc5c6094261c0`.

## Optional native integration: validation in progress

`GARNET_METAL_SCREENED_HEAD` defaults OFF. Initialization builds the derived
index from the unchanged original head; unsupported shapes or metadata use
the existing head. Greedy B1/B2 session prediction uses the seed, screening,
original retained-row refinement and original argmax. Public full-logit graph
execution continues to compute all logits. The index increases resident
memory and initialization work; inference measurements must report these.

Owned validation PID 91274 exited 0 after 1219.3464 s. All 20 stages passed:
the original 19 model-validation stages plus all 51 trained-head queries
through the native context, including original full-logit bits, retained bits,
every rejected row and predictions. Queued PID 3415 verified that terminal
status and the pinned source manifest, then began trained session/recovery
checks before six-profile ABBA. It subsequently exited 0 with six recovery
cases and 72 complete matching requests. Initial whole-model decode gains
are 7.5–10.4%; fresh-process confirmation PID 17037 also exited 0, with
8.2–10.1% decode gains and another 72 complete matching requests.
Those inference observations are recorded separately in
[the native study](../screened-head-inference/README.md).
A fresh matched comparator study is running as PID 20154. The component
timings alone do not establish serving performance.

python3 archive_screened_head.py ROOT ARCHIVE

weights and FP32 accumulation. Public complete logits retain the full head.

in [the component study](../screened-head/README.md).

foreign ownership and unsupported batch fallback. Actual session tests check

and recovery, close/rebuild and actual screening counts.

raw worker logs, 72 complete matching outputs, screening counters, fresh

Four profiles meet 2x decode in this cohort: all B2 profiles and VL B1. VL B1
is only 2.011x, so this is not a repeated threshold claim. Text/coder B1 remain
below 2x and no profile reaches half warm TTFT. A fresh whole-cohort comparator
repeat is still required before claiming a robust target win.

# Screened head plus ordered prefill and partial cache reset

All 26 validation stages passed, followed by two six-profile native ABBA
trials. Independent audits cover 1750 archived files, the original 19 stages,
51 actual trained-head queries, six trained-head session cases, six bounded
reset/recovery cases and 144 complete matching generated outputs across the
two trials. Every actual prefill submission and reset byte count is checked.
The full 2x vLLM / half-TTFT goal remains unmet. This is a native comparison;
no fresh vLLM ratio is claimed for this combination.

The control is the validated screened-head library. The candidate additionally
enables `GARNET_METAL_PREFILL_STREAM` and `GARNET_METAL_DIRTY_PREFIX_RESET`.
Streaming submits ordered prefill work every four layers while CPU encoding
continues. Reset clears the known written KV prefix and fully clears unknown
writers and linear-state layouts. It does not reuse a prior request's prefix,
answer, or image encoding. Every new request still clears all affected state.
All three options remain OFF by default; the original selected builds and
GPT-OSS/Pi/original Mac checkouts are preserved.

## Actual warm measurements

Four warm requests per policy/profile from two fresh sequential workers in
ABBA order. Each worker's first request is excluded. TPS is per batch row;
B2 aggregate throughput is twice this rate. Prompt/image bytes, checkpoint
values, FP32 arithmetic/activations/KV, output caps and stop semantics remain
unchanged. Both VL policies use the same combined CPU frontend and freshly
encode each image. No competing inference runtime intentionally overlaps;
guards sample every 0.5 seconds.

decode changes are smaller. This tradeoff merits further latency work rather
than declaring an all-metric win or rejecting latency gains solely because of
a small decode loss. An older vLLM cohort cannot establish a new matched ratio.

## Numerical, lifecycle and performance scope

The added native context gate checks retained FP32 bits, every rejected head
row and predictions against actual trained references. CTests cover screened
head bounds/nonfinite fallback, ties outside the seed, abort/ownership and
padding, ordered prefill submissions and bounded reset behavior. The original
trained layer, private-KV, serving, vision, exact-tail and extended-prefill

nonfinite poisoning, full reset, private state and screened close/rebuild.

`phases.json` and `confirmation-phases.json` preserve observed init, first
request after init, warm reset/prefill/decode clocks, individual child RSS and
actual counters. GPU/encode/wait clocks overlap and must not be added. Vision
includes reset. Individual child RSS is not aggregate or unique GPU memory.
OS/driver caches were not flushed, and no sum is presented as an observed
hardware-cold latency.

15.2886 ms while host preparation rose only from 0.1590 to 0.1682 ms.

0.1661 ms preparation. This locates most observed extra time in the GPU
interval; it does not establish its kernel/cache/power cause. Small host-only
tracking changes cannot recover the whole measured decode difference.

# Direct exact-seed comparison and native candidate

Two actual same-process trials compare the original 8192-row screened-head
seed against a 1024-row seed. Both use original BF16/FP32 exact seed scores,
the same strict-math INT8-derived filtering index, unchanged error allowances
and original BF16/FP32 refinement. All captured predictions match. The smaller
seed reduces component GPU/wall time in all six ordinary model/batch groups
in both trials; the VL B1 improvement is small and variable. This is a private
greedy-head experiment, not a replacement quantized model.

The complete raw full-logit kernel runs before admission and matches captured
original GPU bits. Both seed policies then check every retained score and every
rejected score against the original full logits, and check greedy/error output.
The candidate additionally executes the existing zero/tiny/large/NaN/Inf/mixed
unsafe-input fallback checks. No numerical allowances were widened. These are
sampled learned-query checks, not certification for all future inputs.

Initial PID 97810 exited 0 in 38.1126 s; repeat PID 98647 exited 0 in 38.1690 s.
The independent audit checks 80 archived files, exact generated code and input
hashes, 102 captured-query pairs (156 row states per policy), 66 candidate
unsafe-input checks, 6,528 raw timed executions, guards and both ABBA rounds.
Each query uses common warming for at least 250 ms, then two ABBA rounds of
eight samples per window. Both timed policies include seed projection,
threshold/norm preparation, screening/refinement and the original argmax in
one command buffer. The timing control is the 8192-row screening policy.

The following means average each ordinary captured step's candidate/control
fraction, excluding the separate mixed-row fixture. Lower is better.

| Model / batch | GPU fraction initial / repeat | Wall fraction initial / repeat |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Qwen3-0.6B / 1 | 0.95967 / 0.96025 | 0.96338 / 0.96418 |
| Qwen3-0.6B / 2 | 0.96129 / 0.95863 | 0.96533 / 0.96340 |
| Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct / 1 | 0.96693 / 0.96227 | 0.97613 / 0.97124 |
| Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct / 2 | 0.95636 / 0.95870 | 0.96680 / 0.97422 |
| Qwen3.5-0.8B / 1 | 0.97696 / 0.99254 | 0.97714 / 0.99265 |
| Qwen3.5-0.8B / 2 | 0.96117 / 0.96923 | 0.96489 / 0.96898 |

## Optional native integration under validation

`GARNET_METAL_SMALL_SCREEN_SEED` defaults OFF and requires SCREENED_HEAD.
It changes the exact seed allocation/dispatch to 1024 rows and supplies that
same constant to the strict Metal compiler. The resulting shader functions
match the audited 1024 component byte for byte after macro substitution.
Original head-shape/batch admission and fallback policies remain unchanged.
The native context records the actual seed dispatch width. Decoder sessions
publish it after successful submission, clear it on run/reset/close/abort,
and expose it for per-prediction benchmark checks. Legacy 8192 controls report
their frozen configured width; the new candidate reports the actual counter.

Synthetic and trained tests compare rejected scores against the smaller actual
seed threshold, rather than the old 8192-row threshold. They verify actual
seed width, retained bits, outside-seed lowest ties and recovery. Additional
trained session checks observe the new property through generic-logit and
float-head fallback, nonfinite poison, reset, private sessions, close and rebuild.

All previous native trials were terminal and archived before source changes.
Installation pins 18 files and preserves 13 verified existing originals from
base `09893ade4d80d39e602000b0e716ff878f82c44d`. An initial staging attempt
found an absent generator script and stopped before extraction. It was
reclassified as a new file; the existing partial backup was verified and
reused without deleting any files. All installed hashes then matched.

Validation PID 99758 subsequently passed all 27 stages. Native PID 294 and
fresh confirmation PID 26793 both completed all six profiles. Independent
audits verify 144 complete outputs and actual seed widths. The
[native measurements](../small-seed-native/README.md) show small, mixed gains:
text B2 decode improves 1.9–2.4%, while text B1 TTFT and VL B2 TTFT regress
twice. The optional policy remains OFF by default. These component ratios
are not whole-model gains; no new vLLM ratio is claimed and the full goal
remains unmet.

# Exact screened-head seed-width exploration

Actual PID 94813 exited 0 in 147.8686 s. Four sequential component workers
test exact seed widths 8192, 1024, 4096 and 32768 against the original full
BF16/FP32 head. All 204 captured-query checks, 312 row states and 132 unsafe
input/fallback checks pass. Every retained score is bit-identical to full
projection; every sampled rejected score is below the actual seed threshold;
greedy predictions match. The existing strict-math bounds and original
refinement are unchanged. This does not certify bounds for all future inputs.

Each width uses the same byte-verified immutable trained head/query assets.
The derived INT8 index only filters rows; it is not a replacement model.
The audit reconstructs exact shader/harness bytes, checks 143 archived files,
source and asset hashes, guard traces, ABBA ordering and 13,056 raw timed
component executions, with eight samples per window and two ABBA rounds.

excluding the separate mixed-row check. Each fraction is screened component
wall time / original full-head wall time within that width's worker.

# Original-order vision context prefetch

Two actual sequential component trials admit the eight-key prefetch kernel
with bit-identical FP32 output. Loads are prefetched while the FMA accumulator
retains the original key order. Softmax is unchanged. The separate Metal library
disables fast math. This avoids the changed reduction order that failed the
earlier trained-grid parallel-context experiment.

The first trial measures five variants over 24 shapes; the independent repeat
measures the selected eight-key variant over the same 24 shapes. All 144
shape/variant checks pass exact output-bit equality and the original FP64
reference bound across four input generations. There are 23,040 timed
submissions, with raw GPU and wall observations preserved in evidence.

For the serving shape (216 tokens, 12 heads, head dimension 64), combined
softmax/context GPU time falls 19.7–34.7% at B1 and 19.4–26.3% at B2 across
the two trials. Wall time falls 14.9–27.1% and 16.7–22.7%, respectively.
These are component measurements, not whole-model speed or TTFT gains.

An optional native integration is OFF by default and admits only this trained
shape at batch 1 or 2; other shapes retain the original route. The actual
trained full-grid gate subsequently passed bit-identical embedding values at
both batches, including two fresh encodes and small-grid fallback/close counts.
Full original-model validation subsequently passed all 27 stages. Two
six-profile native trials show repeated 2.9–3.8% VL TTFT reductions, unchanged
decode and mixed text/coder changes. See [the native evidence](../serial-vision-native/README.md).
These component ratios are not whole-model gains, and no fresh vLLM result
is claimed.

Actual component jobs: PID 62873 exited 0 in 58.6223 s; PID 64132 exited 0 in
18.3778 s. The combined archive SHA-256 is
`3348dc7c205ce8db5c946352d747ef03e61f9eb1155772d60fd37f3e33108351`.
The independent audit checks 51 archived files. Commands and exact generated
shader/harness sources are retained with the raw observations.

The optional vision prefetch kernel reduces image-to-first-token latency in
two actual six-profile native trials. It does not deliver a decode speedup
or establish a new vLLM ratio. Text B1 TTFT regresses in both trials; this
candidate remains OFF by default rather than replacing the general bundle.
The overall 2x-decode/half-TTFT goal remains unmet.

Control and candidate both enable screened greedy heads, ordered prefill
streaming and partial cache reset. Only the candidate enables serial vision
prefetch. Original learned weights, FP32 contraction order, image patches,
prompts, token caps, stop semantics and complete generated outputs remain
unchanged. The separate shader library disables fast math. Admission is
limited to 216 vision tokens, hidden width 768, 12 heads and batch 1 or 2;
other shapes use the original route.

original 19, the actual trained full-grid gate, 51 trained screening queries,
and six recovery stage suites. The full-grid gate checks B1/B2, small-grid
fallback, two fresh encodes per policy and cleared counters after close.

matching outputs across the two trials. Each trial runs fresh sequential
control/candidate/candidate/control workers, three requests per worker. The
first request is reported separately; four warm requests per policy/profile
form each mean. Inference runtimes never intentionally overlap; guards sample
every 0.5 s. Every image request performs fresh encoding with the same combined

# Shape-selected two-output native integration: validation running

This private candidate uses the [three selected geometries](../two-matrix-probe/README.md)
and retains the current four-output compact kernel for every other shape.
Original BF16 learned bits, compact payload, FP32 arithmetic, input lane order,
original fallback and all prefill paths are unchanged. The rejected MLP graph
route remains disabled. This is a decode experiment; it does not address the
remaining first-token-latency gap by itself.

The [preparation record](preparation.json) freezes1,275 copied source files.
Eight existing copies change: context/header, session/header, backend marker,
two benchmark workers and the coalesced primitive. One generated shader is
added. The current retained Mac source/build and protected GPT-OSS/Pi checkouts
are not modified. New private tree:
`/Users/zsdx/garnet-metal-investigation/shape-selected-two-investigation-20261015`.

The primitive keeps all80 original cases and adds24 cases for selected shapes.
It verifies actual dispatch counts, raw original output bits, unchanged FP64
envelope, ownership, abort/recovery and decode-only routing. It also checks
that abort clears the added counters. The fresh build and seven CTests have
completed; all28 trained/native stages are still running under exact PID42435.
No complete validation or full-model performance result is claimed yet.

Controller PID47970 polls that exact handle. After a terminal record it freezes
success or failure, requires an independent frozen-evidence audit of all28
original stages, then dispatches native ABBA only after success. A missing
handle without terminal evidence is an error; observation timeouts do not
restart validation. Controller success means a benchmark was dispatched,
not that it passed or that the performance goal was achieved.

The prepared benchmark uses all six original model/batch profiles and72
complete generated outputs, sequential control/candidate/candidate/control
workers, one first-after-init and two warm requests per worker. It independently
derives expected selected-route counts from original checkpoint tensor headers.
Both source closures, learned assets, commands, monitors, first/warm/init/RSS
and all complete tokens must remain auditable. The retained c186 native library
is the performance control; the original73c10e5d trained reference has a

# Full-shape BF16 decode specialization: head regressions, mixed body gains

Two actual sequential component trials exited 0. The independent audit verified
50 archived files, 34 canonical matrix identities, 136 matrix/batch configurations,
142,836 bit-exact validated executions and 26,112 timed executions. Arithmetic,
learned values and precision are unchanged. No serving change is selected and
no new inference or vLLM speedup is claimed. The full goal remains unmet.

Unlike the earlier single-row experiment, this specializes batch, input width,
output width and both physical strides through Metal function constants. Mode 1
retains all bounds; mode 2 additionally removes output-tail branches only when
N is divisible by the selected kernel's complete tile width, 4 for small-output
and 16 otherwise. Original shaders and default compilation remain the control.
All 34 learned/synthetic fixtures run at B1/B2 with fresh original, negated,
half and doubled FP32 inputs. Every warm/timed result and padding bit matches
the original. The independent FP64 maximum error/bound ratio is 0.0100017 under
the original gamma(ceil(K/32)+32)*sumabs+1e-7 bound.

The native comparison measures mode 2 versus the original; the dimensions
comparison measures mode 2 versus dimension-only mode 1. Both retain two ABBA
rounds, 12 samples per window and at least 250 ms common checked warmup. Raw
arrays and both comparisons are independently recomputed in `verification.json`.

The following are unweighted trained-matrix component wall-time pools, with
synthetic fixtures excluded. The vocabulary head is separate from the first
decoder-layer body matrices. Fractions above 1 are slower. These are not model
TPS or TTFT ratios, and the single sampled layer is not a whole-model weighting.

| Model | Batch | Body candidate/control, initial / repeat | Head candidate/control, initial / repeat |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Qwen3-0.6B | 1 | 1.02904 / 0.98322 | 1.05425 / 1.05790 |
| Qwen3-0.6B | 2 | 1.07293 / 0.95672 | 1.04704 / 1.04993 |
| Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct | 1 | 0.97121 / 1.00500 | 1.11790 / 1.13078 |
| Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct | 2 | 0.96546 / 0.96922 | 1.03133 / 1.01921 |
| Qwen3.5-0.8B | 1 | 0.96907 / 0.94224 | 1.01769 / 0.98809 |
| Qwen3.5-0.8B | 2 | 0.99904 / 0.97018 | 1.03958 / 1.04548 |

A blanket all-projection change is not justified: text body changes direction,
coder B1 body changes direction, and all text/coder heads slow in both trials.
Coder B2 body and VL B1 body have repeated lower times. A body-only serving
candidate could test whether these effects survive a real graph, but that has
not been implemented or measured by this study. No cache, occupancy or register
cause for these timing changes has been proven.

Pipeline creation is outside component projection clocks. Creating two
specialized pipelines for each of 68 matrix/batch configurations took an
observed summed 1048.5767 ms initially and 19.0287 ms on repeat, maximum single
configuration 69.9800/0.5993 ms. Compiler/OS caches are not flushed; this is not
a hardware-cold measurement. Any serving experiment must include this setup
in initialization or first-use costs rather than hiding it.

serving library remain unchanged.

# Native exact seed 1024 versus 8192: small mixed gains

The optional smaller seed passes the complete native gates and 144 complete
outputs across two trials. Some decode gains repeat, especially text B2, but
TTFT is mixed and text B1 / VL B2 regress in both runs. This does not establish
a general serving improvement or a new vLLM target ratio. The option remains
OFF by default, and the full 2x-decode/half-TTFT goal remains unmet.

Both policies use the same screened head, ordered prefill streaming, partial
cache reset and original-order vision prefetch. The candidate changes only
the exact seed width from 8192 to 1024 plus observation counters. Learned
checkpoint values, bounds, FP32 refinement, prompts, images, token caps,
stop rules, complete outputs and fresh image encoding remain frozen. Both
image policies use the same threaded decode / exact striped resize frontend.

Validation PID 99758 exited 0 in 1305.9734 s. All 27 stages pass: the original
19 model/cache/vision/prefill stages, bit-identical trained full-grid vision,
51 actual trained head queries and six trained recovery stage suites. The
head gates compare every rejected original score with the smaller actual
seed's threshold. Context tests check the actual 1024 dispatch width and
Begin/Abort recovery. Trained session tests check the published width through
normal prediction, float-head fallback, generic logits, nonfinite poison,
reset, close/rebuild and private-session isolation. All candidate predictions
in the serving trials record actual seed width 1024 and one head dispatch;
legacy controls report their frozen 8192 configuration.

Initial native PID 294 exited 0 in 1455.1244 s including the validation wait.
Fresh confirmation PID 26793 exited 0 in 160.5934 s. Independent audits check
1,845 archived files, all gates, all 144 complete outputs and every actual
seed/prefill/reset/vision counter. Each profile uses fresh sequential
control/candidate/candidate/control workers. Each worker makes three requests;
the first is separate, and the remaining four warm requests per policy form
the mean. Inference runtimes never intentionally overlap; guards sample at
0.5-second intervals. The original Mac checkout, GPT-OSS and Pi checkouts are
preserved.

# Dependent MLP with existing reference rounding: audited, six profiles excluded

Hypothesis: evaluate the same complete gate/up-SiLU-down workload using
the original trained reference's stage boundaries, correcting the previous
whole-chain FP64 reference mismatch. Four trained blocks remain: text/coder
layer 0 and VL layers 0/3. VL blocks are sequential separate graph calls.
Inputs, actual BF16 checkpoint bits expanded losslessly to FP32, FP32 graph
arithmetic, native library, placeholder/constant policies and all tolerance
coefficients are unchanged. This is a reference correction, not a speed
optimization or a repeat of an identical experiment.

The generated harness makes only three reference substitutions: gate/up dot
products accumulate wider then cast to FP32; activation executes in FP32;
the wider down dot casts to FP32. The verifier reconstructs these changes
and checks the frozen `reference_dense.py` semantics. Historical JSON names
`fp64_worst` and `control_fp64_worst` remain, but here mean error against this
stage-rounded reference, normalized by the unchanged 5e-6+5e-5*abs(reference)
bound. Values over 1 fail. Native comparison uses its separate unchanged bound.

PID52956 is terminal exit 0 (38.223373 s). Audit: 36 files, 48 numerical
records, 12 first graph calls and 384 admitted timed submissions. Six profiles
still fail the reference on high-amplitude alternating pattern 1 in BOTH
unchanged native and graph: text B1/B2 and coder B2, each weight policy.
Worst native/graph normalized reference errors are 2.420709/2.529337,
2.887737/3.140284 and 1.308438/1.286163 respectively. These profiles have no
timing windows. They remain numerical limitations; changing reference
rounding did not make all tests pass.

All 48 graph/native comparisons pass, worst ratio 0.473572. That relative
agreement is not a waiver of independent reference failures. Only coder B1
and VL profiles pass every component gate and are timed below:

reports.title: Exact-coordinate parallel Pillow resize
reports.report_text:
# Exact-coordinate parallel Pillow resize

Two actual CPU trials preserve complete resized RGB and FP32 patch bytes and
reduce fresh preparation by about 7.5–7.9 ms. Their independent audit covers
36 archived files, 1920 compatibility comparisons and 384 timed preparations of
the frozen image. The first actual image-plus-text study passed 48 complete
matching requests and shows lower native warm TTFT at both batches. Confirmation
also passed: the combined independent audit covers 687 archived files, two actual
GPU precision audits and 96 complete matching requests. The full goal remains unmet.

| Batch | Initial selected → strips ms | Repeat selected → strips ms |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 49.3286 → 41.8515 | 49.4151 → 41.9380 |
| 2 | 51.6332 → 43.9928 | 51.8046 → 43.9359 |

Each CPU sample includes fresh source opening/decoding, preprocessing, patch/RGB
file writes and hashes. Both trials have two ABBA rounds per batch and twelve
samples per window, after common warming. These are CPU preparation times, not
model TTFT or decode rates. OS caches were not flushed.

## Method and exactness limits

The optional module uses a persistent four-worker CPU thread pool and Pillow's
own bicubic resizer on vertical output strips. It admits only Pillow 12.3.0 RGB
images with bounded dimensions, at least 262144 source pixels, a changed height,
and a reduced vertical scale denominator that is a power of two. Output cuts
are multiples of the reduced denominator, so source-box boundaries are integers.
Other geometries/modes/versions retain the selected Pillow operation.

Pillow's [resize wrapper](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/python-pillow/Pillow/12.3.0/src/_imaging.c)
passes float32 boxes. Integer boundaries within the admission bounds are exact
there. Its [resampler](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/python-pillow/Pillow/12.3.0/src/libImaging/Resample.c)
computes centers in double precision. The admitted dyadic scale and bounded
integer coordinates preserve center arithmetic exactly. Horizontal resize
geometry remains unchanged, and Pillow keeps the source-row filter halos for
each strip. This restriction avoids arbitrary fractional boxes that could
change coefficients or pixels. It is not a claim about all Pillow versions.

The actual source is 1372×1818 pixels; resized output remains **192×288 pixels
(width×height)**. The vertical scale is 101/16. Four output strips span
64/80/64/80 rows, with integer source boundaries 0/404/909/1313/1818. The same
Pillow filter, dimensions, RGB bytes, normalization order and FP32 patch layout
remain. Source images are fully decoded before concurrent readers start, and
all readers are drained before the caller may close the source.

Each compatibility run covers five source sizes, RGB/RGBA/L, all eight EXIF
orientations, B1/B2, temporal sizes 1/2 and two mean/std settings. Independent
source opens prevent shared lazy loading from hiding mistakes. All 960 cases
match every RGB and FP32 patch byte; 96 actually take the strip route and 864
exercise fallback. Every timed real-image candidate takes the strip route and
matches the canonical patch hash. No image or encoder output is reused.

Actual owned CPU jobs:

| Trial | PID | Exit | Wall seconds |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| striped-frame-probe-20261015 | 17019 | 0 | 58.9717 |
| striped-frame-probe-confirm-20261015 | 19417 | 0 | 58.9505 |

Initial archive SHA-256:
`74321746a280938baade54a9a261f99851c08f53308e3468ea71c3b194355848`.
Combined CPU archive SHA-256:
`3c3183f873854919801f1a872c04e1063e845373b69e63113920d651419e0e26`.
Raw timing arrays, compatibility records, executed sources and independent
verification are under `cpu/`.

## Actual inference study

Owned PID 21826 at `logs/striped-frame-inference-20261015` performs a fresh actual
FP32 GPU dtype audit, then B1/B2 sequential factorial ABBA comparisons. Both
Garnet and vLLM-Metal receive selected or striped common preprocessing equally.
Garnet uses the same selected global-alpha dylib for both policies, SHA-256
`887b70f521d5af7f948bcb32a2cf94842377e2ecb828bc9280ffb38af6fe058f`.
The optional body-shape route is disabled. Models, arithmetic precision,
prompts, pixels, output caps and stops remain frozen. Images are freshly
encoded and cross-request prefix/speculative reuse is disabled. Complete
outputs and unique comparator encoder identities must match before accepting
timings. Initialization, frontend setup and first request after initialization
are separate from warm means. Competing inference runtimes never intentionally
run simultaneously, and the existing guard and contention retries remain.

This remains an additional matched-FP32 study: learned values restore exactly,
while native compact BF16 weight storage and comparator expanded FP32 storage
have different widths and memory traffic. It is not a stock BF16 claim.
The selected common frontend and GPU sources remain unchanged pending evidence.

The initial inference job terminated exit 0 after 472.4574 seconds. Its actual
FP32 GPU audit and all 48 complete requests passed independent verification
over 353 archived files. No profile required a contention retry. Each runtime,
frontend and batch has four warm requests from two fresh workers; first requests
are excluded. Decode is tokens/s per row, with B2 aggregate twice that rate.

| Batch / frontend | Garnet TTFT ms | vLLM TTFT ms | Garnet decode | vLLM decode | Decode ratio | TTFT fraction |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 selected | 205.1015 | 263.4634 | 48.2790 | 25.9573 | 1.85994 | 0.77848 |
| 1 strips | 199.7885 | 256.8373 | 48.3099 | 26.0940 | 1.85138 | 0.77788 |
| 2 selected | 359.3341 | 433.8292 | 44.7026 | 17.1509 | 2.60644 | 0.82828 |
| 2 strips | 355.1581 | 435.8267 | 44.6909 | 17.2465 | 2.59131 | 0.81491 |

Native warm TTFT is 2.59%/1.16% lower at B1/B2. Actual native preparation falls
45.4195→37.4046 and 48.7921→41.3298 ms. Comparator preparation also falls, but
its B2 endpoint TTFT increases 0.46%; other model/protocol variation offsets
the CPU saving there. No decode benefit is established by this CPU change.
Neither batch achieves half TTFT, and B1 decode remains below 2x. This VL-only
study does not replace the last full three-model comparison or permit combining
new native numbers with older comparator measurements.

Frontend setup is about 2 ms for strips and is reported separately from worker
initialization. Its lazy thread startup is included in the first actual request.
Native first-request TTFT after initialization is nearly flat at B1
(355.4569→355.3138 ms) and lower at B2 (569.4517→557.6288 ms). All initialization,
first-request and warm observations remain separate in `inference/verification.json`;
OS/driver caches are not flushed, so these are not hardware-cold observations.

Initial inference archive SHA-256:
`7b00d410349c8c5b699640402bda245c83e495b59e30139ea0af14b413add89a`.
The independent initial audit was uploaded before confirmation PID 30402 at
`logs/striped-frame-inference-confirm-20261015`. Confirmation repeats the actual
GPU dtype audit and both B1/B2 factorial comparisons with the same source,
selected GPU library, canonical image bytes, stops and caps.

Confirmation PID 30402 terminated exit 0 after 467.3233 seconds. Its warm means:

| Batch / frontend | Garnet TTFT ms | vLLM TTFT ms | Garnet decode | vLLM decode | Decode ratio | TTFT fraction |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 selected | 201.0927 | 265.5660 | 48.4578 | 26.2653 | 1.84494 | 0.75722 |
| 1 strips | 198.2176 | 269.8489 | 48.2821 | 26.3806 | 1.83021 | 0.73455 |
| 2 selected | 361.3753 | 427.6725 | 44.7077 | 17.1059 | 2.61359 | 0.84498 |
| 2 strips | 356.5498 | 438.1709 | 44.5479 | 16.8981 | 2.63626 | 0.81372 |

Native TTFT falls 1.43%/1.34% at B1/B2 in confirmation, while decode is 0.36%
lower at both batches. Comparator TTFT rises 1.61%/2.45%, despite preparation
falling about 7.0/8.9 ms. Thus CPU preparation savings repeat, but a consistent
endpoint benefit on both runtimes is not established. The selected frontend
remains unchanged; the optional strips are being tested together with threaded
WebP decoding in a separate study. No results from the two methods are added
together to claim an inference gain.

Confirmation native initialization is 4.1129→4.1164 s at B1 and
4.1230→4.1421 s at B2. First-request TTFT after initialization is
353.8181→335.8964 ms and 569.7545→548.0206 ms. Comparator initialization and
first-request measurements are recorded separately in the verified JSON;

`d1a909f579d0e2ab276de6887200e41f96c63470d456129c62d076a54a6450ed`.

# Combined threaded WebP decode and exact striped resize

Two actual CPU trials reduce fresh image preparation by 37–39%, about 19–20 ms,
while preserving all resized RGB and FP32 patch bytes. The independent audit
covers 56 archived files, 1912 compatibility comparisons and 384 timed frozen
image preparations. These are CPU times, not model TTFT or decode gains.

| Batch | Initial selected → combined ms | Confirmation selected → combined ms |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 49.4648 → 30.2425 | 49.7787 → 30.2271 |
| 2 | 51.8288 → 32.6303 | 51.9895 → 32.3147 |

The optional frontend composes the previously tested conservative static-WebP
decoder with the restricted exact-coordinate Pillow strip resizer. Each request
reads and decodes the original source anew. Metadata, animation and unsupported
WebP containers fall back to Pillow decoding; ineligible resize geometries fall
back to the original resize. The frozen image takes both accelerated routes.
No cached image pixels, embeddings, prefix state or speculative decoding is used.

Each compatibility trial covers 239 fixtures and 956 comparisons, including
lossless/lossy images, RGB/RGBA/L, EXIF orientations, animation and PNG/JPEG/BMP
fallbacks. There are 148 parallel resize calls and 808 resize fallbacks per trial.
Each timed batch has two ABBA rounds with 12 samples per window and common warmup.
Writes and hashes remain inside preparation timing. OS caches were not flushed.

The existing libwebp bridge SHA-256 is
`3c86ac196227b3729477cd24704ea4cea4e796fe5f9933c7a5a20361a32804a3`.
Pillow is pinned to 12.3.0 for the strip path. Input is 1372×1818 and resized
output is 192×288, width×height. GPU library and model data remain unchanged.

Owned CPU jobs terminated exit 0: PID 37557 took 135.0796 s including its wait
for the prior inference confirmation; PID 41308 took 74.7292 s. They did not
overlap inference. Combined archive SHA-256:
`3aa75dc363ec7339bcc47277b87a5d64343d115c724ac4135cfa4661d492a939`.

their independent audit. A fresh real GPU FP32 audit precedes sequential B1/B2
factorial comparisons: selected and combined frontends apply equally to Garnet
and vLLM-Metal, with all complete normalized outputs and canonical pixel hashes
required to match. Guards sample every 0.5 s and require a quiet interval.
Initialization, frontend setup and first request after initialization remain
separate from warm means.

## Initial actual inference results

verified 360 archived files, one actual FP32 GPU audit and 48 complete matching

Hypothesis: reduce per-SIMD accumulator work while preserving the existing
compact four-output storage. Two adjacent SIMDs select the lower/upper half
of the same original quad. BF16 learned bits, 32-lane K partition, explicit
FP32 FMA and original fallback/prefill paths remain unchanged. Private copies
add actual route counters; there is no precision lowering or weight repacking.

in19.949173s. Each audited cohort passed72 mandatory exact-bit/FP64/native
envelope records and189 safety profiles before1,152 timed ABBA samples.

patterns and64/128/256-thread policies. Binary, runtime source, flags, assets
and versions match across cohorts; binary SHA256:
`2c091311f4a419f23cec945840535a5239be09e2030768c334d4997d0efeb541`.

Six of18 policies improved wall time in both runs; seven improved GPU time;
five improved both directions in both runs. Several gains are very small and
