reports.title: Exact GPU packing experiments
reports.report_text:
# Exact GPU packing experiments

These are isolated native Metal matrix-vector experiments on the same M4
Mac mini and original BF16 checkpoint values. They do not measure full model
inference, generated outputs, tokens/s, TTFT or a vLLM advantage. No codec was
integrated into Garnet's production backend.

All four suites exited zero. Each suite used all three existing checkpoints,
their complete output head and first-layer MLP down projection, batches 1/2,
and the unchanged native raw BF16 decode kernel as its control. Each model
process completed before the next started. Pre/post process guards retained
the verified WorldSense service and rejected other inference workers.

The CPU roundtrip checked every prepared matrix value. GPU reconstruction
checked those complete matrices, all 65,536 BF16 bit patterns and a random
4097-value tail. All 48 projection comparisons across the four suites were
bit-exact against the raw kernel for the deterministic FP32 test inputs.
Signed zeros, subnormals, infinities and NaN payload bits were covered by the
bit reconstruction tests. The nonfinite pattern cases were not multiplied.
These checks do not replace full-model numerical and generated-output tests.

Each matrix/batch had four ABBA rounds, with three untimed warm operations and
12 measured operations per policy window. A command buffer completed before
the next operation. GPU and wall medians are retained separately. Packing,
compilation, checkpoint/file hashing and CPU validation are outside GPU times.
Both raw and packed buffers were resident during the microbenchmark; the
allocation is not a claim about a production codec's memory footprint.

## Complete output-head results

Each number below is raw GPU time divided by packed GPU time within the same
suite. Values below 1 mean the packed kernel was slower. The controls used
the same four-output-columns-per-SIMD-group native kernel throughout.

| Model | Batch | 3-bit SIMD prefix | 3-bit rank/popcount | 4-bit fast path, four columns | 4-bit fast path, one column |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Qwen3.5-0.8B | 1 | 0.575 | 0.468 | 0.843 | 0.789 |
| Qwen3.5-0.8B | 2 | 0.562 | 0.459 | 0.842 | 0.698 |
| Qwen3-0.6B | 1 | 0.599 | 0.474 | 0.867 | 0.803 |
| Qwen3-0.6B | 2 | 0.591 | 0.463 | 0.844 | 0.727 |
| Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct | 1 | 0.616 | 0.484 | 0.878 | 0.812 |
| Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct | 2 | 0.599 | 0.476 | 0.854 | 0.736 |

The 128-value 3-bit codec reduced head storage by about 27%; adding subgroup
ranks reduced it by about 25%. The 4-bit codec reduced head storage by about
22%, with roughly 98.7% of Qwen3.5 blocks avoiding its escape-handling path.
GPU unpacking cost erased these storage savings in every complete head test.
All four head profiles are rejected for integration.

The one-column 4-bit kernel improved the small Qwen3 down projection by
1.54x/1.59x in this isolated suite. Its absolute GPU times were about 0.06 ms;
raw small-matrix timings varied between suites. This is a candidate for a
closer layer/full-model test, not a demonstrated inference gain. Qwen3.5
small-projection results were mixed and coder's small projection regressed.
No full-model speed or 2x-target improvement is claimed.

## Evidence and reproduction

- `lossless-gpu-probe-20261013`: 3-bit tags, SIMD prefix escape indexing.
- `lossless-gpu-rank-probe-20261013`: 3-bit tags, rank bytes and popcounts.
- `lossless-gpu-nibble-probe-20261013`: 4-bit tags, uniform escape-free path.
- `lossless-gpu-nibble-single-probe-20261013`: same exact nibble assets, one
  output column per SIMD group. Every reused input digest was verified.

Each directory retains its exact commands/exits, hardware and source hashes,
combined Metal shader, versioned source snapshot, complete input manifests,
input SHA-256 values, preparation log, GPU checks, individual timing windows
and summary. Reproducible checkpoint-derived `.bin` files and the compiled
probe binary are excluded from this checkout's evidence; the private Mac
investigation directories retain them. The source snapshot corresponding to
each suite can regenerate its inputs from the unchanged checkpoint. The
current probe script additionally supports explicit `--single-column` and
verified `--reuse-assets` modes.

Garnet's selected native state-handoff implementation remains unchanged.
The matched full-model results in the parent report still apply. The
2x-throughput and half-TTFT goal is active and unmet for all agreed profiles.

reports.title: Partial output-head bounds
reports.report_text:
# Partial output-head bounds

`partial-head-bounds-fusion-20261013` completed six native inference captures:
all three existing checkpoints, batches 1 and 2, identical saved baseline
prompts/caps/chunk profiles, and the same state-handoff native library. The
VL cases actually re-encoded the canonical real-image patches. Complete token
IDs, prompt IDs and finished flags exactly match the native matched baselines.
This diagnostic capture is not a timing comparison; it reprojects each sampled
state and writes full logits, adding work to the ordinary inference path.

The first eight head queries per stream were captured, for 72 row/step queries.
A standalone native RMS graph supplies the actual normalized FP32 inputs.
Its separate complete BF16-weight projection matches the ordinary full head
bit for bit, including signed-zero checks. Thus this probe removes the earlier
whole-row experiment's approximate CPU normalization limitation. The ordinary
complete head selected every generated token; no pruning executed on the GPU.

The offline analysis divides each vocabulary row into 32/64/128-value blocks.
After a partial dot product, Cauchy bounds cover the remaining dot product.
FP64 norm/partial calculations have conservative rounding allowances, plus
a deliberately conservative FP32 full-dot error envelope. Every bound at
every tested prefix was checked against every corresponding actual GPU logit.
Every actual winner remained eligible, and the FP64 full-dot argmax agrees
with the GPU winner for all samples. This validates the sampled calculations;
it does not certify an unimplemented GPU bound or all future input states.

## Counterfactual weight reads

These percentages are median reductions in head weight reads per captured row,
including the cost of computing 8192 complete seed rows. The seed's actual
maximum GPU logit is the available threshold. Batch 1/2 medians are identical
for these duplicated-prompt workloads; batch 2 still requires a GPU design
that shares weights across rows and tracks their union of eligible candidates.

| Model | 32-value contiguous blocks | 32-value blocks ordered by hidden energy | 128-value contiguous blocks |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Qwen3-0.6B | 30.32% | 33.85% | 25.76% |
| Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct | 28.56% | 36.18% | 24.11% |
| Qwen3.5-0.8B, real-image queries | 23.39% | 29.24% | 19.21% |

The estimates omit bound metadata reads, reductions/norm arithmetic, dispatch,
noncontiguous gather overhead, batch-sharing effects and session integration.
The analysis itself read the complete head to construct/check the bounds.
It did not skip actual CPU/GPU inference work or measure a speed gain.
The `oracle-full-max` policy in the raw reports uses the unavailable complete
winner threshold and is explicitly optimistic feasibility data; it is not
used in the table or proposed as a serving implementation.

These results justify a measured GPU prototype with actual seed calculation,
conservative GPU bounds, shared batch reads and checks against the complete
head. Such a prototype must validate retained logits and selected tokens,
then full generated outputs and matched latency. The public complete-logit
head path must keep its semantics; returning pruned sentinels there would
change the API. The decoder body and first-token targets remain open as well.

## Evidence

Each model/batch directory contains its case, normalized queries, full generated
outputs, output validation, offline report and all candidate-survival curves.
The actual full native GPU logit JSON files remain in the private Mac directory;
their SHA-256 values are in the reports. They are omitted from this checkout's
archive to avoid retaining large reproducible arrays. Source snapshots, native
library/model hashes, all commands/exits and process guards are preserved.

Three failed captures are retained with their exact source versions. The first
two hit the native parser's `case=` keyword limitation before inference. The
explicit-loop edit did not resolve that error. The third corrected the record
key but attempted to build a graph without the required fusion wrapper and
failed during setup. The successful capture uses properly wrapped graphs.
No interrupted or failed capture is included in the successful six-case results.

No production source was changed and no inference speed improvement is claimed.
The full 2x-throughput/half-TTFT objective remains active and unmet.

# Validated wide prefill tiles

The selected native candidate is `build-prefill-wide`, library SHA-256
`01ac8c4f04a91f20fcb3108ba451c3e54fc77daf3c6bc0f6103aa803848ab741`.
It uses a 16x64 output/K64 tile for 16-row prefill projections and a 32x64
output/K32 tile for larger row counts through 32. Small row/output shapes keep
the established kernel; unsupported optional pipelines also fall back. Decode
still uses the original BF16 matrix-vector kernel. Weights remain exact BF16,
with FP32 inputs/accumulation/output. No quantization or model change is involved.

## Selection and verification

`prefill-tile-gpu-20261013` compared five shared-memory geometries against the
unchanged 16x32/K32 kernel using real first-layer matrices from all three models.
All 840 checks were bit-exact, including row counts 3/5/16/17/31/32, irregular
matrix tails and padded input/output strides. The 280 timed matrix profiles
use two ABBA rounds and 12 operations per window. Larger K-only tiles mostly
regressed; wider output tiles gave modest component gains. Isolated timings
were used to choose a candidate, not to claim an inference improvement.

The production candidate then passed all 11 checks: CTest, serving/reset/shared
graph behavior, mixed-image pipeline, real Qwen3.5 linear/full-attention chunks,
both real dense model references, all three complete heads, and small/pretrained
vision. Partial tails, paused rows and chunk sizes 2/4/8/16 are covered by the
Qwen3.5 tests. The actual generated outputs are validated below.

## Close native controls

The text/coder ABBA comparison executed 48 requests, and the native real-frame
ABBA comparison executed another 24. Every generated token ID, prompt ID and
completed-output flag matches the control. Each profile has two fresh processes
per build, one first-use plus two warm requests per process. This table averages
the four warm requests; full first-use and initialization records remain saved.

| Model | Batch | Control TTFT, ms | Candidate TTFT, ms | Reduction |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Qwen3-0.6B | 1 | 105.54 | 103.63 | 1.81% |
| Qwen3-0.6B | 2 | 190.74 | 173.81 | 8.88% |
| Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct | 1 | 75.28 | 71.87 | 4.54% |
| Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct | 2 | 112.31 | 100.70 | 10.33% |
| Qwen3.5-0.8B, actual image | 1 | 697.09 | 692.04 | 0.72% |
| Qwen3.5-0.8B, actual image | 2 | 1186.92 | 1133.62 | 4.49% |

Decode ratios against the controls are approximately 0.995–1.000. There is no
decode-speed gain demonstrated by this prefill-only change. The smallest
batch-1 TTFT changes are modest; the batch-2 reductions justify keeping the
candidate. The image clocks include the common CPU frontend, fresh native
vision encoding and worker protocol. Native frame controls use the same
RGB/patch bytes and complete the same 28-token captions in both batch sizes.

## Updated actual vLLM comparisons

The same candidate completed 48 matched text/coder requests and 24 matched
image requests against the unchanged isolated comparator. Processes ran
strictly sequentially. Prefix reuse/speculation stayed disabled; all checkpoint
files, prompts, image geometry and caps match the frozen profiles. Each runtime
again has separate first-use and warm records, with initialization separate
and filesystem caches unflushed. All workers shut down cleanly.

| Model | Batch | Garnet tokens/s per row | vLLM tokens/s per row | Garnet TTFT, ms | vLLM TTFT, ms |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Qwen3-0.6B | 1 | 56.42 | 74.55 | 103.82 | 50.15 |
| Qwen3-0.6B | 2 | 52.31 | 76.37 | 173.78 | 64.09 |
| Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct | 1 | 72.44 | 92.45 | 71.88 | 34.86 |
| Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct | 2 | 70.03 | 92.67 | 100.07 | 38.16 |
| Qwen3.5-0.8B, actual image | 1 | 43.59 | 48.72 | 692.52 | 202.55 |
| Qwen3.5-0.8B, actual image | 2 | 37.44 | 47.62 | 1139.68 | 327.35 |

Text/coder and VL batch 1 preserve exact complete outputs against vLLM. VL
batch 2 retains the existing different/capped comparator-caption limitation:
native completes 28 tokens, comparator reaches the common 32-token cap. Its
results are matched-input measurements with that output-quality/length caveat.
Native FP32 vision/activations/KV versus comparator BF16 arithmetic remains
disclosed; unchanged checkpoints are not bit-identical internal execution.
All six profiles fail both the 2x-throughput and half-TTFT targets. This is a
validated incremental improvement, not completion of the active objective.

## Evidence and reproduction

The directories retain all actual commands/exits, hardware/model/library/input
hashes, process guards, complete token/caption outputs, numerical logs and
summaries. `prefill-wide-source-20261013` snapshots the candidate C++ source and
all runners. The earlier comparator runner version is saved separately because
native-frame ABBA support was added after the matched vLLM jobs started. The
new runner records its own source digest and selects the appropriate native
build for both frame backends. The native-frame summarizer validates real
execution, complete equal outputs and input hashes before reporting ratios.

Raw checkpoint-derived matrix/patch/RGB arrays and compiled binaries are
excluded from the evidence checkout and retained privately on the Mac or
reproducible from pinned inputs. No original Mac repo, GPT-OSS checkout or Pi
checkout was changed. The full three-model objective remains active and unmet.

reports.title: Measured native GPU partial-head prototypes
reports.report_text:
# Measured native GPU partial-head prototypes

Four suites actually executed native Metal seed calculation, partial bounds,
shared batch weight reads and the unchanged native greedy argmax on the M4.
Each suite checked all 51 head requests: eight captured states in each model's
batch-1 and batch-2 profiles, plus a batch-2 pair combining different actual
states for each model. That is 78 row/state checks per suite, 312 in total.

The raw control matches every original native GPU logit bit. Every retained
candidate logit also matches bit for bit, every pruned logit is strictly below
its actual seed maximum, and every selected token matches the complete head.
All suites exited zero. No checkpoint value was quantized or replaced. These
are captured-state component checks; accelerated full-model generation did
not execute, and no pruned implementation was integrated into production.

## Timed work and comparison

Both policies execute one command buffer and wait for its completion. The raw
policy runs the complete unchanged native BF16 projection and native argmax.
The candidate runs an exact 8192-row seed projection, GPU seed maximum and
hidden residual-norm preparation, the partial-head kernel, then that same
native argmax. Seed rows are reused, and weights remain shared while either
batch row needs a column. The weight residual norms are precomputed outside
timing with upward FP32 rounding and an allowance. Dynamic bound evaluation
and conservative partial/full-dot error allowances execute on the GPU.

Each request has two ABBA rounds, two warm operations per window and eight
measured operations per policy window. GPU and wall-clock medians are saved
separately. Normalization common to both policies, preparation/upload of
constant weights/norms, compilation and CPU checks/readbacks are excluded.
No other investigation inference runtime was alive during these runs.

Numbers below are medians of per-request raw/candidate GPU-time ratios over
the eight ordinary captured states. Values below 1 mean the candidate was
slower. The mixed-state cases remain in the raw reports and quality checks.

| Model | Batch | One column | Four columns | Four columns, skip final bound | Four columns, check every 256 values |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Qwen3-0.6B | 1 | 0.986 | 0.983 | 1.059 | 1.076 |
| Qwen3-0.6B | 2 | 0.835 | 0.894 | 0.890 | 1.009 |
| Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct | 1 | 0.988 | 1.061 | 0.994 | 0.998 |
| Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct | 2 | 0.820 | 0.891 | 0.880 | 0.953 |
| Qwen3.5-0.8B | 1 | 0.848 | 0.893 | 0.881 | 0.953 |
| Qwen3.5-0.8B | 2 | 0.764 | 0.822 | 0.803 | 0.913 |

The final profile's median raw/candidate GPU milliseconds were 3.170/2.936
for text batch 1, 3.223/3.195 for text batch 2, 2.831/2.831 and 2.902/3.033
for coder, and 5.260/5.521 and 5.393/5.884 for VL. The modest isolated gains
are not full-model gains and do not meet either goal target. The coder batch-1
gain in the first wide layout did not persist in the later layouts.

Checking every 128 values counted about 26% fewer text, 24% fewer coder and
19% fewer VL weight-element visits, including the seed. The 256-value cadence
reduced bound overhead but skipped less work: about 23%, 15% and 14%. Raw JSON
calls this field `physical_weight_fraction`; it counts shared weight-element
visits from GPU iteration counters, not measured DRAM transactions. Metadata
traffic, cached/prefetched reads and bound arithmetic are reflected in timings,
not in this element count. The faster per-query cases do not establish a
general speed advantage. All four profiles are rejected for broad integration.

## API and remaining work

Pruned columns receive a finite sentinel only in the private greedy prototype.
The unchanged native argmax still checks actual nonfinite outputs. A public
complete-logit operation could not substitute these outputs without changing
its semantics. No API or production source was changed here. Any later use
needs a specialized prediction path, whole-model output validation and matched
serving timing. Decoder projections, prefill and vision remain optimization
work; the full three-model 2x/half-TTFT goal remains active and unmet.

## Evidence and reproduction

- `pruned-head-gpu-20261013`: one-column partial-head kernel.
- `pruned-head-gpu-wide-20261013`: four columns, bounds every 128 values.
- `pruned-head-gpu-no-final-20261013`: omits the bound after a complete row.
- `pruned-head-gpu-interval2-20261013`: additionally checks every 256 values;
  launched only after the verified preceding owned job exited zero.

Each directory retains exact source snapshots/hashes, combined shader, hardware,
commands/exits, pre/post process guards, input manifests, all checks and timing
windows, and summaries. Reused inputs were verified by every saved digest.
Checkpoint-derived `.bin` inputs and the compiled binary are omitted from this
checkout's archive and retained privately on the Mac. The full normalized
queries/full-logit capture evidence is linked by digest in the manifests and
the preceding `partial-head/` results. This source can regenerate the inputs.

reports.title: vLLM-Metal comparison evidence
reports.report_text:
# vLLM-Metal comparison evidence

Target: Garnet >=2x vLLM-Metal decode throughput and <=0.5x its first-token
latency on the same M4 16 GiB Mac and identical BF16 checkpoints. The first
clean matched baseline executed 48 requests. Garnet is slower in all four
profiles; neither target is met.

## Clean baseline

`baseline/vllm-matched-clean-baseline-20261012/jobs/summary.json` is the
authoritative repeated baseline for native build `d2a7146`. Each row below
averages four warm requests per runtime, following first-use requests in two
fresh processes. Full first-use results, generated token IDs, commands,
individual engine steps, process snapshots and model/library hashes are
retained in that folder. All 48 outputs and prompt token IDs match exactly;
all processes shut down cleanly.

| Model | Batch | Garnet tokens/s per row | vLLM tokens/s per row | Garnet TTFT, ms | vLLM TTFT, ms |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Qwen3-0.6B | 1 | 37.62 | 73.83 | 150.22 | 52.07 |
| Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct | 1 | 62.11 | 92.24 | 96.79 | 34.77 |
| Qwen3-0.6B | 2 | 27.20 | 75.34 | 280.62 | 71.12 |
| Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct | 2 | 55.83 | 92.36 | 157.85 | 38.03 |

Hardware: Apple M4 Mac mini, 16 GiB, macOS 15.6.1. Comparator: isolated
CPython 3.12.15, vLLM 0.30.0+cpu, vLLM-Metal 0.30.0, MLX 0.32.1,
mlx-lm at `9e6acca691e64d6d8bb808c328fcdea459099cca`. Despite the vLLM wheel's
`+cpu` label, the Metal plugin and MLX GPU execution are active and the device
probe reports Apple M4. Both runtimes use the same BF16 checkpoint files.
Garnet uses FP32 activations/KV/accumulation; vLLM uses BF16 model/KV execution.
This compares checkpoint/weight precision, not identical internal arithmetic.

The frozen workload has capacity 256, greedy generation, output cap 64,
no prefix reuse or speculation, identical native prompt IDs, and batch 1/2.
Decode speed uses the complete first-to-final prediction wall interval.
Per-request reset/cache preparation is included in TTFT. Filesystem caches
are not flushed. RSS is individual-process high water, not aggregate worker
or unique GPU memory. Two existing WorldSense service processes were verified
to have no inference/GPU libraries and left running; their CPU/RSS snapshots
are saved. Competing inference runtimes never overlap.

## Visible-cache optimization

Attention now scores and accumulates only the causal visible prefix. Cache
storage, slot bounds, state reset, weight precision and context capacity stay
the same. The inactive-row controls retain their previous fallback behavior.
All 11 numerical/serving/vision validation jobs passed, followed by another
48-request matched suite with identical outputs and clean shutdown. Evidence:
`visible-cache/visible-cache-checks-20261012` and
`visible-cache/vllm-matched-visible-cache-20261012/jobs/summary.json`.

| Model | Batch | Garnet tokens/s per row | vLLM tokens/s per row | Garnet TTFT, ms | vLLM TTFT, ms |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Qwen3-0.6B | 1 | 40.18 | 74.40 | 118.77 | 51.51 |
| Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct | 1 | 67.73 | 92.33 | 75.40 | 34.72 |
| Qwen3-0.6B | 2 | 28.49 | 75.53 | 214.42 | 70.55 |
| Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct | 2 | 61.01 | 92.00 | 113.86 | 38.30 |

Against the native baseline, decode improves 4.8–9.0% and TTFT falls
20.9–27.9%. Neither vLLM-relative target is met. GPU time remains the principal
decode cost; these gains are not evidence of a 2x comparator advantage.

## Rejected prefill experiment

`transposed-gemm/` retains a column-major shared-weight tile experiment that
uses a transposed SIMD-group load. All 11 validation jobs and the 48 matched
requests passed, including exact outputs. However, warm TTFT worsened by
6.4–22.8% against the visible-cache build. The small decode differences are
not persuasive because this experiment changes only GEMM prefill. It was
reverted. `rejected_kernel.diff` records the attempted kernel; the source
branch retains the original GEMM layout.

| Model | Batch | Experimental Garnet TTFT, ms | Visible-cache TTFT, ms |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Qwen3-0.6B | 1 | 136.14 | 118.77 |
| Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct | 1 | 92.58 | 75.40 |
| Qwen3-0.6B | 2 | 228.05 | 214.42 |
| Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct | 2 | 127.74 | 113.86 |

## Rejected decode-address experiment

`u32-decode/` retains a guarded 32-bit index variant of the unchanged BF16
GEMV arithmetic, with the original 64-bit fallback. The matrix reference
test (aligned/odd widths, padded rows and batches) and all three pretrained
vocabulary-head checks passed. All 48 matched requests had exact outputs and
clean shutdown. Decode rates were 40.35/68.22 tokens/s for text/coder batch 1
and 28.96/61.59 for batch 2, only 0.4–1.6% above the visible-cache run.
That difference does not establish a useful gain. The extra kernel/dispatch
path was reverted; `rejected_kernel.diff` preserves its implementation.

## Qwen3.5 image compatibility

Actual Qwen3.5-0.8B image inference succeeded on vLLM-Metal, using the same
existing checkpoint and RealWorld-04 image. The first probe reused its image
identity; those warm timings are not a fresh-frame baseline. The corrected
probe assigns a unique multimodal UUID per request, which identifies all
vLLM image/embedding caches, while disabling processor cache, prefix reuse
and speculation. It executed three requests with 79 prompt tokens and 54
visual tokens each, matching the native 288x192 profile's token geometry.
All produced the same 28-token completed caption and shut down cleanly.

The fresh-process first-use TTFT was 264.29 ms. The two loaded fresh-frame
TTFTs were 195.81 and 195.82 ms, with total response times 751.88 and
748.76 ms. Initialization and full per-step outputs are saved separately in
`u32-decode/vllm-qwen35-fresh-image-probe-20261012`. The earlier probe's
4.42-second first use includes a different compilation/cache state; these
are fresh-process measurements with filesystem/compiler caches unflushed.

These are compatibility measurements, not a matched Garnet speed claim.
The comparator opens/preprocesses the source image inside its request timer;
the previous native image harness consumes prepared FP32 patches. A shared
preprocessing/timing boundary and repeated native/comparator VL comparison
are still required. Internal vision arithmetic also differs (native FP32
versus comparator BF16) despite identical BF16 checkpoint files.

## Optional MPS prefill and operation profiling

`mps-prefill/vllm-matched-mps-prefill-20261012` executed another 48 matched
requests with exact token outputs and clean shutdown. The optional `mps`
prefill policy expands original BF16 weights exactly into FP32 MPS matrices;
decode retains BF16 weights and the default policy remains `shared`.

| Model | Batch | MPS-prefill Garnet TTFT, ms | vLLM TTFT, ms | Native process RSS, GiB |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Qwen3-0.6B | 1 | 113.91 | 49.54 | 3.00 |
| Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct | 1 | 67.54 | 34.56 | 2.38 |
| Qwen3-0.6B | 2 | 181.87 | 64.93 | 3.11 |
| Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct | 2 | 84.99 | 37.74 | 2.39 |

Warm TTFT falls 4.1–25.4% against the visible-cache shared-weight profile,
at roughly twice its native RSS. Decode does not improve. First-use conversion
cost remains in the first request's timing. Neither comparator target is met;
the three-model resident-memory scenario has not been validated with this
optional policy.

An opt-in serialized-operation diagnostic (`GARNET_METAL_PROFILE_OPS=1`)
passed the default matrix test and retained the exact 8-token native text
output. It deliberately submits and waits after each operation, so its timings
are not serving performance or a comparator result. Raw commands, operation
timings and aggregation are in `mps-prefill/op-profile-20261012` and
`mps-prefill/op-profile-build-checks-20261012`.

The diagnostic points to both projection and KV-update cost. Across this
22-token prefill plus 7 subsequent decode steps, prefill matrix operations
sum to 71.70 ms and chunk KV updates to 32.80 ms. Decode matrix operations
sum to 75.89 ms, single-token KV updates to 35.11 ms, and 8 vocabulary-head
projections to 23.89 ms. These isolated sums include different submission
overhead/cache behavior; they guide the next experiment rather than replacing
the normal end-to-end timers. The current chunk KV kernel scans all input
tokens separately for every output cache element, even for contiguous slots.

## Direct slots, aligned copies and private state-buffer handoff

The direct-slot path checks the host controls for a contiguous active prefix
before replacing the per-element chunk scan with direct lookup. Gaps,
overwrites and paused/resumed rows retain the original scan. All 11 checks
and 48 native/vLLM requests passed. A close native ABBA comparison then
confirmed text-model warm TTFT reductions of 9.3% (batch 1) and 8.1% (batch 2),
with unchanged decode speed. Coder reductions were 1.6% and 0.4%.
`direct-slots/` saves those commands, libraries, exact outputs, controls and
the tested source snapshot; these native ABBA gains are not vLLM-relative gains.

The next build adds bit-preserving float4 cache copies where alignment and
uint-index bounds permit, with the scalar fallback retained. Resident sessions
now exchange independently written output buffers with their private state
instead of copying every layer's entire state back. Storage aliases move
together; input/constant storage and overlapping output parts retain the copy
path. The private session state remains protected by the graph/session locks.

All 11 validation jobs passed, including paused rows, resets, chunk/profile
replacement, shared-graph session isolation and independent hidden snapshots.
The mixed image pipeline and pretrained layer/head references passed too.
Another 48 matched native/vLLM requests produced exact outputs and clean
shutdown. `state-handoff/` retains the complete evidence.

| Model | Batch | Garnet tokens/s per row | vLLM tokens/s per row | Garnet TTFT, ms | vLLM TTFT, ms |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Qwen3-0.6B | 1 | 56.94 | 74.52 | 105.69 | 49.74 |
| Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct | 1 | 72.69 | 92.18 | 74.26 | 34.79 |
| Qwen3-0.6B | 2 | 51.88 | 75.85 | 188.86 | 70.82 |
| Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct | 2 | 70.44 | 92.25 | 112.33 | 37.99 |

Against the preceding direct-slot build, native decode improves about 42%
and 84% for text batch 1/2, and 7% and 16% for coder. Memory remains close to
the shared-weight profile. These are meaningful native improvements, but
Garnet still trails vLLM-Metal and every 2x/half-TTFT flag remains false.

## Remaining investigation

The native CLI cannot import NumPy in this SDK build. The actual preprocessing
probe failed before producing any patches; its raw failure is in
`direct-slots/xlang-image-preprocessing-probe-20261012`. A common CPU image
frontend feeding resident native/MLX workers is still needed to establish a
fair image-to-result timing boundary. The runtime/SDK were not modified.

The common frontend and persistent-worker comparison has subsequently executed;
see the matched VL section below. The failed direct-import probe remains intact.

Real full-head query/score samples from all three checkpoints are saved in
`state-handoff/head-bound-feasibility-20261012`. The basic whole-row Cauchy
norm bound prunes no rows in the sampled queries, even when supplied the
true maximum score. No pruning kernel or pruning speed advantage is claimed.
The approximate CPU normalization and 0.1% margin make this feasibility data,
not production proof. Further projection/attention optimization and the
matched VL comparison remain open. The full goal is active and unmet.

## Matched fresh-frame VL comparison

`vl-frames/vllm-matched-vl-file-events-20261012` executed 24 actual requests:
two fresh processes per runtime/batch, each with one first-use and two warm
frames. Every process exited cleanly. Both runtimes received identical resized
RGB pixels and the same 79 prompt IDs/54 visual tokens. Native patch bytes
match the canonical fixture exactly, in batches 1 and 2. Source preparation,
reset and worker transport are included in the parent monotonic first/done
timers; compiler/filesystem caches were not flushed. All learned native
operators execute in Garnet. The common CPU frontend uses the isolated
comparator Python for both runtimes, without importing an inference framework.

| Batch | Garnet tokens/s per row | vLLM tokens/s per row | Garnet TTFT, ms | vLLM TTFT, ms | Garnet total, ms | vLLM total, ms |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 43.47 | 48.59 | 698.28 | 200.47 | 1319.33 | 756.18 |
| 2 | 37.62 | 47.32 | 1186.70 | 327.12 | 1904.38 | 982.92 |

Batch 1 produced exactly the same completed 28-token caption in all 12
requests. Batch 2 native requests produced that same 28-token caption in
both rows, while comparator requests generated a different 32-token caption
and reached the common output cap. Thus batch-2 exact-output/completion checks
fail and its timing is a matched-input measurement with that quality/length
limitation. Neither profile meets either target. Internal native FP32 versus
comparator BF16 arithmetic is disclosed; identical checkpoints are not a claim
of bit-identical internal model execution.

Common source-image preparation costs about 50–54 ms per warm request. Native
batch-1 vision alone costs about 79–82 ms; most remaining TTFT is model prefill.
Each native frame is re-encoded and each comparator row/frame has a unique
encoder-cache identity. The first/done event protocol polls at 1 ms. Diagnostics
are read after the observed done event, so larger comparator logs do not
inflate its response timer. Per-worker times, all captions/token IDs, process
snapshots and input hashes remain available in `frame_summary.json`.

Two earlier attempts are retained: the system-Python frontend lacked Pillow,
and the native stdout ready marker was buffered. The second worker was stopped
through its verified owned control file before any request inference; the
interruption record and terminal failure are preserved. The successful run
uses the isolated frontend and event files. No SDK/runtime was changed.

The VL measurement gap is now closed. Its optimization gap and batch-2 output
discrepancy remain open, alongside the text/coder speed targets. The full goal
remains active and unmet.

## Rejected VL MPS-prefill and decode-geometry experiments

The optional MPS-prefill policy executed 24 fresh-frame requests in
`vl-mps-roofline/vllm-matched-vl-mps-prefill-20261012`. Batch-1 native TTFT
was 789.36 ms versus 698.28 ms with shared BF16 prefill; batch 2 was
1195.74 ms versus 1186.70 ms. Decode did not improve. The same batch-2
comparator caption/output-cap discrepancy persisted. The profile is not
selected for this VL workload; its raw results remain preserved.

`single-column/` retains a decode geometry experiment with one output column
per SIMD group and compile-time batch specialization. All 11 checks passed,
as did 48 native ABBA requests with exact outputs. Decode gains were only
1.0–2.7%, while TTFT increased 2.5–8.8%. The kernel was reverted.
`rejected_kernel.diff` records the implementation; these are native-control
results, not a vLLM advantage.

## Streaming constraint and exact packing feasibility

Apple advertises 120 GB/s for the M4 Mac mini:
[official specifications](https://support.apple.com/en-gb/121555).
The exact checkpoint headers identify 1,191,968,768 BF16 projection/head bytes
for text, 987,922,432 for coder and 1,503,789,056 for Qwen3.5 VL. Reading every
such value once per decode step gives optimistic streaming ceilings of
100.67, 121.47 and 79.80 steps/s, before other traffic or arithmetic. The 2x
comparator targets exceed these ceilings. This is a conditional streaming
roofline, not a universal algorithmic lower bound: caching, exact pruning or
lossless packing can change the assumed bytes read. Header inventories and
the calculation are saved in `vl-mps-roofline/decode-streaming-roofline-20261012`.

`probe_lossless_bf16_codec.py` implements a CPU-only exact-bit prototype:
8 sign/mantissa bits, 3 exponent tags, full exponent escapes and 64-bit
metadata per 256-value block. It round-trips all 65,536 bit patterns, including
signed zeros, subnormals, infinities and NaN payloads, plus non-aligned tails.
Every sampled BF16 matrix block from the real local Qwen3.5 checkpoint also
reconstructs exactly. The weighted sampled storage ratio is 1.3971x
(11.4521 bits/value, roughly 28.4% fewer bytes). This is not quantization.
The report is `vl-mps-roofline/lossless-bf16-codec-report.json`.

At the CPU-prototype stage, no GPU codec or packed-model speed gain had been
demonstrated. That prototype established representation correctness only.
The subsequent GPU checks are recorded below; full-model numerical and
performance validation remains required before a codec could count toward
the goal. All 2x/half-TTFT targets remain unmet.

### Subsequent exact GPU packing measurements

`lossless-gpu/` now closes the GPU representation-feasibility question for
four experimental codecs/schedules. All three checkpoints' complete heads
and first-layer down projections reconstructed exactly on the GPU; all 48
isolated projection comparisons were bit-exact. All four full-head profiles
were slower than the unchanged raw BF16 kernel, despite 22–27% fewer stored
bytes, and are rejected for integration. A small Qwen3 projection improved
in isolation; no full-model gain or generated-output validation is claimed.
The earlier CPU-only paragraph describes the state before these experiments.
Exact commands, source snapshots, hashes, timing windows and limitations are
retained in `lossless-gpu/README.md`. Production native code was not changed;
the matched throughput and TTFT targets remain unmet.

### Partial output-head bounds on actual native queries

`partial-head/` captures actual native normalized head inputs and full GPU
logits from all three models in batches 1/2, including real-image VL inference.
All six complete output sequences match the saved native baselines. Every
tested partial Cauchy bound covers every actual GPU logit across 72 sampled
row/step queries; the earlier approximate CPU-normalization limitation is
removed. Offline fixed-seed estimates suggest 23–36% fewer head weight reads
at 32-value block granularity, before bound/gather/dispatch and batch-sharing
costs. At this stage no pruned GPU kernel or full-model speed gain had been
demonstrated. Exact sources, failed setup attempts, commands, full-logit hashes and
limitations are saved in `partial-head/README.md`.

### Actual GPU partial-head measurements

`pruned-head-gpu/` executed four layouts/cadences, including actual seed
projection, GPU norm/bound preparation, shared batch reads and the native
argmax. All 204 head checks passed: raw and retained logits are bit-exact,
pruned candidates cannot beat the observed seed, and selected tokens match
the complete native head. The checks include 312 row/state instances and
mixed-state batch pairs. They do not constitute accelerated full-model output
or serving validation.

The best text batch-1 component ratio was 1.076x; most other profiles were
near break-even or slower. Lower weight-element visits did not yield a broad
advantage once bound costs were timed. The profiles are rejected for broad
integration. No production source was changed; full-model throughput and
TTFT remain at the previously measured values, with all targets unmet.
Commands, source snapshots, timings and limitations are in
`pruned-head-gpu/README.md`.

### Validated wide prefill tiles

`prefill-tiles/` records five exact-value tile experiments, 840 bit-exact checks,
all 11 native validations, and 144 actual full-model requests across native
controls and updated vLLM comparisons. The selected wide tiles reduce warm
TTFT by 8.9% for text batch 2, 10.3% for coder batch 2 and 4.5% for real-image
VL batch 2 in close native ABBA tests; batch-1 changes are smaller. All native
control outputs remain exact and complete. Decode speed is effectively
unchanged. The candidate is retained in `build-prefill-wide`; the prior
`build-state-handoff` remains intact as its control.

The updated matched vLLM runs still fail every 2x/half-TTFT target. The VL
batch-2 different/capped comparator caption also persists. The full objective
remains active and unmet. `prefill-tiles/README.md` provides the current selected
implementation, complete metrics, precision limits, source snapshots and
first-use/warm accounting.

### Rejected whole-decoder lossless packing

The subsequent `../../20261013/decoder-codec/` evidence tested exact packing on
29 real projection matrices, then an actual native decoder implementation.
All 58 matrix checks, all 11 native validations and all 72 native-control
requests passed with exact outputs. The isolated 1.66–1.93x projection ratios
did not transfer to full inference: text gained about 4–5% decode, coder
batch 1 about 3%, while text/coder TTFT, initialization and memory regressed.
VL decode slowed about 2%. The implementation and CMake option were reverted.
`build-prefill-wide` remains the selected native candidate; all full-goal
targets remain unmet. The rejected source, commands and complete results are
retained in the later report.

### Rejected compute encoder reuse

`../../20261013/encoder-reuse/` records a serial shared-encoder prototype, all
11 existing validations, a new custom-compute abort/recovery test, and 72
actual native ABBA requests. All outputs matched, but decode/TTFT changes were
under about 0.5%. CPU encoding saved roughly 0.08 ms against 13–18 ms of GPU
work/wait per decode step. The reuse implementation was reverted; the focused
transaction test is retained and passed on the selected wide-prefill build.
GPU execution and data movement remain the larger targets. The full objective
remains active and unmet.

### Validated vector state slices

`../../20261013/vector-slices/` records serialized operation attribution,
all 11 native checks, 192 independent bitwise slice checks, 72 native ABBA
requests and 72 fresh matched vLLM-Metal requests. `build-vector-slice` is now
selected. Aligned state slices copy four floats per thread, with bounds/layout
guards and the scalar fallback. Actual image TTFT falls 11.3%/19.6% and decode
gains 4.4%/10.8% versus the wide-prefill control at batch 1/2; text/coder decode
is unchanged. All native control outputs match exactly. The updated matched
image batch-1 result is 45.67 versus 48.06 tokens/s, with TTFT 614.39 versus
204.99 ms. Image batch 2 retains its different/capped comparator caption.
All six profiles still fail both targets. Same BF16 weights and the native
FP32 versus comparator BF16 internal arithmetic limits remain explicit.
The objective remains active and unmet.

### Validated direct recurrent-state outputs

`../../20261013/delta-split/` records a two-output delta kernel and graph fusion,
all 11 native checks, 32 bitwise kernel configurations, transaction checks,
24 native image ABBA requests, a serialized execution diagnostic and 72 fresh
matched vLLM-Metal requests. `build-delta-split` is now selected. It removes
3,852 slice dispatches in the actual batch-2 image diagnostic and writes state
directly to its independent output. Against `build-vector-slice`, image TTFT
falls another 3.65%/6.84% and decode gains 1.77%/3.69% at batch 1/2, preserving
all complete native captions. The fresh matched batch-1 image result is 46.77
versus 48.77 tokens/s, with TTFT 596.34 versus 201.29 ms. All six profiles still
fail both targets; batch-2 comparator output and internal precision caveats
remain. The full objective stays active and unmet.

### Exact scaled FP16 MPS feasibility

`../../20261013/exact-half-probe/` records actual MPS format probes and an
exhaustive CPU bit-roundtrip survey of all rank-two BF16 tensors in the three
checkpoints. Direct BF16 MPS matrix multiplication aborts on this Mac; mixed
FP32 activation/output with scaled FP16 weight storage passes the toy GPU
reference checks. The CPU survey preserves every coder/VL matrix value exactly;
Qwen3 has one exceptional value each in its embedding and head tensors, which
require an exact fallback. This provides a candidate MPS prefill route without
rounding checkpoint weights, but no full-model speed gain or integration is
claimed. `build-delta-split` remains selected, and all performance targets are
still unmet.

### Validated exact scaled FP16 MPS prefill

`../../20261013/exact-half-prefill/` contains the initial prototype, integer
packing and final pointer-hoisted implementation. The selected investigation
build is `build-exact-half-prefill-hoisted`, configured with the optional
`GARNET_METAL_EXACT_HALF_PREFILL=ON`. Exact per-row weight encoding feeds mixed
FP32-activation/output MPS prefill while raw BF16 decode/large heads stay
unchanged. All 11 native checks pass; the integer codec agrees with an
independent oracle in 8,421,120 cases. All 72 native control outputs match.
Warm TTFT falls 11.9–22.7% for text/coder and 5.7–6.1% for actual images.
Decode is essentially unchanged. Removing per-element Metal buffer.contents
calls reduces packing-related initialization from 9–13 s to about 1.4–3.0 s;
startup still exceeds the raw control and text/coder RSS adds 0.7–0.8 GiB.
The option remains off by default. Another 72 actual matched vLLM requests
confirm that all six profiles still miss both targets. Precision and batch-2
image output caveats remain explicit. The full objective stays active.

### Validated vector chunk KV-cache updates

`../../20261013/kv-chunk-vector/` records aligned float4 copies with guarded
32-bit addressing, 144 independent bitwise update cases, all 11 native checks,
72 native ABBA requests and 72 fresh matched vLLM requests. The selected build
is `build-kv-chunk-vector`, retaining the exact-half prefill option. Against
the preceding selected build, Qwen3 TTFT falls 20.2%/24.8% for batch 1/2;
coder falls 3.5–4.4%, and image changes are small. All native outputs match.
Decode is essentially unchanged. The fresh batch-1 Qwen3 result is 56.92 versus
74.02 tokens/s, with TTFT 70.00 versus 49.58 ms. All six profiles still miss
both targets. Failed initial compilation/gated attempts, precision limits and
the existing batch-2 image-output caveat remain saved. The goal stays active.

### Rejected larger decode input tiles

`../../20261013/decode-input-tiles/` records 8/16 input values per lane versus
the established 4, with the same output geometry, BF16 weights and FP32
accumulation. The final component scan covers real first-layer projections,
all runtime-selected heads, batch 1/2 and irregular/padded tails. All 136
numerical checks pass; no consistent component advantage is established.
A coder batch-1 head signal does not repeat in the preceding complete-head
scan. The kernels were not integrated; no serving/vLLM gain is claimed.
The incomplete initial head scan and corrected source provenance remain
saved. `build-kv-chunk-vector` remains selected and both targets remain unmet.

### Rejected exact-scaled FP16 body decode

`../../20261013/half-body-decode/` records a body matvec using the exact-scaled
FP16 cache with FP32 accumulation and inverse output scaling. All 11 native
checks and completed control outputs pass. The initial 72-request native run
shows larger gains against slowed controls; the clean 48-request text/coder
repeat shows only 0.4–1.0% decode improvement with slightly worse TTFT. Two
confirmation attempts are stopped by the unchanged guard when unrelated
release-test xlang3 processes appear, so image gains remain unproven. The
candidate is reverted. A launcher error that rebuilt the control is preserved;
committed source restores the original exact library SHA before corrected
timing. No new vLLM gain is claimed. The selected build and full unmet goal
remain unchanged.

## Comparator teardown compatibility

The preceding 48-request suite in
`baseline/vllm-matched-native-syntax-baseline-20261012` generated identical
outputs but its vLLM workers crashed during shutdown. Its derived summary
flags `clean_backend_shutdown=false`; a parent exit code of zero does not
make that suite clean. Raw failures remain intact.

The private comparator patch skips Torch accelerator cache cleanup for
platforms whose Torch device type is CPU. The Metal plugin uses that metadata
for compatibility while inference runs on MLX. The original vLLM cleanup
checked only its OOT platform enum and entered the Torch accelerator cleanup
path incorrectly. No inference, scheduler or numerical code was changed.
`baseline/vllm-cleanup-compatibility-20261012` contains the exact one-condition
diff, original/patched SHA-256 and provenance; the second full suite proves
clean shutdown. `patch_vllm_metal_cleanup.py` verifies the official wheel's
original source hash and atomically patches only this isolated installation.

`setup/` retains completed setup attempts and the verified wheel-transfer job.
These are installation/network diagnostics, excluded from all inference timing.
The cached-URL setup was interrupted deliberately after verified local wheels
became available; its separate `interruption.json` records that action. A retry
with an incomplete UV copy failed the size/digest guard before installation.

`baseline/` retains the later setup, download, compatibility and benchmark
attempts, including interrupted transfers and early guard/parser failures.
The successful offline installation resolved 161 packages. Verified public
wheels, requirements and installed versions are recorded in the manifests.
All setup/download time is excluded from inference measurements.

The runner files have now passed actual native and vLLM engine execution. See
`test2026/metal/VLLM_COMPARISON.md` for matching, accounting and precision limits.
The GPT-OSS and Pi checkouts were checked clean and were not edited.

reports.title: Rejected lossless decoder packing
reports.report_text:
# Rejected lossless decoder packing

This experiment preserves every BF16 weight bit. It uses 8 sign/mantissa bits,
4 exponent tags, full exponent escapes and per-128-value metadata. The GPU
reconstructs the original bits before FP32 arithmetic. It is not quantization.
The original BF16 buffer is retained for prefill and fallback, and the large
vocabulary head is excluded from packing. The proposed CMake option defaults
off. Both the option and native implementation were reverted after measurement.

## Component evidence

`decoder-codec-gpu-20261013` tested 29 real projection matrices: dense layer 0
from text/coder, plus Qwen3.5 linear layer 0 and full-attention layer 3. Complete
CPU and GPU bit reconstruction passed for every matrix. All 58 batch-1/2
projection comparisons were bit-exact. Four ABBA rounds per case used three
warm operations and 12 measured operations per policy window.

Summed isolated projection-time ratios were 1.93x/1.89x for text batches 1/2,
1.66x/1.67x for coder and 1.91x/1.82x for the combined sampled VL layers.
These tests repeatedly reuse individual matrices. They are not full inference
or a vLLM advantage, and their cache reuse did not transfer to the model runs.

## Actual full-model results

`build-body-codec` compiled with the experimental option enabled. Its native
host packer reconstructs every packed value at weight-load time; numerical
references exercise GPU decoding. All 11 native checks passed, covering trained
dense/hybrid layers, chunks and inactive rows, serving/reset/shared graph state,
complete heads and vision. The native text/coder ABBA suite then executed 48
actual requests; the native real-image ABBA suite executed another 24. Every
prompt, generated token ID and completed-output flag matches the validated
`build-prefill-wide` control. No competing inference runtimes overlapped.

This table averages four warm requests per build/profile from two fresh
processes. Initialization and first-use requests are retained separately.

| Model | Batch | Decode ratio vs control | Control TTFT, ms | Packed TTFT, ms |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Qwen3-0.6B | 1 | 1.051 | 103.26 | 111.15 |
| Qwen3-0.6B | 2 | 1.040 | 173.32 | 182.15 |
| Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct | 1 | 1.027 | 72.89 | 83.80 |
| Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct | 2 | 0.998 | 99.43 | 112.74 |
| Qwen3.5-0.8B, actual image | 1 | 0.982 | 694.27 | 683.76 |
| Qwen3.5-0.8B, actual image | 2 | 0.977 | 1158.57 | 1126.15 |

Text decode gained about 4–5% and coder batch 1 about 3%, while text/coder
TTFT worsened about 5–15%. VL first-token time improved only 1.5–2.8% and its
decode speed regressed 1.8–2.3%. Individual-process peak RSS reached 2.192 GiB
versus 1.555 GiB for text and 1.795 versus 1.263 GiB for coder. This is child
RSS high water, not aggregate/unique GPU memory. Mean batch-1 process
initialization was 4.377 versus 0.984 seconds for text and 3.549 versus 0.775
seconds for coder. Load-time packing contributes to initialization, not warm
request timing. No three-model resident-memory advantage is claimed.

The broad decoder implementation is rejected. The validated wide-prefill source
and CMake file were restored locally and on the Mac; `build-prefill-wide` is
still the selected implementation. The experimental binary remains isolated.
There is no new matched vLLM speed claim from these native-control tests.
The full 2x-throughput/half-TTFT goal remains active and unmet.

## Retained evidence

The complete commands/exits, hardware/model/library/input hashes, process
snapshots, timing windows, numerical logs and output sequences are preserved.
`body-codec-source-20261013` contains the actual experimental native/CMake
sources and build script. `rejected_body_codec.diff` records the reverted change.
`decoder-codec-gpu-20261013/source-snapshot` preserves the separate matrix probe.
Reproducible `.bin`, patch/RGB buffers and compiled binaries are omitted from
this checkout's evidence and retained privately on the Mac. The original
repositories and protected GPT-OSS/Pi worktrees were not modified.

reports.report_text:
# Validated direct delta state outputs

The selected native build is `build-delta-split`, library SHA-256
`979489a5e8ab4ca7731b4a74a9c0ab434e84ef1e52563340d172c5662abbecc3`. A graph optimization recognizes a
packed delta update consumed only by its complete result and recurrent-state
slices. The update writes both independent matrices directly, eliminating
the packed temporary and both slice dispatches. Other graph patterns keep
the packed kernel. Update arithmetic, checkpoints, precision and models are
unchanged; session state exchanges include the second output and its aliases.

## Execution and verification

All 11 native validation jobs passed, covering real dense/Qwen3.5 layers and
heads, vision, partial chunk tails, paused rows, gaps, reset and shared graph
sessions. CTest additionally compares both direct outputs bitwise against
the established packed kernel in 32 configurations: batches 1/2, heads 1/3,
key dimensions 7/128, value dimensions 5/128, active/paused rows and padded
layouts. Both pending/aborted outputs remain unreadable; recovery produces
the original values, and in-place state updates are rejected.

A serialized actual batch-2 image diagnostic executed 1,926 DeltaSplit
operations. Total graph operations fell from 48,068 to 44,216, eliminating
3,852 slice dispatches. The complete caption/prompt IDs match the frozen
native output. Per-operation diagnostics deliberately split GPU submissions
and perturb cache/dispatch behavior; their times are not serving benchmarks.

## Close native image comparison

The ABBA control is the previously selected `build-vector-slice`. Both builds
executed 24 real-image requests in total, sequentially, with identical RGB
and patch bytes, fresh vision encoding and matching complete captions. Each
row averages four warm requests per build; initialization and first-use
records are retained separately, with filesystem caches unflushed.

| Batch | Control TTFT, ms | Candidate TTFT, ms | TTFT reduction | Decode gain |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 616.68 | 594.17 | 3.65% | 1.77% |
| 2 | 916.42 | 853.76 | 6.84% | 3.69% |

These incremental gains support retaining direct outputs. They do not
establish a 2x advantage over vLLM-Metal.

## Fresh three-model vLLM-Metal measurements

The candidate completed another 48 text/coder requests and 24 image requests
against the unchanged isolated comparator on the same M4 16 GiB Mac mini.
Runtime processes never overlap. BF16 checkpoint files, prompts, image
geometry, greedy generation, capacity 256, batches 1/2 and caps remain frozen.
Prefix caching, encoder reuse and speculation are disabled.

| Model | Batch | Garnet tokens/s per row | vLLM tokens/s per row | Garnet TTFT, ms | vLLM TTFT, ms |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Qwen3-0.6B | 1 | 56.77 | 74.77 | 103.05 | 49.68 |
| Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct | 1 | 72.56 | 89.24 | 72.00 | 40.66 |
| Qwen3-0.6B | 2 | 52.26 | 75.89 | 173.73 | 70.19 |
| Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct | 2 | 70.28 | 88.77 | 100.41 | 46.91 |

All six profiles remain below the 2x decode target and above the half-TTFT
target. Text/coder and image batch 1 preserve exact complete comparator
outputs. Image batch 2 retains the existing different/capped comparator
caption: native finishes 28 tokens, comparator reaches the common 32-token
cap. Its row is a matched-input measurement with a quality/length caveat.
Identical BF16 weights do not imply identical internal execution: native
FP32 vision/activations/KV versus comparator BF16 remains explicit.

The full goal stays active and unmet. Full commands/exits, model/input/source
and library hashes, numerical logs, actual token IDs, runtime guards, first-use
records and warm summaries are saved here. Raw RGB/patch arrays and compiled
binaries stay private on the Mac. `candidate-source/` freezes the changed

reports.report_text:
# Rejected compute encoder reuse

The experiment reused one explicitly serial native Metal compute encoder
across custom dispatches, with buffer barriers, and closed it before MPS work,
submission or abort. Dynamic threadgroup memory bindings were reset between
operations. Kernel arithmetic, BF16 values, graph outputs and state layouts
were unchanged. Apple documents multiple kernel dispatches in a compute pass
and resource-ordering barriers in its
[compute encoder documentation](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/metal/mtlcomputecommandencoder).

`build-encoder-reuse` passed all 11 existing native checks, plus a dedicated
custom-compute abort/recovery test. The new test aborts a custom add command,
requires the abandoned output to remain unreadable, then verifies a subsequent
batch completes correctly. It also passed on the restored `build-prefill-wide`
implementation. That transaction test is retained; the reuse code is reverted.

The close native ABBA comparison executed 48 text/coder requests and 24 real
image requests. Every prompt, token/caption sequence and completed-output flag
matched the selected wide-prefill control. There was no inference overlap.
The table averages four warm requests per build/profile; initialization and
first-use records are retained separately, with filesystem caches unflushed.

| Model | Batch | Decode ratio vs control | Control TTFT, ms | Reuse TTFT, ms |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Qwen3-0.6B | 1 | 1.000 | 103.00 | 102.52 |
| Qwen3-0.6B | 2 | 1.004 | 173.84 | 173.92 |
| Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct | 1 | 1.002 | 72.07 | 72.15 |
| Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct | 2 | 1.001 | 100.38 | 100.49 |
| Qwen3.5-0.8B, actual image | 1 | 1.001 | 693.98 | 690.41 |
| Qwen3.5-0.8B, actual image | 2 | 1.003 | 1136.54 | 1132.99 |

No material full-model advantage is established. Warm decode CPU encode time
fell from approximately 0.395–0.420 ms to 0.322–0.336 ms. Native GPU execution
remained approximately 12.7–18.0 ms, with CPU wait roughly 13.1–18.5 ms. These
phase fields are observations within serving steps, not times to add blindly:
GPU/wait can describe overlapping parts of one command's execution. Saving
about 0.08 ms in CPU encoding did not improve the end-to-end decode clock.

The experiment is rejected for integration and its C++ source was restored
locally and on the Mac. `build-prefill-wide` remains selected. There is no new
vLLM comparison or 2x/half-TTFT success claim. The active full objective is unmet;
these results redirect optimization toward GPU execution and data movement.

`encoder-reuse-source-20261013` contains the exact experimental source/build
scripts and the transaction test. `rejected_encoder_reuse.diff` records the
reverted code. Complete commands/exits, source/model/library/input hashes,
numerical logs, process guards, exact outputs, phase records and timing
summaries are retained. Reproducible raw image/patch arrays and compiled
binaries stay private on the Mac. Protected repositories were not changed.

# Validated exact scaled FP16 MPS prefill

The selected investigation build is `build-exact-half-prefill-hoisted`,
library SHA-256 `cf3b155e219458c7ee511279ba3f63a3a88968d696b9bed172f2219357ff52b8`.
Configure with `-DGARNET_METAL_EXACT_HALF_PREFILL=ON`; the option remains
off by default so the original low-memory raw BF16 path is available.

Body matrices up to 16 MiB are represented in FP16 using per-row powers of
two, without rounding checkpoint values. An integer codec verifies exact
representability, with whole-matrix fallback for any incompatible value/range.
Raw BF16 storage is retained for decode and large heads. Multi-token prefill
uses mixed MPS FP32 activation/output with FP16 weight storage, followed by
inverse per-output-column rescaling. Activations, accumulation and KV remain
FP32; this is an exact weight encoding, not reduced-weight-precision inference.

## Verification and native controls

The final build passed all 11 native checks, covering real dense/Qwen3.5
layers and heads, vision, partial tails, paused rows, gaps, reset and shared
graph sessions. The integer codec matches an independent floating conversion
and bit-roundtrip oracle for all 65,280 finite BF16 encodings at all 129
supported scales: 8,421,120 cases. Row-scale selection also matches frexp
for every finite positive BF16 magnitude. Signed zero, odd/padded layouts,
per-row scaling and a rejected encoding with working raw fallback are tested.

Native ABBA executed 48 text/coder requests and 24 actual image requests
against `build-delta-split`, sequentially. Every complete output, prompt and
finish flag matches. Each row averages four warm requests per build/profile.
Initialization and first-use requests remain separate; filesystem caches are
unflushed. Images use equal RGB/patch bytes and fresh vision encoding.

Decode is essentially unchanged; this change targets prefill. Six serialized
actual diagnostics preserve complete outputs and confirm the mixed path runs:

submissions perturb cache/dispatch behavior, so diagnostic times are not
serving-speed evidence.

## Startup and memory

The initial floating-conversion prototype took about 11.2 s to initialize
text, 9.0 s coder and 13.5 s VL. Integer conversion alone improved these only

The extra FP16 body copy still costs approximately 0.7–0.8 GiB in the measured

## Fresh actual vLLM-Metal comparison

The final candidate completed 48 matched text/coder and 24 matched image
requests against the unchanged isolated comparator on the same M4 16 GiB
Mac mini. Processes never overlap. Checkpoints, prompts, image geometry,
greedy generation, capacity 256, batches 1/2 and caps are frozen. Prefix
caching, encoder reuse and speculative decoding remain disabled.

| Model | Batch | Garnet tokens/s per row | vLLM tokens/s per row | Garnet TTFT, ms | vLLM TTFT, ms |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

and image batch 1 preserve exact complete comparator outputs. Image batch 2
retains the existing different/capped comparator caption: native finishes
28 tokens; vLLM reaches the common 32-token cap. That row is a matched-input
measurement with a quality/length caveat. Native FP32 vision/activations/KV
versus comparator BF16 internal arithmetic remains explicit, despite unchanged
BF16 checkpoint weights. The full objective stays active and unmet.

reports.title: Exact scaled FP16 storage feasibility
reports.report_text:
# Exact scaled FP16 storage feasibility

This evidence establishes compatibility and exact weight-storage feasibility,
not a model-inference result or speed improvement. `build-delta-split` stays
selected; no production projection kernel has changed in this experiment.

## Actual MPS compatibility on the M4

The SDK defines MPSDataTypeBFloat16, but MPSMatrixMultiplication rejects it
on this macOS 15.6.1 M4. Three independent BF16 cases abort with signal 6:
FP32 activation/BF16 weight/FP32 output, BF16 activation/weight with FP32
output, and all-BF16 storage. The FP32 control succeeds at 3x7x5 and
16x1024x64. Raw assertion messages and individual nonzero child statuses
remain saved; the runner exit zero means the compatibility survey completed,
not that BF16 multiplication succeeded.

The mixed-input assertion explicitly permits FP32 A/C with FP16 B. A second
GPU probe actually executes that combination, with BF16-derived toy weights
multiplied by 2^16 before exact FP16 storage and output rescaled by 2^-16.
Every toy weight round-trips bitwise to its original BF16-expanded value.
Both GPU shapes pass against independent FP64 dot products. Worst absolute
errors are 4.386e-9 and 2.456e-7, the same reported errors as the FP32 control.
Activation and output storage remain FP32. This does not establish timing
or numerical behavior for an actual Qwen graph.

## Exhaustive checkpoint survey

A CPU-only scan checks every rank-two BF16 tensor in each pinned checkpoint,
including embeddings and vision, rather than only selected runtime projections.
Each row gets a power-of-two scale based on its maximum absolute value.
After FP16 conversion and inverse scaling, all recovered FP32 bit patterns
are compared with the original BF16-expanded bits, including signed zero.
Processing 1,024 rows per window bounds temporary memory. Checkpoints remain
unchanged; this is a proposed storage encoding, not permission to round values.

| Checkpoint | Matrices | Values checked | Nonexact values | Nonexact rows |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Qwen3-0.6B | 198 | 751,566,848 | 2 | 2 |
| Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct | 169 | 493,961,216 | 0 | 0 |
| Qwen3.5-0.8B | 246 | 871,628,800 | 0 | 0 |

The Qwen3 exceptions are:

- `lm_head.weight`: 1 values in 1 rows; coordinates/original/recovered bits are in its JSON report.
- `model.embed_tokens.weight`: 1 values in 1 rows; coordinates/original/recovered bits are in its JSON report.

A production candidate must preserve these exceptional values through an
exact fallback. It must also apply the inverse per-output-column scales on
the GPU and validate FP32 range/rounding behavior, actual layer references,
complete generated outputs, initialization/memory costs and sequential
end-to-end matched performance. BF16 values that do not round-trip must never
be silently replaced with an approximate FP16 value.

The next experiment is an optional exact-scaled FP16 MPS prefill path, keeping
raw BF16 decode and falling back for incompatible matrices. No 2x/half-TTFT
target is achieved here. Compiled probes and raw checkpoint data remain
private on the Mac; commands, source hashes, complete compatibility failures,
CPU survey reports and numerical logs are retained in this folder.

# Rejected exact-scaled FP16 body decode

The selected build remains `build-kv-chunk-vector`, SHA-256
`564b515ab6b0eb68413ef5a54de6beff47d333f8f1fa6a1188562bf6e5c28ec4`.
The candidate reads the existing exact-scaled FP16 body-weight cache in
decode, accumulates in FP32 using the original lane/input grouping, then
reverses each output-column scale. Large heads and incompatible matrices
keep raw BF16. Weight values, FP32 activations/KV, model files and caps remain
unchanged. The candidate C++ and build flag are reverted locally and remotely.

All 11 native numerical/serving/vision checks pass. The first completed
sequential native ABBA run executes 48 text/coder requests and 24 actual image
requests with matching complete outputs, prompts and finish flags. These
initial ratios are not sufficiently reproducible to select the candidate.

| Model | Batch | Initial decode ratio | Initial TTFT fraction |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Qwen3-0.6B | 1 | 1.008 | 0.988 |
| Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct | 1 | 1.001 | 1.009 |
| Qwen3-0.6B | 2 | 1.061 | 0.900 |
| Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct | 2 | 0.999 | 1.012 |
| Qwen3.5-0.8B, image | 1 | 1.119 | 1.001 |
| Qwen3.5-0.8B, image | 2 | 1.058 | 0.969 |

The initial Qwen3 batch-2 and image controls run materially slower than
the preceding selected-build observations. A clean repeated 48-request
text/coder comparison yields only 0.4–1.0% decode gain, with 0.6–2.1% worse
warm TTFT; all outputs still match. Four warm requests per build/profile
are averaged, with first-use and initialization retained separately.

| Model | Batch | Repeat control tokens/s | Repeat candidate tokens/s | Repeat TTFT fraction |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Qwen3-0.6B | 1 | 56.91 | 57.41 | 1.006 |
| Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct | 1 | 72.29 | 72.58 | 1.017 |
| Qwen3-0.6B | 2 | 52.12 | 52.63 | 1.021 |
| Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct | 2 | 70.07 | 70.34 | 1.015 |

Two confirmation attempts are stopped by the unchanged exclusivity guard
after unrelated release-test xlang3 processes appear: PID 65663 interrupts
the first text repeat, and PID 66625 interrupts the subsequent image repeat.
Incomplete/interrupted samples are not used to claim improvement. PID 65663
is missing on read-only follow-up. Unrelated processes are never terminated
and the guard is not relaxed. Image throughput improvement remains unproven.

The first launch mistakenly calls the previous build helper and rebuilds
the control; missing-candidate checks fail and dependent timing jobs are
gated. The control is restored from committed source and its exact SHA-256
is verified before the corrected candidate build. Those launch/restoration
logs remain intact. No timed run uses the accidentally rebuilt control.

The candidate is rejected: repeatable benefit is too small, TTFT regresses
slightly, and larger initial/image gains are not established. There is no
new vLLM benchmark or 2x/half-TTFT claim. The full objective stays active
and unmet. Recorded commands/exits, source/build/model/input hashes, actual
outputs, numerical references, guards and interrupted confirmations are
saved; raw RGB/patch arrays and binaries remain private on the Mac.
Protected GPT-OSS, Pi and original Mac checkouts are untouched.

reports.title: Validated vector chunk KV-cache updates
reports.report_text:
# Validated vector chunk KV-cache updates

The selected investigation build is `build-kv-chunk-vector`, library SHA-256
`564b515ab6b0eb68413ef5a54de6beff47d333f8f1fa6a1188562bf6e5c28ec4`. It retains the optional exact-half
prefill setting used by its `build-exact-half-prefill-hoisted` control.

Aligned chunk KV updates copy four FP32 values per thread using 32-bit
addressing. Head dimensions and data strides must be divisible by four,
and full token/cache/output/control addressing must fit 32 bits. Unsupported
layouts or unavailable optional pipelines retain the scalar path. Contiguous
active prefixes keep direct slot lookup; gaps, duplicate slots and paused
rows preserve latest-active-token selection. Arithmetic, precision, cache
capacity, checkpoint values and generated-output limits are unchanged.

## Validation and native control

All 11 native numerical/serving/vision checks passed. CTest additionally
checks 144 independent bitwise cache references across batch 1/2, heads 1/3,
dimensions 5/8/128, chunks 2/4/16 and four update patterns: contiguous,
paused tails, gaps/resumed rows and duplicate-slot overwrites. Odd dimensions
exercise scalar fallback; signed zeros and varied finite cache bits are kept.

The first build failed due to a mixed-type auto declaration; explicit size_t
fixes it. The failed build and dependency-gated jobs remain saved separately.
No numerical or timed trial ran from that failed attempt.

The close ABBA comparison executed 48 text/coder requests and 24 real image
requests, strictly sequentially. All complete prompts, outputs and finish
flags match. Each row averages four warm requests per build/profile; first-use
and initialization are separate, with filesystem caches unflushed. Images use
identical RGB/patch bytes and freshly execute vision on every request.

| Model | Batch | Control TTFT, ms | Candidate TTFT, ms | Reduction | Decode ratio |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Qwen3-0.6B | 1 | 88.19 | 70.36 | 20.22% | 1.006 |
| Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct | 1 | 56.86 | 54.38 | 4.36% | 0.999 |
| Qwen3-0.6B | 2 | 152.57 | 114.76 | 24.79% | 1.001 |
| Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct | 2 | 78.02 | 75.27 | 3.53% | 0.999 |
| Qwen3.5-0.8B, image | 1 | 560.22 | 558.94 | 0.23% | 0.995 |
| Qwen3.5-0.8B, image | 2 | 798.21 | 789.79 | 1.05% | 0.997 |

The substantial Qwen3 TTFT reduction supports retaining the candidate. Coder
gains are modest; image differences are small. Decode is essentially unchanged
because this optimization affects multi-token cache updates. Startup and
individual native text/coder high-water RSS stay close to the control; full
first-use, initialization and RSS values are in startup_summary.json. RSS
is not aggregate or unique GPU allocation. The inherited exact-half path
still has the separately documented raw-control startup/memory tradeoff.

The actual batch-2 text diagnostic preserves its complete output. Summed
serialized KVChunk GPU attribution falls from 38.75 to 5.24 ms.
These per-operation submissions perturb cache/dispatch behavior and are not
serving latency or a comparator speed claim. The native ABBA table above
establishes the full-request benefit.

## Fresh actual vLLM-Metal comparison

Another 48 text/coder and 24 actual image requests compare the selected build
with the unchanged isolated vLLM-Metal installation on the same M4 16 GiB
Mac mini. Processes never overlap. BF16 checkpoint files, prompts, image
geometry, greedy generation, capacity 256, batch 1/2 and caps remain frozen.
Prefix caching, encoder reuse and speculative decoding are disabled.

| Model | Batch | Garnet tokens/s per row | vLLM tokens/s per row | Garnet TTFT, ms | vLLM TTFT, ms |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Qwen3-0.6B | 1 | 56.92 | 74.02 | 70.00 | 49.58 |
| Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct | 1 | 72.48 | 92.27 | 54.97 | 34.90 |
| Qwen3-0.6B | 2 | 52.08 | 76.28 | 115.03 | 71.70 |
| Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct | 2 | 70.01 | 92.24 | 74.52 | 38.11 |
| Qwen3.5-0.8B, image | 1 | 47.17 | 48.41 | 562.71 | 202.02 |
| Qwen3.5-0.8B, image | 2 | 43.05 | 47.37 | 794.98 | 331.05 |

All six profiles still miss both the 2x throughput and half-TTFT targets.
Text/coder and image batch 1 preserve exact complete comparator outputs.
Image batch 2 retains the different/capped comparator caption: native finishes
28 tokens; vLLM reaches the shared 32-token cap. That row is matched-input
timing with a quality/length caveat. Native FP32 vision/activations/KV versus
comparator BF16 internal arithmetic remains explicit despite the same BF16
checkpoint values. The full objective stays active and unmet.

Commands/exits, failed-attempt evidence, source/model/input/library hashes,
numerical logs, complete outputs, runtime guards, diagnostic attribution and
separate first-use/warm records are retained. Private raw RGB/patch arrays and
binaries remain on the Mac. Protected GPT-OSS, Pi and original Mac checkouts
are untouched.

# Validated vector state slices

The selected native build is `build-vector-slice`, library SHA-256
`fd38413aad05a4946693681ff313810eeb5adcdec5992be66ffcb491612a41a2`. Aligned grouped slices copy four FP32
values per thread using 32-bit indexing. Source widths, starts, counts and row
strides must be divisible by four, and complete input/output addressing must
fit 32 bits; other layouts retain the scalar kernel. Weights, arithmetic,
models, context and outputs are unchanged.

Serialized per-operation diagnostics on all three actual models identified
large recurrent-state slices in Qwen3.5, especially batch 2. Diagnostic
dispatches submit/wait separately and perturb GPU/cache behavior; their
timings are not serving clocks or evidence of an inference speed gain. All
six diagnostic outputs matched the frozen complete native outputs.

## Native control and validation

All 11 native validation jobs passed. A further 192 independent bitwise slice
checks cover aligned/irregular widths, starts and counts, multiple groups,
batch sizes 1/2/5, padded rows, signed zero and varied finite FP32 patterns.
CTest passed on the Mac. The close ABBA comparison executed 48 text/coder
requests and 24 actual image requests, with every prompt/output/finish flag
equal to the selected wide-prefill control. Inference processes never overlap.
Each row averages four warm requests per build/profile; first-use and
initialization measurements remain separate, with filesystem caches unflushed.

| Model | Batch | Control TTFT, ms | Candidate TTFT, ms | Decode ratio |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Qwen3-0.6B | 1 | 103.68 | 104.16 | 0.998 |
| Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct | 1 | 71.88 | 72.35 | 1.001 |
| Qwen3-0.6B | 2 | 173.78 | 173.78 | 1.001 |
| Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct | 2 | 101.85 | 99.94 | 1.000 |
| Qwen3.5-0.8B, image | 1 | 692.62 | 614.38 | 1.044 |
| Qwen3.5-0.8B, image | 2 | 1134.52 | 912.22 | 1.108 |

Text/coder decode is essentially unchanged. The real-image workload gains
4.4%/10.8% decode and reduces TTFT 11.3%/19.6% for batch 1/2, which justifies
retaining the candidate. Input RGB/patch bytes match; vision is freshly
encoded on each request and both native builds complete the same captions.

## Updated vLLM-Metal comparison

Another 48 text/coder requests and 24 image requests compare the candidate
against the isolated unchanged vLLM-Metal installation, strictly sequentially.
Hardware remains the M4 Mac mini with 16 GiB. Checkpoints, prompts, batch 1/2,
capacity 256, greedy decoding and output caps are frozen. Prefix caching,
encoder reuse and speculation remain disabled.

| Model | Batch | Garnet tokens/s per row | vLLM tokens/s per row | Garnet TTFT, ms | vLLM TTFT, ms |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Qwen3-0.6B | 1 | 56.83 | 74.65 | 104.69 | 49.42 |
| Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct | 1 | 72.51 | 92.32 | 72.22 | 34.93 |
| Qwen3-0.6B | 2 | 52.32 | 75.85 | 173.91 | 67.99 |
| Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct | 2 | 70.31 | 92.37 | 99.96 | 37.97 |
| Qwen3.5-0.8B, image | 1 | 45.67 | 48.06 | 614.39 | 204.99 |
| Qwen3.5-0.8B, image | 2 | 41.56 | 47.97 | 911.11 | 325.07 |

All six profiles still fail both the 2x decode and half-TTFT objectives.
Text/coder and image batch 1 preserve exact complete comparator outputs.
Image batch 2 retains the existing different/capped comparator-caption
limitation: native completes 28 tokens; vLLM reaches the common 32-token cap.
That row is a matched-input measurement with a quality/length caveat.
The same BF16 checkpoint weights do not imply identical internal arithmetic:
native uses FP32 vision/activations/KV, comparator uses BF16 execution.

Complete commands, exits, hashes, numerical logs, actual output IDs, process
guards, diagnostic attribution and timing summaries are saved here. Private
RGB/patch arrays and compiled binaries remain on the Mac. `candidate-source/`
snapshots the changed source and reproduction helpers. Protected GPT-OSS,
Pi and original Mac checkouts are untouched. The full objective stays active.
Further work should target GPU projection/attention execution and removing
state-copy operations; this incremental gain does not establish 2x.
